name: Alchemical Sapper
description: ## Alchemical Sapper ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/18› Alchemical sappers are trained to create explosives. ::ab[Diminished Alchemy]{icon=down passive="An alchemical sapper can prepare one fewer extract of each level than normal. If this reduces the number to 0, he can prepare extracts of that level only if his Intelligence allows bonus extracts of that level." alter=Extracts} ::cskill{gain=ke~stl} ::ab[Demolition Bomb (Su)]{l=1 icon=power-ranged ability="An alchemical sapper can create a demolition bomb. This bomb deals double his normal bomb damage, half of which is bludgeoning and piercing damage, the other half of which is fire damage. This bomb ignores a number of points of hardness up to ‹misc/half› the alchemical sapper's level (minimum 1)." special="This counts as an ability that modifies the alchemical sapper's bomb, so it doesn't stack with other discoveries that modify bombs (Primary Bomb Discoveries). The alchemical sapper can't use his demolition bomb with the ‹discovery/fast bombs› discovery." usage="An alchemical sapper can only expend one use of his bomb class feature to create a demolition bomb once per day." incrementPlain="He can~1~4" incrementDesc=create incrementEnd=" demolition bombs per day." alter=Bomb} ::ab[Delayed Bomb (Su)]{l=1 icon=power ability="An alchemical sapper gains the ‹discovery/delayed bomb› discovery at 1st level." special="He does not qualify for the ‹discovery/mutagen› or ‹discovery/cognatogen› discoveries until 8th level." replace=Mutagen} ::ab[Master Engineer (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost passive="An alchemical sapper adds 1/2 his alchemist level to Knowledge (engineering) checks, Craft (stonemasonry) checks, and Craft (traps) checks." replace="Poison resistance"} ::ab[Camouflage Bomb (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost fullround="When deploying a *delayed bomb* or *trip mine* (see below), the alchemical sapper can camouflage the bomb by taking an additional full-round action. Creatures searching for traps must succeed at a Perception check (DC = 10 + the alchemical sapper's alchemist level + his Intelligence modifier) to notice a camouflaged bomb." replace="Swift alchemy"} ::ab[Trip Mine (Su)]{l=6 icon=power ability="An alchemical sapper can expend two uses of his bomb class feature to prepare a special kind of trap called a *trip mine.* This special bomb remains inert until 1 round after it leaves the alchemical sapper's possession, after which time it becomes armed. When a creature enters a square containing an armed trip mine, it explodes, dealing normal bomb damage to all creatures in its square (DC = 10 + 1/2 the alchemical sapper's alchemist level + his Intelligence modifier; Reflex half) and splash damage to every creature adjacent to that square. A trip mine can be disarmed with a successful Disable Device check (with a DC equal to the trip mine's save DC); otherwise, it lasts until the next time the alchemical sapper refreshes his daily bombs." special="If the alchemical sapper expends four uses of his bomb class feature, his trip mine deals damage as per a *demolition bomb;* this does not count against his daily uses of the demolition bomb ability. Other than *demolition bomb,* discoveries that modify bombs cannot apply to trip mine." replace="The discovery gained at 6th level"} ::ab[Selective Detonation (Su)]{l=10 icon=power ability="When an alchemical sapper plants a *trip mine,* he can designate a number of allies up to his Intelligence modifier, allowing the designated allies to pass safely through an armed trip mine's square without causing it to detonate. If another creature triggers the trip mine while an ally is nearby, the ally still takes damage as normal." replace="Poison immunity"}

name: Beastmorph
description: ## Beastmorph ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/25› Beastmorphs study the anatomy of monsters, learning how they achieve their strange powers. They use their knowledge to duplicate these abilities, but at the cost of taking on inhuman shapes when they use mutagens. ::ab[Beastform Mutagen]{l=3 icon=boost passive="A beastmorph's *mutagen* causes him to take on animalistic features - whether those of an animal, a magical beast, an animal-like humanoid (such as a lizardfolk), or a monstrous humanoid. For example, when the beastmorph uses his *mutagen,* he may gain a furry muzzle and pointed ears like a werewolf, scaly skin like a lizardfolk or sahuagin, or compound eyes and mandibles like a giant insect. The beastmorph also gains his choice of one of the abilities listed in the ‹spell/alter self› spell, which persists as long as the *mutagen.* He may select a different ability each time he creates a mutagen." replace="Swift alchemy"} ::ab[Improved Beastform Mutagen]{l=6 icon=boost passive="A beastmorph's *mutagen* grants him additional abilities and options. The alchemist gains his choice of two of the abilities listed in the ‹spell/beast shape I› spell, which persist as long as the *mutagen.* He may select two different abilities each time he creates a *mutagen.*" replace="Swift poisoning"} ::ab[Greater Beastform Mutagen]{l=10 icon=boost passive="A beastmorph's *mutagen* grants him three of the abilities listed in the ‹spell/beast shape II› spell, which persist as long as the *mutagen.* He may select three different abilities each time he creates a *mutagen.*" replace="Poison resistance +2, +4, and +6~poison immunity"} ::ab[Grand Beastform Mutagen]{l=14 icon=boost passive="A beastmorph's *mutagen* grants him four of the abilities listed in the ‹spell/beast shape III› spell, which persist as long as the *mutagen.* He may select four different abilities each time he creates a *mutagen.*" replace="Persistent mutagen"} @HL[Discoveries:] The following discoveries complement the beastmorph archetype: ‹discovery/feral mutagen›, ‹discovery/grand mutagen›, ‹discovery/greater mutagen›, ‹discovery/infuse mutagen›, ‹discovery/mummification›, ‹discovery/spontaneous healing›, ‹discovery/tentacle›, and ‹discovery/wings›.

name: Chirurgeon
description: ## Chirurgeon ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/18› An alchemist who studies anatomy and uses this knowledge to heal is a chirurgeon. A chirurgeon has the following class features. ::ab[Infused Curative]{icon=boost-power l=2 passive="A chirurgeon's extracts of ‹main/cure spells› automatically act as infusions, and can be used by non-alchemists. When a chirurgeon prepares his extracts, he may choose to render any or all of his infused curatives inert and prepare other extracts to replace them (unlike infusions, which continue to occupy the alchemist's daily extract slots until consumed or used)." replace="Poison use"} ::ab[Anaesthetic]{l=5 icon=power-aid passive="A chirurgeon learns how to supplement uses of the Heal skill with painkilling drugs. He gains ‹feat/Skill Focus› (Heal) as a bonus feat. Any use of the Heal skill that has a risk of harming the patient (such as extracting a barb) only deals the minimum damage when performed by a chirurgeon." replace="Poison resistance +4"} ::ab[Power Over Death]{l=10 icon=learn passive="A chirurgeon adds ‹spell/breath of life› to his formula book as a 4th-level extract. His *infused curative* ability applies to this extract." replace="Poison immunity"} @HL[Discoveries:] The following discoveries complement the chirurgeon archetype: ‹discovery/elixir of life›, ‹discovery/healing touch›, ‹discovery/infusion›, and ‹discovery/spontaneous healing›.

name: Clone Master
description: ## Clone Master ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/18› Clone masters practice duplicating existing creatures in order to better understand how to create new life. A clone master has the following class features. ::ab[Bomb]{icon=down passive="A clone master's bombs deal damage one die step lower than normal (regular bombs deal d4s, ‹discovery/concussive bomb«s› deal 1d3s, and so on)." replace=Bombs} ::ab[Lesser Simulacrum]{icon=learn l=7 passive="A clone master adds ‹spell/lesser simulacrum› to his formula book as a 3rd-level extract."} ::ab[Rebirth]{l=8 icon=power-magic ability="A clone master can prepare a clone of himself that awakens if he is slain. Creating the clone costs 5,000 gp, takes 1 week of work, and requires 3 additional weeks for the clone to grow to maturity. If he dies, the clone awakens as if the alchemist had used the ‹spell/clone› spell on himself. He can have one inert of himself at a time. Unused clones created by a clone master do not rot." replace="Poison resistance +6~poison immunity"} ::ab[Simulacrum]{l=13 icon=learn passive="A clone master adds ‹spell/simulacrum› to his formula book as a 5th-level extract."} ::ab[Clone]{l=16 icon=learn passive="A clone master adds *clone* to his formula book as a 6th-level extract."} @HL[Discoveries:] The following discoveries complement the clone master archetype: ‹discovery/alchemical simulacrum›, ‹discovery/doppelganger simulacrum›, ‹discovery/preserve organs›, and ‹discovery/parasitic twin›.

name: Herbalist
description: ## Herbalist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/22› Vine leshys who study the physical and spiritual composition of their own bodies have discovered a strange herbal alchemy all their own. ::prereq{r="Vine Leshy"} ::ab[Herbalism (Su)]{l=1 icon=power ability="An herbalist's studies allow him a unique method of creating alchemical discoveries. He can attempt Profession (herbalist) checks in place of Craft (alchemy) checks for all purposes, and he gains a competence bonus equal to ‹misc/half› his alchemist level on Profession (herbalist) checks to create alchemical items and to forage for and process herbs. An herbalist uses his @HLWisdom score instead of his Intelligence score for all alchemist class abilities." alter="Alchemy~the alchemist's key ability score"} ::ab[Natural Magic]{l=1 icon=learn passive="An herbalist's study of the leshy spirit grants him access to natural magic that eludes other alchemists. Each time he gains access to a new level of extracts (including 1st level), he can add two spells from that spell level on the ‹main/druid spell« list› to his alchemist class spell list; these spells must target a creature or creatures or have a range of &quot&you,&quot& and he must still add them to his formula book as normal before he can prepare them." special="As always, the extracts affect the drinker as if she were the target, so offensive touch spells are a nasty trap for the drinker." replace="Throw Anything"} ::ab[Seedpods (Su)]{icon=zap ability="An herbalist can produce and throw seedpods as ranged touch attacks, similar to the ranged attacks of other leshys. He can create a number of seedpods each day equal to his alchemist level + his Wisdom modifier and can throw them as a standard action with a range increment of 20 feet. A seedpod deals 1d6 points of bludgeoning damage, plus an additional 1d6 points of damage at 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter (this additional damage isn't multiplied on a critical hit or from effects like ‹feat/Vital Strike›). Seedpods are considered weapons and can be selected for feats like ‹feat/Weapon Focus›, and the herbalist can take the ‹feat/Extra Bombs› feat to gain additional daily uses of his seedpods. His seedpods also gain one of the following additional effects unless the target succeeds at a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + half the herbalist's alchemist level + his Wisdom modifier)." imp1="His seedpods can ‹misc/deafen› their target for 1 round like a ‹monster/leaf leshy›." imp2="They can reduce the target's vision to 10 feet for 1 minute (unless the target spends a full-round action to wash the spores from its eyes early) like the spores of a ‹monster/fungus leshy›." imp5="They can ‹rule/entangle<d› their target for 2d4 rounds (unless the target succeeds at a Strength check or Escape Artist check at the save DC to break the vine early) like the seeds of a ‹monster/gourd leshy›." imp8="They can ‹misc/sicken› their target for 1d4 rounds like the spittle of a ‹monster/flytrap leshy›." imp10="They can ‹misc/blind› their target until the end of their next turn like the water jets of a ‹monster/seaweed leshy›." replace="Bombs~poison use~poison resistance~poison immunity"}

name: Horticulturist
sourceBook: Ultimate Wilderness, Heroes of the Wild
description: ## Horticulturist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/35;Heroes of the Wild/24› A horticulturist spends his time cultivating plants and plant creatures, allowing him to experiment with strange and wondrous herbal concoctions. ::ab[Seed Extract]{l=1 icon=learn passive="A horticulturist adds *summon nature's ally I-VI* as 1st- through 6th-level extracts, respectively, to his class extract list. For example, he automatically adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally I› to his formula book at 1st level and adds the next higher-level spell to his formula book each time he gains the ability to use extracts of that level. The horticulturist uses these special extracts to plant a seed that grows into a creature, bypassing the restriction for single target or personal effects. Using these extracts takes 1 round (as the spell's normal casting time), and the creature summoned must be placed in a space adjacent to the horticulturist. The horticulturist can use these extracts to summon only animals and plants on the appropriate summon nature's ally list." special="Creatures the horticulturist summons with these extracts become creatures with the plant type (gaining low-light vision and immunity to mind-affecting, paralysis, poison, polymorph, sleep, and stunning effects) rather than their normal type, but their attack bonuses, Hit Dice, saving throws, and skills don't change. A horticulturist can't choose mutagen discoveries." replace="Mutagen~2nd-level discovery"} ::ab[Herbal Bombs (Su)]{l=1 icon=down-boost ability="A horticulturist's bombs lack the power of a traditional alchemist's but can be fine-tuned in ways normal alchemist explosives cannot. The horticulturist's bombs deal 1d4 points of damage (instead of 1d6), plus 1d4 points of damage for every 2 alchemist levels beyond 1st. When the horticulturist creates a bomb, he can formulate it to affect plants and other creatures normally, affect only plant creatures, or affect only creatures not of the plant type." alter=Bombs} ::ab[Plant Voice (Ex, Su)]{l=2 icon=boost-power passive="A horticulturist gains a +2 bonus on Knowledge (nature) and Survival checks." imp10="He can speak to plants as a constant ‹spell/speak with plants› spell (this ability is supernatural)." replace="Poison resistance~poison use~poison immunity"} ::ab[Plant Familiar (Ex)]{l=4 icon=power ability="A horticulturist creates a Diminutive or Tiny alchemical plant creature that vaguely resembles a kind of animal suitable for a familiar (such as a cat) and acts as his ‹ability/familiar›, granting the horticulturist a skill bonus, the ‹feat/Alertness› feat, and so on. The plant familiar has all the abilities of the animal it resembles (for example, a bat-like plant familiar can fly) but is treated as a creature of the plant type and has familiar abilities based on the horticulturist's alchemist level (though some familiar abilities may be useless to the horticulturist)." special="An alchemist's extracts and mutagens are considered spells for the purposes of familiar abilities like *share spells* or *deliver touch spells.* If a plant familiar is lost or dies, it can be replaced 1 week later through a specialized procedure that costs 200 gp per alchemist level the horticulturist has. The ritual takes 8 hours to complete." replace="The discovery gained at 4th level"} ::ab[Fury of Nature (Sp)]{l=14 icon=magic ability="A horticulturist's connection with nature allows him to bring down nature's fury on his opponents. He can cast one of the following spells, chosen at the time of casting, once per day as a spell-like ability: ‹spell/call lightning storm›, ‹spell/eagle aerie›, or ‹spell/liveoak›." replace="Persistent mutagen"}

name: Ice Chemist
description: ## Ice Chemist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/35› Reclusive alchemists who dwell in the highest mountains or on the frozen tundra devote their skills to mastering the cold. ::ab[Icy Bombs (Su)]{l=1 icon=power ability="An ice chemist's bombs deal cold damage instead of fire damage. In place of an alchemist discovery, she can learn to create bombs that deal fire damage like normal alchemist bombs do, though she can't apply discoveries that modify bombs to such fire bombs that she creates. An ice alchemist's icy bombs can still be poisonous or create thick vapors similar to smoke, but she cannot apply the ‹discovery/explosive<_bomb› or ‹discovery/inferno bomb› discoveries to them." alter=Bombs} ::ab[Cold Sweat (Su)]{l=2 flavor="An ice chemist channels her affinity for cold energy into her personal space, keeping herself and her gear cool." icon=def passive="She gains cold ‹umr/resistance› equal to her alchemist level and can survive comfortably in temperatures as low as -50&deg& Fahrenheit." replace="Poison resistance~poison immunity"} ::ab[Frost Bomb (Su)]{l=2 icon=power ability="An ice chemist gains the ‹discovery/frost bomb› discovery." replace="2nd-level discovery"}

name: Internal Alchemist
description: ## Internal Alchemist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/18› An internal alchemist studies medicine, diet, and the living body to purify the self in the hope of gaining immortality by means of alchemical concoctions and controlling vital energy. Internal alchemists develop unusual physical abilities from heightened knowledge of how their bodies work. An internal alchemist has the following class features. ::ab[Breath Mastery]{l=1 icon=power-def-magic flavor="The internal alchemist can control his breath and the flow of vital energy within his body." ability="Without preparation, he can ‹misc/hold his breath› for a number of minutes equal to his Constitution score (after this, he must begin making Constitution checks or risk suffocation)." fullround="By spending a @HLfull-round_action preparing himself, he can increase this duration to 1 hour per point of Constitution." move="He can put himself into a state of suspended animation as a @HLmove_action, and is then unconscious and appears completely dead; he awakens at a preset time or in response to a condition set by him when he enters this state." passive="The alchemist can survive twice as long as normal without food or water before he starts to take penalties." order=arpm replace="Throw Anything"} ::ab[Bonus Feats]{icon=power passive="An internal alchemist can select ‹feat/Alertness›, ‹feat/Extra Ki›, ‹feat/Great Fortitude›, ‹feat/Improved Critical› (unarmed strike), ‹feat/Improved Initiative›, ‹feat/Improved Unarmed Strike›, ‹feat/Iron Will›, ‹feat/Lightning Reflexes›, ‹feat/Stunning Fist›, or ‹feat/Weapon Focus› (unarmed strike) in place of an alchemical discovery."} ::ab[Disease Resistance]{l=3 icon=def passive="An internal alchemist gains a bonus on all saving throws against disease equal to his alchemist class bonus against poison." special="When he gains the *poison immunity* alchemist class ability, he becomes immune to disease as well." replace="Swift alchemy"} ::ab[Uncanny Dodge]{l=6 flavor="An internal alchemist can react to danger before his senses would normally allow him to do so." icon=def passive="He cannot be caught ‹rule/flat-footed›, nor does he lose his Dexterity bonus to AC if the attacker is invisible. However, he still loses his Dexterity bonus to AC if he is immobilized, or if an opponent successfully uses the feint action (see ‹skill/Bluff›) against him." special="If the internal alchemist already has *uncanny dodge* from a different class, he automatically gains ‹ability/improved uncanny dodge› (as a rogue) instead." replace="Swift poisoning"} @HL[Discoveries:] The following discoveries complement the internal alchemist archetype: ‹discovery/cognatogen›, ‹discovery/elixir of life›, ‹discovery/grand cognatogen›, ‹discovery/greater cognatogen›, ‹discovery/lingering spirit›, ‹discovery/mummification›, and ‹discovery/spontaneous healing›.

name: Interrogator
description: ## Interrogator ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/18› An interrogator extracts vital information from reluctant individuals using alchemical and traditional methods. ::cskill{gain=intm~sm} ::ab[Injections (Su)]{l=1 icon=power usage="An interrogator uses his skill with alchemy to create injections. Each day, an interrogator can create a number of injections equal to his alchemist level + his Intelligence modifier. It takes 1 hour to create the injections. An injection is inert until the interrogator attempts to use it." icon=touch standard="Using an injection is a standard action that requires a melee touch attack. If the attack hits, the target of an injection takes a -2 penalty on its Will saving throws for a number of minutes equal to half the interrogator's class level (minimum 1). If the interrogator is also using a *serum* with this injection, the penalty on Will saves applies to any save against the *serum.* If the melee touch attack fails, the injection isn't delivered but can still be used again - once activated, it remains potent for 1 day." special="An injection that hasn't been administered becomes inert if it leaves the interrogator's possession, reactivating as soon as it returns to his possession. The penalties from multiple injections don't stack, nor do the penalties from injections stack with penalties from a ‹class/mesmerist«'s› stare or a witch's ‹hex/evil eye› hex. Injections are mind-affecting poison effects." replace=Bomb} ::ab[Serums (Su)]{l=1 head icon=power order=wa flavor="An interrogator augments his ability to influence others through supplemental serums." swift="An interrogator prepares his serums at the same time as his injections and he can apply them to any injection as a @HLswift_action before he makes the attack roll for the injection." ability="An interrogator knows one serum at 1st level and can learn another serum in place of a discovery. A creature can be under the effect of only a single serum at a time - with the exception of *memory modification* serum - with any further serums on the same creature replacing the old serum." special="The save DCs of serums are equal to 10 + ‹misc/half› the interrogator's alchemist level + his Intelligence modifier. Unless otherwise noted, a creature that succeeds on its saving throw against a serum is immune to that serum's effects for 24 hours. An interrogator can never gain any sort of mutagen or cognatogen, even from a discovery or another class." replace="Mutagen~persistent mutagen"} ::ab[Charming]{sub icon=magic ability="The injected creature must succeed at a Will save or treat the interrogator favorably, as if affected by ‹spell/charm person› with a caster level equal to the interrogator's alchemist level." imp8="This serum acts as ‹spell/charm monster›."} ::ab[Compliance]{sub icon=magic prereq="8th-level interrogator" passive="On a failed Will save, the subject of this injection is affected by a ‹spell/suggestion› with a caster level equal to the interrogator's alchemist level."} ::ab[Confusion]{sub icon=lower prereq="6th-level interrogator" passive="On a failed Will save, the injected creature is ‹misc/confused› for 1 round per alchemist level the interrogator has."} ::ab[Hypnosis]{sub icon=lower passive="The injected creature must succeed at a Will save or become ‹misc/fascinated› for 1 round per alchemist level the interrogator has."} ::ab[Memory Modification]{sub icon=magic prereq="12th-level interrogator" passive="On a failed Will save, the target of this serum is affected by ‹spell/modify memory› at a caster level equal to the interrogator's alchemist level."} ::ab[Paralytic]{sub icon=magic prereq="8th-level interrogator" passive="On a failed Will save, the injected creature is affected by ‹spell/hold person› with a caster level equal to the interrogator's alchemist level."} ::ab[Truth]{sub icon=magic passive="A creature injected with a truth serum must succeed at a Will save or be compelled to answer the interrogator's questions truthfully. The interrogator can ask one question per 2 alchemist levels (minimum 1). Answers might be brief, cryptic, or repetitive, especially if the injected creature is unfriendly, but they aren't false. If a creature has been subjected to a truth serum within the past week, whether it succeeded at or failed its save, any new serum fails."}

name: Metamorph
description: ## Metamorph ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/19› Metamorphs eschew traditional alchemy, focusing on internal chemistry and the transfiguration of living forms. ::cskill{gain=dis} ::ab[Shapechanger (Su)]{l=1 icon=power-magic standard="At 1st level, a metamorph gains the ability to transform herself into another form. This ability functions like ‹spell/alter self›, except as noted here. The effect lasts for 1 hour per metamorph's alchemist level, or until she changes back. Changing form (to another form or back) is a standard action that doesn't provoke attacks of opportunity. The metamorph is ‹misc/fatigued› for 1 round each time she changes shape." provokes=No special="A metamorph can use this ability once per day at 1st level, and an additional time per day at 4th level, and every 2 alchemist levels thereafter, for a total of nine times at 18th level." imp20="A metamorph can use *shapechanger* as a @HLfree_action once per round, either before or after all her other actions, with no daily limit." imp5="This ability can also function as ‹spell/monstrous physique I›." imp9="This ability can also function as ‹spell/monstrous physique II›." imp11="This ability can also function as ‹spell/monstrous physique III›." imp13="This ability can also function as ‹spell/monstrous physique IV› or ‹spell/giant form I›." imp15="This ability can also function as ‹spell/giant form II›." replace="Alchemy~bombs~extracts~mutagen~Throw Anything"} ::ab[Mutagen (Ex)]{l=1 icon=power ability="A metamorph gains *mutagen* as a normal alchemist. She can take *mutagen* and *cognatogen* discoveries despite not possessing the alchemy class feature that normally grants mutagen."} ::ab[Adaptive Physiology (Ex)]{l=3 icon=def passive="A metamorph gains a 25% chance to negate critical hits and ‹misc/precision damage›, similar to the ‹discovery/preserve organs› discovery." imp6="This chance becomes 50%." imp18="This chance increases to 75%." replace="Swift alchemy~swift poisoning~instant alchemy"}

name: Mindchemist
description: ## Mindchemist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/19› While most alchemists use mutagens to boost their physical ability at the cost of mental ability, some use alchemy for the opposite purpose - to boost the power of the mind and memory. A mindchemist can reach incredible levels of mental acuity, but suffers lingering debilitating effects to his physique. A mindchemist has the following class features. ::ab[Cognatogen]{l=1 icon=power ability="A mindchemist learns how to create a cognatogen, as per the ‹discovery/cognatogen› discovery. (A mindchemist cannot create mutagens unless he selects ‹discovery/mutagen› as a discovery.)" replace=Mutagen} ::ab[Perfect Recall]{l=2 icon=boost passive="When making a Knowledge check, he may add his Intelligence bonus on the check a second time. Thus, a mindchemist with 5 ranks in Knowledge (history) and a +2 Intelligence bonus has a total skill bonus of +9 (5 + 2 + 2) using this ability. The mindchemist can also use this ability when making an Intelligence check to remember something." replace="Poison use"} ::ab[Bonus Feats]{icon=power passive="A mindchemist may select ‹feat/Skill Focus› (Disable Device, Disguise, Heal, any Knowledge skill, Sense Motive, or Spellcraft) in place of a discovery."} ::ab[Languages]{icon=power passive="A mindchemist may learn three ‹misc/languages› in place of a discovery."} @HL[Discoveries:] The following discoveries complement the mindchemist archetype: ‹discovery/grand cognatogen›, ‹discovery/greater cognatogen›, ‹discovery/infuse mutagen›.

name: Preservationist
description: ## Preservationist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/19› Some alchemists are obsessed with collecting and preserving exotic creatures. These preservationists may use bottled animals and monsters as teaching tools, but some learn how to reanimate them for short periods to battle on the alchemist's behalf. A preservationist has the following class features. ::ab[Bottled Ally I]{l=2 icon=skill-learn order=pa passive="A preservationist adds ‹skill/Handle Animal› (WIS) to his list of class skills." ability="He adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally I› to his formula book as a 1st-level extract. When he prepares that extract, he actually prepares a tiny, preserved specimen in a bottle (as with a caster casting the spell, the preservationist doesn't have to choose the creature until he uses the extract). When the alchemist opens the bottle, the specimen animates and grows to normal size, serving the preservationist as per the spell and otherwise being treated as a summoned creature. When the duration expires, the preserved creature decays into powder." special="If the preservationist has the ‹discovery/infusion› discovery, another character can use the infused specimen. The ‹feat/Augment Summoning› feat can be applied to these specimens." replace="Poison use"} ::ab[Bottled Ally II]{l=5 icon=learn passive="A preservationist adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally II› to his formula book as a 2nd-level extract." replace="Poison resistance +4"} ::ab[Bottled Ally III]{l=8 icon=learn passive="A preservationist adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally IV› to his formula book as a 3rd-level extract." replace="Poison resistance +6"} ::ab[Bottled Ally IV]{l=10 icon=learn passive="A preservationist adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally V› to his formula book as a 4th-level extract." replace="Poison immunity"} ::ab[Bottled Ally V]{l=14 icon=learn passive="A preservationist adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally VII› to his formula book as a 5th-level extract." replace="Persistent mutagen"} ::ab[Bottled Ally VI]{l=18 icon=learn passive="A preservationist adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally IX› to his formula book as a 6th-level extract." replace="18th-level discovery"} @HL[Discoveries:] The following discoveries complement the preservationist archetype: ‹discovery/bottled ooze›, ‹discovery/preserve organs›, ‹discovery/tentacle›, ‹discovery/vestigial arm›, and ‹discovery/wings›. @HL[Feats:] The ‹feat/Planar Preservationist› feat may be of particular interest to a Preservationist.

name: Psychonaut
description: ## Psychonaut ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/19› A psychonaut uses his knowledge to explore altered states of consciousness and even other planes of existence. A psychonaut has the following class features. ::ab[Bomb]{icon=down ability="A psychonaut's bombs deal damage ‹misc/one die step› lower than normal (regular bombs deal d4s, ‹discovery/concussive bomb«s› deal 1d3s, and so on). This ability otherwise functions as and replaces the standard alchemist bomb class feature." replace=Bombs} ::ab[Precognition]{l=5 icon=learn passive="A psychonaut adds ‹spell/augury› to his formula book as a 2nd-level extract (this extract does not require a divine focus component)." replace="Poison resistance +4"} ::ab[Psychic Senses]{l=8 icon=learn passive="A psychonaut adds ‹spell/clairaudience/clairvoyance›, ‹spell/detect scrying›, ‹spell/scrying›, and ‹spell/speak with dead› to his formula book as 3rd-level extracts (a *scrying* extract does not require a focus or divine focus component)." special="When a psychonaut uses a *speak with dead* extract, he gains the power to hear the lingering spirit within a corpse rather than enabling the corpse to audibly speak, but the extract otherwise works as the spell." replace="Poison resistance +6"} ::ab[Remote Consciousness]{l=10 icon=learn passive="A psychonaut adds ‹spell/dream›, ‹spell/lesser astral projection›, ‹spell/nightmare›, ‹spell/plane shift›, ‹spell/sending›, and ‹spell/telepathic bond› to his formula book as 4th-level extracts (a *plane shift* extract does not require a focus component)." replace="Poison immunity"} ::ab[Greater Precognition]{l=15 icon=learn passive="A psychonaut adds ‹spell/moment of prescience› to his formula book as a 5th-level extract." replace="15th-level bomb damage increase"} ::ab[Master Precognition]{l=17 icon=learn passive="A psychonaut adds ‹spell/foresight› to his formula book as a 6th-level extract." replace="17th-level bomb damage increase"} @HL[Discoveries:] The following discoveries complement the psychonaut archetype: ‹discovery/confusion bomb›, ‹discovery/eternal potion›, ‹discovery/extend potion›, ‹discovery/lingering spirit›, and ‹discovery/madness bomb›.

name: Ragechemist
description: ## Ragechemist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/25› Some alchemists create mutagens that tap into a primal anger that fuels their physical transformation. These alchemists have little control over their altered selves. ::ab[Rage Mutagen]{l=2 icon=power-boost-down ability="Whenever a ragechemist creates a mutagen that improves his Strength, that mutagen's bonus to Strength increases by +2 and penalizes the alchemist's Intelligence score." order=ap passive="While under the effects of this mutagen, whenever the alchemist takes damage, his rage grows, with detrimental effects. At the end of each turn that he takes hit point damage, the ragechemist must succeed at a Will saving throw (DC 15, or DC 20 if any of the damage came from a critical hit that turn) or take a -2 penalty on Will saving throws and to Intelligence. These penalties end 1 hour after the mutagen ends and stack with themselves." special="If the penalty lowers the ragechemist's Intelligence score to 0, the ragechemist is comatose until 1 hour after the mutagen expires." replace="Poison use"} ::ab[Sturdy Rage]{l=6 icon=def-down passive="Whenever a ragechemist uses his rage mutagen, he also gains a +4 bonus to natural armor, but the penalty on Will saving throws and to Intelligence for taking damage increases to -4." replace="Swift poisoning"} ::ab[Lumbering Rage]{l=10 icon=boost-down ability="Whenever a ragechemist uses his rage mutagen ability, he may have the mutagen also give him a +2 morale bonus to Constitution, but when he takes a penalty on Will saving throws and to Intelligence, he also takes a -1 penalty to Dexterity." replace="Poison immunity"} @HL[Discoveries:] The following discoveries complement the ragechemist: ‹discovery/feral mutagen›, ‹discovery/grand mutagen›, ‹discovery/greater mutagen›, ‹discovery/infuse mutagen›, ‹discovery/tentacle›, and ‹discovery/vestigial arm›.

name: Reanimator
description: ## Reanimator ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/20› A reanimator is an alchemist who has discovered how to infuse a corpse with a semblance of life. Many work in tandem with necromancers to explore the fine border between the worlds of the living and the dead. A reanimator has the following class features. ::ab[Bomb]{l=1 icon=down alter=Bombs ability="A reanimator's bombs deal damage ‹misc/one die step› lower than normal (regular bombs deal d4s, ‹discovery/concussive bomb«s› deal 1d3s, and so on). This ability otherwise functions as and replaces the standard alchemist bomb class feature."} ::ab[Simple Reanimation]{l=7 icon=learn ability="A reanimator adds ‹spell/lesser animate dead› to his formula book as a 3rd-level extract. When he uses that extract, rather than drinking it, he injects it into the corpse he intends to animate, which rises as an undead creature under his control 1 hour later. The extract can only create ‹template/zombie«s› (including variant zombies)." replace="7th-level bomb damage increase"} ::ab[Create Undead]{l=13 icon=learn ability="A reanimator adds ‹spell/create undead› to his formula book as a 4th-level extract. When he uses that extract, rather than drinking it, he injects it into the corpse he intends to animate, which rises as an uncontrolled undead 1 hour later. The extract can only create corporeal undead." replace="13th-level bomb damage increase"} ::ab[Create Greater Undead]{l=15 icon=learn ability="A reanimator adds ‹spell/create greater undead› to his formula book as a 5th-level extract. This otherwise acts similarly to a *create undead* extract." replace="15th-level bomb damage increase"} @HL[Discoveries:] The following discoveries complement the reanimator archetype: ‹discovery/alchemical zombie›, ‹discovery/elixir of life›, ‹discovery/eternal potion›, ‹discovery/mummification›, and ‹discovery/preserve organs›.

name: Vivisectionist
description: ## Vivisectionist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/20› A vivisectionist studies bodies to better understand their function. Unlike a ‹arc-alchemist/chirurgeon›, a vivisectionist's goals are not related to healing, but rather to experimentation and knowledge that most people would consider evil. A vivisectionist has the following class features. ::ab[Sneak Attack]{l=1 icon=power ability="A vivisectionist gains the ‹ability/sneak attack› ability as a rogue of the same level. If a character already has sneak attack from another class, the levels from the classes that grant sneak attack stack to determine the effective rogue level for the sneak attack's extra damage dice (so an alchemist 1/rogue 1 has a +1d6 sneak attack like a 2nd-level rogue, an alchemist 2/rogue 1 has a +2d6 sneak attack like a 3rd-level rogue, and so on)." replace=Bomb} ::ab[Bleeding Attack]{icon=power ability="A vivisectionist may select the ‹talent/bleeding attack› rogue talent in place of a discovery."} ::ab[Torturer's Eye]{l=2 icon=learn passive="A vivisectionist adds ‹spell/deathwatch› to his formula book as a 1st-level extract."} ::ab[Cruel Anatomist]{l=3 icon=boost passive="A vivisectionist may use his Knowledge (nature) skill bonus in place of his Heal skill bonus."} ::ab[Torturous Transformation]{l=7 icon=learn ability="A vivisectionist adds ‹spell/anthropomorphic animal› to his formula book as a 2nd-level extract. When he uses this extract, he injects it into an animal as part of a 2-hour surgical procedure. By using multiple doses of this extract as part of the surgery, he multiplies the duration by the number of extracts used." imp9="A vivisectionist adds ‹spell/awaken› and ‹spell/baleful polymorph› to his formula book as 3rd-level extracts. When he uses the *awaken* or *baleful polymorph* extract, he injects it into the target (not a plant) as part of a 24-hour surgical procedure. He can make *anthropomorphic animal* ‹spell/permanen«t<cy› on a creature by spending 7,500 gp." imp15="A vivisectionist adds ‹spell/regenerate› to his formula book as a 5th-level extract."} ::ab[Crippling Strike]{icon=power l10="A vivisectionist may select the ‹talent/crippling strike› rogue talent in place of a discovery."} @HL[Discoveries:] The following discoveries complement the vivisectionist archetype: ‹discovery/alchemical simulacrum›, ‹discovery/concentrate poison›, ‹discovery/doppelganger simulacrum›, ‹discovery/feral mutagen›, ‹discovery/parasitic twin›, ‹discovery/preserve organs›, ‹discovery/tentacle›, ‹discovery/tumor familiar›, ‹discovery/vestigial arm›, and ‹discovery/wings›.

name: Armored Hulk
description: ## Armored Hulk ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/28› Some barbarians disdain the hides and leather used as armor by most of their kin. Instead they master the heaviest of armors, even those created by more civilized people, to gain greater protection and stability in battle. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=power ability="An armored hulk gains proficiency in heavy armor."} ::ab[Indomitable Stance (Ex)]{icon=boost-def passive="An armored hulk gains a +1 bonus on combat maneuver checks and to CMD for overrun combat maneuvers, and on Reflex saves against ‹umr/trample› attacks. She also gains a +1 bonus to her AC against charge attacks and on attack and damage rolls against charging creatures." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Armored Swiftness (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost passive="When wearing medium or heavy armor, an armored hulk can move 5 feet faster than normal, to a maximum of her speed." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Resilience of Steel (Ex)]{l=3 icon=def passive="While wearing heavy armor, she gains a bonus to AC that applies only on critical hit confirmation rolls. @B-3f-barbarian." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Improved Armored Swiftness (Ex)]{l=5 icon=boost passive="An armored hulk's land speed is faster than the norm for her race by +10 feet." special="This benefit applies when she is wearing any armor, including heavy armor, but not while carrying a heavy load. Apply this bonus before modifying the armored hulk's speed because of any load carried or armor worn. This bonus stacks with any other bonuses to the barbarian's land speed." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the armored hulk archetype: ‹ragepower/boasting taunt›, ‹ragepower/greater guarded life›, ‹ragepower/guarded life›, ‹ragepower/guarded stance›, ‹ragepower/increased damage reduction›, ‹ragepower/no escape›, ‹ragepower/overbearing advance›, ‹ragepower/overbearing onslaught›, ‹ragepower/reflexive dodge›, ‹ragepower/rolling dodge›, ‹ragepower/unexpected strike›.

name: Breaker
description: ## Breaker ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/78› While most barbarians are skilled at breaking things, some find the need to destroy their surroundings an almost uncontrollable urge when in the middle of a *rage.* These barbarians are a danger not only to their foes, but also to the very environment around them. A breaker barbarian has the following class features. ::ab[Destructive (Ex)]{icon=melee-boost passive="Whenever the breaker barbarian makes a melee attack that targets an unattended object or makes a ‹rule/sunder› combat maneuver, she adds ‹misc/half› her barbarian level (minimum +1) on the damage roll." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Battle Scavenger (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost passive="The breaker barbarian suffers no penalty on attack rolls when using an ‹misc/improvised weapon› or a weapon with the ‹misc/broken› condition." imp6="She gains a +1 bonus on damage rolls with improvised or broken weapons." increment="This bonus~6~3" replace="Trap sense"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the breaker archetype: ‹ragepower/ground breaker›, ‹ragepower/smasher›, ‹ragepower/strength surge›.

name: Brutal Pugilist
description: ## Brutal Pugilist ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/78› Some barbarians focus on using their bare hands to tear their opponents limb from limb. These brutal pugilists also learn a great deal about various ‹rule/combat maneuvers›, using them to cripple or crush their foes. A brutal pugilist has the following class features. ::ab[Savage Grapple (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost-melee order=pa passive="The brutal pugilist takes only ‹misc/half› the normal penalties to Dexterity, attack rolls, and combat maneuver checks when she has the ‹rule/grapple«d» condition<s›." ability="She can make an attack of opportunity against creatures trying to grapple her even if they possess the ‹feat/Improved Grapple› feat or the ‹umr/grab› special attack. If she hits with this attack of opportunity, she gains a +2 circumstance bonus to her CMD against the grapple attempt. She cannot make these attacks of opportunity once a grapple has succeeded." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Pit Fighter (Ex)]{l=3 icon=melee-def flavor="The brutal pugilist has learned combat tricks from fighting in pit brawls and gladiatorial arenas." ability="She selects one ‹rule/combat maneuver<s› and gains a +1 insight bonus on her CMB or to her CMD in that maneuver. This bonus increases to +2 if the barbarian is wearing no armor (shields are allowed)." special="At every three levels after 3rd (6th, 9th 12th, 15th, and 18th), the barbarian may select another combat maneuver and add this bonus on her CMB or to her CMD. This bonus can be applied to each maneuver no more than twice, once on CMB and once to CMD." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Improved Savage Grapple (Ex)]{l=5 icon=boost passive="The brutal pugilist takes no penalties to Dexterity, attack rolls, and combat maneuver checks when she has the grappled condition. She also is treated as one size larger than her actual size when determining whether she can be grappled using the ‹umr/grab› ability or ‹umr/swallow«ed<_whole› by another creature." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the brutal pugilist archetype: ‹ragepower/animal fury›, ‹ragepower/brawler›, ‹ragepower/greater brawler›, ‹ragepower/knockback›, ‹ragepower/knockdown›, ‹ragepower/overbearing advance›, ‹ragepower/overbearing onslaught›, ‹ragepower/strength surge›.

name: Brutish Swamper
description: ## Brutish Swamper ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/37› The hardy and insular denizens of the swamp produce warriors of narrow focus and great strength. The prejudice and misunderstanding with which civilized folk often regard barbarians is often even more pronounced in the case of these belligerent outcasts from society, in large part due to the fact that brutish swampers deliberately mock and antagonize the so-called "city folk." To a brutish swamper, an urban lifestyle is one that breeds weakness and lassitude in the body. The brutish swamper has little interest or patience in maintaining alliances or friendship with those who live such soft lifestyles, and this aggression only further encourages feelings of prejudice on both sides of the cultural divide. When a brutish swamper joins an adventuring party, they usually come to value the skills and talents of their more urbanized companions, but never fully understand the desire to live lives surrounded by creature comforts. ::cskill{gain=kg~kl} ::ab[Marsh March (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="A brutish swamper can move through the underbrush and muddy terrain of bogs and swamps at her normal speed without taking damage or suffering other impairments. Briars, mud, thorns, and overgrown areas that have been magically manipulated to impede motion, however, still affect her." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Home (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost passive="A brutish swamper gains a +2 bonus on initiative checks and Knowledge (geography), Perception, Stealth, and Survival checks when in swamps." imp5="The bonus becomes +3." imp8="The bonus becomes +4." imp11="The bonus becomes +5." imp14="The bonus becomes +6." imp17="The bonus becomes +7." imp20="The bonus becomes +8." replace="Uncanny dodge~improved uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Stubborn (Ex)]{l=3 icon=def passive="A brutish swamper resists any attempts to change her attitude or compel her to action. Diplomacy and Intimidate checks against her take a -2 penalty, and no result can shift her attitude more than one step in a 24-hour period." increment="The penalty~3~3~-4~-2" replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Wrastlin (Ex)]{l=6 icon=def-melee passive="While *raging,* a brutish swamper gains a +2 bonus to her CMD against ‹rule/grapple› combat maneuvers and a +2 bonus on damage rolls made as part of successful grapple combat maneuver checks." replace="6th-level rage power"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the brutish swamper archetype: ‹ragepower/brawler›, ‹ragepower/greater brawler›, ‹ragepower/greater tyrant totem›, ‹ragepower/lesser tyrant totem›, ‹ragepower/lizard stride›, ‹ragepower/low-light vision›, ‹ragepower/superstition›, ‹ragepower/tyrant totem›.

name: Cave Dweller
description: ## Cave Dweller ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/37› Unused to the light of the sun, cave dwellers use their subterranean expertise to protect their clans from the manifold dangers of deep caverns and tunnels. The typical cave dweller is perfectly content to live his entire life underground, and he may even view the light of the sun as particularly abhorrent or taboo. While this lifestyle doesn't in and of itself imply evil or sinister intent, many outlanders ignorantly assume that cave dwellers avoid the light of the sun for malicious reasons. In truth, cave dwellers are as capable of goodness and kindness as any other - they just see little reason to venture out of their preferred homelands. When a cave dweller joins an adventuring party, she may retain an inherent nervousness about sleeping under the open sky and may long for the familiar confines of a comforting cavern, but this rarely translates directly into a notable disadvantage. Indeed, many adventuring groups come to value the specialized talents and skills the cave dweller brings to the party. ::cskill{gain=stl lose=ride} ::ab[Tight Tunnels (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="Cave dwellers pursue prey through the winding tunnels of the deep, which rarely accommodate open sprints. A cave dweller can make a single turn up to 90 degrees while ‹rule/run«ning› (though not while ‹rule/charging›). Additionally, a cave dweller takes no penalties to movement speed while ‹misc/squeezing›." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Tunnel Vision (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power-boost passive="A cave dweller gains darkvision to a range of 60 feet and a bonus on Perception checks to detect ambushes, movement, and sound while in darkness. @B-3f-barbarian." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Sun Walker (Ex)]{l=7 icon=def passive="A cave dweller gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC and on saving throws against effects with the light descriptor or that produce bright or sudden light. Any penalties on attack rolls, saving throws, or skill checks because of bright light are reduced by 1." imp10="The bonus becomes +2 and the reduction is now 2." imp13="The bonus becomes +3 and the reduction is now 3." imp16="The bonus becomes +4 and the reduction is now 4." imp19="The bonus becomes +5 and the reduction is now 5." replace="Damage reduction"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the cave dweller archetype: ‹ragepower/animal fury›, ‹ragepower/bestial climber›, ‹ragepower/eclipsing rage›, ‹ragepower/greater eclipsing rage›, ‹ragepower/greater ground breaker›, ‹ragepower/ground breaker›, ‹ragepower/night vision›, ‹ragepower/raging climber›, ‹ragepower/primal scent›, ‹ragepower/sprint›.

name: Drunken Brute
description: ## Drunken Brute ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/78› Barbarians are known for their ability to consume potent drink, but drunken brutes turn drinking into a combat tactic, using the potent liquor to fuel their rage and grant them additional powers. A drunken brute has the following class feature. ::ab[Raging Drunk (Ex)]{icon=power move="While *raging,* the drunken brute can drink a potion, or a tankard of ale or similar quantity of alcohol, as a move action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity. A potion has its normal effect, while an alcoholic drink allows the barbarian to maintain her *rage* that round without expending a round of *rage* for the day (instead of the alcohol's normal effects)." special="For each alcoholic drink consumed while *raging,* the barbarian is ‹misc/nauseated› for 1 round when her *rage* expires, in addition to the normal fatigue that follows a *rage. Tireless rage* does not negate this nauseated condition but the *internal fortitude* rage power does." replace="Fast movement"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the drunken brute archetype: ‹ragepower/boasting taunt›, ‹ragepower/good for what ails you›, ‹ragepower/internal fortitude›, ‹ragepower/liquid courage›, ‹ragepower/moment of clarity›, ‹ragepower/roaring drunk›, ‹ragepower/staggering drunk›.

name: Elemental Kin
description: ## Elemental Kin ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/78› Some barbarian tribes have strong ties to the elemental forces of nature. Their shamans anoint the warriors at birth, tying them to the patron element of the tribe and granting them lasting boons against such forces. An elemental kin has the following class feature. ::ab[Elemental Fury (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost passive="Whenever the elemental kin takes an amount of energy damage equal to or greater than her barbarian level while *raging,* she adds ‹misc/one-third› of her barbarian level to the total number of rounds that she can *rage* that day (1 extra round at 3rd level, 2 rounds at 6th level, and so on)." replace="Trap sense"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the elemental kin archetype: ‹ragepower/elemental rage›, ‹ragepower/energy absorption›, ‹ragepower/energy eruption›, ‹ragepower/energy resistance›, ‹ragepower/greater elemental rage›, ‹ragepower/greater energy resistance›, ‹ragepower/lesser elemental rage›.

name: Hurler
description: ## Hurler ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/78› A raging barbarian is frightening enough in melee, but some become skilled at throwing objects at their foes before closing in for the kill. A hurler has the following class feature. ::ab[Skilled Thrower (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="The hurler is skilled at throwing objects in combat. Increase the range increment of any thrown weapon or object by 10 feet." replace="Fast movement"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the hurler archetype: ‹ragepower/hurling›, ‹ragepower/greater hurling›, ‹ragepower/hurling charge›, ‹ragepower/lesser hurling›, ‹ragepower/strength surge›, ‹ragepower/surprise accuracy›.

name: Invulnerable Rager
description: ## Invulnerable Rager ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/79› Some barbarians learn to take whatever comes their way, shrugging off mortal wounds with ease. These barbarians invite their enemies to attack them, and use pain to fuel their rage. An invulnerable rager has the following class features. ::ab[Invulnerability (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def passive="The invulnerable rager gains ‹rule/DR›/- equal to ‹misc/half› her barbarian level. This damage reduction is doubled against nonlethal damage." replace="Uncanny dodge~improved uncanny dodge~damage reduction"} ::ab[Extreme Endurance (Ex)]{l=3 icon=def passive="The invulnerable rager is inured to either hot or cold climate effects (choose one) as if using ‹spell/endure elements›. In addition, the barbarian gains 1 point of fire or cold ‹umr/resistance› for every three levels beyond 3rd." replace="Trap sense"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the invulnerable rager archetype: ‹ragepower/come and get me›, ‹ragepower/guarded life›, ‹ragepower/increased damage reduction›, ‹ragepower/inspire ferocity›, ‹ragepower/reckless abandon›, ‹ragepower/renewed vigor›.

name: Mounted Fury
description: ## Mounted Fury ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/79› Many barbarian tribes are masters of the horse, teaching their members how to ride from a young age. As a result, barbarians from such tribes are even more terrifying when mounted, using their steeds' speed and strength to great advantage. A mounted fury has the following class features. ::ab[Fast Rider (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="The speed of any mount the barbarian rides is increased by 10 feet." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Bestial Mount (Ex)]{l=5 icon=power-boost ability="The mounted fury gains the service of a feral mount. This ability functions as a druid's ‹sidekick/animal companion›, using the barbarian's level - 4 as her effective druid level. This companion must be one that she is capable of riding and is suitable as a mount. A Medium barbarian can select a ‹companion/camel› or a ‹companion/horse›. A Small barbarian can select a ‹companion/pony› or a ‹companion/wolf›, but can also select a ‹companion/boar› or a ‹companion/dog› if she is at least 8th level. Whenever a barbarian is *raging* while mounted on her bestial mount, the mount gains a +2 morale bonus to its Strength." replace="Uncanny dodge~improved uncanny dodge"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the mounted fury archetype: ‹ragepower/ferocious mount›, ‹ragepower/ferocious trample›, ‹ragepower/greater ferocious mount›, ‹ragepower/greater ferocious trample›, ‹ragepower/spirit steed›.

name: Pack Hunter
description: ## Pack Hunter ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/38› Pack hunter barbarians team up to hunt dangerous prey to feed, to protect their camps, and as a rite of passage. Often, a tribe of pack hunters looks to a specific species of animal (such as wolves) who themselves hunt in packs, and view these animals as sacred manifestations of their people's traditions and values. ::ab[Bonus Feats]{icon=power passive="Whenever a pack hunter would gain a new rage power, she can instead select a ‹main/teamwork feat›. She must still meet the prerequisites for the teamwork feat." alter="Rage power"} ::ab[In and Out (Ex)]{l=3 icon=def passive="A pack hunter gains a dodge bonus to AC against attacks of opportunity. @B-3f-barbarian." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Sympathetic Rage (Ex)]{l=6 icon=boost passive="If an ally within 30 feet is *bloodraging* or *raging,* a pack hunter counts as *raging* even if knocked unconscious. She has to have been *raging* when incapacitated to maintain her *rage,* and she ceases *raging* normally if she depletes her maximum number of rounds of *rage* in a day." replace="6th-level rage power"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the pack hunter archetype: ‹ragepower/contagious rage›, ‹ragepower/increased damage reduction›, ‹ragepower/no escape›, ‹ragepower/pack rage›, ‹ragepower/quick reflexes›, ‹ragepower/unexpected strike›.

name: Raging Cannibal
description: ## Raging Cannibal ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/38;Champions of Corruption/27› While savagery is not inherently evil, some barbaric cultures thrive on depravity and welcome the act of feeding on their own kind. The raging cannibal is a barbarian who feasts upon her fallen opponents not out of hunger, or even a taste for flesh, but rather because she believes consuming her foes and defiling their lost lives demonstrates her strength. This penchant for feasting on the flesh of her kin makes the raging cannibal an awkward companion to travel with for many groups, with rumors revolving around the raging cannibal's culinary exploits often causing tense situations that other party members might be called upon to resolve via diplomacy before the raging cannibal grows frustrated and decides to take matters into her own hands! ::ab[Animal Fury]{l=2 icon=power ability="A raging cannibal must select ‹ragepower/animal fury› as her first rage power." alter="The barbarian's 2nd-level rage power"} ::ab[Consume Vigor (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost-melee ability="When a raging cannibal reduces a creature of the same creature type as herself to 0 or fewer hit points with her bite attack during combat while *raging,* she can consume a chunk of its body to gain a portion of its power. If the creature's CR equals or exceeds her barbarian level, the raging cannibal gains 1 additional round of *rage.* She can never consume the same creature's vigor more than once." imp5="The raging cannibal now gains 2 additional rounds of *rage* each time she uses this ability." incrementPlain="She now~5~3~3" incrementDesc=gains incrementEnd=" rounds of *rage.*" replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Intimidating Gouge (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost-melee passive="When a raging cannibal confirms a critical hit against a creature of the same creature type as herself with her bite attack while *raging,* she gains a bonus on Intimidate checks equal to ‹misc/half› her barbarian level for the duration of the *rage.*" replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Feed from Fury (Ex)]{l=5 icon=boost-melee flavor="A raging cannibal is empowered by eating her enemies during combat." passive="When a raging cannibal confirms a critical hit against a creature of the same creature type as herself with her bite attack while *raging,* she gains a number of ‹rule/temporary hit points› equal to her barbarian level. These temporary hit points stack with other temporary hit points gained from this ability but not with those from other sources. These temporary hit points fade after a period of time equal to 10 minutes per barbarian level." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Razor-Toothed Fury (Ex)]{l=6 icon=boost-melee ability="When using her bite attack, the raging cannibal can take a -1 penalty on her attack roll to add 2 points of ‹rule/bleed› damage to the damage dealt." imp10="The penalty becomes -2 and the bleed damage becomes 4." imp14="The penalty becomes -3 and the bleed damage becomes 6." imp18="The penalty becomes -4 and the bleed damage becomes 8." replace="Damage reduction"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the raging cannibal archetype: ‹ragepower/internal fortitude›, ‹ragepower/intimidating glare›, ‹ragepower/primal scent›, ‹ragepower/scent›, ‹ragepower/terrifying howl›.

name: Savage Barbarian
description: ## Savage Barbarian ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/79› Some barbarians are truly savage, having little training in modern arms. These savage barbarians learn to avoid blows and toughen up their skin. A savage barbarian has the following class features. ::ab[Naked Courage (Ex)]{l=3 icon=def passive="The savage barbarian gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC and a +1 morale bonus on saving throws against fear when wearing no armor (shields are allowed)." increment="p!The bonuses~3~6" replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Natural Toughness (Ex)]{l=7 icon=def passive="The savage barbarian gains a +1 natural armor bonus to AC when wearing no armor (shields are allowed)." increment="The bonus~7~3" replace="Damage reduction"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the savage barbarian archetype: ‹ragepower/flesh wound›, ‹ragepower/guarded stance›, ‹ragepower/increased damage reduction›, ‹ragepower/intimidating glare›, ‹ragepower/rolling dodge›, ‹ragepower/superstition›, ‹ragepower/terrifying howl›.

name: Scarred Rager
description: ## Scarred Rager ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/29› Some barbarians wear marks of prowess and savagery upon their bodies. The scarred rager believes each wound tells the tales of her prowess and bravery. She augments these ragged trophies with brands and tattoos in order to win the notice and favor of her gods, ancestors, or totem spirits. The scarred rager's gnarled and exotic appearance terrifies civilized onlookers, but is awe-inspiring to her savage kin. ::ab[Terrifying Visage (Ex)]{icon=boost-lower passive="A scarred rager adds ‹misc/half› her barbarian level on Intimidate checks against humanoids who are not members of barbarian tribes. When dealing with barbarians, the scarred rager may choose to add this bonus on Diplomacy checks instead. The DC of any fear effect created by the scarred rager also increases by 1." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Tolerance (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def passive="A scarred rager who fails a save against an effect that causes her to become nauseated, sickened, fatigued, or exhausted can make a second save to negate the effect on the start of her next turn. Only one additional save is allowed. If the effect does not allow a saving throw, its duration is halved instead (minimum of 1 round)." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Scarification (Ex)]{l=3 icon=def passive="A scarred rager can ignore a number of points of bleed damage per round. @B-number-3f-barbarian-x." imp15="A scarred rager can ignore 1 bleed effect each round." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Improved Tolerance (Ex)]{l=5 icon=def passive="A scarred rager's *tolerance* ability also applies to effects that would cause her to become dazed, frightened, shaken, or stunned." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the scarred rager archetype: ‹ragepower/auspicious mark›, ‹ragepower/body bludgeon›, ‹ragepower/come and get me›, ‹ragepower/increased damage reduction›, ‹ragepower/inspire ferocity›, ‹ragepower/internal fortitude›, ‹ragepower/intimidating glare›, ‹ragepower/reckless abandon›, ‹ragepower/regenerative vigor›, ‹ragepower/renewed life›, ‹ragepower/renewed vigor›, ‹ragepower/renewed vitality›, ‹ragepower/roused anger›, ‹ragepower/terrifying howl›.

name: Sea Reaver
description: ## Sea Reaver ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/29› Not all barbarians hunt forests, plains, and mountains. Some are raiding terrors on the sea and coasts, pillaging those who hoard treasure and pursuing monsters of the deep. Some sea reavers are no more than hunters of the open sea, while others are raiders striking fear into coastal settlements within reach of the sea reavers' longships. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="A sea reaver is not proficient with medium armor."} ::ab[Marine Terror (Ex)]{icon=power-boost-lower passive="A sea reaver can ‹misc/hold her breath› for a number of rounds equal to four times her Constitution score. In addition, a sea reaver can move normally though squares of standing water or bog that is 1 foot deep. It does not cost her extra movement to traverse these terrains. Lastly, a sea reaver ignores the normal ‹rule/cover› bonus to AC when attacking creatures that are partially immersed in water." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Eyes of the Storm (Ex)]{l=2 icon=lower-boost passive="A sea reaver ignores any ‹rule/concealment› provided by fog, rain, sleet, mist, wind, or other weather effects that is less than total concealment, and any penalties weather applies on Perception checks are halved." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Savage Sailor (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost passive="A sea reaver gains a bonus on Acrobatics, Climb, Profession (sailor), Survival, and Swim checks made in aquatic terrain, including aboard a ship or along shorelines. @B-3f-barbarian." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Sure-Footed (Ex)]{l=5 icon=boost passive="A sea reaver takes no penalties when moving across slick surfaces, whether natural or magical (e.g., ‹spell/grease›, ‹spell/ice storm›, and ‹spell/sleet storm›). She is not at risk of falling, is not denied her Dexterity bonus when moving across such areas, and does not treat them as difficult terrain." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the sea reaver archetype: ‹ragepower/bestial leaper›, ‹ragepower/bestial swimmer›, ‹ragepower/come and get me›, ‹ragepower/hurling charge›, ‹ragepower/raging leaper›, ‹ragepower/raging swimmer›, ‹ragepower/rolling dodge›, ‹ragepower/smasher›.

name: Sharptooth
description: ## Sharptooth ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/39› Coastal hunters and agents of the ocean's rage, sharptooth barbarians emulate the greatest predators of the sea. Sharks, in particular, are respected and admired by many such tribes, if not as manifestations of divine power, then merely as scions of the power and fury of the natural world. ::ab[Swim Like a Fish (Ex)]{icon=power ability="A sharptooth gains a swim speed of 10 feet." imp5="The swim speed becomes 15 feet." imp10="The swim speed becomes 20 feet." imp15="The swim speed becomes 25 feet." imp20="The swim speed becomes 30 feet." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Scent of Blood (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power ability="A sharptooth gains ‹umr/scent›." imp5="She also gains ‹umr/keen scent›." replace="Uncanny dodge~improved uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Ocean Breath (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost passive="A sharptooth gains a bonus equal to ‹misc/one-third› her barbarian level. She adds this number to her Constitution score for the purposes of ‹misc/hold«ing» her breath›. She also adds it as a bonus on Constitution checks to continue holding her breath." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Blood in the Water (Ex)]{l=6 icon=boost flavor="A sharptooth can tear the flesh from living creatures." passive="Her attacks add 3 points of ‹rule/bleed› damage while she is *raging.*" imp12="This bleed damage increases to equal her Constitution modifier if it's higher." replace="6th- and 12th-level rage powers"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the sharptooth archetype: ‹ragepower/animal fury›, ‹ragepower/bleeding blow›, ‹ragepower/contagious rage›, ‹ragepower/pack rage›, ‹ragepower/powerful blow›, ‹ragepower/primal scent›, ‹ragepower/raging swimmer›, ‹ragepower/scent›.

name: Superstitious
description: ## Superstitious ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/79› Many barbarians distrust magic. While most just shy away from magic, others focus their rage on users of such foul arts. These barbarians are naturally distrusting, and develop keen senses to protect them from harm. A superstitious barbarian has the following class features. ::ab[Sixth Sense (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost passive="The superstitious barbarian gains a bonus on initiative and an insight bonus to AC during surprise rounds. @B-3fp-barbarian." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Keen Senses (Ex)]{icon=power l7="The superstitious barbarian gains ‹umr/low-light vision› (triple normal vision range in dim light if she already has low-light vision)." l10="She gains ‹umr/darkvision› 60 feet (or adds 60 feet to the range of any darkvision already possessed)." l13="She gains ‹umr/scent›." l16="She gains ‹umr/blindsense› 30 feet." l19="She gains ‹umr/blindsight› 30 feet." replace="Damage reduction"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the superstitious archetype: ‹ragepower/clear mind›, ‹ragepower/disruptive›, ‹ragepower/roused anger›, ‹ragepower/spellbreaker›, ‹ragepower/superstition›, ‹ragepower/witch hunter›.

name: Titan Mauler
description: ## Titan Mauler ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/30› In lands overrun by giants, dragons, and other hulking beasts, entire fellowships of barbarians hone tactics and traditions with one purpose - to bring low these massive foes. While her enemies' size makes the creatures strong, the titan mauler is even stronger, taking up weapons from her fallen foes that no lesser warrior can lift, and using them when she beseeches the spirits to grant her increased size and greater ferocity against her titanic foes. ::ab[Big Game Hunter (Ex)]{l=1 icon=def passive="A titan mauler gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls and a +1 dodge bonus to AC in melee with creatures larger than themselves." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Jotungrip (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power-down ability="A titan mauler may choose to wield a two-handed melee weapon in one hand with a -2 penalty on attack rolls while doing so. The weapon must be appropriately sized for her, and it is treated as one-handed when determining the effect of ‹feat/Power Attack›, Strength bonus to damage, and the like." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Massive Weapons (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power-down ability="A titan mauler becomes skilled in the use of massive weapons looted from her titanic foes. She can use two-handed weapons meant for creatures one size category larger, but the penalty for doing so is increased by 4. However, the attack roll penalty for using weapons too large for her size is reduced by an amount equal to ‹misc/one-third› of her barbarian level (to a minimum of 0)." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Evade Reach (Ex)]{l=5 icon=def swift="A titan mauler may choose one creature within her line of sight. Until the end of her turn, that target's reach is treated as if it were 5 feet shorter with respect to reaching the titan mauler." imp10="The target's reach is treated as 10 feet shorter." imp15="The target's reach is treated as 15 feet shorter." imp20="The target's reach is treated as 20 feet shorter." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Titanic Rage (Su)]{l=14 icon=boost-down ability="A titan mauler may choose to gain the benefits of ‹spell/enlarge person› when she enters a *rage.* While using *titanic rage,* she must spend 2 rounds of *rage* per round, and she becomes ‹misc/exhausted› rather than fatigued when the *rage* ends." replace="Indomitable will"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the titan mauler archetype: ‹ragepower/body bludgeon›, ‹ragepower/greater ground breaker›, ‹ragepower/ground breaker›, ‹ragepower/knockback›, ‹ragepower/mighty swing›, ‹ragepower/powerful blow›, ‹ragepower/smasher›, ‹ragepower/strength surge›.

name: True Primitive
description: ## True Primitive ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/30› Isolated and xenophobic tribes that dwell in areas untouched by civilization often see anything from cities and organized settlements as strange, dangerous, and decadent. They gain power from their truly primitive nature; their bodies and spirits are hardened by the wild and untainted existence far from the pathetic softness of so-called civilization. Even when forced to mingle with civilization, the true primitive stays apart in both traditions and trappings. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="A true primitive is proficient with ‹eq-armor/hide armor› and armors made from ‹eq-material/bone›. A true primitive is also proficient with bone shields and the following weapons: ‹eq-weapon/battleaxe›, ‹eq-weapon/blowgun›, ‹eq-weapon/club›, ‹eq-weapon/greatclub›, ‹eq-weapon/handaxe›, ‹eq-weapon/longspear›, ‹eq-weapon/shortspear›, ‹eq-weapon/sling›, and ‹eq-weapon/spear›." alter="The barbarian's armor and weapon proficiencies"} ::ab[Illiteracy]{icon=down info="A true primitive cannot read or write, and her superstition about such things leads her to refuse to ever learn to read or write, even if she multiclasses into other classes."} ::ab[Favored Terrain (Ex)]{icon=power ability="A true primitive has a ‹ability/favored terrain› representing her native homeland. This ability functions as the ranger class feature, and the true primitive's bonuses in that terrain improve by +2 at 5th level and every five levels thereafter. However, she does not gain any additional favored terrains." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Trophy Fetish (Ex)]{l=3 flavor="A true primitive collects teeth, bones, hair, and other trophies from vanquished enemies, representing their power and strength." icon=boost-def ability="A true primitive can attach a trophy fetish to one of the traditional true primitive weapons listed above. When wielding that weapon, the true primitive gains a +1 morale bonus on damage rolls. Furthermore, if that weapon has the ‹misc/fragile› property, once per day, the true primitive can ignore the effects of a single natural 1 roll. A trophy fetish can also be attached to a suit of hide or bone armor, granting the true primitive a +1 morale bonus on saving throws. Furthermore, if that armor has the fragile property, once per day, the true primitive can chose not to have the armor break on the confirmation of a critical hit made against her." imp8="A true primitive can use one additional trophy fetish. Multiple trophy fetishes can be attached to the same armor or weapon; their effects stack." imp13="She can now use three trophy fetishes." imp18="She can now use four trophy fetishes." special="A trophy fetish can be sundered (hardness 5, 1 hit point) but is not damaged by area attacks or attacks that do not specifically target it. It has no effect if attached to other types of weapons or armor." replace="Trap sense"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the true primitive archetype: ‹ragepower/animal fury›, ‹ragepower/eater of magic›, ‹ragepower/ghost rager›, ‹ragepower/low-light vision›, ‹ragepower/night vision›, ‹ragepower/primal scent›, ‹ragepower/scent›, ‹ragepower/spell sunder›, ‹ragepower/sunder enchantment›, ‹ragepower/superstition›, ‹ragepower/witch hunter›.

name: Urban Barbarian
description: ## Urban Barbarian ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/31› Every barbarian knows that city life can soften the spirit and the body, but some barbarians take on the trappings and ways of their adoptive homes and bend their savage powers to its challenges. While these urban barbarians' rough edges are smoothed into civility, they can use their primal nature and upbringing to move with the ebb and flow of civilization's natural rhythms. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down passive="An urban barbarian is not proficient with medium armor."} ::cskill{lose=ha~kna~sur gain=diplo~kl~kno~ling~prof} ::ab[Crowd Control (Ex)]{l=1 icon=boost-def passive="An urban barbarian gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls and a +1 dodge bonus to AC when adjacent to two or more enemies. In addition, her movement is not impeded by ‹rule/crowds›, and she gains a bonus equal to ‹misc/half› her barbarian level on Intimidate checks to influence crowds." replace="Fast movement"} ::ab[Controlled Rage (Ex)]{icon=boost-down ability="When an urban barbarian rages, instead of making a normal *rage* she applies a +4 morale bonus to her Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution. This bonus increases to +6 when she gains *greater rage* and +8 when she gains *mighty rage.* She may apply the full bonus to one ability score or may split the bonus between several scores in increments of +2. When using a *controlled rage,* an urban barbarian gains no bonus on Will saves, takes no penalties to AC, and can still use Intelligence-, Dexterity-, and Charisma-based skills. This ability otherwise follows the normal rules for rage." alter=Rage} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the urban barbarian archetype: ‹ragepower/boasting taunt›, ‹ragepower/clear mind›, ‹ragepower/deadly accuracy›, ‹ragepower/guarded stance›, ‹ragepower/intimidating glare›, ‹ragepower/lethal accuracy›, ‹ragepower/no escape›, ‹ragepower/quick reflexes›, ‹ragepower/perfect clarity›, ‹ragepower/sharpened accuracy›, ‹ragepower/surprise accuracy›, ‹ragepower/unexpected strike›.

name: Wild Rager
description: ## Wild Rager ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/31› Rages are barely controlled, but there are those who wholly give in to their more savage side, letting their rages take them to a confusing and uncontrolled place of terrible savagery. These barbarians become beasts, consumed with absolute bloodlust to the point where they cannot tell friend from foe. ::ab[Uncontrolled Rage (Ex)]{icon=down passive="A wild rager's *rage* functions as normal, except that when she reduces a creature to 0 or fewer hit points, she must attempt a Will save (DC 10 + ‹misc/half› the barbarian's level + the barbarian's Constitution modifier) or become *confused.* For the remainder of her current turn, she attacks the nearest creature other than herself. On the following round, refer to the ‹spell/confusion› spell to determine her actions. At the end of this round, and each round thereafter, she can attempt a new saving throw to end the confusion effect." special="The rounds during which she is confused do not count against the rounds she has spent *raging* that day, but she cannot end her *rage* voluntarily, nor can she use rage powers while confused."} ::ab[Wild Fighting (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost-down flavor="Even when not *raging,* wild ragers often fight with reckless, savage abandon." ability="A wild rager using the ‹rule/full-attack› action can make one extra attack per round at her highest base attack bonus. Until the beginning of her next turn, however, she takes a -2 penalty on attack rolls and -4 penalty to AC." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Rage Conversion (Ex)]{l=5 icon=def passive="A wild rager who fails a saving throw against any mind-affecting effect can attempt a new saving throw at the beginning of her next turn. If the save succeeds, that effect ends and she instead rages and becomes confused as noted above." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the wild rager archetype: ‹ragepower/animal fury›, ‹ragepower/bleeding blow›, ‹ragepower/body bludgeon›, ‹ragepower/brawler›, ‹ragepower/crippling blow›, ‹ragepower/greater brawler›, ‹ragepower/intimidating glare›, ‹ragepower/mighty swing›, ‹ragepower/no escape›, ‹ragepower/powerful blow›, ‹ragepower/quick reflexes›.

name: Wildborn
description: ## Wildborn ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/39› Some barbarians are born or bred outside the reach of civilization. These wildborn fight and survive without ever seeing a forge or worked stone, and only dare a trip into the city when no other option is available. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down-power-warning passive="A wildborn is proficient with leather and hide armors (but not shields) and all simple weapons that can be crafted from bone, stone, or wood.
