If she uses any other kind of weapon or armor, she loses her abilities from this archetype (except illiteracy) for the next 24 hours." order=pa ability="A wildborn gains ‹feat/Improved Unarmed Strike› and ‹feat/Catch Off-Guard› as bonus feats." alter="The barbarian's normal weapon and armor proficiencies"} ::ab[Illiteracy]{icon=down info="A wildborn cannot read or write. She can learn to read or write a language only if she takes a level in another class, and even then only by taking 1 or more ranks in Linguistics."} ::ab[Live Off the Land (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost passive="A wildborn adds ‹misc/half› her barbarian level as a bonus on Survival checks to hunt or gather food and gains a bonus on Fortitude saves to resist the effects of extreme temperatures or other environmental effects; the Fortitude save bonus is equal to one-third of her barbarian level." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Bonus Feats]{icon=power special="At 4th level, 10th level and 16th level, a wildborn can choose a bonus feat from the following rather than select a rage power: ‹feat/Alertness›, ‹feat/Animal Affinity›, ‹feat/Athletic›, ‹feat/Great Fortitude›, ‹feat/Improvised Weapon Mastery›, ‹feat/Iron Will›, ‹feat/Lightning Reflexes›, ‹feat/Self-Sufficient›, ‹feat/Stealthy›, or ‹feat/Throw Anything›." alter="Rage powers"} ::ab[Inexhaustible (Ex)]{icon=aid-def l=7 passive="A wildborn recovers nonlethal damage for each minute of rest as if an hour had passed. She applies twice her damage reduction gained from barbarian levels against nonlethal damage." alter="Damage reduction"} @HL[Rage Powers:] The following rage powers complement the wildborn archetype: ‹ragepower/animal fury›, ‹ragepower/beast totem›, ‹ragepower/bestial climber›, ‹ragepower/bestial swimmer›, ‹ragepower/greater beast totem›, ‹ragepower/lesser beast totem›, ‹ragepower/low-light vision›, ‹ragepower/raging climber›, ‹ragepower/raging leaper›, ‹ragepower/raging swimmer›, ‹ragepower/swift foot›.

name: Animal Speaker
description: ## Animal Speaker ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/25› An animal speaker focuses not on the ears and minds of humans, but on the creatures of the wild and those in the underbellies of cities. ::ab[Animal Friend]{icon=boost-def choice="An animal speaker selects a particular kind of animal, such as apes, badgers, bears, boars, cats, snakes, and so on." order=cp passive="The bard gains a +4 bonus on Handle Animal checks to influence animals of his chosen kind. Animals of this kind have a starting attitude of at least &quot&indifferent&quot& toward the bard and never attack him unless he attacks them first." special="Animal companions and magically controlled animals of the bard's chosen kind can be directed to attack the bard if the controlling creature wins an opposed Charisma check against the bard (this check can be made once per round until it succeeds, after which no further checks are needed). Supernatural versions of animals (such as animals with the ‹template/fiendish› template) can attempt an opposed Charisma check against the bard with a +4 bonus on its roll to overcome this hesitation. This ability has no effect on creatures other than animals." replace=Fascinate} ::ab[Nature's Speaker]{icon=boost-magic l5="The animal speaker selects a second kind of animal friend." l11="The animal speaker selects a third kind of animal friend." l17="The animal speaker selects a fourth kind of animal friend." special="The bard can use ‹spell/speak with animals› at will on animals of his selected kinds." replace=Well-versed} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power ability="An animal speaker gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Soothing Performance]{l=3 next icon=power ability="An animal speaker can use bardic performance to influence animals. This works like the druid ability ‹ability/wild empathy›, except he expends 1 round of bardic performance and makes a Perform check. If the bard already has wild empathy from another class, he adds the class levels that provide wild empathy to the result of his Perform check to influence an animal." replace="Inspire competence"} ::ab[Attract Rats]{next l=6 icon=magic ability="The animal speaker can use bardic performance to summon 1d3 ‹monster/rat swarm«s›; they remain as long as he continues performing." imp11="He summons 2d3 swarms instead of 1d3 and the swarms have the ‹template/advanced› creature simple template." imp17="The number of swarms he summons increases to 3d3." replace=Suggestion} ::ab[Summon Nature's Ally]{icon=learn ability="At 1st level, the animal speaker adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally I› to his bard spell list and bard spells known as a 1st-level spell. At 4th level, he adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally II› to his spell list and spells known as a 2nd-level spell, and so on every 3 levels thereafter, until 16th level when he adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally VI› to his 6th-level spell list and spells known." replace="Mass suggestion"}

name: Arcane Duelist
description: ## Arcane Duelist ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/80› A master of the martial applications of steel and spell, the arcane duelist blends both into a lethal combination. ::ab[Arcane Strike]{l=1 icon=power info="Arcane duelists gain ‹feat/Arcane Strike› as a bonus feat at 1st level." replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power ability="An arcane duelist gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Rallying Cry (Su)]{next icon=boost l=1 flavor="An arcane duelist can use performance to rally dispirited allies." ability="Each round he makes an Intimidate check. Any ally (including the bard) within 30 feet may use this check in place of his own saving throw against fear and despair effects. Those already under a fear or despair effect can attempt a new save each round using the bard's Intimidate check." special="Rallying cry does not work on effects that don't allow saves. This is a mind-affecting ability that uses audible components." replace=Countersong} ::ab[Bladethirst (Su)]{next l=6 icon=boost ability="An arcane duelist may use performance to grant one weapon, one natural weapon, one end of a double weapon, or 50 items of ammunition of the same type within 30 feet a +1 enhancement bonus. This enhancement bonus increases by +1 for every three levels after 6th (maximum +5 at 18th level)." special="These bonuses stack with existing bonuses and may be used to increase the item's enhancement bonus up to +5 or to add any of the following weapon properties: ‹magic-enh/defending›, ‹magic-enh/distance›, ‹magic-enh/ghost touch›, ‹magic-enh/keen›, ‹magic-enh/mighty cleaving›, ‹magic-enh/returning›, ‹magic-enh/shock›, ‹magic-enh/shocking burst›, ‹magic-enh/seeking›, ‹magic-enh/speed›, or ‹magic-enh/wounding›. If the weapon is not magical, at least a +1 enhancement bonus must be added before adding special abilities." replace=Suggestion} ::ab[Mass Bladethirst (Su)]{next l=18 icon=boost ability="An arcane duelist can use his *bladethirst* performance to enhance the weapons of as many allies as desired within 30 feet. The bonus provided by this power is +4 if conferred on two allies, +3 for three allies, +2 for four allies, and +1 for five or more allies. The power granted to each weapon must be identical." replace="Mass suggestion"} ::ab[Bonus Feats]{icon=power flavor="An arcane duelist weaves might and magic in his combat style." l2="Gain ‹feat/Combat Casting› as a bonus feat" l6="Gain ‹feat/Disruptive› as a bonus feat" l10="Gain ‹feat/Spellbreaker› as a bonus feat" l14="Gain ‹feat/Penetrating Strike› as a bonus feat" l18="Gain ‹feat/Greater Penetrating Strike› as a bonus feat" replace="Versatile performance~well-versed"} ::ab[Arcane Bond (Ex)]{icon=power head l=5 ability="An arcane duelist gains the arcane bond ability as a ‹class/wizard›, using a weapon as his bonded item, allowing him to cast any one additional spell that he knows once per day." special="He may use the hand holding his bonded weapon for somatic components." replace="Lore master"} :::ab{next title="Bonded Object" flavor="Relevant text from the wizard ability." icon=magic action=Ability} You begin play with a bonded object at no cost. This object is always masterwork quality. Weapons acquired at 1st level are not made of any special material. Weapons must be wielded to have an effect. If you attempt to cast a spell without your bonded object in hand, you must make a ‹rule/concentration› check or lose the spell. The DC for this check is equal to 20 + the spell's level. A bonded object can be used once per day to cast any one spell that you have in your spellbook and are capable of casting, even if the spell is not prepared. This spell is treated like any other spell cast by you, including casting time, duration, and other effects dependent on your level. This spell cannot be modified by metamagic feats or other abilities. You can add additional magic abilities to your bonded object as if you have the required item creation feats and if you meet the level prerequisites of the feat. For example, a wizard with a bonded dagger must be at least 5th level to add magic abilities to the dagger (see ‹feat/Craft Magic Arms and Armor›). The magic properties of a bonded object, including any magic abilities added to the object, only function for the wizard who owns it. If a bonded object's owner dies, or the item is replaced, the object reverts to being an ordinary masterwork item of the appropriate type. If a bonded object is damaged, it is restored to full hit points the next time you prepare your spells. If the object of an arcane bond is lost or destroyed, it can be replaced after 1 week in a special ritual that costs 200 gp per wizard level plus the cost of the masterwork item. This ritual takes 8 hours to complete. Items replaced in this way do not possess any of the additional enchantments of the previous bonded item. You can designate an existing magic item as your bonded item. This functions in the same way as replacing a lost or destroyed item except that the new magic item retains its abilities while gaining the benefits and drawbacks of becoming a bonded item. ::: ::ab[Arcane Armor (Ex)]{icon=def-power l10="An arcane duelist gains Medium Armor Proficiency and can cast bard spells in medium armor with no chance of arcane spell failure." l16="He gains Heavy Armor Proficiency and can cast bard spells in heavy armor with no arcane spell failure chance." replace="Jack of all trades"}

name: Archaeologist
description: ## Archaeologist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/32› No stodgy researcher, this archaeologist meets his research head-on in the field. Archaeologists sacrifice the bard's inspirational performance for a smattering of rogue talents. This archetype also fits rogue-like characters that focus more on learning than on stabbing foes in the back. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{icon=down info="Archaeologists do not gain the *bardic performance* ability or any of its performance types."} ::ab[Archaeologist's Luck (Ex)]{icon=boost-def flavor="Fortune favors the archaeologist." swift="An archaeologist can call on fortune's favor, giving him a +1 luck bonus on attack rolls, saving throws, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls. Maintaining this bonus is a @HLfree_action, but it ends immediately if the archaeologist is killed, paralyzed, stunned, knocked unconscious, or otherwise prevented from taking a free action to maintain it each round." useMod=Cha4 useUnit=round special="Archaeologist's luck is treated as bardic performance for the purposes of feats, abilities, effects, and the like that affect bardic performance. Like bardic performance, it cannot be maintained at the same time as other performance abilities." increment="The bonus~-1~6"} ::ab[Clever Explorer (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost passive="An archaeologist gains a bonus equal to ‹misc/half› his class level on Disable Device and Perception checks. He can disable intricate and complex devices in half the normal amount of time (minimum 1 round) and open a lock as a @HLstandard_action." imp6="An archaeologist can take 10 on Disable Device checks, even if distracted or endangered, and can disarm magical traps." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[Uncanny Dodge (Ex)]{icon=def l=2 ability="An archaeologist gains ‹ability/uncanny dodge›, as the rogue class feature of the same name." replace=Well-versed} ::ab[Trap Sense (Ex)]{l=3 icon=def ability="An archaeologist gains ‹ability/trap sense›, as the rogue class feature of the same name. The bonus granted by *trap sense* is equal to one-third of your archaeologist level."} ::ab[Rogue Talents]{l=4 icon=power ability="An archaeologist gains a ‹ability/rogue talent›. He gains an additional rogue talent for every four levels of archaeologist gained after 4th level. Otherwise, this works as the rogue's rogue talent ability."} ::ab[Evasion (Ex)]{l=6 icon=def ability="An archaeologist gains ‹ability/evasion›, as the rogue ability of the same name."} ::ab[Advanced Talent]{l=12 icon=boost ability="An archaeologist can now choose an ‹ability/advanced rogue talent› instead of a rogue talent."}

name: Archivist
description: ## Archivist ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/80› Some bards greatly prefer academic pursuits to the drama (and sometimes melodrama) of their artistic brethren. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{icon=power head info="An archivist gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Naturalist (Ex)]{next icon=boost ability="An archivist who has identified a creature with a Knowledge check appropriate to its type can use performance to share strategies for defeating it with allies in combat. The archivist and any allies within 30 feet gain a +1 insight bonus to AC and on attack rolls and saving throws against exceptional, supernatural, and spell-like abilities used by creatures of that specific kind of monster (e.g., ‹monster/frost giant«s›, not all giants or all humanoids)." increment="The bonus~-1~6" special="This language-dependent ability requires visual and audible components." replace="Inspire courage"} ::ab[Lamentable Belaborment (Ex)]{next l=6 icon=lower ability="An archivist can bewilder a creature already ‹misc/fascinated› by his performance. Using this ability does not disrupt the fascinate effect, but it does require a @HLstandard_action to activate (in addition to the @HLfree_action to continue the fascinate effect). The target must make a Will save (DC 10 + ‹misc/half› the bard's level + the bard's Cha modifier). Success renders the target immune to this power for 24 hours, but failure leaves the target either ‹misc/dazed› or ‹misc/confused› (archivist's choice) for as long as the performance continues." special="If the target takes damage, this effect ends immediately. This mind-affecting ability relies on audible components." replace=Suggestion} ::ab[Pedantic Lecture (Su)]{next l=18 icon=boost ability="An archivist can affect as many creatures with *lamentable belaborment* as he currently has fascinated. In addition, he may choose to cause targets to fall asleep rather than be dazed or confused." replace="Mass suggestion"} ::ab[Lore Master (Ex)]{icon=boost l2="An archivist may take 20 on Knowledge checks once per day." l8="He may do so twice a day." l14="He may do so three times a day." l20="He may do so four times a day." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[Magic Lore (Ex)]{icon=boost-def passive="An archivist gains a bonus on Spellcraft checks to identify magic items or decipher scrolls equal to half his bard level and may take 10 on such checks. He gains a +4 bonus on saves against magical traps, language-dependent effects, and symbols, glyphs, and magical writings of any kind." ability="An archivist can use Disable Device to disarm magical traps as per a rogue's ‹ability/trapfinding› ability." order=pa replace=Well-versed} ::ab[Jack-of-All-Trades (Ex)]{icon=power l5="An archivist can use any skill, even if the skill normally requires him to be trained." l11="He considers all skills to be class skills." l17="He can take 10 on any skill check, even if it is not normally allowed." replace="Lore master"} ::ab[Probable Path (Ex)]{icon=roll flavor="An archivist can calculate the action likely to bring success with the least risk" l10="Once per day, he can take 10 on any d20 roll." l13="He may do so twice a day." l16="He may do so three times a day." l19="He may do so four times a day." replace="Jack of all trades"}

name: Celebrity
description: ## Celebrity ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/25› Known for being known, a celebrity bard is a master of performance who captures the imagination and attention of his audience. He trades on his charisma, his wit, and his exploits to build his renown - and that of his companions. ::ab[Famous]{l=1 icon=boost choice="A celebrity bard may choose a region where he is famous, and within that region, the locals are more likely to react favorably toward the bard. The bard gains a bonus on Diplomacy and Intimidate checks in that area and to influence people from that area." imp1="This region is a settlement or settlements with a total population of 1,000 or fewer people, and the modifier on Diplomacy and Intimidate checks is +1. As the celebrity grows more famous, additional areas learn of him (typically places where he has lived or traveled, or settlements adjacent to those where he is known) and his bonuses apply to even more people." imp5="The region is a settlement or settlements with a total population of 5,000 or fewer people, and the modifier on Diplomacy and Intimidate checks is +2." imp9="The region is a settlement or settlements with a total population of up to 25,000 people, and the modifier on Diplomacy and Intimidate checks is +3." imp13="The region is a settlement or settlements with a total population of up to 100,000 people, and the modifier to Diplomacy and Intimidate is +4." imp17="The bard's renown has spread far, and most civilized folk know of him (GM's discretion); the bard's modifier on Diplomacy and Intimidate checks is +5." replace="Inspire courage"} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A celebrity gains the following type of bardic performance."} ::ab[Gather Crowd (Ex)]{next l=5 icon=power ability="The celebrity is skilled at drawing an audience to his performances. If he is in a settlement or populated area, he can shout, sing, or otherwise make himself noticed in order to attract an audience to his impromptu stage. The size of the crowd depends on the local population, but typically is a number of people equal to ‹misc/half› the bard's class level &times& the result of the bard's Perform check. The crowd gathers over the next 1d10 rounds." special="If the bard fails to engage the crowd (such as by performing, kissing babies, trying to use fascinate, and so on), it disperses over the next 1d10 rounds." replace="Lore master"} ::ab[Shining Star (Su)]{l=8 icon=boost passive="The celebrity has learned how to focus attention on himself so thoroughly that even the presence of danger does not distract his adoring crowd. When using *fascinate,* a target making a save to break the effect because of a potential threat takes a -4 penalty on that save, and even obvious threats require a save rather than automatically breaking the effect. Creatures affected by the bard's fascinate ability ignore the shaken condition." replace="Dirge of doom"}

name: Court Bard
description: ## Court Bard ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/81› Spending years studying all of the finer points of erudition and etiquette, the court bard takes up the role of resplendent proclaimer and artist-in-residence at the hand of nobility, royalty, and the well-moneyed elite who aspire to join their ranks. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A court bard gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Satire (Su)]{next icon=lower ability="A court bard can use performance to undermine the confidence of enemies who hear it, causing them to take a -1 penalty on attack and damage rolls (minimum 1) and a -1 penalty on saves against fear and charm effects as long as the bard continues performing." imp5="The penalty becomes -2." imp11="The penalty becomes -3." imp17="The penalty becomes -4." special="*Satire* is a language-dependent, mind-affecting ability that uses audible components." replace="Inspire courage"} ::ab[Mockery (Su)]{next l=3 icon=lower flavor="A court bard can subtly ridicule and defame a specific individual." ability="The bard selects one target who can hear his performance. That individual takes a -2 penalty on Charisma checks and Charisma-related skill checks as long as the bard continues performing." imp7="The penalty becomes -3." imp11="The penalty becomes -4." imp15="The penalty becomes -5." imp19="The penalty becomes -6." special="*Mockery* is a language-dependent, mind-affecting ability that relies on audible components." replace="Inspire competence"} ::ab[Glorious Epic (Su)]{next icon=lower l=8 flavor="A court bard can weave captivating tales that engross those who hear them." ability="Enemies within 30 feet become ‹rule/flat-footed› unless they succeed at a Will save (DC 10 + ‹misc/half› the bard's level + the bard's Cha modifier). A save renders them immune to this ability for 24 hours." special="*Glorious epic* is a language-dependent, mind-affecting ability that uses audible components." replace="Dirge of doom"} ::ab[Scandal (Su)]{next icon=lower l=14 flavor="A court bard can combine salacious gossip and biting calumny to incite a riot." ability="Each enemy within 30 feet is affected as if by a ‹spell/song of discord› for as long as it can hear the performance. A successful Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the bard's level + the bard's Cha modifier) negates the effect, and that creature is immune to this ability for 24 hours." special="*Scandal* is a language-dependent, mind-affecting ability that uses audible components." replace="Frightening tune"} ::ab[Heraldic Expertise (Ex)]{icon=boost-roll passive="A court bard gains a bonus equal to half his bard level on Diplomacy, Knowledge (history), Knowledge (local), and Knowledge (nobility) checks (minimum +1)." ability="The court bard can also reroll a check against one of these skills, though he must take the result of the second roll even if it is worse." order=pau useInc=bard~5~+ useF="1~1~5~~5" replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Wide Audience (Su)]{icon=cone-boost ability="A court bard can choose to affect a 60-foot cone instead of a 30-foot radius with bardic performances that affect an area." imp10="The area of such powers is increased by 10 feet (radius) or 20 feet (cone). If the power instead affects multiple creatures, it affects one additional creature than normal." imp15="If the power instead affects multiple creatures, it affects two additional creatures than normal." imp20="If the power instead affects multiple creatures, it affects three additional creatures than normal." special="This does not affect powers that affect only a single creature." replace="Lore master~jack of all trades"}

name: Cultivator
description: ## Cultivator ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/40› Cultivators use music to promote plant growth and influence the behavior of plants both naturally and supernaturally. Most cultivators work in conjunction with local communities to maintain crops and oversee harvests, while others serve as wardens of unspoiled natural wonders. ::cskill{gain=sur} ::ab[Plant Magic]{icon=learn info="A cultivator bard adds the following spells to his bard spell list at the corresponding spell levels: ‹spell/entangle› (1st), ‹spell/greensight› (2nd), ‹spell/plant growth› (3rd), ‹spell/antiplant shell› (4th), ‹spell/tree stride› (5th), ‹spell/green caress› (6th)." alter="The bard's spells"} ::ab[Verdant Voice]{icon=power ability="By combining traditional ‹faith/Green Faith› chants and fey songs into his bardic performance, a cultivator gains the ability to affect a creature of the plant type with mind-affecting bardic performances. However, doing so requires the cultivator to expend 1 additional round of bardic performance each round he maintains a performance augmented by *verdant voice.*" replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Song of Growth (Su)]{icon=def-protect flavor="A cultivator can spontaneously promote massive plant growth with his bardic performance." standard="While he maintains his *song of growth,* the cultivator can select one side of a square within 30 feet of himself and instantly create an opaque barrier of plant matter to block that face, providing total ‹rule/cover›. He can create one barrier as part of starting his bardic performance if he starts the performance as a standard action. The side the cultivator selects must be supported by the ground, and the growth itself cannot support more than 5 pounds of weight. The conjured barrier has hardness 0, AC 5, and 2 hit points per bard level." special="A cultivator can maintain a number of plant growths equal to his Charisma modifier + ‹misc/half› his bard level. These barriers immediately crumble to dust when the cultivator ends his performance." replace=Countersong} ::ab[Resist Nature's Lure (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power-def passive="A cultivator gains ‹ability/resist nature's lure›, as the druid class feature of the same name, but with only a +2 bonus instead of +4." imp4="This increases to a +4 bonus." replace=Well-versed} ::ab[Nature Lore (Ex)]{l=5 icon=power-down ability="The cultivator gains the *lore master* bard ability, except he can use it only on Knowledge (nature) checks and Survival checks to track creatures in natural environments." alter="Lore master"}

name: Daredevil
description: ## Daredevil ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/32› As quick at wordplay as at swordplay, daredevils are dashing heroes, inspiring their allies to match their clever repartee and acrobatic feats. Daredevils often lean toward comedy, dance, oratory, and singing. ::ab[Agile (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="A daredevil adds ‹misc/half› her class level (minimum 1) on Acrobatics, Bluff, Climb, and Escape Artist checks." replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A daredevil gains the following type of bardic performance."} ::ab[Derring-do (Su)]{next icon=def-protect-boost flavor="A daredevil can use her performance to bring out grace in the clumsiest allies." ability="The daredevil and any allies who see her receive a +1 morale bonus on Reflex saving throws and a +2 competence bonus on Dexterity-based skill checks. Allies who move at least 10 feet during their turn gain a +1 dodge bonus to their Armor Class until the start of their next turn." imp5="The skill bonus becomes +4, and the other bonuses become +2." imp11="The skill bonus becomes +6, and the other bonuses become +3." imp17="The skill bonus becomes +8, and the other bonuses become +4." special="This is a mind-affecting ability that uses visual components." replace="Inspire courage"} ::ab[Canny Foe (Ex)]{l=2 icon=melee-def choice="A daredevil can choose one type of ‹rule/combat maneuver<s›." passive="She gains a +2 bonus on her combat maneuver checks to attempt the chosen maneuver and to her CMD to resist that maneuver." order=cp imp6="The daredevil gains a +2 bonus for a second type of combat maneuver." imp10="The daredevil chooses a third combat maneuver to gain a +2 bonus." imp14="The daredevil chooses a fourth combat maneuver to gain a +2 bonus." imp18="The daredevil chooses a fifth combat maneuver to gain a +2 bonus." special="She may not choose the same maneuver twice." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[Dauntless (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def passive="A daredevil gains a +1 morale bonus on saving throws against mind-affecting effects, including all fear effects." increment="This bonus~2~4" replace=Well-versed} ::ab[Scoundrel's Fortune (Ex)]{icon=roll useInc=bard~3~5 useF="5~1~3" l=5 ability="A daredevil can choose to roll two dice instead of one for any skill check, keeping the best result." replace="Lore master"}

name: Demagogue
description: ## Demagogue ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/26› Not content with providing amusing and occasionally instructive performances, the demagogue seeks to inflame and ignite his audience, driving them toward a specific purpose with carefully chosen words and tones that may spark momentous change. ::ab[Famous]{l=1 icon=boost choice="A demagogue may choose a region where he is famous, and within that region, the locals are more likely to react favorably toward him. The bard gains a bonus on Bluff and Intimidate checks in that area and to influence people from that area." imp1="This region is a settlement or settlements with a total population of 1,000 or fewer people, and the modifier on Bluff and Intimidate checks is +1. As the demagogue grows more famous, additional areas learn of him (typically places where he has lived or traveled, or settlements adjacent to those where he is known) and his bonuses apply to even more people." imp5="The region is a settlement or settlements with a total population of 5,000 or fewer people, and the modifier on Bluff and Intimidate checks is +2." imp9="The region is a settlement or settlements with a total population of up to 25,000 people, and the modifier on Bluff and Intimidate checks is +3." imp13="The region is a settlement or settlements with a total population of up to 100,000 people, and the modifier to Bluff and Intimidate is +4." imp17="The demagogue's renown has spread far, and most civilized folk know of him (GM's discretion); the demagogue's modifier on Bluff and Intimidate checks is +5." replace="Inspire courage +1"} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A demagogue gains the following type of bardic performance."} ::ab[Gather Crowd (Ex)]{next l=5 icon=power ability="The demagogue is skilled at drawing an audience to his performances. If he is in a settlement or populated area, he can shout, sing, or otherwise make himself noticed in order to attract an audience to his impromptu stage. The size of the crowd depends on the local population, but typically is a number of people equal to ‹misc/half› the bard's class level &times& the result of the bard's Perform check. The crowd gathers over the next 1d10 rounds." special="If the bard fails to engage the crowd (such as by performing, kissing babies, trying to use *fascinate,* and so on), it disperses over the next 1d10 rounds." replace="Lore master"} ::ab[Incite Violence (Ex)]{next l=6 icon=power ability="The demagogue can use his performance to fan the fury of a crowd of people he has fascinated. Using this ability does not disrupt the *fascinate* effect, but does require a @HLstandard_action to activate (in addition to the @HLfree_action to continue the *fascinate* effect). The bard selects a number of targets equal to his level, who must make Will saves (DC 10 + 1/2 the bard's level + the bard's Charisma modifier) or be affected by ‹spell/rage› for a number of rounds equal to the bard's level. The bard indicates who is the intended target of violence (either after using this ability or as part of the performance leading to it) and the enraged members of the crowd immediately attack the target if possible. The target does not need to be present (&quot&kill the king&quot& is a suitable choice) and can be an object instead of a person (&quot&destroy the prison!&quot& is likewise appropriate). Other members of the crowd may follow suit, though they do not gain the benefits of *rage.*" special="This is a sound-based effect and is affected by *countersong.* If two or more bards are attempting to direct the crowd against different targets, they must make opposed Charisma checks, with the crowd following the directions of the winner." replace=Suggestion} ::ab[Righteous Cause (Ex)]{next l=18 icon=power ability="The demagogue can lift a crowd's emotions and turn them toward a common purpose. First, he must *fascinate* the crowd, and then use *incite violence* without designating a target, at which point he can use *righteous cause.* Instead of driving the crowd with anger, he fills them with purpose. Fascinated creatures must make Will saves (DC 10 + 1/2 the bard's level + the bard's Charisma modifier) to resist. Those who fail are affected by ‹spell/mass suggestion› of a plausible idea that lingers with them for one day. Typical uses of this ability are to spark rebellion, overthrow a king, build a beneficial structure such as an orphanage, or donate money to a cause." replace="Mass suggestion"}

name: Dervish Dancer

features.name: Weapon and Armor Proficiency
features.replaces: Proficiency with the rapier and whip

description: ## Dervish Dancer ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/32› Not all bards inspire others with their performances. Dervish dancers enter a near-mystical trance that allows them to push their bodies beyond normal limits. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=power-down ability="Dervish dancers gain weapon proficiency with the ‹eq-weapon/scimitar› and ‹eq-weapon/kukri›." replace="Proficiency with the rapier and whip"} :::ab{title="Battle Dance" head icon=power action=Ability imp10="A dervish dancer can start a *battle dance* as a @HLswift_action instead of a move action." alter="Bardic performance" special="Dervish dancers gain the *inspire courage, inspire greatness,* and *inspire heroics* bardic performance types as *battle dances,* but these only provide benefit to the dervish dancer himself."} A dervish dancer is trained in the use of the Perform skill, especially dance, to create magical effects on himself. This works like bardic performance, except the dervish dancer only affects himself, and does not need to be able to see or hear his own performance. Battle dancing is treated as bardic performance for the purposes of feats, abilities, effects, and the like that affect bardic performance, except that *battle dancing* does not benefit from the ‹feat/Lingering Performance› feat or any other ability that allows a bardic performance to grant bonuses after it has ended. Battle dancing benefits apply only when the bard is wearing light or no armor. Like bardic performance, it cannot be maintained at the same time as other performance abilities. Starting a *battle dance* is a @HL[move action], but it can be maintained each round as a @HL[free action]. Changing a *battle dance* from one effect to another requires the dervish dancer to stop the previous performance and start the new one as a move action. Like a bard, a dervish dancer's performance ends immediately if he is killed, paralyzed, stunned, knocked unconscious, or otherwise prevented from taking a free action each round. A dervish dancer cannot perform more than one *battle dance* at a time. ::: ::ab[Rain of Blows (Su)]{next icon=boost-def l=6 ability="A dervish dancer can use his *battle dance* to speed up his attacks. When making a ‹rule/full attack› action, he may make one extra attack with any weapon he is holding, as though under the effects of a ‹spell/haste› spell. He also gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls and a +1 dodge bonus to AC and on Reflex saves." increment="p!The bonuses~6~3" special="These bonuses do not stack with the *haste* spell." replace="Suggestion~mass suggestion"} ::ab[Razor's Kiss (Su)]{next icon=boost l=8 passive="A dervish dancer can use his *battle dance* to improve his weapons' critical range. All attacks he makes with manufactured weapons are treated as though he had the ‹feat/Improved Critical› feat. Natural weapons and spells are not affected." replace="Dirge of doom"} ::ab[Leaf on the Wind (Su)]{next l=14 icon=def ability="A dervish dancer can use his *battle dance* to evade attacks with unearthly grace and to shake off the effects of his wounds. Unlike other *battle dances, leaf on the wind* requires a @HLstandard_action each round to start or maintain the performance. Each round it is maintained, including the first, the dervish dancer gains a +6 dodge bonus to Armor Class and on Reflex saves. If wounded, he heals 1 hit point of damage per bard level." replace="Frightening performance"} ::ab[Fleet (Su)]{icon=boost passive="While performing a *battle dance,* a dervish dancer gains a +10 enhancement bonus to his land speed." increment="This bonus~1~4~15~5" incrementEnd=" feet." replace="Bardic knowledge~lore master"} ::ab[Versatile Dance (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost passive="At 2nd level, a dervish dancer gains a bonus equal to ‹misc/half› his level on Perform (dance) checks." order=pa ability="He can use his bonus for his Perform (dance) skill in place of his bonus for Acrobatics." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[Dance of Fury (Su)]{l=12 icon=melee-boost ability="A dervish dancer can attack more than once as he moves while performing a *battle dance.* He can combine a full-attack action with a single move, taking the attacks at any point during his movement, but must move at least 5 feet between each attack. This movement provokes attacks of opportunity as normal." replace="Soothing performance"} ::ab[Battle Fury (Su)]{l=20 icon=melee-boost flavor="The dervish dancer can unleash a whirlwind of blows while performing a *battle dance.*" fullround="He can take a single move action and unleash a single attack at his highest bonus against each target within his reach during any point of his move, up to a maximum number of attacks equal to the dervish dancer's character level. This movement provokes attacks of opportunity as normal." replace="Deadly performance"}

name: Detective
description: ## Detective ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/81› Piecing together clues and catching the guilty with sheer cleverness, the detective is skilled at divining the truth. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A detective gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Careful Teamwork (Su)]{next icon=boost-def ability="A detective uses performance to keep allies coordinated, alert, and ready for action. All allies within 30 feet gain a +1 bonus on Initiative checks, Perception, and Disable Device checks for 1 hour. They also gain a +1 insight bonus on Reflex saves and to AC against traps and when they are ‹rule/flat-footed›." increment="p!The bonuses~-1~6" special="Using this ability requires 3 rounds of continuous performance, and the targets must be able to see and hear the bard throughout the performance. This ability is language-dependent and requires visual and audible components." replace="Inspire courage"} ::ab[True Confession (Su)]{next icon=lower l=9 ability="A detective can use performance to trick a creature into revealing its secrets. Using this ability requires a successful Sense Motive check to see through a Bluff or notice mental compulsion. After 3 continuous rounds of performance, the target must make a Will save (DC 10 + ‹misc/half› the bard's level + the bard's Cha modifier). Success renders the target immune to this power for 24 hours. On a failed save, a liar inadvertently reveals the lie and the truth behind it. A creature under a charm or compulsion reveals the nature of its enchantment and who placed it (if the creature knows) and gains a new saving throw to break free from the enchantment." special="This ability is language-dependent and requires audible components." imp15="Using this power requires only 2 rounds of performance." imp20="This power now only requires 1 round of performance." replace="Inspire greatness"} ::ab[Show Yourselves (Ex)]{next icon=lower l=15 ability="A detective can use performance to compel creatures to reveal themselves when hiding. All enemies within 30 feet must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the bard's level + the bard's Cha modifier). If they fail, they must cease using Stealth, unlock and open doors between themselves and the detective, and dismiss, suppress, or dispel if necessary magical effects that grant ‹spell/invisibility› or any other form of ‹rule/concealment› from the detective. As long as they can hear the performance, affected creatures may not attack or flee until they have eliminated every such effect, though they are freed from this compulsion immediately if attacked." special="Creatures in the area must make this save each round the bard continues his performance. This ability is language-dependent and requires audible components." replace="Inspire heroics"} ::ab[Eye for Detail (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="A detective gains a bonus equal to half his level on Knowledge (local), Perception, and Sense Motive checks, as well as Diplomacy checks to gather information (minimum +1)." replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Arcane Insight (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power-def ability="A detective can find and disable magical traps, like a rogue's ‹ability/trapfinding› ability. In addition, he gains a +4 bonus on saving throws made against illusions and a +4 bonus on caster level checks and saving throws to see through disguises and protections against divination (such as ‹spell/magic aura›, ‹spell/misdirection›, and ‹spell/nondetection›)." replace=Well-versed} ::ab[Arcane Investigation]{icon=learn info="In addition, a detective's class spell list includes the following: 1st-‹spell/detect chaos›/‹spell/detect_>evil›/‹spell/detect_>law›/‹spell/detect_>good›; 2nd-‹spell/zone of truth›; 3rd-‹spell/arcane eye›, ‹spell/speak with dead›, ‹spell/speak with plants›; 4th-‹spell/discern lies›; 5th-‹spell/prying eyes›, ‹spell/stone tell›; 6th-‹spell/discern location›, ‹spell/find the path›, ‹spell/greater prying eyes›, ‹spell/moment of prescience›." imp2="A detective may add one of these spells or any divination spell on the bard spell list to his list of spells known at 2nd level and every four levels thereafter (6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th levels)." replace="Versatile performance"}

name: Dirge Bard
description: ## Dirge Bard ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/26› A composer of sonorous laments for the dead and elaborate requiems for those lost yet long remembered, dirge bards master musical tools and tropes that must appeal to the ears and hearts of both the living and the dead. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A dirge bard gains the following type of bardic performance."} ::ab[Dance of the Dead (Su)]{next icon=power ability="A dirge bard can use his bardic performance to cause dead bones or bodies to rise up and move or fight at his command. This ability functions like ‹spell/animate dead›, but the created skeletons or zombies remain fully animate only as long as the dirge bard continues the performance. Once it stops, any created undead collapse into carrion. Bodies or bones cannot be animated more than once using this ability. Unlike *animate dead,* dance of the dead requires no components and does not have the evil descriptor." replace=Jack-of-all-trades} ::ab[Haunted Eyes (Ex)]{icon=def l=2 passive="A dirge bard gains a +4 bonus on saves against fear, energy drain, death effects, and necromantic effects." replace=Well-versed} ::ab[Secrets of the Grave (Ex)]{icon=boost l=2 passive="A dirge bard gains a bonus equal to ‹misc/half› his bard level on Knowledge (religion) checks made to identify undead creatures and their abilities." ability="A dirge bard may use mind-affecting spells to affect undead as if they were living creatures, even if they are mindless (though spells that affect only humanoids do not affect them, even if they were humanoids in life)." order=pa special="In addition, he may add one ‹main/spells_>necromancy« spell› from the spell list of any arcane spellcasting class to his list of spells known at 2nd level and every four levels thereafter (6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th levels)." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[Haunting Refrain (Su)]{l=5 icon=lower ability="A dirge bard is able to stir primal terrors in the hearts of listeners. He can use a Perform (keyboard) or Perform (percussion) check in place of an Intimidate check to demoralize an opponent, with a bonus equal to half his bard level. In addition, saving throws against any fear effect he creates are made with a -2 penalty." imp10="The penalty becomes -3." imp15="The penalty becomes -4." imp20="The penalty becomes -5." replace="Lore master"}

name: Fey Courtier
description: ## Fey Courtier ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/11› Fey who associate with courts often become bards skilled at navigating the inhuman societies of the trackless wilds. ::prereq{r=Gathlain} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="The fey courtier has access to the following bardic performances."} ::ab[Scorn of the Wilds (Sp)]{next l=8 icon=magic ability="The fey courtier can use bardic performance to permanently mark a creature with nature's displeasure by spending 2 rounds performing while the target remains within 30 feet. The performance includes a litany of the target's misdeeds against fey and nature. Unless the target succeeds at a Will saving throw (DC = 10 + ‹misc/half› the bard's level + his Charisma modifier), it is cursed as per ‹spell/nature's exile› or ‹spell/bestow curse›." imp14="The fey courtier's options expand to include ‹spell/baleful polymorph› and ‹spell/green caress›." special="As part of the performance, the fey courtier must define a condition under which the curse will be lifted, which must relate to making amends for the crime against fey or nature and cannot be suicidal to carry out. A creature that succeeds at its saving throw is immune to the fey courtier's scorn of the wild for 24 hours. This is a curse effect." replace="Dirge of doom~frightening tune"} ::ab[Stone Dance (Sp)]{next l=15 icon=magic ability="The bard's performance can move even the features of the natural world. This performance functions as ‹spell/animate plants› (DC = 10 + half the bard's level + his Charisma modifier) except it can also animate unworked stone and water from natural bodies of water (with statistics equivalent to an appropriate plant)." replace="Inspire heroics"} ::ab[Fey Contacts]{l=2 icon=power-boost passive="Thanks to his fey contacts and knowledge of the byzantine trade customs of the fey courts, a fey courtier can treat any wilderness area with fey residents as a settlement with a certain base value and purchase limit based on his bard level for the purpose of buying and selling magic items (see the table below). The fey courtier can also use these contacts to gather information about the residents, geography, and nearby areas with Diplomacy." replace="Versatile performance"} These rules come from ‹rule/The Settlement Stat Block›: >*There is a 75% chance that any item of [the Base Value] or lower can be found for sale in the community with little effort. If an item is not available, a new check to determine if the item has become available can be made in 1 week. A settlement's purchase limit is the most money a shop in the settlement can spend to purchase any single item from the PCs. If the PCs wish to sell an item worth more than a settlement's purchase limit, they'll either need to settle for a lower price, travel to a larger city, or (with the GM's permission) search for a specific buyer in the city with deeper pockets.* | Bard Level | Base Value | Purchase Limit | | --- | --- | --- | | 2nd | 50 gp | 500 gp | | 6th | 500 gp | 2,500 gp | | 10th | 2,000 gp | 10,000 gp | | 14th | 8,000 gp | 50,000 gp | | 18th | 32,000 gp | 200,000 gp | ::ab[Summon Fey Allies]{l=3 icon=learn-power ability="The fey courtier gains ‹feat/Augment Summoning› as a bonus feat and can call upon natural allies who owe him favors. He adds ‹spell/summon nature's ally I› to his list of 1st-level bard spells known. Whenever he gains access to another spell level, he adds the next-higher *summon nature's ally* spell to his list of bard spells known." special="The fey courtier adds the following creatures to the *summon nature's ally* list: 1st-‹monster/grimple« (gremlin)›, ‹monster/mite›, ‹monster/sprite›; 2nd-‹monster/atomie›, ‹monster/fuath« (gremlin)›, ‹monster/nixie›; 3rd-‹monster/leprechaun›, ‹monster/nuglub« (gremlin)›, ‹monster/pooka›; 4th-‹monster/kelpie›, ‹monster/korred›, ‹monster/twigjack›; 5th-‹monster/lampad›, ‹monster/lurker in light›, ‹monster/swan maiden›; 6th-‹monster/cold rider›, ‹monster/oceanid›, ‹monster/sangoi›." replace="Inspire competence"}

name: Filidh
description: ## Filidh ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/40› By tapping into the world's natural music, specialized bards known as filidhs are able to see not only the tapestry of life but divine portents of the future from the rhythm of all life's song. ::ab[Armor and Weapon Proficiency]{icon=down info="A filidh is proficient with light armor and is prohibited from wearing metal armor. A filidh can wear wooden armor that has been altered by the ‹spell/ironwood› spell. Filidhs are proficient with shields (except tower shields) but can use only those made of wood." special="A filidh who wears prohibited armor or uses a prohibited shield is unable to cast bard spells or use any of his supernatural or spell-like class abilities while doing so and for 24 hours thereafter." alter="Armor and weapon proficiencies"} ::ab[Natural Magic]{icon=magic info="A filidh casts spells as a bard, but the spells are divine, not arcane, and therefore not subject to arcane spell failure. A filidh must use a holy symbol or a musical instrument as a divine focus when a spell includes such a component. He still uses the bard spell list." alter=Spellcasting} ::ab[Nature's Song]{icon=magic useL=bard useUnit=time ability="Filidhs can hear the resonant song generated by all living creatures - a primal music that stretches back to the beginning of time and ahead to the unwritten future. By tapping into this cosmic melody, a filidh can steal glimpses of the future." order=awu swift="A filidh can sacrifice a spell slot to gain an additional number of rounds of bardic performance for that day equal to the spell's level."} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A filidh gains the following types of bardic performances."} ::ab[Echoes of Nature's Song (Su)]{next icon=protect ability="A filidh can use his bardic performance to imbue his allies with subconscious knowledge of their own futures, improving their reflexes and ability to avoid danger. An affected ally receives a +1 insight bonus on Reflex saving throws and to AC." increment="This bonus~-1~6" special="This performance is a mind-affecting ability and relies on audible components." replace="Inspire courage"} ::ab[Divinatory Song (Sp)]{next l=6 icon=magic ability="A filidh can use his performance to create an effect equivalent to ‹spell/divination›, using the filidh's level as the caster level. The filidh and all allies who can hear his performance receive the information provided by the divination as flashes of inspiration and knowledge." special="Divinatory song takes 10 minutes and uses 6 rounds of bardic performance. Divinatory song relies on audible components." replace=Suggestion} ::ab[Voices of Life (Su)]{next l=8 icon=magic ability="A filidh can grant himself and all allies who can hear his performance the ability to speak with animals and plants as if affected by ‹spell/speak with animals› and ‹spell/speak with plants› so long as he maintains this performance." replace="Dirge of doom"} ::ab[Unity of Life (Su)]{next icon=magic-protect l=15 ability="A filidh can use his performance to interlink the life force of two allies who can hear his performance as though they were affected by ‹spell/shield other›, using the filidh's bard level as his caster level. The filidh designates which ally is the warded target and which ally receives half the warded creature's damage." order=af free="The filidh can switch the targets of this ability (and the effect of the performance the targets receive) once per round at the start of each turn that he maintains the performance." replace="Inspire heroics"} ::ab[Song of the Cycle (Su)]{next l=20 icon=protect ability="A filidh can grant awe-inspiring glimpses into the future with his magic. All allies who can see and hear the filidh are affected as though by the personal version of ‹spell/foresight› for the duration of the performance." replace="Deadly performance"}

name: Geisha
description: ## Geisha ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/27› In some cultures, the professional entertainer is a prestigious role. Specially trained entertainers called geisha are praised for their appearance and skill at conversation, music, dancing, singing, poetry, and calligraphy. A geisha provides social intimacy and status but not physical intimacy. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down-magic info="Geisha are proficient in all simple weapons and one ‹class/monk› weapon. Geisha are not proficient in any armor or shield; unlike bards, geisha are subject to arcane spell failure even when casting in light armor or when using a shield." alter="Armor and weapon proficiencies"} ::ab[Tea Ceremony (Su)]{icon=boost ability="By spending 10 minutes preparing an elaborate tea ceremony, a geisha may affect her allies with *inspire courage, inspire competence, inspire greatness,* or *inspire heroics.* The ceremony's effects last 10 minutes. The geisha must spend 4 rounds of bardic performance for each creature to be affected."} ::ab[Geisha Knowledge]{icon=boost passive="A geisha adds ‹misc/half› her class level (minimum 1) on Craft (calligraphy) checks, Diplomacy checks, Knowledge (nobility) checks, and one type of Perform check (act, dance, oratory, percussion, string, or sing); she may make checks with these skills untrained." replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Scribe Scroll]{icon=power ability="A geisha gains ‹feat/Scribe Scroll› as a bonus feat."}

name: Impervious Messenger
description: ## Impervious Messenger ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/20› The impervious messenger is capable of harnessing the unique qualities of bardic magic to keep, transport, and communicate the most precious of secrets and messages, even when subject to the most vigorous forms of observation, be they magical or mundane. ::ab[Bardic Performance (Su)]{head icon=info info="An impervious messenger gains the following types of bardic performances."} ::ab[Chant of Perfect Recall (Su)]{next icon=magic ability="An impervious messenger can spend 1 round of his bardic performance to commit something to memory. This ability functions exactly as per ‹spell/memorize page›, but the impervious messenger is the only recipient and he requires only 1 round to commit a single page to memory. An impervious messenger can commit additional pages worth of material to memory by using additional rounds of his bardic performance, but he can never memorize more than half his total bard level in pages (minimum 1)." replace=Fascinate} ::ab[Song of Subterfuge (Su)]{next l=6 icon=magic ability="An impervious messenger learns to use his performances to project various thoughts into his own mind to disrupt divination attempts. This acts similarly to ‹performance/distraction›, except it only affects the impervious messenger and allows him to use the result of his Perform check in place of saving throws against attempts to read his mind, such as ‹spell/detect thoughts›." imp18="If the impervious messenger succeeds on a saving throw while using *song of subterfuge,* the character who attempted the divination effect must succeed on a Will save (DC = 20 + the impervious messenger's Charisma modifier) or else the impervious messenger instantly learns the nature of the effect and can allow the effect to continue, but provide whatever information he chooses to the divining character rather than the true results of the divination effect." replace="Suggestion~mass suggestion"} ::ab[Unbroken Stride (Su)]{next l=8 icon=boost ability="An impervious messenger draws upon his bardic abilities to imbue himself with grace and speed. While using this bardic performance, an impervious messenger gains an insight bonus equal to ‹misc/half› his bard level on all Acrobatics, Climb, Fly, and Ride checks. In addition, while maintaining this performance, he gains the benefits of the ranger's ‹ability/woodland stride› ability and a +10-foot enhancement bonus to his base land speed." imp12="An impervious messenger using his *unbroken stride* bardic performance also acts as if under the effect of ‹spell/freedom of movement›. In addition, the enhancement bonus to his base land speed increases to +30 feet." replace="Dirge of doom~frightening tune"} ::ab[Cryptic Whisper (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost-def flavor="The impervious messenger internalizes his understanding of language and ciphers, and filters them through his bardic abilities." passive="He adds half his bard level to all Linguistics checks and Bluff checks to deliver secret messages, and he gains a +4 bonus on saving throws against ‹main/glyph spells, »symbol spells,› and language-dependent effects." replace="Bardic knowledge~well-versed"}

name: Magician
description: ## Magician ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/82› A magician dabbles in performance, but sees it as a means to tap into universal energies and channel them. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A magician gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Dweomercraft (Su)]{next icon=boost ability="A magician can use performance to manipulate magical energies. Allies of the magician gain a +1 bonus on caster level checks, ‹rule/concentration› checks, and attack rolls with spells and spell-like abilities." increment="This bonus~-1~6" special="This ability relies on visual and audible components." replace="Inspire courage"} ::ab[Spell Suppression (Su)]{next icon=magic l=8 flavor="A magician can use performance to counter the spells of his foes." ability="Once the bard begins using this performance, he tracks the number of rounds it has been in use. While performing, as an @HLimmediate_action, he can attempt to counter any spell that he can identify using Spellcraft, so long as that spell's level is equal or less than the total number of rounds he has been performing spell suppression. The attempt to counter the spell is made as if using ‹spell/dispel magic›, using the bard's level as the caster level. If successful, the bardic performance immediately ends." special="This ability requires audible components." replace="Dirge of doom"} ::ab[Metamagic Mastery (Ex)]{next icon=magic-boost l=14 ability="A magician can use performance to apply a ‹main/metamagic feat› to a spell he is about to cast without increasing the casting time. The bard must still expend a higher-level slot to cast this spell. This causes the performance to immediately end." special="This ability requires audible components." replace="Frightening tune"} ::ab[Magical Talent (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="A magician gains a bonus equal to ‹misc/half› his level on Knowledge (arcana), Spellcraft, and Use Magic Device checks." replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Improved Counterspell]{icon=power ability="A magician gains ‹feat/Improved Counterspell› as a bonus feat." replace=Countersong} ::ab[Extended Performance (Su)]{l=2 icon=boost swift="A magician can extend the duration of bardic performance after he stops concentrating by sacrificing a spell slot. The performance effect lingers for 1 extra round per level of the spell." special="Only one spell may be sacrificed per performance, and performance types that take affect after a specific number of rounds cannot be extended." replace=Well-versed} ::ab[Expanded Repertoire (Ex)]{icon=learn l2="A magician can add one spell to his spells known from the spell list of any arcane spellcasting class. The spell must be of a level he can cast." l6="He can add another spell, following the same limitations." l10="He can add another spell, following the same limitations." l14="He can add another spell, following the same limitations." l18="He can add another spell, following the same limitations." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[Arcane Bond (Ex)]{l=5 head icon=boost ability="A magician gains the *arcane bond* ability as a ‹class/wizard›. He may not choose a familiar or a weapon as a bonded item." replace="Lore master"} :::ab{next title="Arcane Bond: Bonded Object" flavor="Relevant text from the wizard ability." icon=magic action=Ability} If you select a bonded object, you begin play with one at no cost. Objects that are the subject of an arcane bond must fall into one of the following categories: amulet, ring, staff, wand, or weapon. These objects are always masterwork quality. If the object is an amulet or ring, it must be worn to have effect, while staves, wands, and weapons must be wielded. If you attempt to cast a spell without your bonded object worn or in hand, you must make a ‹rule/concentration› check or lose the spell. The DC for this check is equal to 20 + the spell's level. If the object is a ring or amulet, it occupies the ‹rule/ring or »neck slot› accordingly. A bonded object can be used once per day to cast any one spell that you have in your spellbook and are capable of casting, even if the spell is not prepared. This spell is treated like any other spell cast by you, including casting time, duration, and other effects dependent on your level. This spell cannot be modified by metamagic feats or other abilities. The bonded object cannot be used to cast spells from your opposition schools. You can add additional magic abilities to your bonded object as if you have the required item creation feats and if you meet the level prerequisites of the feat. For example, a wizard with a bonded dagger must be at least 5th level to add magic abilities to the dagger (see ‹feat/Craft Magic Arms and Armor›). If the bonded object is a wand, it loses its wand abilities when its last charge is consumed, but it is not destroyed and it retains all of its bonded object properties and can be used to craft a new wand. The magic properties of a bonded object, including any magic abilities added to the object, only function for the wizard who owns it. If a bonded object's owner dies, or the item is replaced, the object reverts to being an ordinary masterwork item of the appropriate type. If a bonded object is damaged, it is restored to full hit points the next time you prepare your spells. If the object of an arcane bond is lost or destroyed, it can be replaced after 1 week in a special ritual that costs 200 gp per wizard level plus the cost of the masterwork item. This ritual takes 8 hours to complete. Items replaced in this way do not possess any of the additional enchantments of the previous bonded item. You can designate an existing magic item as your bonded item. This functions in the same way as replacing a lost or destroyed item except that the new magic item retains its abilities while gaining the benefits and drawbacks of becoming a bonded item. ::: ::ab[Wand Mastery (Ex)]{icon=boost l10="When a magician uses a wand containing a spell on his spell list, he uses his Charisma bonus to set the wand's save." imp16="When using such a wand, he uses his caster level in place of the wand's caster level." replace="Jack of all trades"}

name: Masked Performer
description: ## Masked Performer ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/20› Not merely an entertainer in a disguise, the masked performer takes on the persona represented by the likeness she wears. Her alter ego might be a theatrical archetype, a legendary hero, or a revered spirit. Masked performers are often the stars of religious plays and festivals, and aficionados easily recognize them and associate them with their most famous role. ::ab[Dual Identity (Ex)]{icon=power ability="This ability acts as the ‹class/vigilante› ability of the same name, except as follows. The masked performer's identities are referred to as social and masked, rather than social and vigilante. Unlike a vigilante, most people who know of the masked performer actually know that the masked performer's identities are one and the same. Nonetheless, the dual identity ability is valuable to the masked performer due to offering her two perspectives on any problem and two different alignments." replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A masked performer gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Seamless Guise (Ex)]{next icon=power-boost ability="A masked performer learns to behave in a way that appears perfectly proper and normal for her current role, on stage or off. She can maintain this performance for 1 hour for every 3 rounds of bardic performance she spends. While this performance is active, she receives a +10 bonus on Disguise and Perform (act) checks to remain in character after she has already established her character. For instance, this bonus does not apply against the initial Perception check when meeting a creature paying attention to her but does apply on the automatic additional Perception check each hour of interacting." replace=Countersong} ::ab[Exaggerated Pose (Su)]{next icon=boost l=3 order=aw ability="A masked performer can enhance her own physical and social abilities by simply altering her posture. When she starts this performance, the masked performer chooses a Strength-, Dexterity-, or Charisma-based skill and gains a +2 competence bonus on checks with that skill as long as she maintains this performance." imp7="The bonus becomes +3." imp11="The bonus becomes +4." imp15="This bonus becomes +5." imp19="The bonus becomes +6." swift="The masked performer can change the chosen skill." special="*Exaggerated pose* is an emotion effect and relies on visual components." replace="Inspire competence"} ::ab[Stage Combat (Su)]{next icon=power l=6 ability="A masked performer gains the benefit of a ‹main/combat feat› she doesn't have as long as she maintains this performance. The masked performer chooses the feat when she starts this performance. The masked performer must meet all the feat's prerequisites." special="As usual when temporarily gaining a feat, if the feat she chooses has any limitations on uses, such as ‹feat/Stunning Fist«'s› daily uses, all uses of that combat feat while maintaining *stage combat* count toward that feat's limit. In the case of Stunning Fist, if the masked performer gained that feat again later the same day, the expended uses would remain expended. *Stage combat* relies on visual components." replace=Suggestion} ::ab[Multiplicity of Masks (Su)]{next icon=magic-aura l=18 ability="A masked performer can cause any number of her allies to appear as herself or as another ally within 60 feet. To be affected, an ally must be within 60 feet of the masker performer and able to see her. As long as the masked performer maintains this performance, enemies perceive all affected allies as the chosen character. If an affected ally is a different size or creature type than the chosen character, enemies can attempt a Will save (DC = 10 + ‹misc/half› the masked performer's bard level + her Charisma modifier) to disbelieve. Otherwise, there is no saving throw, but a successful attack against a disguised ally automatically reveals the ally's true form." special="If an ally moves out of range, that ally reverts to his original form, and the entire effect ends if the ally providing his appearance to the others moves out of range. *Multiplicity of masks* is an illusion (glamer) effect that relies on visual components." replace="Mass suggestion"} ::ab[Social Grace (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power ability="A masked performer gains the ‹soctalent/social grace› vigilante social talent." special="She gains an additional skill with *social grace* 1 level later than a vigilante (at 6th level, 10th level, 14th level, and 18th level)." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[Masked Talents]{icon=power l5="A masked performer gains a rogue talent from the following list: ‹talent/expert leaper›, ‹talent/fast stealth›, ‹talent/ledge walker›, ‹talent/rogue crawl›, ‹talent/rope master›, ‹talent/stand up›, and ‹talent/wall scramble›." l17="A masked performer can choose any of the above talents or an advanced rogue talent from the following list: ‹talent/defensive roll›, ‹talent/fast tumble›, ‹talent/hide in plain sight›, and ‹talent/skill mastery›." special="This ability does not qualify her for the ‹feat/Extra Rogue Talent› feat." replace="Lore master"}

name: Plant Speaker
description: ## Plant Speaker (Vine Leshy only) ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/22› Plant speakers build upon their racial *plantspeech* ability and their storytelling tendencies to create an art form full of deep metaphors and allegory rather than specific details and facts. ::prereq{r="Vine leshy"} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="Plant speakers gain the following bardic performance."} ::ab[Leshy Speaker (Su)]{next icon=magic l9="The plant speaker can speak to its disembodied brethren, the spirits of nature that become leshys. He performs for 10 minutes and spends 7 rounds of bardic performance to gain the effects of ‹spell/commune with nature›." replace="Inspire greatness"} ::ab[Plant Speech]{icon=boost-power l=1 passive="A plant speaker's mind-affecting bard spells and class abilities also affect plants, ignoring plants' immunity to mind-affecting effects." imp2="A plant speaker's racial plantspeech allows him to communicate with all plants, not just plants that match his alternate form." replace="Bardic knowledge~well-versed"} ::ab[Mystical Allegory (Su)]{icon=power-magic l5="The plant speaker can tell a story that matches some of the themes of the current situation in order to gain insight, gaining the effects of ‹spell/augury› by performing for 1 minute and spending 4 rounds of bardic performance." l11="He can perform for 10 minutes and spend 7 rounds of bardic performance to gain the effects of ‹spell/divination›." l17="He can perform for 1 hour and spend 10 rounds of bardic performance to gain the effects of ‹spell/legend lore›, but the information is always vague and incomplete." replace="Lore master"}

name: Ringleader (UI)
description: ## Ringleader (UI) ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/21› Ringleaders are adept in getting the most out of their allies, and they excel at planning for unexpected complications in advance. Often the masterminds behind elaborate heists and infiltrations, ringleaders use their organizational abilities to make sure the plan goes without a hitch, even when the team is split up and unable to communicate with each other on the spot. ::ab[Inspire Competence (Su)]{icon=boost l3="A ringleader can use his performance to help an ally succeed at a task. This ability acts as the ‹performance/inspire competence› bardic performance with the following additions." l8="The ringleader's ally gains a competence bonus on an additional skill (for a total of two skills). In addition, he can end the effect to reroll a check with one of the affected skills (the reroll still applies the bonus from inspire competence). Each ally can only use this latter ability once per day, regardless of the number of skills affected and the number of times they are affected by inspire competence." l14="The ringleader's ally gains a competence bonus on an additional skill (for a total of three skills). In addition, he can take 10 on the affected skills when stressed or distracted." alter="Inspire competence" replace="Dirge of doom~frightening tune"} :::ab{title="Inspired Plan (Su)" icon=boost l=2 action=Ability replace="Versatile performance"} A ringleader can alter his performance so it affects a single ally at a later time. The ringleader must explain his plan to that ally for a number of minutes equal to the number of bardic performance rounds he expends on the effect, and use audible and/or visual components according to the performance altered. This costs the ringleader the chosen number of rounds of bardic performance. At any time before the ringleader recovers bardic performance rounds for the day, the inspired character can activate the performance as a @HL[standard action] wherever she is. When activated, the altered performance affects only the inspired ally and has no audible or visible components. If the performance could normally affect any number of allies, its effects last 2 rounds for each round the ringleader spent on the performance. Otherwise, the effects last 1 round for each round the ringleader spent on the performance. A ringleader can alter only the *countersong, distraction, inspire courage, inspire competence, inspire greatness,* and *inspire heroics* performances in this way. The ringleader makes any necessary choices when establishing the performance, though in the case of *countersong* and *distraction,* the ringleader attempts Perform checks once his ally triggers the plan, ignoring any temporary bonuses or penalties, no matter whether they applied when he explained the plan or when the ally triggers it. A character can be subject to only one inspired plan at a time and cannot be subject to a ringleader's inspired plan and any of the ringleader's normal performances at the same time, but she can benefit from other bardic performances in the interim. The ringleader cannot use inspired plan on himself, but he can have dormant plans ready to trigger on as many different allies as he can afford to affect at once. ::: ::ab[Hidden Plans (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def passive="A ringleader becomes a master of discretion. The ringleader gains a +4 bonus on saving throws against effects that would read his thoughts or compel him to tell the truth." replace=Well-versed} ::ab[Prepared (Ex)]{l=5 icon=power ability="A ringleader expects the unexpected. When the ringleader is in a situation where he could use a particular piece of nonmagical gear, the ringleader can attempt a Knowledge check appropriate to his current situation to have purchased that item in advance. The DC of the check is equal to the item's cost in gp. If he succeeds, he deducts the appropriate cost of the item from his current gp total and now has the item in question on his person. He cannot use this ability to retroactively gain an item that would change his encumbrance to a different load category, though in this case, he can attempt to retrieve such objects from a pack mule, extradimensional storage space, or other location that would not affect his encumbrance." useInc=bard~5 useF="5~1" replace="Lore master"}

name: Sandman
description: ## Sandman ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/82› Combining performance with stealth, trickery, and guile, the sandman uses cleverness to keep others off-balance. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A sandman gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Stealspell (Su)]{next icon=magic ability="A sandman can use performance to steal spells from his foes and add them to his list of spells known. Once the performance is started, the bard can steal a prepared spell or a spell known from another creature with a touch attack as a standard action. The target receives a Will save (DC 10 + ‹misc/half› the bard's level + the bard's Cha bonus) to negate the effect. The sandman may choose a spell to steal, but if the target does not possess the spell, the bardic performance immediately ends. Otherwise the spell stolen is random, but it is always of the highest level that the bard can cast, if possible. The target loses the prepared spell or spell known and the sandman adds it to his list of spells known for as long as the performance continues, after which it reverts to the original recipient." order=an info="While stolen, the bard can cast the spell using his available spell slots. This use does not consume the stolen spell. If the bard steals another spell while a spell is stolen, the previous spell immediately reverts to its original owner." special="This ability requires visual components." replace="Inspire courage"} ::ab[Slumber Song (Sp)]{next icon=magic l6="A sandman can use his performance to cause a creature he has already *fascinated* to fall asleep (as ‹spell/deep slumber›, but with no HD limit). Otherwise, this ability functions like ‹performance/suggestion›." replace=Suggestion} ::ab[Dramatic Subtext (Su)]{next icon=magic l9="A sandman can use bardic performance to cast spells without obvious visual or audible components while retaining the spell's normal effects. Observers must succeed at a Perception check opposed by a sandman's Sleight of Hand check to notice that the sandman is the source of the spellcasting (though spellcasting still provokes attacks of opportunity)." special="The bard must use this performance for at least 2 rounds before casting a spell; otherwise he is automatically detected and the performance ends." replace="Inspire greatness"} ::ab[Greater Stealspell (Su)]{next icon=boost l15="A sandman's *stealspell* power improves. When a target fails a save against his *stealspell* performance, the sandman discovers its spell resistance (if any) and all spells it has prepared or knows. He can then choose which spell to steal. The sandman may forgo stealing a spell and instead reduce the target's SR by an amount equal to half his bard level and gain that amount of spell resistance for as long as he continues performing." special="If he steals additional spell resistance, it stacks with previously stolen SR. If he steals a spell or ceases performing, the spell resistance immediately reverts back to its owner." replace="Inspire heroics"} ::ab[Mass Slumber Song (Sp)]{next icon=boost l18="A sandman can use *slumber song* to affect any number of *fascinated* creatures within 30 feet. Otherwise, this ability functions like ‹performance/mass suggestion›." replace="Mass suggestion"} ::ab[Spell Catching (Su)]{next icon=def-magic l=20 immediate="A sandman who saves against a spell or spell-like ability that targets only him (not including area spells) may respond with his bardic performance. He must attempt a caster level check (DC 10 + the spell's original caster level). If it succeeds, the sandman can absorb the spell effect without harm and immediately recast that spell (using the original caster's level and save DC) or any spell he knows of that level or lower." special="Using this ability consumes a number of rounds of bardic performance equal to the spell's level, even if the check fails." replace="Deadly performance"} ::ab[Master of Deception (Ex)]{icon=boost-power passive="A sandman gains a bonus equal to half his level on Bluff, Sleight of Hand, and Stealth checks." order=pa ability="He may also disarm magical traps with Disable Device as a rogue's ‹ability/trapfinding› ability." replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Sneakspell (Ex)]{icon=boost l2="A sandman adds +1 to the save DC of spells and bardic performance against opponents who are denied their Dex bonus." l6="He gains a +2 bonus on caster level checks to overcome spell resistance against such foes." l10="The save DC now increases by +2." l14="The bonus on caster level checks becomes +4." l18="The save DC now increases by +3." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[Trap Sense (Ex)]{icon=def l=3 passive="A sandman gains a bonus on Reflex saves against traps and a dodge bonus to AC against traps. @B-3mp-bard-x." replace="Inspire competence"} ::ab[Sneak Attack (Ex)]{icon=boost ability="A sandman inflicts extra damage against targets within 30 feet that he flanks or that are denied their Dex bonus to AC against him. This damage is equal to +1d6 points for every five bard levels he has (e.g, a 15th-level sandman would deal +3d6 extra damage)." replace="Lore master"}

name: Savage Skald
description: ## Savage Skald ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/84› Far from civilization, furious tribes have their own war-singers, work-chanters, and lore-keepers, savaging enemies with song and sword alike. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A savage skald gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Inspiring Blow (Su)]{next icon=boost flavor="A savage skald roars his war-cries with each telling blow." immediate="When he confirms a critical hit, he can start this performance (ending any other performances). He gains ‹rule/temporary hit points› equal to his Charisma modifier (if positive), and all allies within 30 feet gain a +1 morale bonus on their next attack roll prior to the start of his next turn.
