These temporary hit points remain until the bard ends his performance." replace=Fascinate} ::ab[Incite Rage (Su)]{next icon=magic l=6 ability="A savage skald can induce a furious rage in one creature within 30 feet. This effect functions as a ‹spell/rage› spell that lasts as long as the target can hear the bard's performance; however, unwilling creatures can be affected if they fail a Will save (DC 10 + ‹misc/half› the bard's level + the bard's Cha modifier). Success renders the target immune to this power for 24 hours. The bard cannot target himself with this ability." special="If the target has the rage class feature, it can instead immediately rage and stay in this rage without consuming rounds of rage per day as long as the bard continues performing. This mind-affecting effect requires audible components." replace=Suggestion} ::ab[Song of the Fallen (Sp)]{next icon=magic l10="A savage skald can duplicate the effect of a ‹magic-wondrous/horn of Valhalla›. This effect requires 10 continuous rounds of performance. This summons barbarians as a silver horn." l13="This summons barbarians as a brass horn." l16="This now summons as a bronze horn." l19="This now summons as an iron horn." special="The warriors remain only as long as the bard continues his performance. This ability requires audible components." replace="Jack of all trades"} ::ab[Berserkergang (Ex)]{next icon=protect l12="A savage skald can inspire a rapturous battle trance that suppresses pain, stunning, and fear effects for one creature." l15="This affects two creatures at once." l18="This now affects three creatures at once." special="Affected creatures also gain DR 5/- (DR 10/- against nonlethal damage); this benefit stacks with the damage reduction class ability of barbarians. This mind-affecting ability requires audible components." replace="Soothing performance"} ::ab[Battle Song (Su)]{next icon=magic l18="A savage skald can affect all allies within 30 feet when using performance to *incite rage.*" replace="Mass suggestion"}

name: Sea Singer
description: ## Sea Singer ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/84› The sea singer calls the blue waters his home, and is much in demand among sea captains wishing good fortune for their crew and hull as they ply the tradewinds far and wide. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A sea singer gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Sea Shanty (Su)]{next icon=boost ability="A sea singer learns to counter seasickness and exhaustion during long sea voyages. Each round of a sea shanty, he makes a Perform skill check. Allies within 30 feet (including the sea singer) may use his Perform check in place of a saving throw against becoming exhausted, fatigued, nauseated, or sickened; if already under such an effect, a new save is allowed each round of the sea shanty, using the bard's Perform check for the save." special="A sea shanty has no effect on instantaneous effects or effects that do not allow saves. This ability requires audible components." replace=Countersong} ::ab[Still Water (Su)]{next icon=magic l3="A sea singer can use performance to calm rough waters within 30 feet, reducing the DC for Profession (sailor) and Swim checks, as well as for Acrobatics and Climb checks aboard ship, by an amount equal to the bard's level (to a minimum of DC 10) for as long he continues to perform. He can extend this duration to 1 hour by playing for 10 consecutive rounds." special="This ability requires audible components." replace="Inspire competence"} ::ab[Whistle the Wind (Su)]{next icon=magic l6="A sea singer can use performance to create a ‹spell/gust of wind›. This wind lasts for as long as he continues his performance. He can extend this duration to 1 minute by playing for 5 consecutive rounds." replace=Suggestion} ::ab[Call the Storm (Su)]{next icon=magic l18="A sea singer can use performance to duplicate ‹spell/control water›, ‹spell/control weather›, ‹spell/control winds›, or ‹spell/storm of vengeance›, using his bard level as the caster level. Using this ability requires 1 round of continuous performance per level of the spell (as if he were a ‹class/druid›). These effects continue for as long as the bard continues performing (the effects of *control weather* happen immediately), but not longer than the spell's normal duration." replace="Mass suggestion"} ::ab[World Traveler (Ex)]{icon=boost-roll passive="A sea singer gains a bonus equal to ‹misc/half› his bard level on Knowledge (geography), Knowledge (local), Knowledge (nature), and Linguistics checks." ability="He can reroll a check against one of these skills, but must take the result of the second roll even if it is worse." order=pau useInc=bard~5~+ useF="1~1~5~~5" replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Familiar]{l=2 icon=power ability="A sea singer acquires an exotic pet - a ‹monster/monkey› or parrot (treat as ‹monster/raven›) - that gains abilities as a wizard's ‹ability/familiar›, using the sea singer's bard level as his wizard level." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[Sea Legs (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def passive="A sea singer gains a +4 bonus on saving throws against air and water effects and effects that would cause the sea singer to slip, trip, or otherwise be knocked ‹rule/prone›. He gains a +2 bonus to CMD against grapple, overrun, and trip." replace=Well-versed}

name: Songhealer
description: ## Songhealer ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/27› Words can harm, but they also heal. The songhealer brings peace and surcease of pain, calming wild emotions and providing a balm for the wounded body. ::ab[Enhance Healing (Su)]{icon=boost useMod=Cha ability="A songhealer can cause any healing effect from a spell completion or spell trigger item to function at a caster level equal to his class level." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A songhealer gains the following type of bardic performance."} ::ab[Healing Performance (Su)]{next icon=magic-aid l=14 ability="A songhealer can use his performance to create an effect equivalent to ‹spell/heal› on a living target (or ‹spell/harm› on an undead target), using the bard's level as the caster level. Using this ability requires 5 rounds of continuous performance, and the target must be able to see and hear the bard throughout the performance." special="The *healing performance* relies on audible and visual components." replace="Frightening tune"} ::ab[Funereal Ballad (Su)]{next l=20 icon=magic-aid ability="A songhealer can use his performance to create an effect equivalent to ‹spell/resurrection› on a dead creature, using the bard's level as the caster level. Using this ability requires 20 rounds of continuous performance, and the target must be within 10 feet of the bard for the entire performance." special="*Funereal ballad* relies on audible and visual components." replace="Deadly performance"}

name: Sorrowsoul
description: ## Sorrowsoul ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/22› It isn't uncommon for a bard to, on occasion, sing mournful tunes or craft elegies that depict the deepest sadness or the most profound suffering. But while most bards who do so create such performances for fame or wealth, the sorrowsoul has known tragedy and loss on a level so intimate, he has bound it to his soul. ::ab[Lyric Sorrow (Su)]{head icon=power info="A sorrowsoul draws upon grief, rage, and tragedy to fuel his bardic performances. When a sorrowsoul begins a bardic performance, he can choose to alter its effects with *lyric sorrow.* If he does so, he uses twice the number of rounds of his bardic performance ability as normal, and even if the sorrowsoul has the ‹feat/Lingering Performance› feat, the performance's effects do not last for any additional rounds." alter="Bardic performance" replace="Soothing performance~versatile performance"} ::ab[Inspire Courage]{next icon=def-boost l1="A sorrowsoul can use his lyric sorrow in conjunction with ‹performance/inspire courage›. When he chooses to do so, he increases his bonuses on saving throws and on weapon attack and damage rolls from +1 to +2, but his other allies receive no benefit." l5="His bonuses become +4." l11="His bonuses become +6." l17="His bonuses become +8."} ::ab[Inspire Greatness]{next icon=boost-def l12="A sorrowsoul can use his lyric sorrow ability in conjunction with ‹performance/inspire greatness› to grant himself 3 bonus Hit Dice, a +3 competence bonus on attack rolls, and a +2 competence bonus on Fortitude saves; if he does so, *inspire greatness* only affects him, not any other allies."} ::ab[Inspire Heroics]{next icon=def l15="When a sorrowsoul uses his lyric sorrow ability in conjunction with the ‹performance/inspire heroics› bardic performance, he gains ‹umr/fast healing› 5 and benefits from a 50% miss chance, as if under the effects of ‹spell/displacement›, in addition to the standard bonuses conferred by this bardic performance. But if he does so, *inspire heroics* only affects him, not any other allies."} ::ab[Darkness Denied (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def passive="A sorrowsoul gains a +4 bonus on saving throws against negative energy and death effects." replace=Well-versed} ::ab[Spurn Harm (Su)]{icon=def flavor="A sorrowsoul can funnel his bardic powers to persevere in the face of seemingly certain death." immediate="A sorrowsoul can spend 3 rounds of his daily bardic performance to gain a +2 insight bonus on all saving throws for 1 round." imp11="A sorrowsoul also gains spell resistance equal to 11 + his bard level when using this ability." imp17="He also gains DR 10/- when using this ability." replace="Lore master"}

name: Sound Striker
description: ## Sound Striker **Source** ‹source/Ultimate Magic« pg. 27›, [errata](https://paizo.com/paizo/faq/v5748nruor1fz#v5748eaic9t4f) They say that words can cut deeper than any blade, and the sound striker proves this true. Using music and words as a weapon, he can focus his performances into a deadly delivery. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A sound striker gains the following types of bardic performance. Neither performance can be performed more quickly than a standard action."} ::ab[Wordstrike (Su)]{next icon=zap l=3 standard="The sound striker bard can spend 1 round of bardic performance to direct a burst of sonically charged words at a creature or object. This performance deals 1d4 points of damage plus the bard's level to an object, or half this damage to a living creature." replace="Inspire competence"} ::ab[Weird Words (Su)]{next icon=zap l6="The bard can start a performance that is always a @HLstandard_action to speak up to one word per 4 bard levels laden with sonic energy. Each word deals 4d6 points of sonic damage as a ranged touch attack with a range of 30 feet. The bard adds his charisma modifier on damage rolls with weird words. Multiple words that strike the same target stack into a single powerful attack, applying energy resistance and bonuses on damage rolls only once. The bard can target all words at the same or different targets, but he unleashes all words simultaneously. Each word costs 1 round of bardic performance." replace=Suggestion}

name: Street Performer
description: ## Street Performer ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/85› Whether acrobat, troubadour, or thespian, the street performer mixes with the masses, singing for his supper. ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A street performer gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Disappearing Act (Su)]{next icon=power-aura l1="A street performer can use performance to divert attention from an ally. All creatures within 30 feet that fail a Will save (DC 10 + ‹misc/half› the bard's level + the bard's Cha modifier) treat one creature chosen by the bard as if it were ‹rule/invisible›." l5="This performance now affects two allies." l11="The bard can render three allies invisible." l17="The bard can now affect four allies." special="If the targets take any action that would cause them to become visible, they become visible to everyone. The bard cannot use this ability on himself. This ability is a mind-affecting effect that requires visual components." replace="Inspire courage"} ::ab[Harmless Performer (Su)]{next icon=def l3="A street performer can use performance to appear meek and unworthy of being attacked. While using this performance, whenever an enemy targets the street performer, the enemy must succeed at a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the bard's level + the bard's Cha bonus) or be unable to attack the bard this round, as per ‹spell/sanctuary›. The enemy loses the attack that targeted the bard, but may spend additional attacks targeting other creatures. If the opponent was targeting the street performer with a spell, it must succeed at a ‹rule/concentration› check at the same DC or lose the spell. If this check succeeds, it may target another creature with the spell instead." special="This mind-affecting ability requires audible or visual components." replace="Inspire competence"} ::ab[Madcap Prank (Su)]{next icon=lower l9="A street performer can use performance to discomfit a target within 30 feet, causing its clothing to become tangled, its headgear to fall down over its eyes, or even causing it to slip and fall or otherwise be made to appear a fool. The target must make a Reflex save (DC 10 + 1/2 the bard's level + the bard's Cha modifier) each round that it hears or sees the performance, or it takes one of the following random effects each round: 1-‹misc/blinded›, 2-‹misc/dazzled›, 3-‹misc/deafened›, 4-‹rule/entangled›, 5-fall ‹rule/prone›, 6-‹misc/nauseated›. Each effect lasts 1 round." replace="Inspire greatness"} ::ab[Slip through the Crowd (Su)]{next icon=boost l15="A street performer's disappearing act enables affected creatures to move through crowd squares and enemy-occupied squares without impediment. Affected creatures are treated as if having ‹spell/greater invisibility›, but enemies gain a new saving throw to notice them each time they are attacked." replace="Inspire heroics"} ::ab[Gladhanding]{icon=boost ability="A street performer earns double the normal amount of money from ‹skill/Perform› checks." standard="He may use a Bluff check in place of a Diplomacy check to improve a creature's attitude for 1 minute, after which its attitude becomes one step worse than originally." order=as replace=Countersong} ::ab[Streetwise]{icon=boost passive="A street performer gains a bonus equal to half his level on Bluff, Disguise, Knowledge (local), and Sleight of Hand checks, Diplomacy or Intimidate checks made to influence crowds, and Diplomacy checks to gather information (minimum +1)." replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Quick Change (Ex)]{icon=power l=5 standard="A street performer can don a disguise by taking a -5 penalty on his check." swift="He can take 10 on Bluff and Disguise checks and use Bluff to create a diversion to hide." ability="He can Take 20 on a Bluff or Disguise check once per day." order=swa imp11="He can Take 20 twice a day." imp17="He can Take 20 three times a day." replace="Lore master"}

name: Thundercaller
sourceBook: Ultimate Wilderness, Varisia, Birthplace of Legends
description: ## Thundercaller ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/41;Varisia, Birthplace of Legends/11› Thundercallers bear the knowledge of the ancients, wielding it like a weapon to protect the land for which they care so deeply. Their voices ring like thunder, calling the sky's wrath down upon their enemies and summoning furious rage to bolster their allies. ::ab[Bound to the Land (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="A thundercaller gains a bonus equal to ‹misc/half› her level on Handle Animal checks, Knowledge (nature) checks, and Survival checks." replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A thundercaller gains the following types of bardic performance."} ::ab[Thunder Call (Su)]{next icon=magic l3="The thundercaller can start a performance to unleash a deafening peal of thunder. This allows the thundercaller to spend a round of performance to create an effect similar to the spell ‹spell/sound burst› (having the same range and area and allowing the same saving throw)." l7="The sonic damage dealt by this blast of sound increases to 3d8." l11="The damage becomes 5d8." l15="The damage becomes 7d8." l19="The damage becomes 9d8." special="A creature that succeeds at its saving throw against thunder call is immune to the stunning effect but still takes sonic damage. Beginning this performance is always a @HLstandard_action." replace="Inspire competence"} ::ab[Incite Rage (Su)]{next icon=magic-aura l6="The thundercaller can induce a furious rage in one creature within 30 feet. This effect functions as the ‹spell/rage› spell and lasts as long as the target can hear the thundercaller's performance. Any unwilling creature targeted is affected if it fails a Will saving throw (DC = 10 + half the thundercaller's level + the thundercaller's Charisma modifier). A target that succeeds at its saving throw is immune to this power for 24 hours. The thundercaller cannot target herself with this ability." special="If the target has the rage class feature, it can instead immediately rage and stay in this rage without consuming rounds of rage per day as long as the thundercaller continues performing. This performance is a mind-affecting effect and relies on audible components." replace="Suggestion~mass suggestion"} ::ab[Call Lightning (Su)]{next icon=zap l8="The thundercaller can use her performance to summon bolts of lightning, as per the spell ‹spell/call lightning›. The lightning storm lasts for as long as she continues her performance, calling down one bolt of lightning per round as a @HLstandard_action. The damage of these lightning bolts can be increased in stormy areas or can be limited as *call lightning* describes." replace="Dirge of doom"} ::ab[Call Lightning Storm (Su)]{next icon=zap l14="The thundercaller can use her performance to summon bolts of lightning, as per the spell ‹spell/call lightning storm›. The lightning storm lasts for as long as she continues her performance, calling down one bolt of lightning per round as a @HLstandard_action. The damage of these lightning bolts can be increased in stormy areas or can be limited as *call lightning* describes." replace="Frightening tune"}

name: Wit
description: ## Wit ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/23› The wit is a master of clever repartee and verbal dueling, moving through noble courts like a fish through water. ::ab[Way with Words (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="A wit gains a bonus on Bluff, Diplomacy, Intimidate, Linguistics, and Sense Motive checks. @B-4m1-bard-x. He also gains a number of edges at the beginning of any ‹rule/verbal duel<s› equal to this bonus." replace="Bardic knowledge"} ::ab[Counterargument]{icon=down ability="A wit can use only Perform (act, comedy, or oratory) to perform a countersong." alter=Countersong} ::ab[Bardic Performance]{head icon=power info="A wit gains the following bardic performance."} ::ab[Cutting Remark (Su)]{next icon=zap l=3 standard="A wit can wound with his words. The wit can spend 1 round of bardic performance to deal 1d4 points of nonlethal damage + the wit's bard level to a creature within 30 feet. Damage reduction applies to this damage." imp8="A target who takes damage from cutting remark is also ‹misc/sickened› for as long as it remains within 30 feet of the wit and for 1 round thereafter. Additionally, the nonlethal damage counts as magic for purposes such as overcoming damage reduction." imp14="A target who takes damage from cutting remark must also succeed at a Will save (DC = 10 + ‹misc/half› the wit's bard level + his Charisma modifier) or be ‹misc/dazed› for 1 round. A creature that makes a successful save is immune to the dazing effect of the wit's cutting remark for 24 hours." special="Cutting remark is a mind-affecting, language-dependent effect, and relies on audible components." replace="Inspire competence~dirge of doom~frightening tune"} ::ab[Quick Witted (Ex)]{icon=power-boost l2="A wit can always act in a surprise round (though he remains ‹rule/flat-footed› until he acts). In addition, the wit adds half his bard level on initiative checks." replace="Versatile performance"} ::ab[On the Ball (Ex)]{icon=roll useInc=bard~6~5 useF="5~1~6" l5="Rather than roll for initiative, the wit can treat his roll as if it was a 10 (adding any modifiers as usual)." l20="When the wit uses this ability, he can instead treat his roll as if it was a 20." replace="Lore master"} ::ab[Duel Master (Ex)]{l=10 icon=boost order=pa passive="The wit does not lose any edges for being at an extreme disadvantage in a verbal duel and can either ask about one additional bias when successfully using Sense Motive to determine an audience's biases or automatically seed one of the biases that he discovered." ability="Once during a verbal duel, he can reassign an appropriate skill from one tactic to another tactic in which he didn't assign any skills. The original tactic is treated as being unprepared for the rest of the duel." replace=Jack-of-all-trades}

name: Beast Rider
description: ## Beast Rider ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/36› The cavalier is defined not only by his dedication to his order or his skill on the battlefield, but also by the special relationship he maintains with his mount. Where some cavaliers are simply skilled with horses or well-trained knights, the beast rider spends his life in constant pursuit of the most perfect mount, forming bonds with greater, more powerful, and more exotic creatures. ::ab[Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="A beast rider is proficient with light and medium armor, and with shields (with the exception of tower shields)."} :::ab{l=1 head icon=power replace="Mount~expert trainer" action=Ability title="Exotic Mount (Ex)"} A beast rider forms a bond with a strong, loyal companion that permits him to ride it as a mount. This mount functions as a druid's ‹sidekick/animal companion›, using the beast rider's level as his effective druid level. The animal chosen as a mount must be large enough to carry the beast rider (Medium or Large for a Small character; Large or Huge for a Medium character). The beast rider does not take an armor check penalty on ‹skill/Ride› checks while riding his mount. The mount is always considered combat trained, and begins play with ‹feat/Endurance› as a bonus feat. A beast rider's mount does not gain the *share spells* special ability. Each time the beast rider increases in level, he can choose to select a new, more impressive mount better suited to his increased power. Anytime a feat or ability allows a mount to make a hoof attack, it can make a claw, slam, or other analogous attack instead. ::: ::ab[Small Size]{next icon=power l1="Small-sized beast riders can choose a ‹companion/pony› or ‹companion/wolf› mount." l4="A Small beast rider can also choose an ‹companion/allosaurus›, ‹companion/ankylosaurus›, ‹companion/arsinoitherium›, ‹companion/aurochs›, ‹companion/bison›, ‹companion/boar›, ‹companion/brachiosaurus›, ‹companion/elephant›, ‹companion/glyptodon›, ‹companion/hippopotamus›, ‹companion/mastodon›, ‹companion/megaloceros›, ‹companion/riding »dog›, ‹companion/giant snapping turtle›, ‹companion/triceratops›, or ‹companion/tyrannosaurus›." l7="He can also choose a dinosaur (‹companion/deinonychus› or ‹companion/velociraptor›)."} ::ab[Medium Size]{next icon=power l1="Medium beast riders can choose a ‹companion/camel› or ‹companion/horse›." l4="A Medium beast rider can also choose an allosaurus, ankylosaurus, arsinoitherium, aurochs, bison, brachiosaurus, elephant, glyptodon, hippopotamus, ‹companion/lion›, mastodon, megaloceros, giant snapping turtle, ‹companion/tiger›, triceratops, or tyrannosaurus as his mount. Additional mounts might be available with GM approval." l7="A Medium beast rider can select any creature whose natural size is Large or Huge, provided that creature is normally available as a Medium-sized animal companion at 7th level (like a ‹companion/bear›). To generate statistics for such a mount, apply the following modifications: **Size** Large; **Ability Scores** Str +2, Dex -2, Con +2. Increase the damage of each of the mount's natural attacks ‹misc/by one die« size›." special="A beast rider cannot choose a mount that is not capable of bearing his weight, that has fewer than four legs, or that has a fly speed (although the GM may allow mounts with a swim speed in certain environments)."}

name: Courtly Knight
description: ## Courtly Knight ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/24› Some cavaliers strive to be just as effective at the court of a local lord as on the field of battle. These courtly knights are equally at home in a duel with words or swords. ::ab[Social Presence (Ex)]{l=1 icon=boost passive="A courtly knight gains a bonus on all Bluff, Diplomacy, Intimidate, and Sense Motive checks. @B-4f1-cavalier. A courtly knight starts any ‹rule/verbal duel<s› with an extra edge she can use for only the *presence* tactic unless she is at a significant or extreme disadvantage in the duel." replace=Tactician} ::ab[Imperious Attitude (Ex)]{l=9 icon=power flavor="A courtly knight develops a commanding demeanor, and the strength of her conviction is often enough to get others to do as she asks, merely because she expects it to be done." ability="In a social setting, the courtly knight can attempt Diplomacy checks to make a request of a creature whose attitude toward her is unfriendly, provided that creature does not intend to harm or oppose the courtly knight or her allies in the immediate future. Further, whenever she attempts a Diplomacy check to make a request, a courtly knight can first attempt an Intimidate check (DC = 20 + the creature's Charisma modifier). If she succeeds, she gains a +5 bonus on the subsequent Diplomacy check. Neither aspect of imperious attitude applies if the requested creature considers itself to be of an equal or higher social rank than the courtly knight, which includes creatures that don't understand or value the concept of social ranks." replace="Greater tactician"} ::ab[Grand Boast (Ex)]{l=17 icon=power ability="Whenever a courtly knight uses her *challenge* class feature against an opponent who is at full health and under no negative afflictions, conditions, spells, or other effects, she can make a grand boast, declaring that she can defeat her foe with ease. She does not gain the benefits of her *challenge* (including any additional benefits granted by her *order*) when making a grand boast. If she successfully defeats the target of her *challenge* within 1 minute, however, she is vindicated in her boast and gains the benefits of her *challenge* against all allies of the defeated enemy who witnessed her grand boast and who are of the same or lower CR as the defeated enemy." special="If any of the courtly knight's allies attack the initial target of the *challenge* or assist the courtly knight after the boast, this ability has no effect." replace="Master tactician"}

name: Daring General
description: ## Daring General ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/24› Most cavaliers are great tacticians, but some stand above the rest for their ability to lead troops under their command, and inspire them to great accomplishments. Those cavaliers most gifted at command often become daring generals. :::ab{l=6 title="Aides-de-Camp (Ex)" action=Ability head icon=power imp12="The daring general gains an additional cohort (though see Special below) and a number of additional followers equal to the number of followers he gained from the Leadership feat (doubling his followers)." imp18="The daring general gains a third cohort (though see Special below) and a number of additional followers equal to the number of followers he gained from the Leadership feat (ending up with triple the number of followers normally granted by Leadership)." special="All cohorts that the daring general gains from this ability must have levels only in classes that grant a full base attack bonus (such as barbarian, fighter, paladin, or ranger), and must be at least 4 levels lower than the daring general himself. When determining the kinds of cohorts the daring general can attract, he treats his Leadership score as 3 lower for each subsequent cohort (effectively taking a -3 penalty for the second cohort and a -6 penalty for the third cohort)." replace="Bonus feats gained at 6th, 12th, and 18th levels"} A daring general gains a modified version of the ‹feat/Leadership› feat, even if he doesn't meet the prerequisites. All followers that the daring general gains as a result of this version of the Leadership feat can only have levels in the ‹npcclass/warrior› class. Additionally, the daring general can grant special roles to his cohorts, as outlined below. Unless otherwise stated, only one cohort can fill any given role at any given time. Designating a cohort as filling a special role requires a 24-hour ceremonial ritual. Beyond the rules noted above, if the daring general uses his followers to create an army using the ‹rule/mass combat› rules, that army starts with one extra ‹rule/army_>tactic<s› of the daring general's choice and a +2 bonus to its morale score. The daring general can assign each of his followers individually to serve as either footmen or honor guards (described below). He does not need to assign either role to a given follower, if he prefers. He can change the role of a follower at any time, but it takes 1 day per level for the follower to change her tactics to suit her new role. Followers with a particular role must group together with other followers with the same role to form an army in mass combat. ::: ::ab[Groom (Cohort Role)]{next icon=boost ability="The groom cares for the daring general's mount. She does not take an armor check penalty on Ride checks while riding the cavalier's mount. Additionally, once per day, the groom can spend 10 minutes preparing the daring general's mount for battle. If she does, the mount's speed increases by 10 feet and its Dexterity score increases by 2. These benefits last for 1 hour."} ::ab[Squire (Cohort Role)]{next icon=def ability="The squire's main task is to care for the daring general's arms and armor. If the squire aids the daring general in donning his armor, it takes ‹misc/half› as much time to don as it would if someone else aided the daring general. Additionally, when the squire is adjacent to the daring general, as a @HLstandard_action, she can grant a +2 bonus to the daring general's AC against the first attack made against the daring general before the squire's next turn. This counts as an application of the ‹rule/aid another<_2› action, but the squire does not need to threaten the attacker in question."} ::ab[Standard Bearer (Cohort Role)]{next icon=power ability="The daring general's standard bearer can carry his banner in his stead, granting the benefits of his *banner* ability (and later, his *greater banner* ability) to all allies within 60 feet of the standard bearer. If the standard bearer becomes unconscious or dead, she ceases to grant these benefits."} ::ab[Footman (Follower Role)]{next icon=boost-down passive="Each follower gains a +2 bonus on attack and damage rolls, but takes a -2 penalty to her AC and on saving throws. A footman unit gains a +2 bonus to its OM and takes a -2 penalty to its DV in mass combat."} ::ab[Honor Guard (Follower Role)]{next icon=def-down passive="The follower gains a +2 bonus to her AC and on saving throws, but takes a -2 penalty on attack and damage rolls. An honor guard unit gains a +2 bonus to its DV and takes a -2 penalty to its OM in mass combat."} ::ab[Shared Challenge (Ex)]{l=12 icon=power-boost passive="When a daring general issues a *challenge,* his followers and cohorts take up that *challenge* alongside him. Whenever the daring general uses his *challenge* class feature, as long as the *challenge* remains in effect, each of the daring general's followers and cohorts that are within 30 feet of him gain a +4 morale bonus on attack rolls made against the target of his *challenge.*" replace="Demanding challenge"} ::ab[Supreme Tactician (Ex)]{l=20 icon=power ability="At 20th level, whenever the daring general uses his *tactician* ability, he can grant any number of teamwork feats that he knows to his allies, and when he uses his *tactician* ability as a @HLstandard_action in combat, it does not count against his daily uses of *tactician.*" replace="Supreme charge"}

name: Emissary

features.name: In or Out of the Saddle (Ex)

description: ## Emissary ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/36› Cavaliers serve many roles on the battlefield, from bold leaders and shock troops to dashing knights and mounted juggernauts. Some cavaliers, however, focus more on speed and mobility than they do on the raw power of the mounted charge. On foot or in the saddle, the emissary is usually first to meet the enemy, with a pointed lance, a drawn sword, or terms for surrender. ::ab[Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="An emissary does not gain proficiency with heavy armor."} ::ab[Bonus Feats]{icon=power passive="An emissary can select ‹feat/Endurance›, ‹feat/Fleet›, or ‹feat/Run› in addition to the list of combat feats whenever he gains a bonus feat."} ::ab[In or Out of the Saddle (Ex)]{icon=power-boost l=1 ability="An emissary gains ‹feat/Mounted Combat› as a bonus feat. In addition, he can move at normal speed when wearing medium armor." replace=Tactician} ::ab[Battlefield Agility (Ex)]{l=5 icon=power ability="An emissary learns to be more aware of the threats that surround him in combat, and shares this awareness with his loyal steed. Both the emissary and his mount gain ‹feat/Mobility› as a bonus feat." replace=Banner} ::ab[Mounted Acrobatics (Ex)]{l=9 icon=power ability="An emissary is even more adept at hopping on and off his steed, and even dropping alongside its flanks mid-gallop. He gains ‹feat/Trick Riding› as a bonus feat, even if he does not meet the prerequisites. The emissary can employ this feat even when wearing medium armor." replace="Greater tactician"} ::ab[Mounted Dervish (Ex)]{l=14 icon=power-boost ability="An emissary becomes a fearsome, mobile foe on the battlefield. He gains ‹feat/Mounted Skirmisher› as a bonus feat, even if he does not meet the prerequisites. In addition, whenever the emissary is mounted and takes the ‹rule/charge› action, he adds 10 feet to his mount's speed." replace="Greater banner"} ::ab[Erratic Charge (Ex)]{l=20 icon=power ability="An emissary learns to ride through the thick of combat, striking and then moving away with blinding speed. Whenever the emissary is mounted and takes the ‹rule/charge› action, he can first move 10 feet and make a melee attack. This first attack is not a charge, but a regular melee attack, and the movement counts toward the total allowed movement for the round. After making this attack, the emissary must still move in a straight line to reach the target of his charge, and he takes a -5 penalty on the attack roll for the attack at the end of his charge." replace="Supreme charge"}

name: Gendarme
description: ## Gendarme ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/37› The gendarme cares less for the finer points of tactical precision than he does for the exhilaration of the charge: the rush of wind through the visor of his helmet, the feel of his couched lance, the satisfying shriek of armor giving way before his weapon's force as the point drives past metal into his foes. ::ab[Bonus Feats]{icon=power ability="A gendarme trains to be a mounted terror, almost to the exclusion of all other abilities. He gains bonus feats at 1st level, 5th level, and then every three levels thereafter, but must select these bonus feats from the following list: ‹feat/Improved Bull Rush›, ‹feat/Mounted Combat›, ‹feat/Power Attack›, ‹feat/Ride-By Attack›, ‹feat/Spirited Charge›, ‹feat/Spring Attack›, and ‹feat/Unseat›." special="If the gendarme has already selected all of the listed feats, then he may select his bonus feats from those feats listed as ‹main/combat feat«s›." replace="Tactician~greater tactician~master tactician~cavalier bonus feats"} ::ab[Transfixing Charge (Ex)]{l=20 icon=boost passive="A gendarme represents the epitome of mounted combat. Whenever he makes a ‹rule/charge› attack while mounted, he deals triple the normal damage (quadruple if using a ‹eq-weapon/lance›); this damage includes all increases from the Spirited Charge feat and from the use of a lance. In addition, if the gendarme confirms a critical hit on a charge attack while mounted, the attack deals maximum damage for the weapon wielded. Additional damage from weapon properties, magic effects, precision-based bonuses, or other increases are rolled normally." replace="Supreme charge"}

name: Green Knight
description: ## Green Knight ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/44› Some knights serve nature itself and can be found protecting unspoiled natural places or serving fey beings. ::ab[Beast Tongue (Ex)]{l=1 icon=power ability="A green knight can use Diplomacy to improve an animal's attitude. *Beast tongue* otherwise functions like the druid's ‹ability/wild empathy› ability, using the green knight's Diplomacy modifier and using her cavalier level as her effective druid level, and it counts as that ability for the purpose of other effects (such as feat prerequisites or effects that alter or improve *wild empathy*)." replace=Tactician} ::ab[Implacable Knight (Ex)]{icon=power l=1 ability="A green knight gains ‹feat/Endurance› and ‹feat/Diehard› as bonus feats." replace=Mount} ::ab[Nature's Servant (Ex)]{icon=info info="A green knight must select the ‹order/order of the Green›." alter=Order} ::ab[Ferocious (Ex)]{icon=boost-def l3="A green knight is not staggered when below 0 hit points." l9="Taking actions when below 0 hit points does not cause her to lose hit points." replace="Cavalier's charge"} ::ab[Woodland Stride (Ex)]{icon=power l4="A green knight gains the druid's ‹ability/woodland stride› ability." replace="Expert trainer~banner"} ::ab[Stalwart (Ex)]{icon=def l9="Whenever a green knight succeeds at a Fortitude or Will save against an effect that has a reduced effect on a successful save, she instead negates the effect." replace="Greater tactician"} ::ab[Oaken Vitality (Su)]{icon=def flavor="Nature protects a green knight from many afflictions." l11="The green knight becomes immune to disease, ‹rule/infestations›, and poison." replace="Mighty charge~greater banner"} ::ab[Take Their Heads (Su)]{icon=boost flavor="A green knight's blade is blessed by mighty fey powers and unerringly seeks out foes' necks." l17="Any slashing weapon a green knight wields gains the ‹magic-enh/vorpal› weapon special ability." replace="Master tactician"} ::ab[Indestructible (Su)]{icon=boost-def l20="A green knight is virtually impervious to death. She gains a +6 bonus to her Constitution score. In addition, the green knight becomes immune to death effects and to effects that would kill her without reducing her to 0 hit points, unless the effect involves decapitation. If she is decapitated, the green knight can continue to act normally. Reattachment requires the head and body to be joined and the application of any effect that restores hit points." replace="Supreme charge"}

name: Honor Guard
description: ## Honor Guard ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/37› Certain cavaliers are trained not as advance combatants, but as loyal guards, standing as firm defenders in the face of threats to their chosen charge. These honor guards are sometimes merely ornamental, performing their functions on a ceremonial basis, but a surprising number are capable, deadly opponents, able to take down a threat long before their liege knows of the danger. To be an honor guard is to constantly place one's self in harm's way, and to always be willing to lay down one's life at a moment's notice. ::ab[Sworn Defense (Ex)]{l=1 icon=down-def passive="Whenever an honor guard issues a challenge, he can select one ally as his ward for the duration of the challenge. Whenever the honor guard is adjacent to his ward, he takes a -1 penalty to Armor Class, and the ward receives a +1 dodge bonus to AC." alter=Challenge} ::ab[Intercept (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power-def ability="An honor guard learns to better disrupt the attacks of his enemies. He gains ‹feat/Bodyguard› as a bonus feat, even if he does not meet the prerequisite. In addition, whenever the honor guard uses the ‹rule/aid another<_2› action to increase an ally's Armor Class, the bonus to Armor Class granted by the aid another action increases by +1." replace="Cavalier's charge"} ::ab[Warding Charge (Ex)]{l=11 icon=def flavor="An honor guard can flash across the battlefield to protect his ward against the target of his challenge." immediate="Whenever the target of the honor guard's challenge makes an attack against his ward, the honor guard can move up to his speed and make a single melee attack against the target of his challenge. This movement and attack can be made as a ‹rule/charge› if the movement qualifies." replace="Mighty charge"} ::ab[Defensive Challenge (Ex)]{l=12 icon=lower passive="Whenever an honor guard declares a challenge, his target must pay particular attention to him and his ability to intercept attacks. As long as the target is within the threatened area of the cavalier, it takes a -2 penalty on attack rolls against anyone other than the honor guard." replace="Demanding challenge"}

name: Hussar

features.name: Skillful Rider (Ex)
features.replaces: Bonus feats gained at 6th, 12th, and 18th levels

description: ## Hussar ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/25› Agile and maneuverable cavalry, hussars make up for their relatively light armor with their speed and cunning. They are known for doggedly pursuing their foes even in tight spaces, across rooftops, and in other places that mounted cavalry could normally never reach. ::ab[Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="A hussar is proficient with light armor, but not with medium or heavy armor or with shields." replace="The cavalier's normal armor proficiencies"} ::cskill{gain=acro~ea~stl~sur} ::ab[Fast Mount (Ex)]{icon=boost flavor="A hussar is able to spur on any mount that he rides to faster speeds than other riders." passive="The base speed of any creature that the hussar is riding increases by 10 feet, plus an additional 5 feet for every five cavalier levels he possesses. This applies to all forms of movement that the mount possesses." replace="Tactician~banner~greater banner"} ::ab[Skillful Rider (Ex)]{l=6 icon=boost flavor="A hussar and his mount work in tandem to achieve amazing accomplishments of dexterity while riding." passive="As long as the hussar is mounted, whenever he or his mount is required to attempt an Acrobatics, Climb, Escape Artist, Fly, Stealth, or Swim check, he can use his own modifier or his mount's, whichever is higher. Additionally, regardless of whose bonus is used, the hussar gains an additional +2 bonus on all skill checks to overcome obstacles as part of a chase." imp12="The bonus increases to +4." imp18="The bonus increases to +6." replace="Bonus feats gained at 6th, 12th, and 18th levels"} ::ab[Maneuverable Mount (Ex)]{l=9 flavor="A hussar is able to maneuver his mount with exceptional grace and poise, even in areas that would normally be a difficult fit for such a creature." icon=boost-def passive="Any creature that the hussar is riding can ‹misc/squeeze› into a space that is at least half as wide as its normal space without taking the normal penalties on attack rolls and AC for doing so, though it still moves at half speed." special="If the mount attempts to squeeze into a space less than half its space's width, it must use the Escape Artist skill to do so, and takes the normal penalties." replace="Greater tactician"} ::ab[Sudden Swerve (Ex)]{l=17 icon=power flavor="A hussar's control over his mount is advanced enough to allow the mount to turn on the spot, even when charging forward at full speed." ability="Whenever the hussar makes the ‹rule/charge› or ‹rule/run› action while mounted, he can make a single turn of up to 90 degrees at any one point during this movement." replace="Master tactician"}

name: Luring Cavalier
description: ## Luring Cavalier ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/38› Those who study the perfection of strategy and tactics know that picking the battlefield can grant advantages that only overwhelming numbers of allies can eclipse. The luring cavalier is a special type of cavalier that helps accomplish that goal. Typically, he uses a bow or other ranged weapon to lure opponents toward him, and then makes strategic retreats to position his enemies exactly where he wants them. ::ab[Far Challenge (Ex)]{icon=ranged-boost-down useInc=cavalier~3~1 useF="1~1~3" swift="A luring cavalier can use his *far challenge* ability. When he does, the luring cavalier chooses one target within sight to *challenge.* The luring cavalier's ranged attacks deal extra damage whenever the attacks are made against the target of his challenge. This extra damage is equal to the luring cavalier's level." order=uwap ability="Additionally, once per day, the luring cavalier may spend a use of his *far challenge* ability to double the potential extra damage of his ranged attack. Before making the attack roll, he can choose to spend a use of his *challenge* to deal twice his cavalier level in extra damage on a successful hit instead of just his cavalier level in extra damage. If the attack misses, the use of the *challenge* is wasted." passive="Challenging a foe requires subtle deceits and strategies. The cavalier must make it look like he is a soft target. The subject of the far challenge gains a +4 bonus on attack rolls made against him." special="This challenge remains in effect until the target is dead or unconscious, until the target hits the luring cavalier with a melee attack, or until the combat ends. If this challenge ends because the target hits the luring cavalier with a melee attack, this challenge changes to the effects of the normal cavalier *challenge,* and gains any *order* benefit the luring cavalier has." replace=Challenge} ::ab[Careful Aim]{l=3 icon=ranged-boost passive="When a luring cavalier makes a ranged attack with his highest base attack bonus, he can ignore the penalties for firing up to three range increments away. If he is using a firearm, he can target touch AC up to two range increments away." special="This effect stacks with effects that allow the cavalier to make ranged attacks farther without penalty or that allow him to target touch AC with a firearm beyond the first range increment." replace="Cavalier's charge"} ::ab[Infuriating Aim (Ex)]{icon=lower l=11 passive="When a luring cavalier confirms a critical hit with a ranged attack made at his highest base attack bonus against the target of a *far challenge,* the target becomes infuriated for 1 round. While infuriated, the target must spend its turn moving closer to the cavalier, making move, ‹rule/run›, or ‹rule/charge› actions only (challenged creature's choice)." special="This is a mind-affecting effect." replace="Mighty charge"} ::ab[Versatile Challenge (Ex)]{l=12 icon=power ability="A luring cavalier can expend a use of his *challenge* to gain the benefit of *far challenge* or the normal cavalier *challenge.* He can even change the type of *challenge* an opponent is under the effects of as a @HLswift_action, as long as the target of the *challenge* is within line of sight." replace="Demanding challenge"} ::ab[Supreme Aim (Ex)]{l=20 icon=boost passive="The luring cavalier gains the *careful aim* bonus and the effect of *infuriating aim* on all ranged attacks." replace="Supreme charge"}

name: Musketeer
description: ## Musketeer ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/38› Some cavaliers are entrusted by their masters with the care and use of expensive and powerful oddities: firearms. Capable of inflicting shocking amounts of destruction without the aid of magic, these musketeers lead the advance of their troops, firing devastating fusillades long before the enemy can prepare for the armed charge that follows. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down-power info="A musketeer does not gain proficiency in heavy armor. Musketeers are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, and with firearms. A cavalier's levels stack with any fighter levels he possesses for the purpose of meeting the level prerequisite for feats that specifically select a firearm, such as ‹feat/Weapon Specialization›."} ::ab[Gifted Firearm (Ex)]{icon=power-ranged-warning l1="At 1st level, a musketeer is gifted by his order with a firearm (either a ‹eq-weapon/pistol› or a ‹eq-weapon/musket›). This weapon is both a symbol of the cavalier's duty and a focus for much of his talent. He cannot sell this weapon. He also gains the ‹feat/Gunsmithing› feat." l8="When wielding his gifted weapon, as a @HLstandard_action, the mustketeer can focus himself to gain a number of benefits for 1 minute per cavalier level. The musketeer can use this ability twice per day, plus one additional time per day for every four levels beyond 8th. Starting out, the musketeer gains the benefit of the ‹feat/Improved Critical› feat." l11="While focused, he can reduce the misfire chance of his weapon by 1 (to a minimum of 1). This doesn't stack with the similar benefits of ‹magic-enh/reliable› magic weapon special ability." l17="While focused, the musketeer can double the range increment of his weapon. This doesn't stack with the ‹magic-enh/distance› magical ability." l20="During a period of such focus, the musketeer can engage in a flurry of gunfire. The cavalier can expend one of his daily *challenges* to make a ‹rule/full attack› with his firearm. The musketeer ignores the normal load times for his weapon, but must still expend enough doses of powder and enough bullets to complete each attack." special="If the musketeer's gifted firearm is destroyed, the cavalier loses this ability for 30 days while a replacement weapon is crafted for him. During this 30-day period, the musketeer takes a -1 penalty on weapon and damage rolls." replace=Mount} ::ab[Swift Powder (Ex)]{icon=power l4="The musketeer gains ‹feat/Rapid Reload› (musket) or Rapid Reload (pistol) as a bonus feat." l14="Each time the musketeer issues a *challenge,* he may reload a wielded firearm as a @HLfree_action." replace="Expert trainer"}

name: Saurian Champion
description: ## Saurian Champion ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/45› These primeval cavaliers idolize dinosaurs as apex predators and value them as powerful, oversized mounts. ::cskill{gain=acro~kna~per~sur} ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="A saurian champion does not gain proficiency with medium or heavy armor." alter="Weapon and armor proficiencies"} ::ab[Savage Combatant (Ex)]{icon=down info="A saurian champion does not rely on lethal charges or firing from afar as more &quot&civilized&quot& cavaliers do, preferring to rampage among his foes instead. Saurian champions do not deal double damage when ‹rule/charging› with a ‹eq-weapon/lance› (or similar weapon) while mounted. While mounted, a saurian champion cannot attack with ranged weapons other than thrown weapons."} ::ab[Titanic Challenge (Ex)]{icon=down-boost ability="A saurian champion considers only the largest creatures a true challenge. His *titanic challenge* adds only ‹misc/half› his level on damage rolls against Medium or smaller creatures, but he adds a +1 bonus on attack rolls against a target of his *challenge* that is at least two size categories larger than himself (Huge for Medium saurian champions) and a +2 bonus on attack rolls against a Colossal target of his *challenge.*" alter=Challenge} ::ab[Wild Warrior (Ex)]{icon=down info="A saurian champion hails from primeval lands where the civilized orders hold little sway. He does not select an *order* or gain any *order*-related benefits." replace=Order} :::ab{icon=power title="Dinosaur Mount (Ex)" action=Ability alter=Mount replace="Tactician~greater tactician~master tactician"} A saurian champion bonds with a dinosaur companion that willingly serves as his mount. This mount functions as a cavalier's normal mount with the following adjustments: - The saurian champion's mount must be a dinosaur (see ‹ability/druid companions› for all the available options). - The saurian champion can ride mounts of his size category and larger, rather than only those of a larger size. - Increase the mount's Strength score by 8 for the purpose of determining its carrying capacity. - Whenever an ability or feat allows the saurian champion's mount to make a hoof attack, the mount can make a claw or bite attack instead. ::: ::ab[Nimble Rider (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def passive="A saurian champion gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC when mounted. Anything that causes the saurian champion to lose his Dexterity bonus to AC also causes him to lose this dodge bonus." increment="The bonus~2~6"} ::ab[Fierce Devotion (Ex)]{l=5 icon=power ability="A saurian champion's mount gains the *devotion* ability (instead of at 6th level), and its effects also apply against emotion and fear effects. The mount is immune to the effects of ‹umr/unnatural aura›." replace=Banner} ::ab[Quick Rider (Ex)]{l=8 icon=power ability="A saurian champion can attempt ‹skill/Ride› checks to fast mount or fast dismount his mount even if it's more than one size category larger than himself."} ::ab[Titanic Mount (Ex)]{l=10 icon=boost passive="A saurian champion's mount increases in size by one category (even if the base creature normally does not reach that size). The creature receives the appropriate size penalty on attack rolls and to AC (-1 if growing to Large or -2 if growing to Huge) and a -2 penalty to Dexterity (to a minimum Dexterity score of 1), its base damage increases by ‹misc/one size category›, and its reach increases to 10 feet (if it wasn't already). It also gains a +2 size bonus to its Strength and Constitution score." imp12="The bonus to Strength becomes +4 and his mount's natural armor bonus increases by +1." imp14="The Strength bonus becomes +6, the Constitution bonus becomes +4, and the natural armor now increases by +2." imp15="The mount's reach increases to 15 feet." imp16="The Strength bonus becomes +8, and the natural armor now increases by +3." imp18="The Strength bonus becomes +10, the Constitution bonus becomes +6, and the natural armor now increases by +4."} ::ab[Primeval Devotion (Ex)]{l=14 icon=def passive="The bonus on saving throws provided by the mount's *devotion* ability increases by 2. In addition, the mount adds half this bonus to other saving throws." replace="Greater banner"}

name: Standard Bearer
description: ## Standard Bearer ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/39› Not all cavaliers are content to ride at the head of a charge, leading from the front and facing down their enemies directly. Some prefer to stand away from the fray, their banners a beacon shining brightly over the battlefield, rallying their troops to victory. The standard bearer employs the banner of his order, his lord, or his own house to raise the spirits of his allies and warns enemies of impending doom. ::ab[Banner (Ex)]{l=1 icon=power ability="A standard bearer gains the *banner* ability. This ability is identical to the standard cavalier's *banner* ability, except that the morale bonus on saving throws against fear effects is equal to 2 + ‹misc/one-fifth› your cavalier level, and the morale bonus on attack rolls made as part of a charge is equal to 1 + one-fifth your cavalier level." replace=Mount} ::ab[Mount (Ex)]{l=5 icon=power ability="A standard bearer gains the service of a loyal and trusted mount. This mount is identical in all ways to the standard cavalier's mount." replace=Banner} ::ab[Banner of Solace (Ex)]{l=11 icon=boost-def flavor="A standard bearer's banner becomes an even more potent symbol of protection and inspiration to those around him." fullround="Once per day, while his banner is displayed, the standard bearer can wave it through the air, granting all allies within 60 feet ‹rule/temporary hit points› equal to 1/2 his cavalier level, and a +2 morale bonus on their next damage rolls. The temporary hit points last for 10 minutes or until depleted, whichever occurs first." imp15="The morale bonus becomes +3." imp19="The morale bonus becomes +4." replace="Mighty charge"} ::ab[Awesome Pennon (Ex)]{l=20 icon=boost-def flavor="A standard bearer's banner has become a powerful rallying point to his allies, and a bane to his foes." passive="Whenever his banner is visible, allies of the standard bearer within 60 feet gain a +1 morale bonus on attack rolls, immunity to fear effects, and a +3 morale bonus on saving throws against mind-affecting effects." replace="Supreme charge"}

name: Strategist
description: ## Strategist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/39› Some cavaliers make a lifelong mission out of their exceptional ability to direct troops on the battlefield, combining tactical insight with a preternatural skill at improving the teamwork of their allies in order to win the day. Such strategists are masters at learning the strengths and weaknesses of those they fight alongside, and at employing those observations at the most opportune moments. The best of them are also skilled at determining the strengths and weaknesses of their enemies, as well as at countering some of those strengths with their own formidable abilities. ::ab[Tactician (Ex)]{icon=boost l=1 ability="As the cavalier class feature, except that a strategist can use this ability once per day, plus one additional time for every four levels after 1st (to a maximum of five times per day at 17th level)." alter=Tactician} ::ab[Drill Instructor (Ex)]{l=4 icon=power ability="A strategist learns to train his fellow adventurers in the nuances of squad combat. By spending 10 minutes and expending 1 use of his *challenge* ability, the strategist can grant the use of a ‹main/teamwork feat› that he knows to up to four of his allies, similar to the *tactician* ability. As with *tactician,* allies need not meet the prerequisites of the granted feat, but they retain the use of this feat for 10 minutes plus 1 minute for every two levels the cavalier possesses, as long as the cavalier is visible and can be heard by his allies." special="If the cavalier falls unconscious or cannot be both seen and heard, his allies lose the benefit of the granted feat until the condition is remedied." replace="Expert trainer"} ::ab[Tactical Advantage (Ex)]{l=14 icon=power free="Whenever a strategist uses his *tactician* ability to grant the use of a teamwork feat to his allies, he can move up to his speed either before or after granting the feat. This movement provokes attacks of opportunity normally." replace="Greater banner"} ::ab[Strategic Supremacy (Ex)]{l=18 icon=power-lower ability="A strategist gains the ability not only to improve his allies' abilities, but also to disrupt the teamwork of his enemies. Whenever the strategist uses the *tactician* ability, he can choose to cancel out the effects of one teamwork feat employed by any of his opponents within 30 feet instead of granting the use of a teamwork feat to his allies." replace="The cavalier's 18th-level bonus feat"}

name: Cardinal
description: ## Cardinal ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/64› While a cleric's faith is her highest priority, her church may wield significant political power in some regions. In these cases, cardinals arise from the ranks of the clergy, engaging in the game of intrigue on behalf of their churches. While some cardinals manage to join the world of politics and retain the purity of their faith, many cardinals find that they must compromise some part of their beliefs in pursuit of their church's political power, and some cardinals even fall prey to the corrupting influence of their power. ::ab[Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="A cardinal is proficient in light armor, but not shields." replace="Armor proficiencies"} ::ab[Political Skill]{icon=skill-boost-down order=np info="A cardinal adds ‹skill/Bluff› (CHA), ‹skill/Intimidate› (CHA), ‹skill/Knowledge (geography)› (INT), and ‹skill/Knowledge (local)› (INT) to her list of class skills." passive="She gains a number of skill ranks equal to 6 + her Intelligence modifier at each level, instead of the normal 2 + her Intelligence modifier. However, she gains only one domain, and her base attack bonus from cleric levels is equal to ‹misc/half› her class level (which is the same as for a sorcerer or wizard)." replace="Spontaneous casting ability" alter="Domains~class skills~skill ranks per level~base attack bonus"}

name: Cloistered Cleric
description: ## Cloistered Cleric ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/31› Cloistered clerics typically live in a temple and rarely interact with the outside world. They are bookish and well learned in the lore of the faith, paying less attention to its magical and martial aspects. A cloistered cleric has the following class features. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="Cloistered clerics are proficient with light armor and with the following weapons: ‹eq-weapon/club›, ‹eq-weapon/heavy mace›, ‹eq-weapon/light mace›, ‹eq-weapon/quarterstaff›, and ‹eq-weapon/sling›. They are not proficient with shields."} ::cskill{gain=ka~kd~ke~kg~kh~kl~kna~kno~kp~kr post="She gains 4 + Int modifier skill ranks per level."} ::ab[Diminished Spellcasting]{icon=down info="A cloistered cleric chooses only one domain from her deity's list of domains, and her number of non-domain spells per day for each spell level is one less than normal (for example, a 4th-level cloistered cleric has three cantrips, two 1st-level spells, one 1st-level domain spell, one 2nd-level spell, and one 2nd-level domain spell). If this reduces the number of spells per day for that level to 0, she gains only the bonus spells she would be entitled to based on her Wisdom score for that level, plus her domain spell for that level."} ::ab[Breadth of Knowledge]{l=1 icon=boost-power passive="A cloistered cleric gains a bonus on Knowledge skill checks equal to ‹misc/half› her class level (minimum +1) and can make Knowledge skill checks untrained."} ::ab[Well-Read (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost-def passive="A cloistered cleric gains a +2 bonus on skill checks, caster level checks, and saving throws if such rolls pertain to mundane or magical glyphs, runes, scrolls, symbols, and other writings."} ::ab[Verbal Instruction (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost ability="A cloistered cleric can use the ‹rule/aid another› action to assist an ally (or multiple allies) within 30 feet on a skill or ability check. She can instruct a number of allies equal to one-third of her cleric level with the same action. The allies must be able to hear and understand the cleric's instructions. If all allies are not engaged in the same task, using this ability is a @HLfull-round_action rather than a @HLstandard_action."} ::ab[Scribe Scroll (Su)]{icon=power l=4 ability="A cloistered cleric gains ‹feat/Scribe Scroll› as a bonus feat."}

name: Crusader
description: ## Crusader ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/40› Crusaders serve the militant arm of a church, ready to stand guard over the religion's holy places and to be its swift, avenging arm against those who resist its truth. ::ab[Diminished Spellcasting]{icon=down info="A crusader chooses only one domain and gains one fewer spell of each level than normal. If this reduces the number to 0, she may cast spells of that level only if they are domain spells or if her Wisdom allows ‹rule/bonus spells› of that level." alter=Domain~spellcasting} ::ab[Bonus Feat]{icon=power l1="A crusader gains a bonus feat from the following list: ‹feat/Heavy Armor Proficiency›, ‹feat/Improved Shield Bash›, ‹feat/Martial Weapon Proficiency›, ‹feat/Saving Shield›, ‹feat/Shield Focus›, ‹feat/Tower Shield Proficiency›, and ‹feat/Weapon Focus›&#42&." l5="A crusader gains another feat from the list above." l10="A crusader gains another bonus feat, and may also choose from the following feats: ‹feat/Exotic Weapon Proficiency›, ‹feat/Greater Shield Focus›, ‹feat/Greater Weapon Focus›&#42&, ‹feat/Improved Critical›&#42&, ‹feat/Shield Slam›, ‹feat/Shield Specialization›, and ‹feat/Weapon Specialization›&#42&." l15="A crusader gains another bonus feat from either list." l20="A crusader gets a fifth bonus feat from either of the lists above, or either ‹feat/Greater Shield Specialization› or ‹feat/Greater Weapon Specialization›&#42&." info="Bonus feats marked with an asterisk (&#42&) must be applied to the favored weapon of the crusader's deity." special="A crusader need not meet the normal class- or level-based prerequisites for these bonus feats."} ::ab[Legion's Blessing (Su)]{l=8 icon=magic-power flavor="A crusader gains the ability to confer beneficial spells quickly to a large group of allies." fullround="The crusader may confer the effects of a single harmless spell with a range of touch to a number of creatures equal to ‹misc/half› her cleric level. The spell's range remains touch, so all intended recipients must be within the crusader's reach when the spell is cast. Using the *legion's blessing* expends the prepared spell, but it also requires the crusader to sacrifice another prepared spell three levels higher, as when spontaneously using a *cure* or *inflict* spell. The higher-level spell is not cast but is simply lost, its magical energy used to power the legion's blessing."}

name: Divine Strategist
description: ## Divine Strategist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/40› The divine strategist leads the armies of the faithful, not from the front lines but through her clever strategy and tactical acumen. ::ab[Domains]{icon=down info="A divine strategist gains only a single domain."} ::ab[Master Tactician (Ex)]{icon=power-boost-roll order=ap ability="A divine strategist can always act in a surprise round even if she fails to make a Perception check to notice enemies, though she is considered ‹rule/flat-footed› until she acts." passive="The divine strategist gains a bonus on initiative checks equal to ‹misc/half› her cleric level. Allies able to see and hear the divine strategist gain a bonus on initiative checks equal to 1/4 the divine strategist's level. This is a language-dependent ability." imp20="A divine strategist's initiative roll is automatically a natural 20." replace="Channel energy"} ::ab[Caster Support (Su)]{icon=boost-def ability="A divine strategist can use the ‹rule/aid another<_2› action to assist another divine spellcaster, granting a circumstance bonus on caster level checks and ‹rule/concentration› checks until the beginning of the divine strategist's next turn. @B-4f2-cleric-x." special="The allied caster must remain adjacent to the divine strategist to gain this benefit. Caster support can be used to assist arcane spellcasters or characters using magical items, but they gain only half the normal bonus."} ::ab[Tactical Expertise (Ex)]{l=8 icon=boost order=pw flavor="A divine strategist knows how to take best advantage of tactical opportunities." passive="Whenever she is ‹rule/flanking› or makes an attack of opportunity, she may add her Intelligence bonus (if any) as a bonus on the attack roll." swift="Once per day she may add her Intelligence modifier as a bonus on any single d20 roll made as part of a ‹rule/readied action›. She can use this ability one additional time per day for every two levels after 8th."}

name: Evangelist
description: ## Evangelist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/40› The evangelist is the voice of her religion in the world. Where others nurture the faith among believers, an evangelist proclaims the coming glory of her deific patron and issues the clarion call to all around to heed the truth, or obey the call to war and crusade against the enemies of the church. ::ab[Single-Minded]{icon=down info="An evangelist focuses her skills and learning on proclamation rather than the fine details of the church's deeper mysteries or martial training. Thus, she may select only one domain and does not gain Medium Armor Proficiency or Shield Proficiency."} ::ab[Public Speaker]{icon=skill-boost passive="An evangelist gains ‹skill/Perform› (CHA) as a class skill. In addition, she is trained to project her voice with great skill and effect; the DC to hear her speak in difficult conditions is reduced by an amount equal to her class level plus her Charisma modifier (minimum 0)."} ::ab[Sermonic Performance]{icon=power l=1 ability="An evangelist gains the ability to deliver a select number of supernatural and spell-like performances through the force and power of her divinely inspired preaching and exhortation. This ability is similar in all respects to ‹ability/bardic performance› as used by a bard of the same level (including interactions with feats, spells, and prestige classes), using Perform (oratory) as the evangelist's performance skill. However, an evangelist gains only the following types of bardic performance: ‹performance/countersong›, ‹performance/fascinate›, and ‹performance/inspire courage›." imp9="The evangelist learns the ‹performance/inspire greatness› performance." imp15="The evangelist learns the ‹performance/inspire heroics› performance." special="Due to what this replaces, the cleric does not get *channel energy* until 3rd level, and her damage maxes out at 7d6 points at 19th level." replace="The 1st-, 9th-, and 15th-level channel energy abilities"} ::ab[Spontaneous Casting]{icon=magic info="An evangelist does not gain the ability to spontaneously cast *cure* or *inflict* spells by sacrificing prepared spells. However, an evangelist can spontaneously cast the following spells by sacrificing a prepared spell of the noted level or above." alter="Spontaneous casting" s1=Command s2=Enthrall s3=Tongues s4=Suggestion s5="Greater command" s6="Geas/quest" s7="Mass suggestion" s8=Sympathy s9=Demand}

name: Merciful Healer
description: ## Merciful Healer ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/41› The merciful healer is a master of battlefield revivification, sustaining and restoring allies to keep them in the fight. ::ab[Willing Healer]{icon=down info="A merciful healer must choose the ‹domain/Healing› domain. She does not gain a second domain. If the cleric worships a deity, that deity must be one that grants the Healing domain."} ::ab[Channel Energy (Su)]{l=1 icon=power ability="As the cleric ability, save that a merciful healer must channel positive energy, and when she does, she cannot choose to target undead. This ability is otherwise identical to the cleric ability of the same name." replace="Channel energy"} ::ab[Combat Medic (Ex)]{icon=def passive="A merciful healer does not provoke attacks of opportunity when using the Heal skill to stabilize another creature or casting healing spells."} ::ab[Merciful Healing (Su)]{icon=power-aid l3="A merciful healer can channel positive energy to relieve one or more harmful conditions. The merciful healer chooses one of the following harmful conditions: ‹misc/fatigued›, ‹misc/shaken›, or ‹misc/sickened›. When the merciful healer channels energy she can remove the chosen condition from one living creature that she heals within her channel energy burst." l6="She can choose another condition. It can be one of those she didn't choose at 3rd level, or one of the following conditions: ‹misc/dazed›, diseased, or ‹misc/staggered›. She can remove either selected condition from up to two creatures within her channel energy burst." l9="She gains another condition, and can choose an above condition or one of the following conditions: cursed, ‹misc/exhausted›, ‹misc/frightened›, ‹misc/nauseated›, or poisoned. She can remove that condition, or a condition she previously chose, from one or two creatures within the burst." l12="She can choose a lower-level condition or one of the following conditions: ‹misc/blinded›, ‹misc/deafened›, ‹rule/paralyzed›, or ‹misc/stunned›. She can remove that condition or one she previously chose from one, two, or three creatures within her channel energy burst." special="Feats and effects that affect a paladin's ‹ability/mercy› also affect this ability."} ::ab[True Healer (Su)]{l=8 icon=power-roll ability="When a merciful healer channels holy energy, she can choose to apply the benefits of *merciful healing* or to reroll any 1s when determining how much damage she heals with the holy energy. She must choose which benefit to take before she rolls to see how much damage she heals."}

name: Separatist
description: ## Separatist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/32› A radical cleric, unsatisfied with the orthodoxy of her deity's teachings, forges her own path of defiant divine expression. Though most members of her faith would call her a separatist or heretic, she continues to receive spells from her deity. Charismatic separatists may develop a large following of like-minded believers and eventually found a splinter church of their deity - and they are just as likely to be the cause of a holy civil war as the branches of the religion fight to determine which is the true faith. ::prereq{other="Must worship a deity."} ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="Separatists do not gain proficiency in their deity's favored weapon (though they are not prohibited from using it or learning its use)."} ::ab[Forbidden Rites]{icon=down-power choice="A separatist selects one domain from her deity's domain list, and a second domain that is not on her deity's domain list. This second domain cannot be an alignment domain that doesn't match the cleric's or her deity's alignment. For example, a lawful good separatist cleric of a neutral good deity cannot choose the ‹domain/Chaos› or ‹domain/Evil› domain with this ability, but can select the ‹domain/Law› domain even though her deity isn't lawful." passive="Granted powers from the cleric's second domain function as if the cleric's level, Wisdom, and Charisma were 2 lower than normal (minimum level 1) in terms of effect, DC, and uses per day. This also means the separatist doesn't gain the domain's higher-level ability until 2 levels later than normal. If the second domain grants additional class skills, the separatist gains these as normal. In all other respects, this ability works like the standard cleric's domain ability." replace=Domains order=cp}

name: Theologian
description: ## Theologian ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/32› A theologian is an expert on one particular area of her religion. She is so focused on that area that she eschews the broader sweep of her deity's dogma and focuses intensely upon that aspect of it, embodying its power in all she does. Theologians tend to be more zealous than other clerics, and many crusades are started by theologians. A theologian has the following class features. :::ab{icon=down-boost-magic title="Focused Domain" action=Ability replace=Domains} A theologian chooses only one domain from her deity's portfolio rather than the normal two domains. All level-dependent effects of the granted powers from the theologian's domain function as if she were two cleric levels higher than her actual cleric level. This does not allow her to gain domain-granted powers earlier than normal. A theologian can prepare domain spells using her non-domain slots. She cannot use her spontaneous casting ability on domain spells, even if they are prepared in non-domain slots. In all other respects, this works like and replaces the standard cleric domain ability. ::: ::ab[Domain Secret (Ex)]{l=5 icon=boost-magic choice="The theologian chooses one domain spell. That spell becomes permanently modified with one of the following metamagic feats: ‹feat/Bouncing Spell›, ‹feat/Disruptive Spell›, ‹feat/Ectoplasmic Spell›, ‹feat/Enlarge Spell›, ‹feat/Extend Spell›, ‹feat/Focused Spell›, ‹feat/Intensified Spell›, ‹feat/Silent Spell›, ‹feat/Still Spell›. This metamagic feat does not increase the level of the spell. Once chosen, this modification cannot be changed. The domain specialist need not have the metamagic feat to apply it to a spell using this ability." imp10="The domain specialist may choose an additional domain spell to modify in this way. She cannot modify the same spell more than once." repeat="The domain specialist may choose an additional domain spell to modify in this way, following the restrictions above.~15~5"}

name: Undead Lord
prerequisites: other="Deity's portfolio must include the Death domain, or a similar domain that promotes undeath."
description: ## Undead Lord ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/32› An undead lord is a cleric focused on using necromancy to control undead. Her flock is the walking dead and her choir the keening spirits of the damned. This unliving congregation is the manifestation of her unceasing love affair with death. ::prereq{other="Deity's portfolio must include the Death domain, or a similar domain that promotes undeath."} ::ab[Death Magic]{icon=down info="An undead lord must select the ‹domain/Death› domain (and the ‹domain/Undead› subdomain, if available in the campaign). She does not gain a second domain. In all other respects, this works like the standard cleric's domain ability." replace=Domains} ::ab[Corpse Companion (Su)]{icon=power ability="With a ritual requiring 8 hours, an undead lord can animate a single ‹template/skeleton› or ‹template/zombie› whose Hit Dice do not exceed her cleric level. This corpse companion automatically follows her commands and does not need to be controlled by her. She cannot have more than one corpse companion at a time. It does not count against the number of Hit Dice of undead controlled by other methods. She can use this ability to create a variant skeleton such as a bloody or burning skeleton, but its Hit Dice cannot exceed ‹misc/half› her cleric level. She can dismiss her companion as a @HLstandard_action, which destroys it."} ::ab[Bonus Feats]{icon=power l1="All undead lords gain ‹feat/Command Undead› as a bonus feat." l10="She may select one of the following as a bonus feat: ‹feat/Channel Smite›, ‹feat/Extra Channel›, ‹feat/Improved Channel›, ‹feat/Quick Channel›, ‹feat/Skeleton Summoner›, ‹feat/Undead Master›."} ::ab[Unlife Healer (Su)]{icon=aid l8="The undead lord's spells, spell-like abilities, and supernatural abilities used to heal undead heal an extra 50% damage." l16="These effects automatically heal the maximum possible damage for the effect + the extra 50%. This does not stack with abilities or feats such as ‹feat/Empower Spell› or ‹feat/Maximize Spell›."}

name: Aerie Protector
description: ## Aerie Protector ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/47› The aerie protector guards nature's nests and lairs in the highest mountains, and she is only ever truly at ease when under vast expanses of open sky. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="Aerie protectors are proficient with ‹eq-weapon/javelin«s› and ‹eq-weapon/shortbow«s› but not with scimitars or scythes. Aerie protectors are not proficient with medium armor." alter="Weapon and armor proficiency"} :::ab{title="Nature Bond" icon=info action=Choice alter="Nature bond"} If the aerie protector chooses an animal companion as her nature bond, she must choose an animal with a fly speed. She can use spells or other effects to alter her companion's fly speed, but it must be able to fly on its own before it becomes her companion.
