Alternatively, the ranger can polymorph into the form of an eagle or similar raptor as if the caster of *beast shape IV.*"} ::ab[Form of the Jackal]{next icon=def-magic ability="The ranger becomes thin and hyperactive, his movements taking on a nervous spryness. While in this form, the ranger does not provoke attacks of opportunity due to movement. Alternatively, the ranger can polymorph into the form of a jackal or other canine creature as if the caster of *beast shape IV.*"} ::ab[Form of the Otter]{next icon=power-boost-magic ability="The ranger's hands and feet grow webs, and his body grows an oily fur that is water resistant. While in this form, the ranger gains a swim speed of 60 feet and a +5 bonus on Swim checks. Alternatively, the ranger can polymorph into the form of an otter or similar river mammal as if the caster of *beast shape IV.*"}

name: Skirmisher
description: ## Skirmisher ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/128› Many rangers rely on spells, but there are some who eschew aid from divine powers for their own reasons. Skirmishers rely on their wits, their wisdom, and sometimes even instinct to aid in their quests. A skirmisher has the following class features. ::ab[Hunter's Tricks]{head icon=power flavor="A skirmisher ranger learns the use of *hunter's tricks,* which typically grant a boon or bonus to the ranger or a nearby ally." l5="The ranger learns one trick, selected from the list below." incrementOrd="He learns~7~2" incrementDesc=his incrementEnd=" trick." usage="A number of times per day equal to 1/2 his ranger level + his Wisdom modifier" special="Tricks are usually @HLswift_actions, but sometimes @HLmove or @HLfree actions that modify a @HLstandard_action, usually an attack action. Once a trick is chosen, it can't be retrained. A ranger cannot select an individual trick more than once." replace="Spellcasting ability"} ::ab[Aiding Attack (Ex)]{next icon=boost free="The ranger can use this trick when he hits a creature with an attack. The next ally who makes an attack against the target creature before the start of the ranger's next turn gains a +2 circumstance bonus on that attack roll."} ::ab[Bolster Companion (Ex)]{next icon=protect immediate="The ranger can use this trick when his animal companion is hit with an attack or a combat maneuver. The companion's AC and combat maneuver defense increase by +4 for the purposes of that attack. If the attack still hits, the animal companion only takes half damage (if any). The animal companion must be able to see and hear the ranger to benefit from this trick."} ::ab[Catfall (Ex)]{next icon=def immediate="The ranger can use this trick when he falls 20 or more feet, ignoring the first 20 feet of the fall when calculating the ‹rule/falling« damage›. If the ranger takes no damage from the fall, he does not fall prone."} ::ab[Chameleon Step (Ex)]{next icon=power-boost move="The ranger can move up to twice his speed. The ranger does not take any penalty on Stealth checks for movement during this move. This move provokes attacks of opportunity as normal."} ::ab[Cunning Pantomime (Ex)]{next icon=power standard="The ranger can communicate with a single creature as if using the ‹spell/tongues› spell for 10 minutes. Because the communication is slow and lacks subtlety, the ranger suffers a -4 penalty on all Bluff and Diplomacy checks relating to the creature he is communicating with when using this trick."} ::ab[Defensive Bow Stance (Ex)]{next icon=def swift="Until the start of his next turn, the ranger's ranged attacks do not provoke attacks of opportunity."} ::ab[Deft Stand (Ex)]{next icon=def move="The ranger can spend a move action to stand up without provoking attacks of opportunity."} ::ab[Distracting Attack (Ex)]{next icon=lower free="The ranger can use this trick before he makes an attack. If the attack hits, the target takes a -2 penalty on all attack rolls for 1 round."} ::ab[Hateful Attack (Ex)]{next icon=boost free="The ranger can use this trick when he makes an attack against one of his *favored enemies.* The ranger doubles the threat range of his weapon for this attack. This does not stack with other abilities that increase a weapon's threat range."} ::ab[Heel (Ex)]{next icon=protect immediate="The ranger can use this trick when his animal companion moves. When the companion moves, the square it starts out in is not considered threatened by any opponent it can see, and therefore visible enemies do not get attacks of opportunity against it when it moves from that square. The companion must end this movement in a square adjacent to the ranger. The animal companion must be able to see and hear the ranger to take this movement."} ::ab[Hobbling Attack (Ex)]{next icon=lower free="The ranger can use this trick when he hits with an attack. The target of the attack's land speed is reduced by 1/2 for 1d4 rounds."} ::ab[Quick Climb (Ex)]{next icon=boost move="The ranger can climb at his full speed without penalty."} ::ab[Quick Healing (Ex)]{next icon=aid swift="The ranger can make a Heal check to administer first aid on an adjacent dying character." move="Alternatively, the ranger can administer a potion to an unconscious character." order=wm} ::ab[Quick Swim (Ex)]{next icon=boost move="The ranger can swim at his full speed without penalty."} ::ab[Ranger's Counsel (Ex)]{next icon=boost swift="The ranger can grant all allies within 30 feet that are within line of sight and can hear him a +2 bonus on skill checks with a single skill of his choice. The ranger must have at least one rank in the chosen skill. This bonus lasts for 1 round."} ::ab[Rattling Strike (Ex)]{next icon=lower free="The ranger can use this trick before he makes a melee attack. If the attack hits, the target is shaken for 1d4 rounds."} ::ab[Second Chance Strike (Ex)]{next icon=roll immediate="When he misses with a melee attack, the ranger may reroll his attack at a -5 penalty."} ::ab[Sic-Em (Ex)]{next icon=power swift="The ranger's animal companion makes one melee attack against an adjacent creature. The animal companion must be able to see and hear the ranger to make this attack."} ::ab[Skill Sage (Ex)]{next icon=roll free="The ranger can roll twice on any one skill check and take the better result. He must have at least 1 rank in that skill to use this ability."} ::ab[Stag's Leap (Ex)]{next icon=power free="The ranger can attempt a running jump without moving 10 feet before the jump."} ::ab[Surprise Shift (Ex)]{next icon=power swift="The ranger can move 5 feet. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity and does not count as a 5-foot step."} ::ab[Tangling Attack (Ex)]{next icon=lower free="The ranger can use this attack when he makes an attack. If the attack hits, the target is entangled for 1 round."} ::ab[Trick Shot (Ex)]{next icon=ranged standard="The ranger can make a ranged attack that ignores ‹rule/concealment› (but not total concealment), soft ‹rule/cover›, and partial cover."} ::ab[Uncanny Senses (Ex)]{next icon=boost immediate="The ranger gains a +10 insight bonus on Perception checks for 1 round."} ::ab[Upending Strike (Ex)]{next icon=power free="The ranger can use this trick just before he makes a melee attack. If the attack hits, he may make a free ‹rule/trip› combat maneuver against the target."} ::ab[Vengeance Strike (Ex)]{next icon=power immediate="The ranger can use this trick when an enemy adjacent to him hits an ally with a melee or ranged attack. The ranger can make a single melee attack at his highest base attack bonus against the creature who attacked his ally."}

name: Spirit Ranger
description: ## Spirit Ranger ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/129› Some rangers nurture a connection with the spirits that reside in all things. By communing with these spirits, the spirit ranger can gain glimpses of things to come. A spirit ranger has the following class features. ::ab[Spirit Bond (Ex)]{l=4 icon=magic ability="Instead of forming a bond with his hunting companions or an animal companion, the spirit ranger forms a bond with the spirits of nature themselves. Each day, as long as he is within one of his *favored terrains,* the ranger can cast ‹spell/augury› as a spell-like ability with a caster level equal to his ranger level." order=a2 ability2="In addition, he can call upon these spirits to cast any one ranger spell that he is capable of casting, without having to prepare the spell." incrementOrd="He can cast~8~4" incrementDesc=a incrementEnd=" additional spell in this way." replace="Hunter's bond"} ::ab[Wisdom of the Spirits (Sp)]{l=12 icon=boost ability="The spirit ranger can use his *augury* spell-like ability even when he is not in one of his *favored terrains.* If he is within one of his *favored terrains,* the ranger can cast ‹spell/divination› instead. Like *augury,* the caster level of the divination is equal to the ranger's level." replace=Camouflage}

name: Stormwalker
description: ## Stormwalker ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/72› Rangers who walk in the tempest unafraid draw the power of the storm into themselves and become stormwalkers. ::ab[Combat Style Feat (Ex)]{l=2 icon=down ability="A stormwalker must choose the archery ‹ability/combat style<s›." alter="Combat style"} ::ab[Thundershot (Su)]{l=4 icon=boost flavor="A stormwalker can wreathe his weapon in lightning." standard="He can grant a single weapon he holds the ‹magic-enh/shock› special ability for 1 minute; while under this effect, the weapon counts as magic for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction." useMod=Wisdom3 imp12="Weapons affected by this ability gain the ‹magic-enh/shocking burst› special ability, instead." replace="Hunter's bond"} ::ab[Wind Treader (Ex)]{l=8 icon=def-boost passive="A stormwalker becomes immune to the effects of strong ‹rule/wind<s›. He can move without hindrance in windy conditions, and his ranged attacks take no penalties from nonmagical wind." replace="Swift tracker"} ::ab[Flash Step (Su)]{l=11 icon=power-ranged flavor="A stormwalker can move across the battlefield like a bolt of lightning." fullround="He can transform into lightning and move to any unoccupied square within 60 feet without provoking attacks of opportunity. He can make a single ranged attack before or after this movement." replace=Quarry} ::ab[Control Weather (Sp)]{l=16 icon=magic ability="A stormwalker can cast ‹spell/control weather› as a spell-like ability once per day." replace="Improved evasion"} ::ab[Flash Shot (Su)]{l=19 icon=ranged ability="When a stormwalker uses *flash step,* he can make a ranged attack both before and after his movement. Both of these attacks are made at his highest base attack bonus." replace="Improved quarry"}

name: Summit Sentinel
description: ## Summit Sentinel ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/72› Some rangers eschew the path of the swift skirmisher and embrace the implacable strength of the mountain. ::ab[Roots of the Mountain (Su)]{l=2 icon=power-def ability="A summit sentinel gains ‹feat/Toughness› as a bonus feat." move="She can enter a defensive stance for 1 minute. While in this stance, the summit sentinel's speed is reduced to 5 feet, she gains a +2 enhancement bonus to her natural armor, and she gains a +2 bonus to her CMD against maneuvers that would move her or knock her prone. If the ranger loses contact with the ground or other solid surface, the stance ends immediately." useMod=Constitution3 order=amu incrementMulti="The enhancement bonus to natural armor increases to +~ and the bonus to CMD becomes +~.~2/4;3/1;4/2" replace="Combat style feats"} ::ab[Mountain Mastery (Ex)]{l=3 icon=down info="A summit sentinel must select mountains as her *favored terrain,* and she does not gain additional *favored terrains* at higher levels." increment="The bonus from this *favored terrain*~5~5~4~2" imp8="A summit sentinel draws strength from the earth. When she and her target are both in contact with the ground or an earthen floor, the summit sentinel gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls against the target." imp18="The bonus on attack and damage rolls increases to +2." alter="Favored terrain"} ::ab[Spells]{icon=learn ability="A summit sentinel adds ‹spell/stoneskin› to the ranger spell list as a 4th-level spell." alter=Spells} ::ab[Rockslide (Su)]{l=8 icon=cone standard="Once per day, a summit sentinel can create a rushing wave of earth and stone. The summit sentinel chooses a point on the ground or floor within 30 feet. Rippling waves of earth and stone emanate from the chosen point in a 25-foot cone in a direction of the summit sentinel's choice. Each creature in the area takes 4d6 points of bludgeoning damage and is pushed to the end of the cone. A target that succeeds at a Reflex save (DC = 10 + half the ranger's level + the ranger's Wisdom modifier) takes half damage and is not pushed." replace="Swift tracker"} ::ab[Invincible (Su)]{l=17 icon=def flavor="A summit sentinel takes on the unyielding hardness of the mountains." passive="While in her *roots of the mountain* defensive stance, she is immune to critical hits and ‹misc/precision damage›." replace="Hide in plain sight"}

name: Tidal Hunter
description: ## Tidal Hunter ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/73› The tidal hunter draws strength from the fish and other wildlife of the deep. ::ab[Waterborn (Su)]{icon=power ability="A tidal hunter can breathe water for up to 10 minutes per ranger level each day." imp6="He can breathe underwater indefinitely." replace="Wild empathy~6th-level combat style feat"} ::ab[Keen Scent (Ex)]{icon=power ability="A tidal hunter gains ‹umr/scent› as per the universal monster rule." imp12="While in water, the tidal hunter can detect particularly strong or distinct odors (such as blood) up to 1 mile away." replace=Track~camouflage} ::ab[Aquatic Mastery (Ex)]{icon=down l3="A tidal hunter must select water as his *favored terrain,* and he doesn't gain additional *favored terrains.*" repeat="The bonus from this *favored terrain* increases by 2.~8~5" alter="Favored terrain"} ::ab[Wave Rush (Ex)]{l=7 icon=power ability="A tidal hunter gains a swim speed equal to his base speed. If he already has a swim speed, it increases by 10 feet." replace="Woodland stride"} ::ab[Tidal Surge (Sp)]{l=16 icon=magic flavor="A tidal hunter gains control over water, and he can use the tides to attack his foes." ability="Once per day, he can cast ‹spell/tidal surge› as a spell-like ability." replace="Improved evasion"}

name: Toxic Herbalist
description: ## Toxic Herbalist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/74› Saviors and destroyers in equal measure, toxic herbalists use nature's bounty to craft remedies and poisons. ::ab[Toxic Touch (Ex)]{icon=def passive="A toxic herbalist studies the safe handling of deadly substances. He cannot accidentally poison himself when he applies poison to a weapon." replace="Wild empathy"} ::ab[Nature's Mercy (Ex and Su)]{l=3 icon=power-aid order=a2 flavor="A toxic herbalist's knowledge of the natural world offers respite from wounds and illness." ability="Once per day, he can spend 1 hour in a wilderness area gathering herbs and other natural materials and combine them into a medicinal poultice - this hour can be integrated with the hour required for the ranger to prepare spells." ability2="Placing the poultice on a wound or ingesting it is a @HLstandard_action; the creature receiving the poultice heals a number of hit points equal to 1d6 + the ranger's Wisdom modifier." incrementPlain="The ranger can now~3~8" incrementDesc=create incrementEnd=" poultices per day." imp8="A poultice neutralizes one poison affecting the recipient, as per ‹spell/neutralize poison›." imp13="A poultice also attempts to cure one disease affecting the recipient, as per ‹spell/remove disease›." special="The caster level of the neutralizing/curing effects is equal to the toxic herbalist's level. These additional effects are supernatural effects." replace=Endurance} ::ab[Sudden Onset (Ex)]{l=4 icon=boost-learn swift="A toxic herbalist can administer a poultice he created via *nature's mercy* or poison a weapon as a swift action." order=wn info="Additionally, the toxic herbalist adds the following spells to the ranger spell list at the indicated spell levels." s1="Nauseating dart~ray of sickening" s2="Pernicious poison~pox pustules" s3="Poison~toxic gift" s4="Absorb toxicity~cloudkill" replace="Hunter's bond"} ::ab[Grim Harvest (Ex)]{l=8 icon=power ability="A toxic herbalist can spend 1 hour foraging for poisonous substances to create a dose of poison (this hour can be integrated with the hour required to prepare spells or poultices). The toxic herbalist rolls 1d20 and adds his ranger level and his Intelligence modifier. The DC of this check is equal to the Craft DC of the poison he wishes to create. If he succeeds at this check, the ranger creates 1 dose of the chosen poison. The poison remains potent for a number of hours equal to the toxic herbalist's level, regardless of the means used in attempts to preserve it, and it can't be sold." special="This ability functions only while the toxic herbalist is within one of his *favored terrains.*" replace="Swift tracker"} ::ab[Potent Venom (Ex)]{l=11 icon=boost flavor="A toxic herbalist's poisons become even deadlier." ability="When he poisons a *favored enemy,* the DC of the poison's saving throw increases by half the toxic herbalist's *favored enemy* bonus against that target." replace=Quarry} ::ab[Poisonous Reaper (Ex)]{l=19 icon=boost passive="A single dose of poison on a toxic herbalist's weapon remains potent for the entirety of a full attack, instead of for a single strike." replace="Improved quarry"}

name: Transporter
description: ## Transporter ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/43› Transporters specialize in smuggling people as efficiently as possible through harsh and difficult environments. Individuals such as escaped political exiles, refugees fleeing danger, and various criminals all seek the transporter's services. While some transporters actively work to serve justice or a political cause, others are wily opportunists filling a need and profiting from the high price that desperate people are willing to pay for safe, discrete passage. ::ab[Trailbreaker (Ex)]{icon=boost flavor="A transporter constantly works to obscure his trail." passive="He increases the Survival DC to track him, or a group of which he is a part, by an amount equal to half his ranger level (minimum 1). This does not stack with similar abilities, such as a ‹arc-inquisitor/traceless operative«'s› *trackless* ability." replace="Wild empathy"} ::ab[Plot Course (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power-boost ability="A transporter can spend 1d4 hours and attempt a DC 15 Knowledge (geography) check to plot a subtle course of travel between his current location and another destination. The transporter's course of travel is almost never direct, as it is optimized for smuggling. Thereafter, the transporter gains a +2 bonus on initiative, Knowledge (geography), Perception, Stealth, and Survival checks involving traveling along his plotted course." incrementMulti="If the transporter's Knowledge (geography) check exceeds the DC by ~, the bonuses increase to +~.~3/5;10/10;4/2" replace="Favored terrain" special="A transporter can gain the benefits of only a single plotted course at any given time. If the transporter ever strays from the course or attempts to plot a new course for any reason, he loses the benefits of his current course immediately. A transporter can retry his Knowledge (geography) check to plot a course as long as he spends 1d4 hours each time."} ::ab[Smuggler's Bond (Ex)]{l=4 icon=down-boost order=np info="A transporter must choose his allies as his *hunter's bond,* not an animal companion." passive="Instead of granting the transporter's *favored enemy* bonus to his allies as a move action, he instead grants his *plot course* bonus to his allies constantly." alter="Hunter's bond"} ::ab[Hideaway (Ex)]{icon=power ability="A transporter@FN1 can spend 1 hour and attempt a DC 20 Survival check to create a hidden shelter, useful for staying unseen by patrols of enemy creatures. The transporter's shelter can hold the transporter and one additional creature for every 2 by which the transporter exceeds the DC. The created shelter incorporates scents from the local area, preventing creatures on the inside from being detected by the ‹umr/scent› ability of creatures outside of the shelter, and vice versa. Additionally, its floor is either elevated or constructed of a different substance than the nearby ground, preventing creatures outside of the shelter from using ‹umr/tremorsense› to detect creatures inside, and vice versa. Finally, the clever structure of the hideaway causes creatures outside of the shelter to take a -10 penalty on Perception checks to notice creatures inside, as if through a 1-foot-thick wall, while only causing creatures inside to take a -2 penalty on Perception checks to notice creatures outside." special="These bonuses do not apply if the enemy creatures are intimately familiar with the area in which the hideaway was built (such as an area right near their home)." replace="Woodland stride"} :::fakeFootnotes @FN[There is no listed level at which this ability is granted. Given that it replaces a 7th-level ability, the intention was probably that this ability would also be gained at 7th level. Consult your GM.]{from=1} :::

name: Trapper
description: ## Trapper ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/65› A trapper is a ranger who focuses exclusively on traps, rather than learning conventional magic. A trapper has the following class features. ::cskill{gain=dd} ::ab[Trapfinding]{icon=boost-power passive="A trapper adds 1/2 her ranger level on Perception skill checks made to locate traps and on Disable Device skill checks (minimum +1)." order=pa ability="A trapper can use Disable Device to disarm magic traps."} ::ab[Trap]{icon=power l5="A trapper learns how to create a ‹rangertrap/snare trap› and one other ‹ability/ranger trap<s› of her choice." repeat="She learns another trap.~7~2" special="The trapper can use these traps a total number of times per day equal to 1/2 her ranger level + her Wisdom modifier. Once a trap is learned, it can't be unlearned and replaced with a different type of trap. The trapper cannot select an individual trap more than once." replace="Spellcasting ability"} ::ab[Launch Trap]{l=10 icon=ranged ability="A trapper can affix a magical ranger trap to an arrow, crossbow bolt, or thrown weapon, allowing her to set the trap remotely or use it as a direct attack. Attaching the trap to the projectile is part of the @HLfull-round_action of creating a new trap. The trapped projectile is fired or thrown in the normal manner. If fired at a square, the trap is treated as if the ranger had set the trap in that square, except the DC is 5 lower than normal. If fired at a creature, the target takes damage from the ranged weapon and is treated as if it had triggered the trap (saving throw applies, if any). The attack has a maximum range of 60 feet, and range increments apply to the attack roll." special="The duration of the trapped projectile starts from when it is created, not from when it is used."}

name: Trophy Hunter
description: ## Trophy Hunter ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/67› Some rangers have taken up the mysteries of black powder in order to become big game hunters. Finding firearms useful for taking down large and dangerous prey, they enter the fight with the crack of black powder fire, often ranging far and wide in their safaris and searches for ever-more-dangerous denizens of the wild to track, study, appreciate - and kill. While this might strike some as going against the ranger's usual respect for nature and the creatures of the wild, trophy hunters understand that they are just more pieces in nature's grand puzzle, and that the laws of the jungle - the right to kill and feed on those weaker than you, and the need to establish dominance through cunning and bloodshed - are both their rights and their duty as the current top of the food chain. ::ab[Improved Tracking (Ex)]{l=1 icon=boost-power ability="A trophy hunter gains a +2 bonus on Survival skill checks when following or identifying tracks. When he tracks, he can also attempt a Knowledge (nature) check at DC 15. On a success, the trophy hunter can discern the type and condition of any animals or magical beasts he tracks. By studying their tracks, the trophy hunter is able to identify a rough approximation of their health, maneuverability, and their general behavior as compared to the norm." replace="Wild empathy"} ::ab[Firearm Style]{l=2 icon=power ability="A trophy hunter gains the ‹feat/Amateur Gunslinger› feat and ‹feat/Exotic Weapon Proficiency› (firearms), and can use any 1st-level ‹ability/gunslinger deed<s›." repeat="The trophy hunter can take a ‹main/grit feat› or select a gunslinger deed of his level or lower, ranger's choice.~6~4" replace="All combat style feats"} ::ab[Hunter's Aim (Ex)]{l=4 icon=zap flavor="A trophy hunter gains a specific understanding of the weaknesses and vulnerabilities of his *favored enemies,* and his careful study of these enemies reveals the best way to hurt them." ability="When the trophy hunter makes a firearm attack against a *favored enemy,* he can target touch AC in the first two range increments of his firearm." special="This ability stacks with other effects that increase the range increments to target touch AC, adding one range increment to the effect." replace="Hunter's bond"}

name: Urban Ranger
description: ## Urban Ranger ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/130› For the urban ranger, the streets and sewers of the city are just as dangerous as the barren wastelands or the deep forests. An urban ranger has the following class features. ::cskill{gain=dd~kl lose=ha~kna} ::ab[Favored Community (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost ability="The urban ranger forms a bond with a community. While inside the limits of this community, he gains a +2 bonus on initiative checks and Knowledge (local), Perception, Stealth, and Survival skill checks. An urban ranger traveling through his favored community leaves no trail and cannot be tracked (although he may leave a trail if he so desires)." repeat="An urban ranger may select an additional favored community. In addition, the skill bonus and initiative bonus in any one favored community (including the one just selected, if so desired) increases by +2.~8~5" special="For the purposes of this ability, a community is any settlement consisting of 100 or more individuals. The community may be larger than this minimum. Outlying farms, fields, and houses are not considered part of a community." replace="Favored terrain"} ::ab[Trapfinding (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power ability="An urban ranger can find and disable traps, as the rogue class feature of the ‹ability/same name»<trapfinding›." replace=Endurance} ::ab[Push Through (Ex)]{l=7 icon=boost ability="An urban ranger is never slowed by ‹rule/difficult terrain› in his favored communities. In addition, he can move through the space occupied by local citizens as if they were allies. This does not apply to creatures intent on harming the ranger. Areas that are enchanted or magically manipulated to impede motion, however, still affect him." replace="Woodland stride"} ::ab[Blend In (Ex)]{icon=boost-power l12="An urban ranger can use his Stealth bonus in place of a Disguise skill check in any of his favored communities. This disguise does not take an action to don. He must make a check whenever someone attempts to pick him out from the local citizens. If his check is successful, he blends into the crowd. While not invisible, enemies do not notice his presence and take no actions against him unless they are taking actions against the local citizens in general." replace=Camouflage} ::ab[Invisibility Trick (Sp)]{l=17 icon=magic swift="The urban ranger can cast ‹spell/greater invisibility› on himself as a wizard of his ranger level." useMod=Wisdom useM=1 replace="Hide in plain sight"}

name: Warden
description: ## Warden ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/68› All rangers have a bond with the wilderness, but the warden may have the strongest. This protector sits guard in the middle of the wilderness, keeping a lookout for any dangers that might spill from the deeper wilderness beyond, and protecting civilization from the savagery of nature - and vice versa. His long weeks, months, and sometimes years of isolation cause him to "hear" what the land is saying. Not all are crazy. ::ab[Master of Terrain (Ex)]{icon=power l1="A warden selects his first *favored terrain.*" repeat="He gains another favored terrain.~3~5" replace="1st favored enemy"} ::ab[Live in Comfort (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power info="A warden is truly at home within his *favored terrains.* He knows all the signs of the wilderness. He rarely gets lost. He can easily live off the land in comfort, and can provide for companions." order=na ability="The warden can take 10 on any Survival check involving any of his *favored terrains,* even when in immediate danger and distracted. If the warden is not in immediate danger and distracted, he can take 20 even if the check has a penalty for failure." replace="All combat style feats"} ::ab[Terrain Bond (Ex)]{l=4 icon=boost-def flavor="A warden forms a bond with the land itself, enabling him to direct others in such terrain." passive="When in his *favored terrain,* the warden grants all allies within line of sight and that can hear him a +2 bonus on initiative checks and Perception, Stealth, and Survival skill checks. Also, as long as they travel with him, the warden's allies leave no trail and can't be tracked. The warden can choose for the group to leave a trail, or even for specific members of the group to leave a trail if he so desires." replace="Hunter's bond"} ::ab[Able Explorer (Ex)]{l=5 icon=roll passive="When making an Acrobatics, Climb, Fly, Ride, or Swim check in any of his *favored terrains,* a warden can make two skill checks and take the higher." replace="2nd, 3rd, and 4th favored enemies"} ::ab[Wilderness Whispers (Su)]{l=20 icon=power-def ability="A warden cannot be surprised and always acts as if he had rolled a natural 20 on any initiative check while within any of his *favored terrains.* A warden can always move at full speed while using Survival to follow tracks without penalty." replace="5th favored enemy~master hunter"}

name: Wild Soul
description: ## Wild Soul ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/75› Hailing from primitive roots in the wild, some rangers venture to more civilized lands and learn their ways. Wild souls carry these more refined teachings back to the frontier lands of their birth, and they employ that knowledge in defense of their homes. ::ab[Unfettered Soul]{icon=warning info="A wild soul swears to himself never to make use of advanced technology, alchemy, arcane magic, or firearms. He also must oppose their use on his person, refusing to be a willing target and attempting a saving throw if possible (even if the effect is harmless or beneficial). Violating this oath causes a wild soul to lose the abilities granted by this archetype until he ‹spell/atone«s<ment›."} ::ab[Nemesis (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="A wild soul gains a +2 bonus on Intimidate, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, Spellcraft, and Survival checks against creatures that wield advanced technology, alchemical weapons (including an alchemist's bombs), or firearms and against those that cast arcane spells (this does not apply to creatures that use spell-like abilities). Likewise, he gains a +2 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against such opponents." order=pa ability="The wild soul can attempt Craft (alchemy), Knowledge (arcana), and Spellcraft checks untrained when attempting to identify enemy magic or advanced technology." increment="p!These bonuses~0~5~3" replace="Favored enemy"} ::ab[Nemesis Defense (Ex)]{l=8 icon=def passive="A wild soul adds his *nemesis* bonus on saving throws against advanced technology, alchemical items (including an alchemist's bombs and extracts), and arcane spells. He also adds this bonus to his AC against advanced technological items, alchemical items (including alchemist bombs), arcane spells that require attack rolls, and firearms." replace="Swift tracker"} ::ab[Break the Interloper (Su)]{l=11 icon=lower-aid ability="When a wild soul hits an arcane spellcaster, a creature with *extract* slots, or a creature with *grit* (but not grit-like pools such as *panache*) with a weapon attack, the target either loses its highest-level available spell or extract slot or loses 1 point of grit, and the wild soul gains 5 ‹rule/temporary hit points›." special="A target of this ability can negate this effect with a successful Fortitude save (DC = 10 + half the ranger's level + his Wisdom modifier). Regardless of the outcome of the saving throw, the target is immune to this ability for 24 hours." replace=Quarry} ::ab[Dizzying Onslaught (Ex)]{l=19 icon=lower flavor="A wild soul lands punishing blows that devastate his nemeses' ability to focus." ability="When he confirms a critical hit against a creature against whom his *nemesis* bonus applies, for 1 minute the target must succeed at a ‹rule/concentration› check (DC = 20 + the wild soul's Wisdom modifier + twice the spell's level) to cast an arcane spell, create an *extract,* or use an alchemist's bomb, and the target can't spend or gain *grit.*" replace="Improved quarry"} ::ab[Nemesis Slayer (Ex)]{l=20 icon=power flavor="A wild soul becomes death incarnate to his nemeses." standard="He can make a single attack against a *nemesis* at his full attack bonus. If the attack hits, the target takes damage normally and must succeed at a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + half the wild soul's level + his Wisdom modifier) or die. The wild soul can instead deal an amount of nonlethal damage equal to the creature's current hit points, which the target can negate with a successful save at the same DC." usage="Five times per day, but cannot be used against the same creature more than once in a 24-hour period" replace="Master hunter"}

name: Wild Stalker
description: ## Wild Stalker ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/68› Civilization grows stronger and more decadent with each passing year. It tears into unclaimed wilderness and destroys the fragile ecology in its constant push for expansion and exploitation. The wild stalker forsakes the bonds of community and lives in the trackless wilds far from others of his kind, or perhaps grew up there, never knowing of civilization as anything more than his enemy. He drives pioneers back to civilization and strives to keep the land unspoiled. ::ab[Strong Senses (Ex)]{l=1 icon=power-boost flavor="A wild stalker's life among the wild has sharpened his senses." ability="He gains low-light vision and a bonus on Perception checks equal to 1 + ‹misc/one-fourth› of his ranger level. If he already has low-light vision, the bonus becomes 2 + one-fourth of his ranger level.@FN1" replace="1st favored enemy"} ::ab[Uncanny Dodge (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def ability="A wild stalker gains ‹ability/uncanny dodge› as the barbarian class feature." replace="2nd-level combat style feat"} ::ab[Rage of the Wild (Ex)]{l=4 head icon=power ability="A wild stalker gains the *rage* ability as the ‹class/barbarian› class feature, but its barbarian level is considered to be his ranger level - 3." replace="Hunter's bond"} ::ab[Rage (Ex)]{next icon=boost-down flavor="Text from the barbarian class." usage="2 rounds/day + double your barbarian level + your Constitution modifier" free="You can enter (or end) a *rage.* You gain a +4 morale bonus to your Strength and Constitution, as well as a +2 morale bonus on Will saves. The increase to Constitution grants you 2 hit points per Hit Dice, but these disappear when the *rage* ends and are not lost first like ‹rule/temporary hit points›." order=ufp passive="While in *rage,* you take a -2 penalty to Armor Class, and you cannot use any Charisma-, Dexterity-, or Intelligence-based skills (except Acrobatics, Fly, Intimidate, and Ride) or any ability that requires patience or concentration. You are ‹misc/fatigued› after *rage* for a number of rounds equal to 2 times the number of rounds spent in the *rage.* You cannot enter a new *rage* while fatigued or ‹misc/exhausted› but can otherwise enter *rage* multiple times during a single encounter or combat. If you fall unconscious, your *rage* immediately ends, placing you in peril of death." special="Temporary increases to Constitution, such as those gained from *rage* and spells like ‹spell/bear's endurance›, do not increase the total number of rounds that a barbarian can *rage* per day. The total number of rounds of *rage* per day is renewed after resting for 8 hours, although these hours do not need to be consecutive."} ::ab[Rage Powers]{l=5 icon=power ability="A wild stalker ranger gains a single ‹ability/rage power<s›, as the barbarian class feature." repeat="He gains another rage power.~10~5" replace="2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th favored enemy"} ::ab[Wild Talents (Ex)]{l=6 icon=power-boost choice="A wild stalker can either take a rage power, or gain a +2 insight bonus into any one of the following skills: Acrobatics, Climb, Perception, Stealth, Survival, or Swim.@FN2" repeat="The wild stalker can gain one of these two benefits again.~10~4" replace="6th-, 10th-, 14th-, and 18th-level combat style feat"} :::fakeFootnotes @FN[The original text reads: *"This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels after 1st."* This implies a 1/5/9/13/17 progression, which would only reach +5/+6 at 20th level, but the text continues, *"(to a maximum of +6 &#91&or +7&#93& at 20th level),"* which only makes sense if the bonus increases *at 4th level* and every four levels thereafter. This is the interpretation used here.]{from=1} @FN[The original text reads: *"The wild stalker can gain one of these two benefits again every five levels after 6th (to a maximum of 4 times at 20th level)."* The listed progression only gives three benefits (at levels 6/11/16), not four. Either the maximum is wrong, or the level progression is wrong. Given that this ability replaces four bonus feats (at levels 6/10/14/18), the latter interpretation has been used here, and the ability is granted every *four* levels instead of five (which matches the levels of the bonus feats).]{from=2} :::

name: Wilderness Explorer
description: ## Wilderness Explorer ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/74› Wilderness explorers are adept at making peaceful contact with remote societies. ::cskill{gain=diplo~kl lose=intm~kd} ::ab[Cultural Contact (Ex)]{icon=power order=pa passive="A wilderness explorer gains the ability to communicate with creatures with which he doesn't share a common language. Only basic concepts can be conveyed or understood, such as &quot&I need help,&quot& &quot&I come in peace,&quot& &quot&Come over here,&quot& &quot&Go over there,&quot& and the like. This allows the wilderness explorer to ignore the common language requirement of social interaction and language-dependent spells and effects, but he can do so only when the information being shared is relatively simple. The creature with which the wilderness explorer communicates must understand at least one language for this ability to function." ability="Additionally, a wilderness explorer can peacefully influence the initial attitude of humanoids that have Intelligence scores of 2 or lower. This ability functions just like *wild empathy,* but it works on humanoids instead of on animals. The wilderness explorer can also use this ability to influence a monstrous humanoid with 2 or lower Intelligence, but the wilderness explorer takes a -4 penalty on the check." replace="Wild empathy"} ::ab[Hazard Sense (Ex)]{l=4 icon=def flavor="A wilderness explorer gains an intuitive understanding of natural hazards and traps fashioned from a natural environment." passive="He gains a bonus on Reflex saves against natural hazards and wilderness traps and a dodge bonus to AC against attacks from wilderness traps. Both of these bonuses are equal to ‹misc/one-fourth› of his ranger level." replace="Hunter's bond"} ::ab[Indigenous Spirit (Su)]{l=8 icon=def flavor="A wilderness explorer attracts the aid of native spirits, which reward his appreciation of their home with whispered warnings." ability="The wilderness explorer gains ‹ability/uncanny dodge› as long as he remains within one of his chosen *favored terrains.* This works like the barbarian ability of the same name." replace="Swift tracker" alter="Favored terrain"} ::ab[Guardian Spirit (Su)]{l=11 icon=def flavor="A wilderness explorer gains the aid of indigenous spirits, which favor him when he is defending himself against multiple foes that surround him." ability="He gains ‹ability/improved uncanny dodge›; this ability functions only while the ranger is within one of his *favored terrains.*" replace=Quarry alter="Favored terrain"} ::ab[Manifest Spirit (Su)]{l=19 icon=def flavor="A wilderness explorer is shielded from magic by those guardian spirits that favor him." special="He gains spell resistance equal to 11 + his ranger level. This ability functions only while the wilderness explorer is within one of his *favored terrains.*" replace="Improved quarry" alter="Favored terrain"}

name: Acrobat
description: ## Acrobat ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/132› Agility and daring are both excellent rogue traits, and their confluence can create spectacular feats of acrobatics. Whether they are daring thieves, infiltrating assassins, or intrepid spies, proper training in acrobatics is a valuable boon for rogues. ::ab[Expert Acrobat (Ex)]{l=1 icon=boost passive="An acrobat does not suffer any armor check penalties on Acrobatics, Climb, Fly, Sleight of Hand, or Stealth skill checks while wearing light armor. When she is not wearing armor, she gains a +2 competency bonus on Acrobatics and Fly skill checks." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Second Chance (Ex)]{l=3 icon=roll ability="An acrobat can reroll any Acrobatics, Climb, or Fly skill check she has just made. This reroll is made at a -5 penalty. She must take the second result, even if it is worse. An acrobat can use this ability only once on any given skill check." useInc=rogue~3 useF="3~1" replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Expert leaper~fast getaway~ledge walker~nimble climber~peerless maneuver~rogue crawl~stand up"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Defensive roll~fast tumble~improved evasion"}

name: Bandit
description: ## Bandit ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/71› Bandits, brigands, and highwaymen hone their craft along the roadsides and byways of the world, where they leap from the shadows to plunder the spoils of passing travelers. Bandits tend to have a variety of skills; sometimes these skills are similar to a ranger's, but a bandit's tactics always deal with surprise followed by intimidation, with the clear threat of naked force if intimidation does not do the trick. But not all bandits are ruthless thugs. There are those who become outlaws in opposition to tyrants or similar oppressors. These bandits target the status quo and distribute their spoils back into the needy hands of the peasantry. ::ab[Ambush (Ex)]{l=4 icon=power flavor="A bandit becomes fully practiced in the art of ambushing." ability="When she acts in the surprise round, she can take a move action, standard action, and swift action during the surprise round, not just a move or standard action." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Fearsome Strike (Ex)]{l=8 icon=lower flavor="A bandit can terrify an opponent with a single hit." useMod=Charisma useM=1 ability="When a bandit confirms a critical hit and deals sneak attack damage to an opponent, she can choose to make the opponent ‹misc/frightened› for a number of rounds equal to her Charisma modifier (minimum 1). She cannot use this ability in conjunction with a critical feat." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Assault leader~combat trick~cunning trigger~snap shot~strong impression~surprise attack~terrain mastery~underhanded~weapon training"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Hide in plain sight~knock-out blow~opportunist"}

name: Burglar
description: ## Burglar ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/132› Adept at infiltration, trap removal, and lock picking, burglars prey on the homes of the wealthy and forgotten tombs alike. Such riches are guarded with vicious traps and hazards, but the devious mind of the burglar allows her to find such dangers and avoid them. ::ab[Careful Disarm (Ex)]{l=4 icon=def passive="Whenever a burglar attempts to disarm a trap using Disable Device, she does not spring the trap unless she fails by 10 or more. If she does set off a trap she was attempting to disarm, she adds double her *trap sense* bonus to avoid the trap." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Distraction (Ex)]{l=8 icon=def ability="Whenever a burglar is detected while using Stealth, she can immediately attempt a Bluff skill check opposed by the Sense Motive skill of the creature that spotted her. If this check succeeds, the target assumes that the noise was something innocent and disregards the detection. This only functions if the creature cannot see the rogue. This ability can only be used once during a given Stealth attempt. If the same creature detects the rogue's presence again, the ability has no effect." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Fast picks~fast stealth~nimble climber~quick disable~trap spotter"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Knock-out blow~skill mastery~thoughtful reexamining"}

name: Chameleon
description: ## Chameleon ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/71› An absolute master of disguise, a chameleon effortlessly blends into any environment. Whether disappearing into crowded city streets, vanishing into desert sands, or slipping into the darkness of subterranean tunnels, the chameleon relies upon her ability to become part of her surroundings. ::ab[Misdirection (Ex)]{l=1 icon=boost flavor="A chameleon begins her career knowing that the secret to disappearing lies in deceiving the senses of her observers." ability="Every day she gains a pool of stealth points equal to her ranks in Bluff. These points refresh at the start of each day. Before making a Stealth check, she can choose to put stealth points into the roll, gaining a bonus on Stealth checks equal to the number of stealth points she puts into the roll." special="If she gains a bonus on Bluff checks because of a feat (such as ‹feat/Skill Focus› &#91&Bluff&#93&), she adds a number of points to her stealth pool equal to the bonus the feat grants." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Effortless Sneak (Sp)]{l=3 icon=power ability="The chameleon chooses a single terrain from the ranger's ‹ability/favored terrain› class feature. While she is within that terrain, she can take 10 on any Stealth check she can make within that terrain." repeat="She chooses a new type of terrain and gains this ability with the newly picked terrain.~6~3" replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Camouflage~fast stealth~quick disguise~terrain mastery"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Hide in plain sight~master of disguise"}

name: Charlatan
description: ## Charlatan ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/72› A charlatan is a master of lies and deception. Whether creating simple cons or elaborately woven hoaxes capable of swaying the masses and those in positions of power, a charlatan is often a purveyor of snake-oil, forgeries, and rumormongering. ::ab[Natural Born Liar (Ex)]{l=1 icon=lower ability="When a charlatan successfully deceives a creature with a Bluff, that creature takes a -2 penalty on the charlatan's Bluff checks for the next 24 hours. This ability does not stack with itself." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Grand Hoax (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power flavor="The charlatan begins to master the art of the *grand hoax* and learns to create deceptions designed to bestow harm upon her foes." ability="She gains the ‹talent/rumormonger› advanced talent, even though she is not yet 10th level." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Black market connections~coax information~convincing lie~honeyed words~underhanded"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Hard minded~skill mastery~unwitting ally"}

name: Consigliere

features.name: Field Boss (Ex)
features.replaces: Rogue talent normally gained at 10th level

description: ## Consigliere ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/44› Consiglieres act as trusted mediators and administrators for crime families and various criminal organizations, and many serve as the right hand to the leaders of such groups. Other consiglieres prefer to work as independent operators and sell their advice and expertise to the highest bidder. Though some consiglieres insulate themselves from violence and criminal activities, many enjoy getting their hands dirty leading strike teams or gangs of hardened thugs. ::cskill{gain=kno lose=kd} ::ab[Convincing Attitude (Ex)]{icon=power l1="A consigliere gains ‹feat/Persuasive› as a bonus feat." l2="He gains the ‹talent/charmer› rogue talent (or the ‹talent/certainty› &#91&Diplomacy&#93& rogue talent if he is an unchained rogue)." l3="If a consigliere attempts a Diplomacy check and fails to influence a creature's attitude by 5 or more, the creature's attitude remains unchanged instead of decreasing by one step." replace=Trapfinding~evasion} ::ab[Combat Advisor (Ex)]{icon=boost l4="Whenever a consigliere misses with a melee attack against an opponent, he can designate an ally within 30 feet of the target to receive a +1 insight bonus on her next attack roll against that opponent before the consigliere's next turn." l8="The insight bonus increases to +2." replace="Uncanny dodge~improved uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Bonus Feats (Ex)]{icon=power l4="A consigliere can choose to gain a single ‹main/teamwork feat› instead of a single rogue talent. (This substitution can only be used once, at either 4th, 6th, or 8th level.)" l12="The consigliere can choose to gain teamwork feats instead of rogue talents as many times as she chooses." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Field Boss (Ex)]{l=10 icon=power standard="A consigliere can grant a teamwork feat to all allies within 30 feet who can see and hear her. This teamwork feat must be one the consigliere knows. Allies retain the use of this feat for 3 rounds plus 1 round for every 2 rogue levels the consigliere has. Allies do not need to meet the prerequisites of this teamwork feat." useInc=rogue~4~10 useF="10~1~4" replace="Rogue talent normally gained at 10th level"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent all="assault leader~black market connections~shades of gray~coax information~honeyed words~certainty|Bluff; unchained rogue only"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Hard minded~opportunist~redirect attack~rumormonger~skill mastery~slippery mind~unwitting ally"}

name: Cutpurse
description: ## Cutpurse ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/132› Everyone who lives in the city understands that a wealthy man stays wealthy by guarding his purse while wandering the streets and markets. Cutpurses are often trained by guilds to collect the guild's tax from local businesses on a daily basis, whether through intimidation or pickpocketing. Some find themselves taking up the mantle of adventurer, and their talents are generally appreciated in this role, but the cutpurse is still the first person her companions look to when an item goes missing. ::ab[Measure the Mark (Ex)]{icon=power ability="When a cutpurse makes a Sleight of Hand check to take something from a creature, the target makes its Perception check before the rogue makes her Sleight of Hand check, and the rogue knows the Perception check result. She can decide whether or not to make the check based on the results of the target's Perception check. If the rogue elects not to make the check, she can make a Bluff check, opposed by the target's Sense Motive, to prevent the target from noticing the attempt." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Stab and Grab (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power fullround="A cutpurse can make an attack and also make a Sleight of Hand check to steal something from the target of the attack. If the attack deals sneak attack damage, the rogue can use Sleight of Hand to take an item from the creature during combat; otherwise this ability can only be used in a surprise round before the target has acted. If the attack is successful, the target takes a -5 penalty on the Perception check to notice the theft." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Combat swipe~fast fingers~fast getaway~hard to fool~minor magic~slow reactions~surprise attack"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Crippling strike~fast tumble~skill mastery"}

name: Desert Raider
description: ## Desert Raider ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/76› Desert raiders constantly threaten caravans that cross vast, desolate expanses. Some desert raiders are tribespeople who raid to supplement their hardscrabble existence, while others are career thieves who take to the desert to avoid the noose. To survive, a desert raider must learn the secrets of the deserts and become inured to their dangers. Though most often associated with hot deserts, desert raiders can also operate in tundra, where sunlight on snow can blind as easily as on sand. ::cskill{gain=kg~sur lose=kd~swim} ::ab[Desert Tracker (Ex)]{icon=def-boost passive="A desert raider is immune to the ‹misc/dazzled› condition. A desert raider adds half her level (minimum 1) as a bonus on Survival skill checks to follow or identify tracks in desert terrain." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Sun at Your Back (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power flavor="A desert raider can use the reflected light of the blinding sun to conceal her presence." ability="A desert raider in bright light can attempt Stealth checks without cover or concealment but takes a -5 penalty on her check. The desert raider cannot use this ability to hide from creatures immune to the ‹misc/blinded› or dazzled conditions." replace="Rogue talent gained at 2nd level"} ::ab[Light Step (Ex)]{l=3 icon=def-boost passive="The DC of Survival checks to track the desert raider increase by 2 + ‹misc/one-third› of her rogue level. In addition, she gains a bonus on Perception checks to avoid being surprised by a foe. This bonus on is equal to one-third of her rogue level." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Fast stealth~getaway artist~ledge walker~rogue crawl~stand up~surprise attack"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Hide in plain sight~stealthy sniper"}

name: Driver
description: ## Driver ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/72› A driver makes her living driving vehicles in the service of those who can pay for her considerable talents. She may be a wagon-driver practiced at smuggling contraband, an accomplished musher blazing arctic trails, or a seemingly refined coach driver placing her roguish talents in the service of a wealthy patron. ::ab[Hard Drive (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="When driving a vehicle that uses a group of animals or magical beasts as muscle propulsion, the DCs of all driving checks are reduced by 2, the maximum speed of the vehicle increases by 10 feet, and the acceleration increases by 5 feet." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Driver's Fortitude (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power flavor="The driver learns to keep driving and maintain control of her vehicle, even when mortally wounded." ability="If the driver drops below 0 hit points but is not dead, she can attempt a DC 15 Fortitude save each round to remain conscious and in control of her vehicle, though she may take no other actions." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Firearm training~getaway artist"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Feat~getaway master"}

name: Fey Prankster
description: ## Fey Prankster ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/12› Fey pranksters specialize in tricking others to teach a lesson or for their own entertainment. ::prereq{r=Gathlain} ::ab[Treacherous Plants (Sp)]{icon=power ability="The fey prankster can cause plants to distract nearby creatures. To use this ability, the fey prankster attempts a Bluff check to create a distraction to hide as a @HLswift_action or to ‹rule/feint› against an adjacent opponent as a @HLmove_action, so long as the target is adjacent to plants. He gains a bonus on this check equal to half his rogue level (minimum +1)." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Improved Dirty Trick]{l=2 icon=power ability="The fey prankster gains ‹feat/Improved Dirty Trick› as a bonus feat. He need not meet the prerequisites." replace="Rogue talent gained at 2nd level"} ::ab[Steal Appearance (Sp)]{l=4 icon=magic ability="The fey prankster can exchange the appearance of two adjacent items of the same size. He can also exchange the appearance of two creatures if at least one is willing and both are adjacent. Affecting an unwilling creature or an item it wears or carries requires a successful ‹rule/dirty trick› combat maneuver against that creature. If he succeeds, the objects or creatures are each disguised as the other as if with ‹spell/veil› cast at his rogue level. The Will save DC to resist or disbelieve the illusion is equal to 10 + half the rogue's level + his Intelligence modifier." imp8="The fey prankster can also exchange the locations of the two targets by succeeding at a DC 20 Sleight of Hand check. If he succeeds, observers can't tell which is the original based on movement without succeeding at a Perception check against his Sleight of Hand result." replace="Uncanny dodge~improved uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Greater Dirty Trick]{l=6 icon=power ability="The fey prankster gains ‹feat/Greater Dirty Trick› as a bonus feat. He does not need to meet the prerequisites." replace="Rogue talent gained at 6th level"} ::ab[Plant Traps (Su)]{l=8 icon=power usage="3 times/day" fullround="The fey trickster can modify a plant (but not plant creatures) into a trap. The Perception and Disable Device DCs for the trap are each equal to 15 + his rogue level. A Tiny or larger plant can be used to perform a ‹rule/trip› or dirty trick combat maneuver using the fey trickster's CMB and the plant's size. A Large or larger plant can be used to create a ‹spell/snare› as per the spell. The save DC is equal to 12 + the rogue's Intelligence modifier." special="The fey trickster can trigger any plant trap he created as a @HLstandard_action as long as he is within 60 feet of it." replace="Rogue talent gained at 8th level"} ::ab[Unseen Trickster]{l=12 icon=power ability="The fey trickster can attempt Stealth checks in areas with plants even if he does not have ‹rule/cover› or ‹rule/concealment›." replace="Rogue talent gained at 12th level"}

name: Guild Agent
description: ## Guild Agent ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/45› Guild agents are members of a thieves' guild or other shadowy organization. What they lose in independence, they more than make up for in benefits gained due to their association's infrastructure. Guild agents come at all levels of the organization, from a lowly recruit all the way up to the guildmaster himself. ::ab[Honor Among Thieves (Ex)]{icon=warning info="A guild agent must remain a member in good standing of a thieves' guild (he starts at rank 1 with her guild when using the ‹rule/organizational influence› system). If the guild agent leaves his guild, he loses all of the abilities granted by this archetype and does not gain their replacements. If he joins a new guild, the guild agent regains his abilities, though depending on how he joins the guild, he may regain his abilities all at once or gradually over time. Even if the guild in question operates in multiple locations, the guild agent chooses a settlement as a base of operations for his own activities."} ::ab[Guild Connections (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power-boost ability="A guild agent gains the ‹talent/black market connections› rogue talent. Furthermore, he can ask his guild for tips about the local scene, granting him a bonus equal to half his rogue level on Knowledge (local) checks and Diplomacy checks to gather information, as long as the information in question pertains to the guild agent's base of operations." imp4="The guild agent also gains the ‹soctalent/gossip collector› vigilante social talent and his base of operations counts as his area of renown for the purpose of determining the effects of gossip collector." replace="Evasion~uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Pull Rank (Ex)]{l=8 icon=power ability="A guild agent has attained sufficient rank to call in lesser guild members to assist him with a job. He can call lesser members of a number and level equal to the number of followers he would have if he had the ‹feat/Leadership› feat (including the +2 bonus for his guildhouse), to a maximum of a number of lesser members equal to his rogue level. If the guild agent possesses the Leadership feat, he gains twice as many followers as normal. If he spends a favor, he can combine this with the command team organizational influence benefit to gain even more lesser members for a particularly difficult job. Each time the guild agent uses the lesser members recklessly and gets them killed, he loses at least 1 influence with his guild." replace="Improved evasion"} ::ab[Criminal Mastermind (Ex)]{l=20 icon=power ability="Except in an unusually powerful guild, a guild agent has become the true power behind the guild. The guild agent has built up a nearly worldwide reputation under a particular criminal epithet (such as &quot&The Silver Shadow&quot&), known by criminals and law enforcement officers everywhere. This works like the ‹soctalent/renown› vigilante social talent except as follows. It applies in all towns and cities on the same continent as the guild agent's base of operations, without requiring him to select a particular settlement. He has only one identity, and only other criminals and members of the underworld treat their attitudes toward the guild agent as one step closer to helpful at all times (rather than while only in his social identity), while the bonus on Intimidate checks applies against everyone at all times (rather than while only in his vigilante identity)." replace="Master strike"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Assault leader~certainty|unchained rogue only~getaway artist"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Getaway master~hunter's surprise~opportunist~rumormonger~skill mastery"}

name: Heister

features.name: Ferret's Grace (Ex)
features.replaces: Uncanny dodge~rogue talent gained at 4th level

features.name: Unseen (Ex)
features.replaces: Improved uncanny dodge~rogue talent gained at 8th level

description: ## Heister ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/45› Notorious for their stealth, imagination, and elaborately planned thefts and capers, heisters specialize in breaking into secure locations, stealing items of value, and escaping undetected. Heisters often work as members of or independent operatives contracted to criminal organizations, crime families, or wealthy individuals inclined to unlawful activity. ::ab[Rum Dubber (Ex)]{l=2 icon=boost passive="Whenever a heister attempts to open a lock without a set of ‹eq-misc/thieves' tools›, the DC increases by 2, instead of 10." replace="Rogue talent gained at 2nd level"} ::ab[Ferret's Grace (Ex)]{l=4 icon=power ability="A heister gains ‹feat/Stealthy› as a bonus feat. Additionally, a heister counts as a creature one size category smaller than she actually is when determining whether or not she is ‹misc/squeezing› into an enclosed space. Finally, when a heister uses the ‹skill/Escape Artist› skill to move through a tight space where her head fits but her shoulders do not, the DC is 20, instead of 30." replace="Uncanny dodge~rogue talent gained at 4th level"} ::ab[Unseen (Ex)]{l=8 icon=power ability="A heister masters hiding in underground and urban terrain. She can use the Stealth skill to hide in underground and urban terrain, even while being observed. She also gains the ‹talent/terrain mastery› rogue talent twice, once each for underground and urban terrain." replace="Improved uncanny dodge~rogue talent gained at 8th level"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Certainty|unchained rogue only~expert leaper~fast getaway~fast picks~fast stealth~getaway artist~ledge walker~quick disable"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Cutting edge|unchained rogue only~fast tumble~getaway master~hidden mind~skill mastery"}

name: Investigator
description: ## Investigator >***Note:** This is a rogue archetype, and has no relation to the ‹class/investigator› hybrid class.* ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/133› Not all rogues work against the law. Investigators use their skills to serve the law, often in the employ of nobles or in the pursuit of noble causes. In some cities cabals of investigators work for rulers or bureaucracies, but often an investigator is a free agent who pursues whatever mysteries come across her path. Of course, not all investigators serve the law. Crime lords and guildmasters often have squads of investigators serving their own nefarious purposes. ::ab[Follow Up (Ex)]{icon=roll-boost ability="An investigator can roll twice on any Diplomacy check made to gather information, and receives the information for both results. This takes the same amount of time as one check. If the lesser of the two checks reveals false information, the rogue is aware of it. False information is not revealed in this way if the people she questioned do not know it to be false." replace=Trapfinding} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Coax information~fast picks~follow clues~hard to fool~minor magic"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Hunter's surprise~slippery mind~thoughtful reexamining"}

name: Knife Master
description: ## Knife Master ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/72› The knife master is a trained killer who specializes in close-up combat and the wave and weave of knife fighting. In her hands, daggers and other similar light blades become truly deadly instruments.. ::ab[Hidden Blade]{icon=boost passive="A knife master adds 1/2 her level on Sleight of Hand checks made to conceal a light blade." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Sneak Stab (Ex)]{icon=boost-down info="A knife master focuses her ability to deal sneak attack damage with daggers and similar weapons to such a degree that she can deal more sneak attack damage with those weapons at the expense of sneak attacks with other weapons." order=na ability="When she makes a sneak attack with a ‹eq-weapon/dagger›, ‹eq-weapon/kerambit›, ‹eq-weapon/kukri›, ‹eq-weapon/punching dagger«s›, ‹eq-weapon/starknife›, or ‹eq-weapon/swordbreaker dagger›, she uses d8s to roll sneak attack damage instead of d6s. For sneak attacks with all other weapons, she uses d4s instead of d6s." special="This ability is identical in all other ways to sneak attack, and supplements that ability." alter="Sneak attack"} ::ab[Blade Sense (Ex)]{l=3 icon=def passive="A knife master is so skilled in combat involving light blades that she gains a dodge bonus to AC against attacks made against her with light blades. @B-3f-rogue." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Befuddling strike~combat trick~offensive defense~surprise attack~underhanded~weapon training"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Another day~confounding blades~deadly sneak~entanglement of blades~unwitting ally"}

name: Master of Disguise
description: ## Master of Disguise ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/46› A master of disguise feels no need to advertise her skills to build a reputation. Instead, she believes that never letting her adversaries know her true identity protects her from bad luck or missteps on a job. ::ab[Consummate Actor (Ex)]{icon=boost-power l1="A master of disguise adds half her rogue level (minimum 1) on all Disguise checks and on Bluff checks to stay in character while using Disguise." l2="She gains the ‹talent/quick disguise› rogue talent, and she can create a disguise twice as quickly as normal even for that rogue talent (she can create a disguise that encompasses only minor details as a @HLstandard_action)." replace="Trapfinding~rogue talent gained at 2nd level"} ::ab[Grandmaster of Disguise (Ex)]{l=10 icon=power ability="A master of disguise gains the ‹talent/master of disguise› advanced rogue talent and can use it an unlimited number of times per day. Because she must still don a physical disguise to gain this bonus, it doesn't stack with the bonuses from spells like ‹spell/alter self› and ‹spell/disguise self›, but since it is completely nonmagical, it is more reliable when scrutinized under magical detection." replace="Rogue talent gained at 10th level"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Camouflage~false friend~major magic~minor magic~obfuscate story~shades of gray~steal the story"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Hard minded~hidden mind~skill mastery~slippery mind~unwitting ally"}

name: Phantom Thief
description: ## Phantom Thief ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/46› Also known as gentleman thieves or lady thieves, phantom thieves don't know the desperation of a hard life like many rogues. Instead, they come from the ranks of the elite, having grown bored with their finery, and seek thrills from acts of daring, skill, and crime. Phantom thieves don't need the money, so they often perform acts such as breaking into a secure vault for the thrill, leaving a calling card rather than robbing the place. ::cskill{gain=ha~heal~ride~spc~sur~ka~kd~ke~kg~kh~kl~kna~kno~kp~kr} ::ab[Refined Education (Ex)]{icon=boost l1="The phantom thief selects one of her rogue class skills and adds half her rogue level on all skill checks using that skill." repeat="She selects an additional rogue class skill and adds half her rogue level on all skill checks using that skill as well.~3~2" imp4="She gains *rogue's edge* skill unlocks with each of these skills rather than selecting one skill every 5 levels, and she adds half her rogue level to her number of ranks to determine when she receives a skill unlock (so a 7th level rogue (phantom thief) with 7 ranks in a chosen skill would count as having 10 ranks and receive the second skill unlock)." replace="Debilitating injury~sneak attack~trapfinding" alter="Rogue's edge (unchained rogue only)"} ::ab[Broad Education (Ex)]{flavor="A phantom thief's broad studies with expensive tutors keep her up to speed in both martial and magical knowledge, as well as in her skills." icon=power ability="She can select the ‹talent/combat trick›, ‹talent/minor magic›, and ‹talent/major magic› rogue talents as many times as she likes, and she can select the ‹feat/Skill Focus› feat as a rogue talent, also as many times as she likes. Finally, she can select a vigilante ‹ability/social talent<s› instead of a rogue talent, except for *social grace* and vigilante social talents that would require her to be a craftsman or professional." special="For the purpose of vigilante social talents, a phantom thief does not have a vigilante identity and is always considered to be in her social identity." alter="Rogue talent"} ::ab[Social Sense (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost flavor="A phantom thief's social sixth sense allows her to avoid danger in social situations and to act first when it breaks out." passive="She receives a bonus on Sense Motive checks to avoid being surprised by a foe, on Bluff checks to surprise a foe, and on initiative checks for surprise rounds that involved Bluff and Sense Motive checks to determine surprise. @B-3fp-rogue." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Master of All (Ex)]{l=20 icon=roll ability="A phantom thief can reroll any skill check as long as it is a class skill in which she is trained. She must take the second result, even if it is worse." usage="Once per minute" replace="Master strike"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Certainty|unchained rogue only~combat trick~major magic~minor magic"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Cutting edge|unchained rogue only~feat~hidden mind~rumormonger~skill mastery"}

name: Pirate
description: ## Pirate ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/73› A pirate breaks from the confines of country and king to commit her crimes upon the high seas. She holds allegiance only to her ship and its captain (if even that much is true), and lives a lawless life upon the waves, plundering ships and shorelines as suits her whim. ::ab[Sea Legs (Ex)]{l=1 icon=power flavor="A pirate becomes adept at moving on ships, boats, and similar vessels." ability="She gains the ‹feat/Sea Legs› feat as a bonus feat, even if she does not meet the prerequisites." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Swinging Reposition (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power ability="A pirate incorporates a ship's masts, rigging, ropes, sails, and other such structures into her combat style. Provided she is wearing light armor or no armor, when fighting in an environment where such structures exist, the rogue incorporates them into her movement, and does not have to move in a straight line when making either a ‹rule/charge› attack or a ‹rule/bull rush› combat maneuver." special="Once she completes her attack or maneuver, she can reposition herself. Immediately after making the charge or bull rush, she can move 5 feet as a @HLfree_action, even if the charge ends her turn. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity." replace="2nd-level rogue talent"} ::ab[Unflinching (Ex)]{flavor="Pirates are a salty and steadfast lot." icon=def l3="A pirate gains a bonus on saving throws against fear and mind-affecting effects. @B-3f-rogue." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Black market connections~combat trick~finesse rogue~firearm training~hold breath~rope master~strong stroke"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Getaway master~hard minded~unwitting ally"}

name: Poisoner
description: ## Poisoner ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/134› Some consider poisoning an evil act. The poisoner knows poison is just a tool toward an end, and is no different than any other weapon. Some poisoners see themselves as great equalizers, as they are able to craft weapons that the weakest of creatures can wield to devastating effect, but most have no lofty delusions about their work. ::ab[Poison Use (Ex)]{l=1 icon=def ability="A poisoner is trained in the use of poison and cannot accidentally poison herself when applying poison to a blade." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Master Poisoner (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power-boost ability="A poisoner can use Craft (alchemy) to change the type of a ‹rule/poison›. This requires 1 hour of work with an ‹eq-misc/alchemist's lab› and a Craft (alchemy) skill check with a DC equal to the poison's DC. If successful, the poison's type changes to contact, ingested, inhaled, or injury. If the check fails, the poison is ruined." order=ap passive="The poisoner also receives a bonus on Craft (alchemy) skill checks when working with poison equal to 1/2 her rogue level." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Distracting attack~lasting poison~surprise attack~swift poison~weapon training"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Deadly cocktail~hunter's surprise~opportunist"}

name: Rake
description: ## Rake ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/134› The rake is a rogue who is open about her skills and talents, often to the point of being boastful. Usually she has the protection of an important figure who finds her services useful, but sometimes her bravado is enough to keep enemies away. She is often used as a face for the group for diplomacy, gathering information, negotiations, or to gain the most lucrative contracts and quests from local authorities. ::ab[Bravado's Blade (Ex)]{icon=power ability="When a rake hits an opponent and deals sneak attack damage, she can forgo 1d6 points of that damage and make a free ‹skill/Intimidate› check to demoralize the foe. For every additional 1d6 points of sneak attack damage she forgoes, she receives a +5 circumstance bonus on this check." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Rake's Smile (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost passive="A rake gains a morale bonus on Bluff and Diplomacy checks equal to ‹misc/one-third› of her rogue level." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Befuddling strike~charmer~honeyed words~surprise attack"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Another day~redirect attack~skill mastery"}

name: River Rat
sourceBook: Ultimate Wilderness, People of the River
description: ## River Rat ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/76;People of the River/21› What highway robbers are to roads, river rats are to waterways. Skilled at hiding amid reeds and roots, these rogues strike the unwary from the shallows as others would from the shadows. Despite their strong association with banditry, river rats make excellent guides and hunters. ::cskill{gain=kna lose=kd} ::ab[Swamper (Ex)]{l=1 icon=boost passive="A river rat gains a bonus equal to half her rogue level on Swim checks (minimum +1). She takes no penalty on Acrobatics or Stealth checks for being in bogs and undergrowth." ability="A river rat ignores ‹rule/difficult terrain› caused by light undergrowth and shallow bogs, and it costs her only 2 squares of movement to enter a square of ‹rule/deep bog› or ‹rule/heavy undergrowth›, rather than 4 squares of movement." order=pa special="All of these abilities apply only when she is wearing light or no armor and carrying no more than a light load." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Rat's Resilience (Ex)]{flavor="A river rat is inured to dangers presented by disease-carrying parasites, poisonous fish, and other toxic river denizens." icon=def passive="A river rat gains a bonus on saving throws against disease and poison effects. @B-3f-rogue." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Camouflage~hold breath~rogue crawl~stand up~strong stroke~survivalist"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Hide in plain sight~opportunist~skill mastery~stealthy sniper"}

name: Roof Runner
description: ## Roof Runner ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/74› A specialized urban acrobat, the roof runner makes her home high atop the spires and gables of great cities.
