She is skilled at traveling these uneven surfaces at full speed, performing daring leaps and deftly balancing upon narrow and precarious ledges. ::ab[Roof Running (Ex)]{l=1 icon=power flavor="A roof runner becomes entirely adept at moving across the tops of buildings, spires, and similar locations." ability="Provided she is wearing light armor or no armor, the roof runner can move at full speed while traveling across the tops of buildings or similar structures, and takes no penalties on any Dexterity-based Skill checks or Reflex saves that might be incurred from moving about on a roof." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Tumbling Descent (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power ability="A roof runner can use her Acrobatics skill to attempt a rapid descent from a rooftop or another surface, ricocheting against another surface and then diving through an opening (such as a balcony or window) directly below. So long as she has at least two surfaces no farther than 10 feet apart to bounce against, she can ricochet her body back from one to the next, descending great distances with a single check. The DC is 10 + 5 for every additional 10-foot increment descended beyond the initial 10 feet dropped. If she fails, she falls the full distance." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Expert leaper~ledge walker~nimble climber~stand up~terrain mastery"} @HL[This advanced rogue talent complements this archetype:] ‹talent/Fast tumble›

name: Sanctified Rogue
description: ## Sanctified Rogue ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/74› The sanctified rogue serves a higher purpose, acting as a representative of a church or cult, or following the tenets of a specific faith or deity. While most sanctified rogues share the beliefs or ideals of the religions they represent, not all of them are necessarily pious. A handful of disreputable holy thieves serve purely as mercenaries. At the other end of spectrum, however, more sanctified rogues adhere to the tenets of their faith with fanatical devotion. Regardless, all seem blessed with the ability to call upon divine favor to aid them in times of need. ::ab[Divine Purpose (Su)]{l=4 icon=def flavor="The favor of a deity or religious institution grants a special blessing on a sanctified rogue, shoring up some of her weaknesses." passive="She gains a +1 sacred bonus on Fortitude and Will saving throws." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Divine Epiphany (Su)]{l=8 icon=magic ability="Once per day, a sanctified rogue can peer into the immediate future and predict the results of a specific action as if she had cast an ‹spell/augury› spell. The caster level of this spell is equal to the sanctified rogue's rogue class level." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Esoteric scholar~major magic~minor magic"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Feat~skill mastery"}

name: Scout
description: ## Scout ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/134› Not all rogues live in the city. Scouts frequently roam the wilderness, often banding together as bandits, but sometimes serving as guides, as trailblazers, or as companions to a ranger or barbarian warrior. More comfortable with sneaking and hiding outdoors, the scout is still effective in the city and the dungeon. ::ab[Scout's Charge (Ex)]{l=4 icon=melee ability="Whenever a scout makes a ‹rule/charge›, her attack deals sneak attack damage as if the target were ‹rule/flat-footed›. Foes with *uncanny dodge* are immune to this ability." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Skirmisher (Ex)]{l=8 icon=power ability="Whenever a scout moves more than 10 feet in a round and makes an attack action, the attack deals sneak attack damage as if the target was flat-footed. If the scout makes more than one attack this turn, this ability only applies to the first attack. Foes with *uncanny dodge* are immune to this ability." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Assault leader~camouflage~cunning trigger~survivalist~trap spotter"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Hunter's surprise~skill mastery~stealthy sniper"}

name: Sharper

features.name: Sticky Fingers (Ex)
features.replaces: Rogue talents gained at 2nd, 6th, and 8th levels

features.name: Audacious Overconfidence (Ex)
features.replaces: Rogue talents gained at 4th, 10th, and 16th levels

description: ## Sharper ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/47› Sharpers use trickery and deception to part an owner from his valuables. Pathological risk-takers, they distinguish themselves from con artists and burglars by virtue of the simplicity and boldness of their schemes, which are usually impromptu, rather than carefully orchestrated. Many sharpers consider themselves romantic figures and foster the image of a resourceful, dashing rogue living by wits and luck while subverting authority at every turn. ::ab[Scam Artist (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="A sharper gains a bonus equal to half her rogue level (minimum +1) on all Bluff and Sleight of Hand checks." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Sticky Fingers (Ex)]{icon=power l2="A sharper receives ‹feat/Improved Steal› as a bonus feat." l6="She receives ‹feat/Greater Steal› as a bonus feat." imp8="She receives ‹feat/Quick Steal› as a bonus feat." special="The sharper gains these feats even if she doesn't meet the prerequisites." replace="Rogue talents gained at 2nd, 6th, and 8th levels"} ::ab[Lucky Save (Su)]{icon=def flavor="When a sharper's wits aren't enough to pull her out of a bad situation, her luck still just might save her." l3="She gains a +1 luck bonus on all saving throws." increment="This bonus~3~6" replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Audacious Overconfidence (Ex)]{l=4 icon=roll-def ability="After failing an attack roll, skill check, or saving throw, a sharper can reduce her saving throw bonus from *lucky save* by 1 for 24 hours in order to reroll the failed roll." useInc=rogue~6~4 useF="4~1~6" special="The decreases to her bonus from *lucky save* stack with each other." replace="Rogue talents gained at 4th, 10th, and 16th levels"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Certainty|unchained rogue only~charmer~convincing lie~deft palm~false friend~fast fingers~follow along~honeyed words~obfuscate story~shades of gray~steal the story"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Another day~cutting edge|unchained rogue only~defensive roll~hidden mind~improved evasion~redirect attack~skill mastery"}

name: Sly Saboteur
description: ## Sly Saboteur ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/77› Sly saboteurs are irregular soldiers who specialize in sabotage and surprise attacks. Though they often face enemies with greater numbers or resources (or both), sly saboteurs have the advantage of knowing the local people and terrain. They might be rebels fighting against a corrupt government, or they might be members of a militia opposing an invading force. Some are environmentalists who sabotage the tools of industry in order to protect unspoiled nature. ::cskill{gain=sur lose=kd} ::ab[Scamper (Ex)]{l=3 icon=power ability="A sly saboteur can move through 5 feet of ‹rule/difficult terrain› each round as if it were normal terrain." incrementPlain="This distance~3~3~10~5" incrementEnd=" feet." special="This ability allows the sly saboteur to take a 5-foot step into difficult terrain. This ability applies only when she is wearing light armor or no armor and carrying no more than a light load, and it stacks with the ‹feat/Acrobatic Steps› and ‹feat/Nimble Moves› feats." replace="Trap sense"} ::ab[Catastrophic Failure (Ex)]{l=4 icon=boost ability="When a sly saboteur uses Disable Device to rig a device to fail, she can increase the DC of the check by 5. If she does so and succeeds at the check, when the device fails, users take damage equal to the sly saboteur's sneak attack, or they take half that amount with a successful Reflex save (DC = 10 + half the sly saboteur's level + her Dexterity modifier)." special="The type of damage depends on the nature of the device but is typically bludgeoning, fire, piercing, or slashing." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Disable Magic Device (Su)]{l=8 icon=power ability="A sly saboteur can use Disable Device to rig a magic item to fail as if it were an extremely complex device. If the item's effect is instantaneous, the effect is countered the next time the item is activated, but the activation still consumes a charge or use. If the item's effect is continuous or has a duration, the effect fails after 1d4 rounds or minutes of use (sly saboteur's choice). This ends the duration or suppresses a continuous effect for 1d4 rounds (as the spell ‹spell/dispel magic›). This ability cannot be used on artifacts." special="If this ability is combined with the *catastrophic failure* ability, the resulting damage is untyped magic and is not reduced by damage reduction or energy resistance." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Cunning trigger~fast stealth~getaway artist~quick disable~quick trapsmith~rogue crawl~trap spotter~wall scramble"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Frugal trapsmith~hide in plain sight~knock-out blow~rumormonger~skill mastery~stealthy sniper"}

name: Sniper
description: ## Sniper ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/134› Some say that the sniper is the worst kind of assassin: a killer who waits silently in the shadows and then strikes from a distance without remorse. Snipers, of course, understand that such protestations about "cowardice" and "honor" regarding their profession are in fact merely the bleatings of sheep fearing the slaughter and pay them no heed. Most snipers take pride in their formidable abilities, which allow them to take life quickly, quietly, and efficiently, then disappear into their surroundings without a trace. ::ab[Accuracy (Ex)]{l=1 icon=ranged-boost passive="A sniper halves all range increment penalties when making ranged attacks with a bow or crossbow." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Deadly Range (Ex)]{icon=ranged-boost l3="A sniper increases the range at which she can apply her sneak attack damage by 10 feet." incrementPlain="This range~3~3~20~10" incrementEnd=" feet." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Camouflage~snap shot~sniper's eye~weapon training"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Defensive roll~master of disguise~stealthy sniper"}

name: Snoop
description: ## Snoop ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/47› Snoops are the underworld's version of detectives. They often act as information peddlers, specializing in gathering secrets through investigation, subterfuge, and coercion, and selling or trading those secrets for personal gain. ::ab[Inspiration (Ex)]{l=1 head icon=power ability="A snoop gains an ability similar to the ‹class/investigator«'s› inspiration class ability. The snoop begins with an inspiration pool equal to ‹misc/half› her rogue level plus her Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). Unlike an investigator, a snoop can only use inspiration on skill checks, not on attack rolls or saving throws. This ability is otherwise identical to the investigator class ability of the same name." replace=Trapfinding~evasion} ::ab[Inspiration (Ex)]{next icon=boost order=afu flavor="Text from the investigator class." usage="You can only use inspiration once per check or roll." ability="Your inspiration pool refreshes each day, typically after you get a restful night's sleep." free="You can expend one use of inspiration from your pool to add 1d6 to the result of a check, including any on which you take 10 or 20. This choice is made after the check is rolled and before the results are revealed." special="You can use inspiration on any Knowledge, Linguistics, or Spellcraft skill checks without expending a use of inspiration, if you're trained in the skill."} ::ab[Investigator Talents (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power ability="Each time she selects a new rogue talent, a snoop can instead select one of the following investigator talents: ‹invtalent/eidetic recollection›, ‹invtalent/empathy›, ‹invtalent/hidden agendas›, ‹invtalent/inspired alertness›, ‹invtalent/inspired intimidator›, ‹invtalent/item lore›, or ‹invtalent/underworld inspiration›. Her effective investigator level for the purpose of these talents is equal to her rogue level." special="She still can't use inspiration on attack rolls or saving throws (so, for instance, she can't use the second part of *hidden agendas*)."} ::ab[Uncanny Snoop (Ex)]{icon=boost l4="A snoop gains a +2 bonus on Intimidate checks when trying to force an opponent to give her information (or Bluff and Diplomacy checks for the same purpose if she has the ‹talent/coax information› rogue talent). She also gains a +2 bonus on Sense Motive checks to tell if someone's information is false." imp8="These bonuses increase to +4." replace="Uncanny dodge~improved uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Master of Whispers (Ex)]{l=8 icon=power ability="A snoop receives the ‹talent/rumormonger› advanced rogue talent." replace="Rogue talent gained at 8th level"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Black market connections~certainty|unchained rogue only~coax information~fast stealth~follow clues~strong impression"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Cutting edge|unchained rogue only~hard minded~hidden mind~skill mastery~thoughtful reexamining"}

name: Spy
description: ## Spy ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/135› The best spies are like chameleons, but not only can they change their appearances to fit the situation, they can also change their personalities, allegiances, and even loves if that's what it takes to achieve their clandestine goals. Spies are the ultimate manipulators, and even those who commission their services sometimes find that they've merely served the spies' own interests. ::ab[Skilled Liar (Ex)]{icon=boost passive="Whenever a spy uses ‹skill/Bluff› to attempt to deceive someone, she gains a bonus on the opposed roll equal to 1/2 her rogue level (minimum +1). This bonus does not apply to feint attempts or attempts to pass secret messages." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Poison Use (Ex)]{l3="A spy is trained in the use of poison and cannot accidentally poison herself when applying poison to a blade." icon=def replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Canny observer~guileful polyglot~honeyed words~major magic~minor magic~quick disguise"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Crippling strike~master of disguise~stealthy sniper"}

name: Survivalist
description: ## Survivalist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/74› The survivalist focuses her talents on surviving harsh and unforgiving conditions that would kill a lesser rogue. Whether in blazing deserts or frigid arctic wastes - or simply the cold, hard reality of the streets - the survivalist uses her training to both ensure her own success and provide for the safety of her allies. ::ab[Hardy (Ex)]{l=1 icon=def ability="A survivalist is already prepared to endure extreme hardships and environmental conditions. She can go twice the normal number of days without water and triple the normal number of days without food before feeling the effects of either thirst or starvation." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Endure Elements (Sp)]{l=3 icon=magic ability="A survivalist rogue can use ‹spell/endure elements› once per day as a spell-like ability. The survivalist's caster level is the same as her rogue level." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Hold breath~iron guts~resiliency~strong stroke~survivalist~terrain mastery~wall scramble"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Another day~defensive roll~feat~skill mastery"}

name: Swashbuckler
description: ## Swashbuckler >***Note:** This is a rogue archetype, and has no relation to the ‹class/swashbuckler› hybrid class.* ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/135› A paragon of mobile swordplay, the swashbuckler is a rogue who focuses almost exclusively on honing her skill at arms and perfecting daring acrobatic moves and elaborate flourishes that border on performance. ::ab[Martial Training (Ex)]{l=1 icon=power ability="The swashbuckler may select one martial weapon to add to her list of weapon proficiencies. In addition, she may take the ‹talent/combat trick› rogue talent up to two times." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Daring (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost passive="A swashbuckler gains a morale bonus on Acrobatics checks and saving throws against fear. @B-3f-rogue." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Offensive defense~positioning attack~powerful sneak~weapon training"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Crippling strike~entanglement of blades~redirect attack"}

name: Sylvan Trickster
description: ## Sylvan Trickster ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/77› Sylvan tricksters are rogues who model themselves after the mischievous fey of legend. Though not spellcasters, sylvan tricksters learn minor magical abilities reminiscent of those favored by fey creatures. The journey for many sylvan tricksters began in childhood, learning at an elder's knee the stories of the fey and the secrets of how to resist their tricks. Sylvan tricksters often live in areas where the boundary with the First World is thin, and a few have even been there: voluntarily or not. ::cskill{gain=kna lose=kd} ::ab[Languages]{icon=power ability="A sylvan trickster learns Sylvan as a bonus language."} ::ab[Wild Empathy (Ex)]{icon=power ability="A sylvan trickster can improve an animal's attitude. This ability functions as the ‹class/druid› ability of the ‹ability/same name»<wild_empathy›, using the sylvan trickster's rogue level as her effective druid level." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Fey Tricks]{icon=power ability="A sylvan trickster can select a witch ‹ability/hex<es› in place of a rogue talent." imp10="The sylvan trickster can select a hex or ‹ability/major hex<es› in place of a rogue talent." imp18="A sylvan trickster can select a hex, major hex, or ‹ability/grand hex<es› in place of a rogue talent." special="She cannot select any hex more than once." alter="Rogue talents"} ::ab[Resist Nature's Lure (Ex)]{l=4 icon=def ability="A sylvan trickster gains ‹ability/resist nature's lure› as the druid ability of the same name." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Fey Resistance (Ex)]{icon=def l8="A sylvan trickster gains DR 2/cold iron." incrementPlain="This damage reduction~11~3~4~2" incrementEnd="/cold iron." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Camouflage~charmer~honeyed words~major magic~minor magic~survivalist~terrain mastery"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Familiar~hide in plain sight"}

name: Thug
description: ## Thug ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/135› Some criminals steal with finesse, their victims only discovering the crime when the rogue is long gone and the coin already spent. A thug, on the other hand, cares nothing for finesse. Through both threat and violence, the thug gets what she wants by the promise of force, and has no problem making good on that promise as needed. ::ab[Frightening (Ex)]{icon=lower ability="Whenever a thug successfully uses ‹skill/Intimidate› to demoralize a creature, the duration of the ‹misc/shaken› condition is increased by 1 round. In addition, if the target is shaken for 4 or more rounds, the thug can instead decide to make the target ‹misc/frightened› for 1 round." replace=Trapfinding} ::ab[Brutal Beating (Ex)]{l=3 icon=lower ability="Whenever a thug deals sneak attack damage, she can choose to forgo 1d6 points of sneak attack damage to make the target ‹misc/sickened› for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 her rogue level. This ability does not stack with itself - only the most recent duration applies." replace="Trap sense"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Offensive defense~powerful sneak~strong impression~weapon training"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Crippling strike~deadly sneak~knock-out blow"}

name: Trapsmith
description: ## Trapsmith ‹SOURCE Advanced Player's Guide/135› Some rogues are not content with just disabling traps - they love to build them, finding a captivating beauty in the turning of gears and the slither of ropes over pulleys. The trapsmith may have started out putting together traps in order to better understand how to disable them, but for most, it's long since gone beyond that - they now relish the challenge of creating the perfect combat machine. ::ab[Careful Disarm (Ex)]{l=4 icon=def ability="Whenever a trapsmith attempts to disarm a trap using Disable Device, she does not spring the trap unless she fails by 10 or more. If she does set off a trap she was attempting to disarm, she adds double her *trap sense* bonus to avoid the trap." replace="Uncanny dodge"} ::ab[Trap Master (Ex)]{l=8 icon=power ability="Whenever a trapsmith disarms a trap using Disable Device, she can bypass it even if her check did not exceed the DC by 10 or more. If it is a magic trap that allows specific creatures to pass it without danger, she can modify which creatures it allows to pass, adding her allies and restricting enemies if she desires." replace="Improved uncanny dodge"} ::list[These rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Befuddling strike~cunning trigger~quick disable~quick trapsmith"} ::list[These advanced rogue talents complement this archetype]{link=talent hl all="Another day~frugal trapsmith~skill mastery"}

name: Elementalist Shifter
description: ## Elementalist Shifter ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/78› Rather than drawing power from bestial aspects, elementalist shifters channel power from the Inner Sphere and can take on powerful elemental forms at the cost of the greater diversity available to traditional shifters. Although the elementalist shifter's powers seem more outlandish and supernatural than those of others of their kind, they remain equally immersed in the druidic traditions; their focus is simply rooted in expressions of nature found in extraplanar regions: the planes of Air, Earth, Fire, and Water. ::ab[Languages]{icon=power info="An elementalist shifter adds Aquan, Auran, Ignan, and Terran to her list of available bonus languages." alter=Languages} ::ab[Elemental Aspect (Su)]{l=1 icon=power choice="An elementalist shifter chooses one elemental aspect (‹‹see below/#elemental-aspects››) rather than a *shifter aspect.* This ability otherwise functions as *shifter aspect.*" incrementOrd="She gains~0~5" incrementDesc=her~a incrementEnd=" elemental aspect." incrementMax=16 alter="Shifter aspect"} ::ab[Elemental Speech (Su)]{icon=power ability="When in her *elemental aspect,* an elementalist shifter gains the benefit of ‹spell/tongues› with creatures of the elemental subtype that matches her *elemental aspect.*" replace="Wild empathy"} ::ab[Elemental Strike (Su)]{l=1 icon=melee swift="An elementalist shifter can charge her melee attacks with elemental energy. The elementalist shifter can charge her attacks only with an element she has chosen with *elemental aspect.* Once charged, each melee attack the elementalist shifter makes until the start of her next turn deal additional 1d6 points of energy damage based on the element she chooses when taking this action (see ‹‹Elemental Aspects/#elemental-aspects›› below)." increment="This additional damage~0~4" incrementEnd="d6 points of energy damage." special="An elementalist shifter can't use *elemental strike* while under a polymorph effect." replace="Shifter claws"} ::ab[Elemental Form (Su)]{l=4 icon=magic-down ability="When an elementalist shifter uses *wild shape,* she is instead affected as if by ‹spell/elemental body I›, but she gains only the benefits listed in her *elemental aspect.* While in an *elemental form,* the elementalist shifter can speak only the elemental language associated with that form, and she can do so only if she knows it." alter="Wild shape"} ::ab[Omnielementalist (Su)]{head l=9 icon=boost ability="An elementalist shifter can fuse two *elemental forms* together, gaining combined powers of the different aspects and manifesting them in ways that bring to mind powerful natural weather phenomena. When the elementalist shifter takes on one minor form each from two of her *elemental aspects,* she gains an additional ability as long as she maintains the form. The effects of the abilities depend on the elemental combination, as detailed below." replace="Chimeric aspect~greater chimeric aspect"} ::ab[Ash Storm (Su)]{next icon=def ability="By combining air and fire, the elementalist shifter surrounds herself with a storm of swirling ash, granting her a 20% miss chance against ranged attacks."} ::ab[Downpour (Su)]{next icon=magic ability="The elementalist shifter combines the powers of air and water to generate a torrential downpour in her square and squares adjacent to her. This rain automatically extinguishes all nonmagical fires in her square and squares adjacent to her (including flames on creatures that have caught on fire). It also has a chance to extinguish ongoing magical fire (but not instantaneous magical fire effects such as ‹spell/fireball›) within or that enters the area, as if the elementalist shifter had cast ‹spell/dispel magic›, using her elementalist shifter level as her caster level for the effect."} ::ab[Mudslide (Su)]{next icon=aura ability="Combining the elements of earth and water causes the elementalist shifter to generate an aura of mud. This mud extends out to all squares adjacent to her and counts as ‹rule/difficult terrain›; it moves with her and vanishes when she ends her *elemental aspect.*"} ::ab[Sandstorm (Su)]{next icon=aura ability="Combining the high winds of air and fine particulates of earth produces a sandstorm that extends out to a radius of 20 feet from the elementalist shifter. All ‹rule/light level«s› in the area diminish by one step, and creatures caught in the effect take 1d6 points of nonlethal damage each round they remain within the *sandstorm.*"} ::ab[Steam Cloud (Su)]{next icon=aura ability="When the elementalist shifter enters a minor form of fire and water at the same time, the heat of fire and moisture of water generate an explosive area of steam around her out to a radius of 20 feet as per ‹spell/obscuring mist›. The mist remains in place until she ends her *elemental aspect;* it doesn't move with her."} ::ab[Volcanic Stride (Su)]{next icon=magic standard="By combining earth and fire, the elementalist shifter can damage the ground around herself. She can deform a region of natural or artificial rock in her space, turning it into difficult terrain and causing creatures that pass through it to take an amount of fire damage equal to that dealt by her *elemental strike* with no save. Affected terrain remains transformed until the shifter ends her *elemental aspect.*"} ::h3[Elemental Aspects]{jl} Elementalist shifters do not infuse their bodies with bestial qualities taken from animal aspects. Rather, they take into themselves raw elemental power from the planes of Air, Earth, Fire, and Water. The following aspects are used by the elementalist shifter archetype; they cannot be selected as aspects by other shifters. ::ab[Air]{icon=power head info="You take on the power of an air elemental, gaining the ability to fly and to control powerful gusts of wind. You take inspiration from the patterns of clouds in the sky, the tumultuous fury of the storm, and the gentle caress of a cooling breeze. Flying creatures, such as bats and birds, are your favorites. Spring is your favored season - a time when storms bring freshness to the world but that lacks the brutality of winter's devastation."} ::ab[Minor Form]{icon=boost next ability="You gain a +2 enhancement bonus to your Dexterity score." imp8="This bonus increases to +4." imp15="This bonus increases to +6."} ::ab[Major Form]{icon=magic-def next ability="Your shape changes to that of a ‹monster/Medium air elemental›. While you are in this form, you gain a fly speed of 60 feet (average maneuverability) and airborne creatures take a -1 penalty on attack and damage rolls against you." imp8="Your fly speed increases to 100 feet (perfect) and you gain the ability to transform yourself into a whirlwind as a standard action for 1 round per 2 shifter levels you have. This otherwise functions as per the ‹umr/whirlwind› universal monster rule." imp15="You gain ‹feat/Improved Natural Attack› with your slam."} ::ab[Earth]{icon=power head info="You take on the power of an earth elemental, gaining the ability to burrow through the earth and deliver powerful blows. You take comfort in caverns, mountainous regions, and areas rent by canyons and chasms, and you feel a deep kinship to burrowing animals of all types. Be it the soothing feel of fresh topsoil or the devastating fury of an earthquake, you understand the raw power of earth. Your favored season is fall - the traditional time of the harvest, when bounty from the earth is offered."} ::ab[Minor Form]{icon=magic next ability="You gain a +2 enhancement bonus to your Constitution score." imp8="This bonus increases to +4." imp15="This bonus increases to +6."} ::ab[Major Form]{icon=magic-boost-down next ability="Your shape changes to that of a ‹monster/Medium earth elemental›. While you are in this form, your base speed is reduced to 20 feet, but you gain a burrow speed of 10 feet, and you gain a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls if both you and your target are touching the ground. If the target is airborne or waterborne, you take a -4 penalty on attack and damage rolls against it. These modifiers also apply to ‹rule/bull rush› and ‹rule/overrun› combat maneuvers, whether you are initiating or resisting these kinds of attacks." imp8="Your burrow speed increases to 20 feet and you gain ‹umr/earth glide› as per the universal monster rule." imp15="You gain Improved Natural Attack with your slam."} ::ab[Fire]{icon=power head info="You take on the power of a fire elemental, becoming a being of living flame that can burn enemies and move with great speed. You enjoy regions where precipitation rarely intrudes, such as desert landscapes and dry savannas, but the slopes of volcanoes hold the greatest majesty to you. You enjoy the companionship of swiftly moving creatures and those who enjoy basking in the sun, for you empathize with their appreciation of the daytime's warmth. Forest fires are things of beauty to you, yet you respect fire and would never think to wantonly inflict it upon the natural world. Summer is your favorite season, for this is a time of heat waves and blistering sunny days."} ::ab[Minor Form]{icon=magic next ability="You gain a +2 enhancement bonus to your Dexterity score." imp8="This bonus increases to +4." imp15="This bonus increases to +6."} ::ab[Major Form]{icon=magic-def-down-power next ability="Your shape changes to that of a ‹monster/Medium fire elemental›. While you are in this form, your base speed changes to 50 feet and you gain ‹umr/immunity› to fire, ‹umr/vulnerability› to cold, and the ‹umr/burn› special attack as per the universal monster rule, dealing damage equal to your slam attack whenever a creature fails its Reflex save against that ability." imp8="You gain Improved Natural Attack with your slam." imp15="You deal fire damage equal to double your slam damage against opponents that fail their saves against your burn ability."} ::ab[Water]{icon=power head info="You take on the power of a water elemental, gaining the ability to move swiftly in water, rain down crashing blows on your enemies, and transform into a swirling vortex. You identify with aquatic animals of all types, be they water-breathing creatures such as fish, amphibians such as newts or frogs, or air-breathing mammals such as whales or walruses. The unrelenting churn of waves on the shoreline, the soothing babble of a gentle stream, and the pounding kiss of a deluge of rain all bring joy to your heart. Your favored season is winter, for it is at this time that the most powerful of storms bring water to all the world."} ::ab[Minor Form]{icon=magic next ability="You gain a +2 enhancement bonus to your Strength score." imp8="This bonus increases to +4." imp15="This bonus increases to +6."} ::ab[Major Form]{icon=magic-boost-down-magic next ability="Your shape changes to that of a ‹monster/Medium water elemental›. While you are in this form, your base speed is reduced to 20 feet but you gain a swim speed of 60 feet, and if both you and your target are touching water, you also gain a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls. If the target is touching the ground, you take a -4 penalty on attack and damage rolls against it. These modifiers apply to bull rush and overrun combat maneuvers, whether you are initiating or resisting these kinds of attacks." imp8="Your swim speed increases to 90 feet, your touch automatically extinguishes nonmagical flames of size Large or smaller, and you can dispel magical fires as per ‹spell/dispel magic› using your shifter level as your effective caster level." imp15="You gain Improved Natural Attack with your slam and the *vortex* special ability, which functions identically to the air aspect's *whirlwind* ability but can form only underwater and cannot leave the water."}

name: Fiendflesh Shifter
description: ## Fiendflesh Shifter ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/80› By forging dark pacts with extraplanar forces, fiendflesh shifters invoke sinister powers to assume the strengths of daemons, demons, or devils. Fiendflesh shifters care nothing for the natural world and are instead consumed by an ever-growing lust for power at any price. To other shifters, the fiendflesh shifter is often viewed as a monster herself - an intrusion into the natural order of things and a foe who must be sought out and destroyed. Very few druids will ever willingly ally with fiendflesh shifters; this leaves these outcasts to live bitter, lonely lives or to seek out fiendish cults or other abhorrent faiths for support and companionship. ::ab[Alignment]{icon=warning info="A fiendflesh shifter must be evil in alignment. If the fiendflesh shifter becomes nonevil, she loses all powers granted by this archetype." alter=Alignment} ::ab[Infernal Claws (Ex)]{icon=melee flavor="A fiendflesh shifter's claws are infused with the unholy power of the evil Outer Planes." l1="A fiendflesh *shifter's claws* are treated as evil weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. This ability otherwise functions as the *shifter claws* class feature." alter="Shifter claws"} ::ab[Fiendish Aspect (Su)]{l=1 icon=magic-power-melee-def swift="A fiendflesh shifter can temporarily transform her body into an amalgam of otherworldly evil creatures. While in this form, the fiendflesh shifter gains darkvision out to a range of 60 feet (or doubles the range of her darkvision if she already has it), a gore natural attack that deals 1d6 points of damage (1d4 points of damage if the shifter is Small), and DR 1/good." useL=shifter3 useUnit=minute useNC=1 imp5="The fiendflesh shifter's DR increases to 2/good and she also grows a pair of bat-like wings when in her *fiendish aspect,* granting her a fly speed of 30 feet with average maneuverability." imp10="The fiendflesh shifter's DR increases to 5/good, and the electricity and fire resistance provided by her *fiendish resilience* ability (see below) doubles while she's in her *fiendish aspect.*" imp15="The fiendflesh shifter's DR increases to 7/good and her fly speed increases to 60 feet." imp20="The fiendflesh shifter's DR increases to 10/good. She also gains ‹umr/immunity› to electricity and fire and spell resistance equal to 15 + her shifter level." replace="Wild shape~shifter aspect"} ::ab[Fiendish Resilience (Su)]{l=2 icon=def passive="A fiendflesh shifter gains a +1 natural armor bonus to her AC and ‹umr/resistance› 5 to electricity and fire, but only while unencumbered and either wearing no armor or wearing light or medium nonmetal armor." repeat="The natural armor bonus increases by 1.~4~8" incrementPlain="Her resistance to electricity and fire~0~8~10~5" replace="Defensive instinct"} ::ab[Chimeric Fiend (Su)]{head l=9 icon=def ability="When a fiendflesh shifter uses her *fiendish aspect* ability, she can gain an additional ability from the list below. The fiendflesh shifter can change which ability she gains each time she uses *fiendish aspect.*." replace="Chimeric aspect"} ::ab[Daemon]{next icon=def passive="Acid resistance 10 and a +4 profane bonus on saves against disease."} ::ab[Demon]{next icon=def passive="The shifter's electricity resistance doubles."} ::ab[Devil]{next icon=def passive="The shifter's fire resistance doubles."} ::ab[Greater Chimeric Fiend (Su)]{head l=14 icon=power ability="A fiendflesh shifter's *chimeric fiend* ability grants her additional bonuses as noted below." replace="Greater chimeric aspect"} ::ab[Daemon]{next icon=boost-def passive="The shifter gains a +4 enhancement bonus to her Constitution score and immunity to disease."} ::ab[Demon]{next icon=boost passive="The shifter gains a +4 enhancement bonus to her Strength score and increases the damage die of all natural attacks ‹misc/by one step›."} ::ab[Devil]{next icon=boost-power passive="The shifter gains a +4 enhancement bonus to her Dexterity score and ‹umr/see in darkness› as per the universal monster rule."}

name: Leafshifter
description: ## Leafshifter ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/18› Rather than assume aspects taken from the traits of natural animals, a leafshifter transforms into plant-animal hybrids that resemble ‹monster/living topiar«ies<y›. This affords the leafshifter the savage power of the animal kingdom while also granting her the strength and timelessness of plant life. ::prereq{r=Ghoran} ::ab[Shifter's Slam (Ex)]{icon=melee ability="This ability functions as the *shifter claws* class feature, except the leafshifter gains two slam attacks instead of two claw attacks. These slam attacks are made with her arms, which are covered in jagged bark and thorns, so these attacks deal bludgeoning and piercing damage." alter="Shifter claws"} ::ab[Leafshifter's Aspect (Su)]{head icon=power ability="This ability functions as the *shifter aspect* ability of the standard shifter, except a leafshifter doesn't gain the minor forms of her aspects. Instead, whenever she gains a new aspect, she chooses one of the plant focus abilities from the ‹arc-hunter/plant master› hunter archetype (listed below) to associate with her new aspect. This choice cannot be changed once made." alter="Shifter aspect"} ::ab[Assassin Vine]{next icon=boost passive="The creature gains a +2 bonus on combat maneuver checks to ‹rule/grapple›." increment="This bonus~1~7~3"} ::ab[Brambles]{next icon=def passive="When the creature is hit by an unarmed strike or natural attack, the attacker takes 1 point of piercing damage." imp8="This increases to 2 points." imp15="This becomes 3 points."} ::ab[Creeping Vine]{next icon=boost passive="The creature gains a +4 competence bonus on Climb checks." increment="This bonus~1~7~6~2"} ::ab[Giant Flytrap]{next icon=boost passive="The creature gains a +4 competence bonus on Stealth checks." increment="This bonus~1~7~6~2"} ::ab[Mushroom]{next icon=def passive="The creature gains a +4 enhancement bonus on saves against poison." increment="This bonus~1~7~6~2"} ::ab[Oak]{next icon=def passive="The creature gains a +2 enhancement bonus to CMD." increment="This bonus~1~7~4~2"} ::ab[Shrieker]{next icon=power passive="The creature gains darkvision with a range of 60 feet." imp8="The range increases by 30 feet." imp15="The creature also gains ‹umr/blindsense› with a range of 10 feet."} ::ab[Spore]{next icon=boost passive="The creature gains a +4 competence bonus on Fly checks." increment="This bonus~1~7~6~2"} ::ab[Water Lily]{next icon=boost passive="The creature gains a +4 competence bonus on Swim checks." increment="This bonus~1~7~6~2"}

name: Oozemorph

features.name: Fluidic Body (Su)
features.replaces: Chimeric aspect~greater chimeric aspect~wild shape~shifter aspect

description: ## Oozemorph **Source** ‹source/Ultimate Wilderness« pg. 81›, [official Paizo FAQ](https://paizo.com/paizo/faq/v5748nruor1hj) While most shifters are trained in druidic traditions that allow them to tap into animalistic powers, others look instead to the simplest forms of life for inspiration. Known as oozemorphs, these shifters focus on the ooze - a form of life as simple in construction as it is dangerous in combat. While some shifters consider the oozemorph to be unsettling or even vile, these shifters merely embrace a stranger form of life than most. They are not inherently evil, yet they are often misunderstood by druidic circles and these circles' shifter champions. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down info="An oozemorph is proficient with all simple weapons and light armor." replace="Weapon and armor proficiencies"} ::ab[Compression (Ex)]{icon=power ability="An oozemorph gains ‹umr/compression› as per the universal monster rule. This ability can be used regardless of the current form the oozemorph has taken."} ::ab[Fluidic Body (Su)]{icon=power-def-down replace="Chimeric aspect~greater chimeric aspect~wild shape~shifter aspect" useInc=shifter~2 useM=1 order=num info="An oozemorph's base form is not that of her race but rather that of a protoplasmic blob that has the same volume and weight. An oozemorph treats her creature type as both ‹type/ooze› and her base creature type from her race for the purposes of effects targeting creatures by type (such as ‹magic-enh/bane› weapons and a ranger's ‹ability/favored enemy›). In this form, the oozemorph is immune to critical hits and ‹misc/precision damage› and can't be flanked. However, she has no magic item slots and she cannot benefit from armor; cast spells; hold objects; speak; or use any magic item that requires activation, is held, or is worn on the body. An oozemorph reverts to this formless state whenever she is unconscious or in an area of antimagic. This is treated as a polymorph effect." move="An oozemorph can assume a humanoid form. This transformation is identical to ‹spell/alter self›, except for the base duration. Each hour after this duration, the oozemorph must succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save or revert back to her fluidic body until she rests for at least 8 hours. This save DC increases by 1 for each additional hour spent maintaining the form. Ending this transformation at any time reverts the oozemorph back to her ooze form and renders her ‹misc/fatigued› for a number of minutes equal to the number of hours she maintained the form." imp8="The oozemorph can treat this ability as ‹spell/beast shape I›" imp15="She can treat this ability as ‹spell/beast shape II› or ‹spell/giant form I›." special="*Fluidic Body* is essentially two effects in one. The first, which is a permanent part of your character once you become an oozemorph, is that your base form is now an ooze shape. Even if you lose fluidic body for some reason (‹spell/antimagic field›, violating your code of conduct, etc) your base form is still the amorphous ooze-like form. The other half of the ability is a supernatural ‹spelldef/polymorph› effect to transform into humanoid (and later bestial) forms.~~~Despite having an ooze-like shape, an oozemorph's base form is not an ooze, though it does also count as an ooze for the purposes of effects targeting creatures by type. The ooze-like form doesn't gain any abilities of the ooze creature type except as stated by the archetype itself. This form retains the base senses and land speed of the oozemorph's original race, as well as racial abilities like ‹race/dwarf«s'› *greed* or ‹race/gnome«s'› *obsession* that don't depend on shape, but it loses abilities dependent on form, including form-based speeds like ‹race/strix«'s› flight (and most other racial speeds beyond land speed), racial natural attacks like ‹race/catfolk«s'› claws, and other abilities like ‹race/tiefling«s'› prehensile tail. However, if the oozemorph possesses a racial ability denied her in her ooze-like form and transforms into a member of her own race with fluidic body, she gains the full benefits of that racial ability for that duration, even if it isn't usually granted when using *alter self* (or the appropriate spell for a non-humanoid oozemorph). An oozemorph's compression, damage reduction, and morphic weaponry function in its ooze-like form and any form it takes via fluidic body, though not in forms it takes via other polymorph effects.~~~An oozemorph can carry items floating in its mass that are considered to be attuned. When it turns into a humanoid form via fluidic body, it can equip any number of those items (even armor, which usually takes time to don), leaving the rest on the ground in its space. If it turns into an animal via fluidic form, the items meld into the new form and grant some passive benefits, as normal for polymorph effects."} ::ab[Morphic Weaponry (Ex)]{flavor="An oozemorph can create a number of natural weapons to fight with from any portion of her body, regardless of her current form." icon=melee l=1 move="An oozemorph can form two primary natural attacks that each deal 1d6 points of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, chosen by the oozemorph when she forms them." swift="An oozemorph can change the damage type of any number of her natural weapons." order=mw repeat="An oozemorph gains an additional primary natural attack.~6~9" special="The total number of natural attacks an oozemorph has at any given time includes those gained via her current form. For example, an 8th-level oozemorph who has taken the form of a wolf with *beast shape I* has a bite attack as part of that form; she can create only two additional natural attacks via *morphic weaponry,* for a total of three attacks available to her at that level. If the oozemorph later reverts to a humanoid form with no natural weapons, she can instead create three *morphic weapons.*" replace="Shifter claws"} ::ab[Ooze Empathy (Ex)]{icon=down ability="An oozemorph gains the shifter's *wild empathy* class feature, but she can use it only to influence the attitude of oozes with an Intelligence score of 2 or lower. An oozemorph can use this ability on mindless oozes; when she does so, she imparts a modicum of intellect to the ooze to allow it to respond to her commands." alter="Wild empathy"} ::ab[Damage Reduction (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def passive="An oozemorph gains DR 4/slashing while unencumbered and either wearing no armor or wearing light nonmetal armor." incrementPlain="This damage reduction~0~4~6~2" replace="Defensive instinct"} ::ab[Clinging Ooze (Ex)]{l=4 icon=power ability="When in her natural form, an oozemorph gains a climb speed of 10 feet." replace="Woodland stride"}

name: Rageshaper
description: ## Rageshaper ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/82› Not all shifters represent the balance of nature. The rageshaper is a destructive force of nature brought to bear - a wild and uncontrollable engine of annihilation fueled by wrath. Rageshapers fly into bloodletting frenzies and rain down devastation like unstoppable natural disasters. ::ab[Alignment]{icon=info-warning info="A rageshaper can be any nonlawful alignment. A rageshaper who becomes lawful cannot take any further levels in rageshaper, but he does not lose access to any rageshaper abilities he has already gained." alter=Alignment} :::ab{icon=boost head action=Ability title="Devastating Form (Su)" replace="Wild shape~shifter aspect" imp10="The rageshaper can grow up to a maximum of two size categories larger with *devastating form* and his *rage* is now treated as *greater rage.*" imp20="The rageshaper can grow up to a maximum of three size categories larger with *devastating form* and his *rage* is treated as *mighty rage.*"} A rageshaper can enter a state of intense fury, transforming into a living engine of destruction. This ability functions as the ‹class/barbarian«'s› *rage* class feature, except entering this state of fury requires a @HLfull-round_action that provokes attacks of opportunity and has additional effects as noted below. At the start of the rageshaper's next turn, he not only gains the benefit of *rage* but also grows one size category larger (though worn equipment and held items do not increase in size). Armor or clothing the rageshaper wears that doesn't accommodate his changing size immediately gains the ‹misc/broken› condition. If insufficient room is available to accommodate this change, the rageshaper attains the maximum possible size for the available space and can attempt a Strength check (using his increased Strength) to burst any enclosures in the process. If the check fails, he is constrained but not harmed by the materials enclosing him. [Look here](rule/adding_racial_hit_dice) for rules on attribute and skill bonuses and penalties due to a change of size. A rageshaper can remain in his *devastating form* for a number of rounds per day equal to his shifter level. He can dismiss *devastating form* only with a successful Will save (DC = 10 + his shifter level) made as a @HLfree_action. On a failed save, the attempted remains in *devastating form* for an additional round. If the rageshaper does not successfully end his *devastating form* before he runs out of daily rounds, the next time he fails his Will save to revert, he flies into an uncontrollable frenzy as if affected by ‹spell/confusion›, but he treats a roll of 26-50 as "attacks nearest creature." Each round the rageshaper spends in an uncontrollable frenzy, the Will save DC to exit devastating form decreases by 2. When a rageshaper ends his *devastating form* ability, he is ‹misc/fatigued› for a number of rounds equal to twice the number of rounds he spent in *devastating form.* A rageshaper cannot enter *devastating form* again while fatigued or exhausted. If a rageshaper falls unconscious, his *devastating form* ends immediately. ::: ::ab[Rage (Ex)]{next icon=boost-down flavor="Relevant text from the barbarian ability." ability="You gain a +4 morale bonus to your Strength and Constitution, as well as a +2 morale bonus on Will saves. The increase to Constitution grants you 2 hit points per Hit Dice, but these disappear when the *rage* ends and are not lost first like ‹rule/temporary hit points›." order=ap passive="While in *rage,* you take a -2 penalty to Armor Class, and you cannot use any Charisma-, Dexterity-, or Intelligence-based skills (except Acrobatics, Fly, Intimidate, and Ride) or any ability that requires patience or concentration." special="Temporary increases to Constitution, such as those gained from *rage* and spells like ‹spell/bear's endurance›, do not increase the total number of rounds that a barbarian can *rage* per day. The total number of rounds of *rage* per day is renewed after resting for 8 hours, although these hours do not need to be consecutive."} ::ab[Greater Rage (Ex)]{next icon=boost-def flavor="Relevant text from the barbarian ability." passive="When you enter a *rage,* the morale bonus to your Strength and Constitution increase to +6 and the morale bonus on your Will saves increases to +3."} ::ab[Mighty Rage (Ex)]{next icon=boost-def flavor="Relevant text from the barbarian ability." passive="When you enter a *rage,* the morale bonus to your Strength and Constitution increase to +8 and the morale bonus on your Will saves increases to +4."} ::ab[Terrible Slam (Su)]{icon=melee ability="A rageshaper can deliver blows that demolish his foes. This functions as the *shifter claws* class ability, except his natural weapons are treated as slam attacks. Additionally, rather than granting the ability to bypass different kinds of damage reduction, the rageshaper's *terrible slam* ignores some of an object's hardness." imp1="*Terrible slam* ignores 5 points of an object's hardness." incrementPlain=This~0~5~10~5 incrementEnd=" points." alter="Shifter claws"} ::ab[Invulnerable Defenses (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def flavor="A rageshaper becomes difficult to harm in his *devastating form.*" passive="Whenever the rageshaper takes on his *devastating form* and is unencumbered and either wearing no armor or wearing light or medium nonmetal armor, he gains a +2 natural armor bonus to his AC and DR 2/-." replace="Defensive instinct~chimeric aspect~greater chimeric aspect"} ::ab[Unrestrained Stride (Ex)]{l=3 icon=boost-def ability="Whenever the rageshaper is in *devastating form,* he ignores movement penalties from ‹rule/difficult terrain› and is immune to the ‹rule/entangled› condition." replace="Woodland stride"} ::ab[Terrible Leap (Ex)]{l=5 icon=power move="When a rageshaper is in his *devastating form,* he can perform a *terrible leap* without attempting an Acrobatics check, jumping any distance up to his move speed (upward movement counts as double, as when flying)." useL=shifter replace="Trackless step"}

name: Verdant Shifter
description: ## Verdant Shifter ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/83› Verdant shifters have an affinity for plants rather than animals and gain a plant-like form that grows in power as they do. Verdant shifters are the enemies of creatures that would despoil the natural world, and they seek to maintain balance with civilization and industry to ensure the sanctity of wild spaces. ::ab[Speak with Plants (Sp)]{l=1 icon=magic useMod=Charisma3 ability="A verdant shifter gains the ability to cast ‹spell/speak with plants› as a spell-like ability." replace="Wild empathy"} ::ab[Verdant Body (Su)]{l=1 icon=power-def-boost ability="A verdant shifter takes on plant qualities as vines grow over her body, flowers bloom in her hair, and bark grows from her skin. The verdant shifter is treated as both her normal creature type and a plant creature for purposes of spells or effects that target a creature by type (such as ‹magic-enh/bane› weapons and a ranger's ‹ability/favored enemy›). *Verdant body* also grants the verdant shifter a 25% immunity to critical hits and ‹misc/precision damage› (such as ‹ability/sneak attack›)." imp5="The verdant shifter gains a +2 enhancement bonus to her Constitution score." imp8="The enhancement bonus to her Constitution score increases to +4 and her immunity to critical hits increases to 50%." imp15="The enhancement bonus her Constitution score increases to +6." replace="Shifter aspect"} ::ab[Wild Armor (Ex)]{l=2 icon=def passive="A verdant shifter gains a natural armor bonus to her AC while unencumbered and either wearing no armor or wearing light or medium nonmetal armor. @B-4f2-shifter." replace="Defensive instinct"} ::ab[Plant Shape (Su)]{l=6 icon=magic ability="A verdant shifter's *wild shape* ability instead functions as ‹spell/plant shape I›." useL=shifter imp12="This ability instead functions as ‹spell/plant shape II›." imp18="It functions as ‹spell/plant shape III›." special="This ability otherwise functions as the standard *wild shape* shifter class feature." alter="Wild shape" replace="Chimeric form~greater chimeric form"}

name: Weretouched
description: ## Weretouched ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/83› Weretouched shifters are scions of lycanthropic forces, whether hereditary or supernaturally imposed. They can assume both animal and hybrid forms, as a lycanthrope does. ::ab[Lycanthrope Aspect (Su)]{l=1 icon=down-def ability="A weretouched gains the *shifter aspect* ability, except the animal aspect chosen is the only animal aspect the weretouched can gain." special="This alters her other class features, as detailed in each relevant class feature. Otherwise, this ability functions identically to *shifter aspect.*" imp5="A weretouched gains DR/silver equal to ‹misc/half› her shifter level, to a maximum of DR 10/silver at 20th level. Additionally, a weretouched shifter becomes immune to a lycanthrope's ‹umr/curse of lycanthropy›." alter="Shifter aspect"} ::ab[Lycanthropic Empathy (Ex)]{l=1 icon=boost-down ability="A weretouched gains *wild empathy* and a +4 bonus on *wild empathy* checks, but this ability works only on the type of animal she chose for her lycanthrope aspect." alter="Wild empathy"} ::ab[Lycanthropic Wild Shape (Su)]{l=4 icon=down-power-boost ability="When a weretouched uses *wild shape,* she can assume only the form of an animal of the same type as her lycanthrope aspect. However, instead of assuming a major form, she can assume a hybrid form that mixes the traits of her natural form and the major form of her aspect. While in a hybrid form, she gain a +2 size bonus to her Strength score, a +2 natural armor bonus to her AC, and all of the natural attacks and abilities listed by her major form. A weretouched also counts as being in her natural form for the purpose of determining whether she can extend her *shifter claws.*" special="A weretouched's hybrid form is roughly the same size and shape as her natural form, albeit with bestial qualities such as digitigrade legs or shaggy fur, so her equipment does not merge into her new form when she shifts between her natural form and hybrid form. In addition, the size of a weretouched's hybrid form is the same as the size of her natural form. This otherwise counts as assuming a major form using *wild shape.*" alter="Wild shape"}

name: Crossblooded
description: ## Crossblooded ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/69› A crossblooded bloodline combines the powers of two distinct heritages. In most cases, sorcerers with this bloodline are the offspring of two sorcerers from different ancestries, but occasionally a crossblooded sorcerer arises from the conjunction of other powers. A draconic sorcerer who is also the culmination of a great destiny, an abyssal sorcerer from a family that dealt with devils, and an arcane sorcerer raised from birth by fey are all possible sources for crossblooded bloodlines. The sorcerer may gain access to the skills, feats, and some of the powers of both bloodlines she is descended from, but at the cost of reduced mental clarity and choice (see *Drawbacks* below). ::ab[Bloodlines]{icon=power choice="A crossblooded sorcerer selects two different ‹ability/sorcerer_bloodlines›."} ::ab[Class Skill]{icon=skill info="A crossblooded sorcerer receives the bonus class skill from both of her bloodlines. If these are the same skill, this does not grant any additional benefit."} ::ab[Bonus Spells]{icon=learn info="A crossblooded sorcerer may select her bonus spells from either of her bloodlines. The sorcerer also has the choice to learn a lower-level bonus spell she did not choose in place of the higher-level bonus spell she would normally gain. Lower-level bonus spells learned this way always use the spell level that they would be if the sorcerer had learned them with the appropriate bonus spell.~~~For example, a 3rd-level ‹sorcbloodline/aberrant›/‹sorcbloodline/abyssal› crossblooded sorcerer has the choice of learning ‹spell/cause fear› or ‹spell/enlarge person› as her bloodline bonus spell. If she selected *cause fear* as her 3rd-level bonus spell, at 5th level she could use her new bonus spell to learn *enlarge person* instead of ‹spell/bull's strength› or ‹spell/see invisibility›, and she would add it to her list of 1st-level spells known (just as if she had learned it as her 3rd-level bonus spell)."} ::ab[Bonus Feat]{icon=power info="A crossblooded sorcerer combines the bonus feat lists from both of her bloodlines and may select her bloodline bonus feats from this combined list."} ::ab[Bloodline Arcana]{icon=power ability="A crossblooded sorcerer gains the bloodline arcana of both her bloodlines."} ::ab[Bloodline Powers]{icon=power repeatAt="A crossblooded sorcerer gains one of the two new bloodline powers available to her at this level.~1~3~9~15~20" special="At 3rd-level and above, when given the choice of a two new bloodline powers, she may instead select a lower-level bloodline power she did not previous choose."} ::ab[Drawbacks]{icon=down info="A crossblooded sorcerer has one fewer spell known at each level (including cantrips) than is presented on the sorcerer spells known table. Furthermore, the conflicting urges created by the divergent nature of the crossblooded sorcerer's dual heritage forces her to constantly take some mental effort just to remain focused on her current situation and needs. This leaves her with less mental resolve to deal with external threats. A crossblooded sorcerer always takes a -2 penalty on Will saves."}

name: Broodmaster
description: ## Broodmaster ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/78› Most summoners bond with one eidolon for their entire lives, but the broodmaster forges a link with multiple smaller eidolons that make up his brood. Separately, a broodmaster's eidolons are no match for a summoner's single eidolon, but taken as a whole, an eidolon brood makes up in quantity what it lacks in individual power. ::ab[Eidolon Brood]{l=2 icon=power ability="Instead of a single eidolon, a broodmaster summons two Small ‹sidekick/eidolon«s› to his side, each less powerful than the single eidolon of a standard summoner. Each eidolon has it own base form and associated base statistics and free evolutions. Regardless of the number of eidolons in the brood, each eidolon has the same base attack bonus and base saving throw bonuses, but the rest of the eidolons' base statistics must be divided between the eidolons, including Hit Dice (minimum 1), skill points, number of feats, armor bonus, Str/Dex bonus, evolution pool (but see below), and maximum number of natural attacks. Individual eidolons in the brood must purchase evolutions separately. Once a broodmaster decides on the forms and abilities of his eidolons, they cannot be changed until the summoner gains a level.~~~**Example:** A 2nd-level broodmaster can summon two eidolons. Each eidolon has 1 Hit Dice, BAB +2, +3 on its two ‹misc/good saves› and +0 on its bad save. The broodmaster decides to give the first eidolon 4 skill points, one feat, a +1 armor bonus, a +1 bonus to Strength, 2 points from the evolution pool, and a maximum of two attacks. The remaining 4 skill points, +1 armor bonus, +1 bonus to Dexterity, and 2 points from the evolution pool go to the second eidolon, but it gains no feats and can have only one natural attack." special="The broodmaster must dismiss all of his eidolons at one time. Likewise, all of the eidolons in a brood are banished if the broodmaster is unconscious, asleep, or killed. However, each eidolon in the brood is sent back to its home plane individually when its hit points are reduced to a negative number equal to or greater than its Constitution score." replace=Eidolon} --- The following are new class features of the broodmaster archetype. Those with the same name as the standard summoner class have slightly different rules, but otherwise work as and replace the standard summoner class features of the same name. ::ab[Brood Link (Su)]{l=2 icon=protect ability="A broodmaster forms a close bond with his eidolons. This ability works like the standard summoner *life link* ability, except the broodmaster can only sacrifice hit points to prevent damage to one eidolon in the brood at a time. If two or more eidolons in the brood take enough damage to send them back to their home plane, the broodmaster can only sacrifice hit points to prevent damage to one of them." replace="Life link"} ::ab[Bond Senses (Su)]{icon=power l2="The broodmaster can only share the senses of one eidolon in his brood at a time."} ::ab[Shield Ally (Ex)]{icon=def l4="The broodmaster or an ally can only gain the bonuses from *shield ally* once, regardless of how many eidolons in the brood are within reach."} ::ab[Maker's Call (Su)]{icon=power l6="The broodmaster can only call one eidolon in the brood to his side with each use of this ability."} ::ab[Transposition (Su)]{icon=magic l8="The broodmaster swaps his location with that of one eidolon in the brood with each use of this ability."} ::ab[Larger Brood]{icon=boost l8="The broodmaster can spend 4 evolution points from the evolution pool for the ‹evolution/large› evolution; unlike with other evolutions, he spends these 4 points before he assigns evolution points to his individual eidolons (for an 8th-level broodmaster with 11 evolution points, this leaves 7 evolution points to distribute among the eidolons). This allows him to summon two Medium eidolons, four Small eidolons, or one Medium eidolon and two Small eidolons." l13="If the broodmaster has purchased the large evolution for his brood, he can spend an additional 6 evolution points from the evolution pool for the 'huge' option of the large evolution, distributing the remaining points among his eidolons. This allows him to call two Large eidolons, four Medium eidolons, eight Small eidolons, or any similar combination in which two smaller eidolons count as one eidolon of one size larger."} ::ab[Greater Shield Ally (Su)]{icon=protect l12="The broodmaster or an ally can only gain the bonuses from *greater shield ally,* regardless of how many eidolons in the brood are within reach."} ::ab[Brood Bond (Su)]{icon=def l14="A summoner's life becomes linked to his brood. This functions as the *life bond* ability, except the broodmaster can only transfer damage to one eidolon in the brood at a time. If that eidolon takes enough damage to send it back to its home plane, all excess damage remains with the broodmaster, killing him." replace="Life bond"} ::ab[Merge Forms (Su)]{icon=def-power l16="The broodmaster can only merge with one eidolon in the brood at a time." replace="Merge forms"} ### Hoarders of Summoned Monsters The broodmaster and ‹arc-summoner/master summoner› archetypes can potentially have 5, 10, or even more summoned creatures in play. This is a deliberate feature of these archetypes, and means that the summoner can potentially be a strong candidate for "solo" adventuring by one player. However, in the hands of an inexperienced or moderately experienced player, dealing with all of those creatures in combat can take a long time, forcing other players to wait extended periods between their turns in the initiative. It is strongly recommended that GMs only allow these archetypes for experienced players, or decide on a way to speed up the summoner's turn (such as by allowing other players to control some of the summoned monsters).

name: Evolutionist
description: ## Evolutionist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/79› Changing an eidolon's evolutions is normally a slow process. As a summoner progresses in levels, his control over his eidolon's abilities increases. But an evolutionist possesses greater power over his eidolon's form, and is able to evolve his eidolon and its abilities to meet any challenge or face any threat as it comes up, seemingly on a whim. ::ab[Mutate Eidolon (Su)]{l=6 icon=power ability="An evolutionist can change his eidolon's ‹ability/evolutions› as if he had gained a level. To mutate his eidolon, the evolutionist must perform an arcane ritual that requires 24 hours of uninterrupted concentration and costs 200 gp per summoner level in material components." replace="Maker's call"} ::ab[Evolve Base Form (Su)]{l=8 icon=power ability="Whenever he gains a level, the evolutionist can change his eidolon's base form to a new base form. Once chosen, this base form is set until the evolutionist gains another summoner level." replace=Transposition} ::ab[Transmogrify (Sp)]{l=12 icon=magic ability="The evolutionist can cast ‹spell/transmogrify› as a spell-like ability once per day without the need for a material component. This ability has a casting time of 1 minute." replace="Greater shield ally"}

name: Leshy Caller
description: ## Leshy Caller ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/94› A leshy caller summons creatures from the First World and forges a bond with a leshy eidolon. ::ab[Leshy Eidolon]{icon=info info="When a leshy caller summons her eidolon, the eidolon's body is created from extraplanar plant material and imbued with the intelligence of a leshy spirit. Its statistics are changed from those of a standard eidolon as shown below."} ::ab[Type]{icon=info info="The eidolon is still an outsider, and its statistics don't change, but it also counts as a plant. As it isn't truly a plant, it doesn't gain the plant immunities."} ;;;ab{head title="Base Form" icon=info action=Info alter=Eidolon} The leshy caller chooses one of the base forms listed below for her eidolon. When the eidolon is summoned in an environment matching one of these base forms, the leshy caller can change the eidolon's base form to the matching form by sacrificing one daily use of her *summon nature's ally* ability as a @HL[free action]. Plant eidolon base forms are as follows. :::block{title="Cactus (Desert)"} ::row[Size]{info=Medium} ::row[Speed]{info="30 ft."} ::row[AC]{info="+2 natural armor"} ::row[Saves]{info="Fort (good), Ref (good), Will (bad)"} ::row[Attack]{info="sting (1d4)"} ::row[Ability Scores]{info="Str 14, Dex 14, Con 13, Int 7, Wis 10, Cha 11"} ::row[Free Evolutions]{info="‹evolution/limbs› (arms), limbs (legs), ‹evolution/sting›"} ::: :::block{title="Conifer (Forest, Mountain)"} ::row[Size]{info=Medium} ::row[Speed]{info="30 ft."} ::row[AC]{info="+2 natural armor"} ::row[Saves]{info="Fort (good), Ref (bad), Will (good)"} ::row[Attack]{info="2 claws (1d4)"} ::row[Ability Scores]{info="Str 14, Dex 12, Con 15, Int 7, Wis 10, Cha 11"} ::row[Free Evolutions]{info="‹evolution/claws›, ‹evolution/limbs› (arms), limbs (legs)"} ::: :::block{title="Fungus (Swamp, Underground)"} ::row[Size]{info=Medium} ::row[Speed]{info="30 ft."} ::row[AC]{info="+2 natural armor"} ::row[Saves]{info="Fort (good), Ref (good), Will (bad)"} ::row[Attack]{info="bite (1d6)"} ::row[Ability Scores]{info="Str 14, Dex 14, Con 13, Int 7, Wis 10, Cha 11"} ::row[Free Evolutions]{info="‹evolution/bite›, ‹evolution/limbs› (arms), limbs (legs)"} ::: :::block{title="Leaf (Forest, Jungle, Swamp)"} ::row[Size]{info=Medium} ::row[Speed]{info="30 ft."} ::row[AC]{info="+2 natural armor"} ::row[Saves]{info="Fort (good), Ref (good), Will (bad)"} ::row[Attack]{info="slam (1d8)"} ::row[Ability Scores]{info="Str 16, Dex 12, Con 13, Int 7, Wis 10, Cha 11"} ::row[Free Evolutions]{info="‹evolution/limbs› (arms), limbs (legs), ‹evolution/slam›"} ::: :::block{title="Seaweed (Aquatic)"} ::row[Size]{info=Medium} ::row[Speed]{info="20 ft., swim 40 ft."} ::row[AC]{info="+2 natural armor"} ::row[Saves]{info="Fort (good), Ref (good), Will (bad)"} ::row[Attack]{info="slam (1d8)"} ::row[Ability Scores]{info="Str 12, Dex 14, Con 15, Int 7, Wis 10, Cha 11"} ::row[Free Evolutions]{info="‹evolution/limbs› (arms), ‹evolution/slam›, ‹evolution/swim› (2)"} ::: ;;; ::ab[Summon Nature's Ally (Sp)]{icon=magic ability="A leshy caller can cast ‹spell/summon nature's ally› as a spell-like ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + her Charisma modifier." info="At levels where a regular summoner would gain access to a new level of *summon monster* as a spell-like ability, the leshy caller instead gains the equivalent *summon nature's ally* spell; at 19th level, she can cast ‹spell/summon nature's ally IX› or ‹spell/gate›." passive="When a leshy caller gains a *summon nature's ally* spell as a spell-like ability, she adds it to her class spell list (though she must still select it as a spell known if she wants to gain the ability to cast it as a normal spell). She adds ‹monster/leaf leshy«s›, ‹monster/gourd leshy«s›, ‹monster/fungus leshy«s›, ‹monster/seaweed leshy«s›, and ‹monster/lotus leshy«s› to her list of creatures for *summon nature's ally I, II, III, IV,* and *V,* respectively." order=anp alter="Summon monster"}

name: Master Summoner
description: ## Master Summoner ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/80› Most summoners forge a bond with a single, powerful eidolon, but some summoners seek to control a variety of creatures. The master summoner sacrifices the power of his eidolon in favor of summoning a plethora of otherworldly creatures to aid him. ::ab[Lesser Eidolon]{icon=down info="A master summoner's class level is halved (minimum 1) for the purposes of determining his ‹sidekick/eidolon«'s› abilities, Hit Dice, evolution pool, and so on. The eidolon otherwise functions as normal." replace=Eidolon} ::ab[Summoning Mastery (Sp)]{l=1 icon=magic-boost ability="A master summoner can cast ‹spell/summon monster I› as a spell-like ability a number of times per day equal to 5 + his Charisma modifier. The summoner can use this ability when his eidolon is summoned." special="Only one *summon monster* spell may be in effect while the eidolon is summoned. If the summoner's eidolon is not summoned, the number of creatures that can be summoned with this ability is only limited by its uses per day. This ability otherwise functions as the summoner's normal *summon monster I* ability. Other than these restrictions, there is no limit to how many *summon monster* or ‹spell/gate› spells the summoner can have active at one time." replace="Summon monster I~shield ally"} ::ab[Augment Summoning]{l=2 icon=power ability="A master summoner gains ‹feat/Augment Summoning› as a bonus feat. He does not have to meet any requirements for this feat." replace="Bond senses"} ### Hordes of Summoned Monsters The ‹arc-summoner/broodmaster› and master summoner archetypes can potentially have 5, 10, or even more summoned creatures in play. This is a deliberate feature of these archetypes, and means that the summoner can potentially be a strong candidate for "solo" adventuring by one player. However, in the hands of an inexperienced or moderately experienced player, dealing with all of those creatures in combat can take a long time, forcing other players to wait extended periods between their turns in the initiative. It is strongly recommended that GMs only allow these archetypes for experienced players, or decide on a way to speed up the summoner's turn (such as by allowing other players to control some of the summoned monsters).

name: Synthesist
description: ## Synthesist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/81› Rather than summon an eidolon to serve by his side, the synthesist fuses his eidolon's essence to his own. Instead of two creatures, the synthesist is a fusion of the summoner and eidolon into a single being. :::ab{title="Fused Eidolon" action=Ability icon=power-boost-def-down replace="Eidolon~bond senses~life bond"} A synthesist summons the essence of a powerful outsider to meld with his own being. The synthesist wears the eidolon like translucent, living armor. The eidolon mimics all of the synthesist's movements, and the synthesist perceives through the eidolon's senses and speaks through its voice, as the two are now one creature. The synthesist directs all of the eidolon's actions while fused, perceives through its senses, and speaks through its voice, as the two are now one creature. While fused with his eidolon, the synthesist uses the eidolon's Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution, but retains his own Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma. The synthesist gains the eidolon's hit points as ‹rule/temporary hit points›. When these hit points reach 0, the eidolon is killed and sent back to its home plane. The synthesist uses the eidolon's base attack bonus, and gains the eidolon's armor and natural armor bonuses and modifiers to ability scores. The synthesist also gains access to the eidolon's special abilities and the eidolon's evolutions. The synthesist is still limited to the eidolon's maximum number of natural attacks. The eidolon has no skills or feats of its own. The eidolon must be at least the same size as the synthesist. The eidolon must have ‹evolution/limbs› for the synthesist to cast spells with somatic components. The eidolon's temporary hit points can be restored with the ‹spell/rejuvenate eidolon› spell. While fused, the synthesist loses the benefits of his armor. He counts both as his original type and as an outsider for any effect related to type, whichever is worse for the synthesist. Spells such as ‹spell/banishment› or ‹spell/dismissal› work normally on the eidolon, but the synthesist is unaffected. Neither the synthesist nor his eidolon can be targeted separately, as they are fused into one creature. The synthesist and eidolon cannot take separate actions. While fused with his eidolon, the synthesist can use all of his own abilities and gear, except for his armor. In all other cases, this ability functions as the summoner's normal eidolon ability (for example, the synthesist cannot use his *summon monster* ability while the eidolon is present). ::: The following class abilities function differently for synthesist summoners. ::ab[Fused Link (Su)]{l=1 icon=protect ability="The synthesist forms a close bond with his eidolon. Whenever the temporary hit points from his eidolon would be reduced to 0, the summoner can, as a @HLfree_action, sacrifice any number of his own hit points. Each hit point sacrificed this way prevents 1 point of damage done to the eidolon (thus preventing the loss of the summoner's temporary hit points), preventing the eidolon from being killed and sent back to its home plane." replace="Life link"} ::ab[Shielded Meld (Ex)]{l=4 icon=def passive="Whenever the synthesist is fused with his eidolon, he gains a +2 shield bonus to his Armor Class and a +2 circumstance bonus on his saving throws." replace="Shield ally"} ::ab[Maker's Jump (Sp)]{l=6 icon=magic useInc=summoner~6 useF="6~1" ability="Whenever the synthesist is fused with his eidolon, the synthesist can cast ‹spell/dimension door› as a spell-like ability using his caster level. This ability only affects the fused synthesist and eidolon." replace="Maker's call~transposition"} ::ab[Greater Shielded Meld (Ex)]{l=12 icon=def passive="Whenever the synthesist is fused with his eidolon, he gains a +4 shield bonus to his Armor Class and a +4 circumstance bonus on his saving throws." replace="Greater shield ally"} ::ab[Split Forms (Su)]{l=16 icon=magic useL=summoner useNC swift="The synthesist and his fused eidolon can split into two creatures: the synthesist and the eidolon. Both have the same evolutions. The synthesist emerges in a square adjacent to the eidolon if possible. All effects and spells currently targeting the fused synthesist-eidolon affect both the synthesist and the eidolon." special="The synthesist can end this effect at any time as a @HLfull-round_action. For the duration of this effect, the eidolon functions as a normal eidolon of the summoner's class level." replace="Merge forms"}

name: Avenging Beast

features.name: Spellcasting
features.replaces: Vigilante talents gained at 4th, 8th, 10th, 14th, and 16th level

description: ## Avenging Beast ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/96› Some vigilantes turn to natural traditions and supernatural forces to transform into beasts, unleashing a primal fury on their foes before returning to an ordinary guise. ::cskill{gain=kna~spc lose=dd~ke~perf~soh} ::ab[Skill Ranks per Level]{icon=down info="An avenging beast gains a number of skill ranks equal to 4 + his Intelligence modifier at each level, instead of 6 + his Intelligence modifier." alter="Skill ranks per level"} ::ab[Animal Mask (Ex)]{icon=power info="An avenging beast gains an ornate animal-headed mask that is a focus for his power and must be worn when assuming his vigilante identity. This mask symbolizes one specific animal, and the animal cannot be changed once chosen.
