Without this mask, an avenging beast cannot assume his vigilante identity." special="An avenging beast who loses his mask can replace it after 1 week through a specialized ritual that takes 8 hours to complete and costs 200 gp per avenging beast level." alter="Dual identity"} ::ab[Spellcasting]{icon=learn-magic ability="An avenging beast casts divine spells as a ‹class/hunter› and uses the ‹main/spells_>hunter«'s spell list›." replace="Vigilante talents gained at 4th, 8th, 10th, 14th, and 16th level"} ::ab[Patron Spells]{icon=learn ability="An avenging beast selects a ‹ability/patron animal<s› type. This ability functions like the ‹spell/beast shape I› spell, except as noted here. The effect lasts for 1 hour per druid level, or until you change back." special="You lose your ability to speak while in animal form because you are limited to the sounds that a normal, untrained animal can make, but you can communicate normally with other animals of the same general grouping as your new form. (The normal sound a wild parrot makes is a squawk, so changing to this form does not permit speech.)"}

name: Brute
description: ## Brute ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/54› Either through the results of magical experimentation or bizarre natural sparks, some vigilantes can transform into brutish versions of themselves, becoming larger, more terrifying in appearance, and far more formidable in combat - though at a price. ::ab[Chaotic Vigilante (Ex)]{icon=warning info="A brute's vigilante alignment must be chaotic, and his vigilante identity and his social identity must be within one step of each other on the alignment axis." alter="Dual identity"} ::ab[Brutish Fortitude (Ex)]{icon=def-down info="A brute's base Fortitude save bonus from his vigilante levels is equal to 2 + half his vigilante level, and his base Reflex and Will save bonuses are equal to 1/3 his vigilante level." alter="Base saving throws"} ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiency]{icon=down-power info="A brute isn't proficient with medium armor or martial weapons. However, he gains ‹feat/Improved Unarmed Strike› as a bonus feat." alter="Armor and weapon proficiencies"} :::ab{title="Brute Form (Ex)" action=Ability icon=power-down replace="Vigilante specialization" imp5="While in his vigilante identity, the brute gains a +1 bonus on melee attack and damage rolls." increment="This bonus~7~6."} Though it is sometimes difficult to maintain, a brute has a measure of control over his abilities. While in his vigilante identity, a brute becomes one size category larger, gaining no ability score adjustments but otherwise gaining [all adjustments](rule/adding_racial_hit_dice) for his new size, including [additional reach](rule/big_and_little_creatures_in_combat), if appropriate. A brute's vigilante identity is savage and dangerous. While in his vigilante identity, the brute takes a -2 penalty to AC, as well as to all ability checks and skill checks that rely on Charisma, Dexterity, or Intelligence. Furthermore, the brute cannot use any Charisma-, Dexterity-, or Intelligence-based skill (except Acrobatics, Fly, Intimidate, and Ride) or any ability that requires patience or concentration (such as spellcasting). When a brute is in mortal peril, such as when combat starts, if he is in his social identity, he must succeed at a Will save (DC = 20 + 1/2 his vigilante level) or enter his vigilante identity. Entering his vigilante identity in this way is a horrifying and painful process that takes 1 full round, during which he is ‹rule/flat-footed›, and it typically allows his enemies to see his transformation and learn his identity. The brute's vigilante identity can't always tell friend from foe. While he still attacks enemies preferentially during a battle, when there are no more enemies around, each round he must succeed at a Will save (DC = 20 + 1/2 his vigilante level) or continue fighting against his allies or bystanders. Allies can use the ‹rule/aid another› action to assist this saving throw with skills like Diplomacy, as they attempt to calm him down. On a successful save, he slowly turns back to his social identity over the course of 1 minute (or shorter if he has a social talent that reduces that time). A brute uses his vigilante level as his base attack bonus, but only while he is in his vigilante identity. He uses his normal base attack bonus to qualify for feats and other abilities, although when in his vigilante identity, he uses his increased base attack bonus to determine the effects of feats (such as ‹feat/Power Attack›) and other abilities. A brute's mundane clothes and armor do not increase in size with him, and any such items he wears while changing into his vigilante identity lose one-quarter of their hit points. Magical clothes and accessories increase in size with the vigilante, however (though his magical armor and weapons initially do not, as normal). A brute can stay in his vigilante identity for up to 2 hours at a time, for a total of up to 6 hours in a 24-hour period. When threatened in his vigilante identity, he has the potential to damage bystanders or allies. After switching from his vigilante identity to his social identity, he is ‹misc/fatigued› for the same amount of time (rounds, minutes, or hours) that he spent in his vigilante identity and cannot remove or ignore this fatigue by any means except by waiting the appropriate amount of time. If he enters his vigilante identity while fatigued, once he switches back to his social identity, he becomes ‹misc/exhausted› for the amount of time he just spent in his vigilante identity, and he also can't remove or ignore the exhaustion by any means other than waiting the appropriate length of time. A character with immunity to fatigue or exhaustion cannot adopt a brute form at all; that immunity prevents the transformation as an effect that would cause fatigue or exhaustion. An exhausted brute can only enter his vigilante identity for a number of rounds equal to ‹misc/half› his vigilante level (minimum 1); following these rounds, the brute immediately falls unconscious, or into a stupor if he is somehow prevented from falling unconscious. In this state, a brute can be healed as normal (and, if he has 0 hit points or more, he returns to consciousness after receiving any amount of magical healing or a DC 15 Heal check), but he cannot enter his vigilante identity for 1 hour. ::: ::ab[Brute Talents]{head icon=power info="A brute can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general vigilante talents." alter="Vigilante talents"} ::ab[Awesome Blow (Ex)]{next prereq="8th-level vigilante" flavor="The brute has learned that his body is his most formidable weapon." icon=power ability="He gains the ‹feat/Awesome Blow› monster feat as a bonus feat, but only while in his vigilante identity. He can ignore the feat's prerequisites. His *awesome blow* combat maneuver deals an amount of damage equal to 1d6 plus his Strength modifier, or his unarmed strike damage, whichever is better." imp16="The brute can use Awesome Blow against a creature of any size, and he can ‹rule/bull rush›, ‹rule/drag›, ‹rule/reposition›, and ‹rule/trip› creatures of any size."} ::ab[Heavy Punches (Ex)]{next flavor="The brute eschews civilized combat and prefers to wade into a fight with his fists swinging." icon=melee-boost ability="While in his vigilante identity, the brute's unarmed strikes deal damage as if he were a ‹class/monk› of his size and vigilante level." special="If he has levels in other classes that provide monk advancement for unarmed strike damage, his vigilante level stacks with those levels whenever he is in his vigilante identity." imp1="Your unarmed strike deals 1d6 (Medium) or 1d8 (Large) damage." imp4="Your unarmed strike now deals 1d8 (Medium) or 2d6 (Large) damage." imp8="Your unarmed strike now deals 1d10 (Medium) or 2d8 (Large) damage." imp12="Your unarmed strike now deals 2d6 (Medium) or 3d6 (Large) damage." imp16="Your unarmed strike now deals 2d8 (Medium) or 3d8 (Large) damage." imp20="Your unarmed strike now deals 2d10 (Medium) or 4d8 (Large) damage."} ::ab[Scale Surroundings (Ex)]{next prereq="4th-level vigilante" flavor="Instead of letting physical barriers stop him, the brute can simply climb over them." icon=power ability="He gains a climb speed of 30 feet when he is in his vigilante identity."} ::ab[Sizing Equipment (Ex)]{next flavor="The brute has learned how to adjust his magic armor so that it provides him some protection while in his vigilante identity." icon=boost-def passive="Magic armor the brute wears that is sized for his social identity provides an armor bonus equal to its normal armor bonus - 1 while he is in his vigilante identity. In addition, wielding a magic weapon properly sized for his social identity deals damage as if it were a magic weapon properly sized for his vigilante identity, but it imposes a -1 penalty on attack rolls." imp6="He takes no penalties when using such weapons and armor, and his weapons and armor work in all ways (including damage dice) as if they were of the vigilante's new size." special="This talent only applies to magic arms and armor; inappropriately sized mundane arms and armor are not affected."} ::ab[Total Destruction (Ex)]{next order=as flavor="The brute is adept at rampaging through an area, throwing whatever is available at his opponents." icon=power ability="The brute gains ‹feat/Throw Anything› as a bonus feat." standard="While in his vigilante identity, he can throw any unattended object up to two size categories smaller than he is up to 60 feet if he is Medium and 80 feet if he is Large. This deals 1d6 points of bludgeoning damage if he is Medium or 1d8 if he is Large, and the brute adds 1-1/2 times his Strength modifier to this damage." imp8="He can also throw a creature up to two size categories smaller than himself, but he must succeed at a combat maneuver check against that creature's CMD to do so. The thrown creature lands ‹rule/prone› and takes an amount of damage equal to the damage dealt to the target of the throw (as noted above), whether the brute hits or misses." imp16="He can instead throw an object one size category larger than himself at creatures within a 10-foot radius from the object's point of impact. These creatures must succeed at a Reflex save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the brute's vigilante level + his Strength modifier) or take 1d6 points of damage per vigilante level."} ::ab[Tear Them Apart (Ex)]{l=20 icon=melee-boost flavor="A brute has learned how to tear at his enemies' bodies when he hits with multiple attacks." ability="When he takes a full attack action while in his vigilante identity, if a brute hits an opponent with at least two attacks, he deals an additional 1d10 points of damage plus 1-1/2 times his Strength modifier. If he hits an opponent with four attacks during a full attack action while in his vigilante identity, he instead deals an additional 3d10 points of damage plus 1-1/2 times his Strength modifier. The damage occurs after he has taken his last attack with the full attack action. This counts as a ‹umr/rend› and does not stack with other abilities that grant rend." replace="Vengeance strike"}

name: Cabalist
description: ## Cabalist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/55› Appearing to be an upstanding member of society, the cabalist clandestinely follows the tenets of a secret society. Practice with blood sacrifices, necromancy, and shadow magic gives a cabalist a reputation as a sinister and dangerous vigilante. ::cskill{gain=ka~spc lose=dd~ke~per~sur} ::ab[Skill Ranks per Level]{icon=down info="The cabalist gains a number of skill ranks equal to 4 + his Intelligence modifier at each level, instead of 6 + his Intelligence modifier skill ranks." alter="Skill ranks per level"} ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiencies]{icon=down-power ability="A cabalist is not proficient with medium armor. Like a ‹class/magus›, he can cast cabalist spells while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance." alter="Armor and weapon proficiencies"} ::ab[Spellcasting and Spellbook]{icon=magic ability="A cabalist casts arcane spells and cantrips as a magus. He prepares spells using a spellbook, choosing them from the 6th-level and lower spells from the ‹main/witch spell« list›; higher-level witch spells are not on the cabalist's spell list." special="A cabalist has a spellbook that functions in the same way as a magus's spellbook but uses the 6th-level and lower spells from the witch spell list." replace="4th-, 8th-, 10th-, 14th-, and 16th-level vigilante talents"} ::ab[Spill Blood (Ex)]{icon=boost ability="A cabalist can cause bleeding when he deals piercing or slashing damage with a melee attack (or a ranged attack within 30 feet) against a living foe who is unaware of his presence, who considers him an ally, or who is denied its Dexterity bonus to AC. The amount of ‹rule/bleed› damage is equal to the cabalist's level." special="A cabalist can't deal this bleed damage to a creature with total ‹rule/concealment›." replace="Vigilante specialization"} ::ab[Cabalist Talents]{head icon=power info="A cabalist can select from the following vigilante talents, in addition to general vigilante talents." alter="Vigilante talents"} ::ab[Bond of Blood (Sp, Su)]{next icon=aid flavor="The cabalist has a magical bond to life-giving blood." ability="When the cabalist deals bleed damage or 5 or more points of piercing or slashing damage to an adjacent living creature, he gains 1d6 ‹rule/temporary hit points›. These temporary hit points last for 1 hour, and the cabalist can't gain temporary hit points again from *bond of blood* during that hour (even if he loses all the temporary hit points from *bond of blood* before that time)." increment="The number of temporary hit points gained~0~4" incrementEnd="d6." imp4="The cabalist can also activate ‹spell/blood armor› once per day as a spell-like ability as a @HLswift_action."} ::ab[Familiar (Ex)]{next icon=power ability="The cabalist gains a ‹sidekick/familiar›, using his vigilante level as his effective wizard level. The ‹ability/familiar› also has a social identity as a seemingly normal animal, though cabalists with outlandish familiars might still need to hide them."} ::ab[Living Shadow (Sp)]{next prereq="12th-level vigilante" icon=magic ability="Once per day, the cabalist can become a living shadow as though he were using ‹spell/shadow body›. This effect lasts for 1 round per vigilante level, and the cabalist can't cast spells while in this form." imp14="The cabalist can remain as a living shadow for 1 minute per vigilante level instead, and can cast spells while he is a living shadow."} ::ab[Necromantic Focus (Ex)]{next icon=power-learn ability="The cabalist gains ‹feat/Spell Focus› (necromancy) as a bonus feat. He also adds the following additional spells to his spellbook, provided he can cast spells of the given level." s1="Cause fear" s2="Blindness/deafness" s3="Bestow curse" s4=Poison s5="Feast on fear" s6="Slay living"} ::ab[Shadow Jump (Su)]{next prereq="10th-level vigilante" icon=magic ability="The cabalist gains the ‹pclass/shadowdancer«'s› *shadow jump* ability with an effective shadowdancer level equal to his vigilante level - 6. If he has levels in shadowdancer, those levels stack with his vigilante levels to determine the total distance per day he can shadow jump (to a maximum of 320 feet per day)." imp4="*A shadowdancer gains the ability to travel between shadows as if by means of a ‹spell/dimension door› spell. The limitation is that the magical transport must begin and end in an area with at least some dim light. A shadowdancer can jump up to a total of 40 feet each day in this way; this may be a single jump of 40 feet or four jumps of 10 feet each.*" imp6="*The total distance increases to 80 feet.*" imp8="*The total distance increases to 160 feet.*" imp10="*The total distance increases to 320 feet.*" special="*This amount can be split among many jumps, but each one, no matter how small, counts as a 10-foot increment.*"} ::ab[Tattoo Chamber (Su)]{next icon=magic order=a2 ability="The cabalist can magically absorb items through a tattoo on his hand or wrist and easily retrieve them or activate their magical abilities without making them manifest. The items seemingly disappear into the tattoo, but actually enter an extradimensional space that the cabalist can access via the tattoo. Stowing an item in this way requires a @HLfull-round_action, and the space can store a number of items equal to 1 + ‹misc/one-third› of his vigilante level. These items must be items the cabalist can hold in one hand." ability2="Retrieving a stowed item requires mentally activating the tattoo as a @HLswift_action. The item appears in the cabalist's hand, so worn items must still be donned to gain their benefits." special="The cabalist can also activate any ‹misc/spell-trigger› abilities of a stored item as though he were wielding the item, producing the magic effect from his tattoo rather than from the item. If the cabalist dies while items are within his tattoo chamber, those items fade into existence within 5 feet of the corpse."} ::ab[Bloodbound Spell (Ex)]{l=5 icon=lower flavor="A cabalist gets an advantage when casting spells against bleeding foes." ability="Whenever the cabalist casts a spell against a foe that is taking bleed damage, the foe takes a -1 penalty on its saving throw against the spell (or to its AC if the spell requires an attack roll). This penalty increases to -2 if the spell is from the necromancy school." replace="Startling appearance"} ::ab[Bloody Horror (Ex)]{l=11 icon=lower free="When a cabalist casts a spell and one of the targets (or one creature in the area for an area spell) is taking bleed damage, the cabalist can make an Intimidate check to demoralize all targets of the spell (or all creatures in the area for an area spell). The cabalist rolls only one Intimidate check and applies the result to all the targets." special="Once a creature has been the target of this ability (regardless of whether or not it was successful), it is immune to that cabalist's bloody horror for 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear effect." replace="Frightening appearance"} ::ab[Shadowy Appearance (Sp)]{l=17 order=ai icon=def-magic flavor="A cabalist becomes cloaked in shadow while in his vigilante identity." ability="He gains a continuous 20% miss chance (as per ‹spell/blur›). The cabalist can deactivate or reactivate this effect as a @HLstandard_action." immediate="Once per day, he can gain the benefits of ‹spell/greater invisibility› for 1d6 rounds." replace="Stunning appearance"}

name: Gunmaster
description: ## Gunmaster ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/57› Firearms can be potent tools for striking fear into the hearts of enemies, and canny vigilantes use this to their advantage. Gunmasters brandish firearms like extensions of their will, taking down their foes with deadly accuracy and skill. ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiencies]{icon=power-down info="A gunmaster is proficient with all firearms but not with martial weapons or medium armor." alter="Weapon and armor proficiencies"} ::ab[Gunmaster]{icon=power ability="A gunmaster gains the ‹class/gunslinger«'s› gunsmith ability. Additionally, the ‹feat/Gunsmithing› bonus feat allows the gunmaster to repair and restore his initial battered firearm as if he were a gunslinger." imp5="The gunmaster gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with all firearms." increment="This bonus~5~4" replace="Vigilante specialization" head} ::ab[Gunsmith]{flavor="Text from the gunslinger class ability." next icon=power ability="You gain ‹feat/Gunsmithing› as a bonus feat, and one of the following firearms of your choice: ‹eq-weapon/blunderbuss›, ‹eq-weapon/musket›, or ‹eq-weapon/pistol›. Your starting weapon is battered, and only you know how to use it properly. All other creatures treat your gun as if it had the ‹misc/broken› condition. If the weapon already has the broken condition, it does not work at all for anyone else trying to use it." special="This starting weapon can only be sold for scrap (it's worth 4d10 gp when sold)."} ::ab[Gunmaster Talents]{head icon=power info="A gunmaster can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general vigilante talents." alter="Vigilante talents"} ::ab[Deadeye (Ex)]{next icon=boost useInc=vigilante~4~2 useF="2~1~4" ability="The gunmaster can resolve an attack against touch AC instead of normal AC when firing one increment beyond his firearm's first range increment. The gunmaster still takes the -2 penalty on attack rolls for shooting a target outside the firearm's first range increment." special="A gunmaster can spend multiple daily uses to resolve an attack at a further range increment (for instance, he can spend three uses to resolve an attack three increments beyond his first range increment)."} ::ab[Death's Shot (Ex)]{next icon=power prereq="20th-level vigilante" immediate="Three times per day, when the gunmaster scores a critical hit, he can attempt to kill his enemy instantly. When the gunmaster uses this talent, the target must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw with a DC equal to 10 + 1/2 the gunmaster's vigilante level + his Dexterity modifier. On a failed saving throw, the target dies instantly."} ::ab[Gunmaster Initiative (Ex)]{next icon=boost prereq="4th-level vigilante" ability="The gunmaster gains a +2 bonus on initiative checks. Furthermore, if he has the ‹feat/Quick Draw› feat, his hands are free and unrestrained, and the firearm is not hidden, he can draw a single firearm as part of the initiative check."} ::ab[Lightning Reload (Ex)]{next icon=power prereq="12th-level vigilante" useInc=vigilante~2 swift="A gunmaster can reload a single barrel of a one-handed or two-handed firearm once per round. If he has the ‹feat/Rapid Reload› feat or is using an alchemical cartridge (or both), he can reload a single barrel of the weapon as a @HLfree_action each round instead." provokes=No} ::ab[Quick Clear (Ex)]{next standard="Once per day, the gunmaster can remove the broken condition from a single firearm he is currently wielding, as long as that condition was gained by a firearm misfire." imp12="Once per day, when the gunmaster rolls a misfire with a gun that has the broken condition, she can prevent the gun from exploding, though it retains the broken condition." icon=power} ::ab[Nimble (Ex)]{l=4 icon=def passive="A gunmaster gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC while wearing light or no armor. Anything that causes the gunmaster to lose her Dexterity bonus to AC also causes the gunmaster to lose this dodge bonus." increment="This bonus~6~4" replace=Unshakable}

name: Magical Child
description: ## Magical Child ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/57› Some vigilantes, no matter their age, carry a spark of capricious whimsy under which flows a powerful current of magic and wonder. They keep these wondrous abilities secret, though they are aided in their endeavors by creatures just as magical as they are. ::cskill{gain=ka~kp~spc lose=dd~ke~per~sur} ::ab[Skill Ranks per Level]{icon=down info="A magical child gains a number of skill ranks equal to 4 + her Intelligence modifier at each level, instead of the normal 6 + her Intelligence modifier skill ranks." alter="Skill ranks per level"} ::ab[Weapon and Armor Proficiencies]{icon=down-power info="A magical child is not proficient with medium armor. She can cast summoner spells (see spellcasting below) while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance." alter="Armor and weapon proficiencies"} ::ab[Spellcasting]{icon=learn-magic ability="A magical child casts arcane spells and cantrips as an unchained summoner. She can cast any spell she knows without preparing it ahead of time, assuming she has not yet used up her allotment of spells per day for the spell's level, and she chooses her spells known from the ‹main/unchained summoner spell« list› (she cannot choose spells that would affect an eidolon)." special="A magical child's selection of spells is extremely limited; use the Summoner Spells Known table of the ‹class/unchained summoner› to determine how many spells the magical child knows at each level. A magical child needs to commune with her *animal guide* (see below) for 1 hour in order to replenish her daily spell slots." replace="4th-, 8th-, 10th-, 14th-, and 16th-level vigilante talents"} ::ab[Transformation Sequence (Su)]{icon=boost-down ability="A magical child's transformation between identities is assisted by magic. This makes it faster than usual, but also more noticeable. A magical child can normally transform between her identities in 5 rounds, though this improves to a @HLstandard_action with the ‹soctalent/quick change› social talent and a @HLswift_action with the ‹soctalent/immediate change› social talent. However, the transformation is quite a spectacle, involving loud sounds or music, brilliant colorful energies, and swift motions."} ::ab[Animal Guide (Ex)]{icon=power l1="A magical child starts play with a magical spirit guide in the form of a ‹sidekick/familiar›, using her vigilante level as her effective wizard level. The ‹ability/familiar› also has a social identity as a seemingly normal animal, though vigilantes with outlandish familiars might still need to hide the familiar." imp3="The magical child's familiar reveals another aspect of its form, and its vigilante identity changes into a creature on the ‹feat/Improved Familiar› list that would be available to a 3rd-level spellcaster (the animal guide's social identity always remains as the original normal animal). The Improved Familiar feat's alignment restrictions apply to this ability, but only the magical child's vigilante identity needs to have an alignment that fulfills the alignment requirements of the improved familiar. The familiar's new vigilante form choices are permanent." imp5="The familiar can change its vigilante identity to a new familiar available at 5th level." imp7="The familiar can change its vigilante identity to a new familiar available at 7th level." imp9="The familiar gains the ‹umr/change shape› universal monster ability if it doesn't already have it. It can use this ability at will when in its vigilante identity to transform into any of its previous vigilante identities." special="In vigilante form, a magical child's familiar gains an amount of DR/magic equal to her vigilante level. This doesn't stack with any DR/magic that her vigilante form might already possess. If a magical child's familiar dies, its consciousness simply leaves its body, and the magical child can replace its body after 24 hours. To do so, she must conduct an 8-hour ritual that costs 200 gp per her vigilante level, but once the ritual is complete, the familiar returns in a new body. It retains all of its memories from its earlier service to the magical child." replace="Vigilante specialization"} ::ab[Staunch Ally (Ex)]{icon=power ability="A magical child's familiar counts as the magical child for purposes of the *startling appearance, frightening appearance,* and *stunning appearance* abilities, and it can calculate its DCs using either its own Charisma modifier or the magical child's, whichever is better." imp20="The familiar can make *vengeance strikes* as if it were the magical child." alter="Startling appearance~frightening appearance~stunning appearance~vengeance strike"}

name: Mounted Fury
description: ## Mounted Fury ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/58› Some vigilantes form special bonds with the creatures they use as steeds, considering these loyal and trusted mounts just as much heroes or antiheroes as they might be. Mounted furies often masquerade as anonymous stable hands or humble quartermasters to mask their vigilante activities. ::cskill{gain=ha lose=swim~umd} ::ab[Thorough Change]{icon=down info="A mounted fury must take care when changing from one identity to another, including making any changes necessary to ensure that his mount is not associated with his social identity and vice versa (although if anyone suspects him of being anything other than what he appears to be while in his social identity, he need not make a separate Disguise check for his mount). The mounted fury always requires 1 minute to change identities, regardless of other effects that reduce the time required, and he cannot choose the ‹soctalent/immediate change› or ‹soctalent/quick change› social talents." alter="Dual identity"} ::ab[Mount (Ex)]{icon=power ability="A mounted fury gains the service of a loyal and trusty steed to carry him into battle. This mount functions as a druid's ‹sidekick/animal companion›, using the mounted fury's vigilante level as his effective druid level. The creature must be one that he is capable of riding and is suitable as a mount. A Medium mounted fury can select a ‹companion/camel› or a ‹companion/horse›. A Small mounted fury can select a ‹companion/pony› or a ‹companion/wolf›, but can also select a ‹companion/boar› or a ‹companion/riding »dog› if he is at least 4th level. The GM might approve other animals as suitable mounts. A mounted fury can exchange or replace his mount the same way that a druid exchanges or replaces her animal companion." passive="A mounted fury does not take an armor check penalty on Ride checks while riding his mount. The mount is always considered combat trained and begins play with ‹feat/Light Armor Proficiency› as a bonus feat. A mounted fury's mount does not gain the *share spells* ability." imp3="A mounted fury's bond with his mount is strong, with the pair learning to anticipate each other's moods and moves. The mounted fury's mount shares all his ‹main/teamwork feat«s›, without needing to meet the prerequisites (although while mounted, the mounted fury and his mount do not count as separate creatures for the purpose of these feats)." imp5="The mounted fury's mount benefits from the vigilante's *startling appearance* as if it were the vigilante." special="Should a mounted fury's mount die, the mounted fury may find another mount to serve him after 1 week of mourning. This new mount does not gain the *link* or *devotion* special abilities until the next time the mounted fury gains a level." ability2="A mounted fury can select avenger ‹ability/vigilante talents›, despite not being an avenger. He can also select a teamwork feat for which he qualifies in place of a vigilante talent." imp10="He gains an additional teamwork feat each time he selects a teamwork feat in place of a vigilante talent (if he selected any teamwork feats in place of vigilante talents before 10th level, he gains an additional teamwork feat at 10th level for each time he did so)." order=ap2 replace="Vigilante specialization"} ::ab[Furious Charge (Ex)]{l=6 icon=boost-def flavor="A mounted fury learns to make more accurate charge attacks while mounted." passive="The mounted fury and his mount receive a +4 bonus on melee attack rolls on a ‹rule/charge› while mounted (instead of the normal +2). In addition, the mounted fury and his mount don't take any penalty to AC after making a charge attack while mounted." replace="Vigilante talent gained at 6th level"} ::ab[Mighty Charge (Ex)]{l=12 icon=boost-melee flavor="A mounted fury learns to make devastating charge attacks while mounted." passive="He doubles the critical threat range of any weapons he wields during a charge while mounted, as well as the critical threat range of the mount's attacks. This increase does not stack with other effects that increase the threat range of weapons." order=pa ability="In addition, the mounted fury can make a free ‹rule/bull rush›, ‹rule/disarm›, ‹rule/sunder›, or ‹rule/trip› combat maneuver if his charge attack is successful. This free combat maneuver does not provoke an attack of opportunity." replace="Vigilante talent gained at 12th level"} ::ab[Vengeance Strike (Ex)]{l=20 icon=down info="A mounted fury need not be mounted while he studies a target against whom he plans a *vengeance strike,* but he must be mounted when he makes the strike's attack." alter="Vengeance strike"}

name: Psychometrist

features.name: Implements and Focus Powers (Su)
features.replaces: Vigilante talents gained at 2nd, 6th, 12th, and 18th levels

description: ## Psychometrist ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/59› Wise vigilantes know that there is power in certain seemingly unremarkable items. Psychometrists aren't spellcasters; instead, they collect strange items or create their own uncanny gadgets that seem to only work for them. Psychometrists often hide their clandestine activities behind the guise of an eccentric peddler, curator, tinker, or artificer. ::cskill{gain=ka~kh lose=kd~ke} ::ab[Occult Awareness]{l=1 icon=power ability="A psychometrist gains ‹feat/Psychic Sensitivity› as a bonus feat." replace="Social talent gained at 1st level"} ::ab[Implements and Focus Powers (Su)]{l=2 order=ca icon=power choice="A psychometrist learns to use the powers of one ‹ability/implement« school<s› from the ‹class/occultist› class; the conjuration implement school is not available to a psychometrist. This implement school does not allow the psychometrist to cast any spells of that school of magic, though, and he can't use spell trigger or spell completion magic items from any schools without succeeding at the appropriate Use Magic Device check." ability="The psychometrist treats his vigilante level as his occultist level for purposes of determining how his implements' focus powers work, and for determining at what level he may choose certain focus powers. Unlike an occultist, each of a psychometrist's focus powers has its own associated implement or gadget. For example, a psychometrist might own a scabbard implement to use the *legacy weapon* focus power and an implement that is a pair of boots to use the *sudden speed* focus power. The psychometrist must assign mental focus separately to each implement each day, and he doesn't gain resonant powers his implements. Otherwise, this ability acts like the occultist's implements class feature." repeat="The psychometrist learns to use one additional implement school.~0~6" special="Each time a psychometrist learns an implement school, he learns the base focus power from that school, plus one focus power from each implement school he has previously learned (but not from the new school he just learned). The psychometrist can use focus powers only by expending *mental focus* (see below). Unless otherwise noted, the DC for any saving throw against a focus power equals 10 + 1/2 the psychometrist's vigilante level + the psychometrist's Intelligence modifier.~~~The psychometrist can select a school he already knows, and in this case, he gains a total of two new focus powers from that school (instead of learning the base focus power from the new school)." replace="Vigilante talents gained at 2nd, 6th, 12th, and 18th levels"} ::ab[Mental Focus (Su)]{l=2 head icon=power ability="Like an occultist, a psychometrist has *mental focus* he can invest into his implements each day to allow him to utilize abilities tied to them. A psychometrist has a number of points of *mental focus* equal to ‹misc/half› his vigilante level plus his Intelligence modifier."} :::ab{next title="Mental Focus (Su)" flavor="Relevant text from the occultist class ability." icon=magic action=Ability} You have a number of points of mental focus; these points refresh each day. You can divide this mental focus between your implements in any way you desire. If an implement is lost or destroyed, the focus invested in it is lost as well, though you still refresh those points of focus normally. Once mental focus is invested inside an implement, you can expend the mental focus stored in the implement to activate the associated focus powers you know. You refresh your mental focus once each day after receiving at least 8 hours of sleep. After refreshing your mental focus, you must spend 1 hour preparing your implements and investing them with this power. Mental focus that is not used before the next time you refresh your focus is lost. You can choose to save generic mental focus inside your own body instead of investing all of it, but expending this focus comes at a higher cost. Any focus power you activate with generic focus costs twice as much mental focus to use (and to maintain, if applicable). You can expend your generic focus through an appropriate implement on any focus power you know. ::: ::ab[Object Reading (Su)]{l=2 head icon=power ability="A psychometrist can read information from items he examines, and gains the occultist's *object reading* ability." replace=Unshakable} ::ab[Object Reading (Su)]{flavor="Text from the occultist class ability." next icon=power ability="You learn how to read information from items you examine. Examining an item in this way requires you to spend 1 minute handling the item. If the item is a magic item, you learn its properties and command word as if you had successfully examined the item using ‹spell/detect magic› and succeeded at a ‹skill/Spellcraft› check. This ability does not reveal whether the item is cursed unless your class level is equal to or greater than the caster level of the item. If the item has any historical significance, you learn one piece of information about its past (as determined by the GM). Finally, if the item was last used no longer than 1 day ago per your class level, you learn one piece of information about the last creature to use the item. This information might be a glimpse of the creature's appearance, a brief vision of what it saw while using the item, or perhaps its emotional state when it last used the item. The GM determines what information is gained in this way. This functions like the ‹skill/psychometry« occult skill unlock›, but doesn't require a skill check and can be used at will."} ::ab[Psychometric Strike (Su)]{l=20 icon=boost passive="A psychometrist gains twice the usual benefits of *vengeance strike* (up to the same maximum) against an opponent who possesses an object that once belonged to the psychometrist." alter="Vengeance strike"}

name: Warlock
description: ## Warlock ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/60› Practicing magic in secret, the warlock obscures her arcane scholarship from public view. Her study of these arts allows her to hide her dual nature and enchant her enemies - or simply blast them with furious magical attacks. ::cskill{gain=ka~spc lose=dd~ke~per~sur} ::ab[Skill Ranks per Level]{icon=down info="The warlock gains a number of skill ranks equal to 4 + her Intelligence modifier at each level, instead of 6 + her Intelligence modifier skill ranks." alter="Skill ranks per level"} ::ab[Armor Proficiencies]{icon=down-power ability="A warlock is not proficient with medium armor. Like a ‹class/magus›, she can cast her spells while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance." alter="Armor proficiencies"} ::ab[Spellcasting]{icon=learn ability="A warlock casts arcane spells and cantrips as a magus. She prepares spells using a spellbook, choosing them from the 6th-level and lower spells from the ‹main/spells_>sorcerer›/‹main/spells_>wizard› spell list; higher-level sorcerer/wizard spells are not on the warlock's spell list." replace="4th-, 8th-, 10th-, 14th-, and 16th-level vigilante talents"} ::ab[Spellbook]{icon=learn ability="A warlock has a spellbook that functions in the same way as a magus's spellbook but uses the 6th-level and lower spells from the sorcerer/wizard spell list."} ::ab[Mystic Bolts (Su)]{icon=melee-ranged order=an ability="A warlock can sling projectiles of magical energy at will by shooting a bolt or touching her foe. A melee mystic bolt requires the target to be within reach, and a ranged mystic bolt is a ranged attack with a range of 30 feet. A mystic bolt deals points of damage equal to 1d6+‹misc/one-fourth› of her vigilante level." info="The warlock must choose one type of damage for her mystic bolt: acid, cold, electricity, or fire. Attacking with a mystic bolt takes the place of one of the warlock's normal attacks, and she can make a full attack using mystic bolts. The warlock vigilante attacks with mystic bolts as though they were light one-handed weapons, and the bolts can be used for ‹rule/two-weapon fighting› (with each hand creating one mystic bolt) and feats and abilities that apply to weapon attacks (unless they're excluded from that feat, such as with ‹feat/Power Attack›). ‹feat/Weapon Focus› (ray) doesn't apply to mystic bolts, but a warlock can take Weapon Focus (mystic bolt) and apply it to both melee and ranged mystic bolts.~~~Creating a mystic bolt requires the hand to be free, but the bolt appears only briefly, so a warlock using mystic bolts has a free hand any time she isn't attacking with a mystic bolt. The warlock threatens with a mystic bolt, but only if she has a hand free." special="Because mystic bolts are impermanent, a spell that targets a single weapon (like ‹spell/magic weapon›) can't affect it, nor can a mystic bolt be made with magic weapon special abilities. Abilities that affect all weapon attacks the warlock makes, such as the *arcane striker* warlock talent, function with mystic bolts." repeat="The warlock chooses another damage type from the list above.~7~6" imp7="Each time she creates a mystic bolt, she can have it use any one of the damage types she has selected." replace="Vigilante specialization"} ::ab[Piercing Bolts (Ex)]{icon=touch-zap l3="The warlock can choose one mystic bolt per round to be a touch attack. This turns a melee mystic bolt into a melee touch attack or a ranged mystic bolt into a ranged touch attack." l5="The warlock can treat all of her mystic bolts as touch attacks." replace=Unshakable} ::ab[Warlock Talents]{head icon=power info="A warlock can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general ‹ability/vigilante talents›." alter="Vigilante talents"} ::ab[Arcane Striker (Su)]{next icon=power ability="The warlock gains ‹feat/Arcane Strike› as a bonus feat." imp12="When she activates Arcane Strike, she can choose to also give her weapons the ‹magic-enh/flaming›, ‹magic-enh/frost›, ‹magic-enh/shock›, or ‹magic-enh/thundering› weapon special ability. She makes this choice each time she activates Arcane Strike, and it lasts for the same duration." imp16="She adds ‹magic-enh/anarchic›, ‹magic-enh/axiomatic›, ‹magic-enh/flaming burst›, ‹magic-enh/holy›, ‹magic-enh/icy burst›, ‹magic-enh/shocking burst›, and ‹magic-enh/unholy› to the list of special abilities she can select. She can choose to apply an alignment-based weapon special ability only while in her vigilante identity, and only if it matches the alignment of her vigilante identity."} ::ab[Elemental Armor (Su)]{next icon=def passive="When in her vigilante identity, the warlock gains armor made of elemental energy. She is surrounded by a nimbus of ice, lightning, or flames, granting her resistance 5 to cold, electricity, or fire, respectively. The damage type must be chosen when she selects this talent, and it can't be changed." imp4="The warlock's armor deals 1d6 points of damage of the chosen energy type to any creature striking the warlock with a natural weapon or a non-reach melee weapon. A creature that attempts a ‹rule/grapple› combat maneuver check against the warlock also takes this damage. A creature can take damage in this way no more than once per round." imp8="The energy resistance increases to 10." imp12="The damage increases to 2d6 points." imp16="The warlock becomes immune to the chosen damage type while in her vigilante identity."} ::ab[Familiar (Ex)]{next icon=power ability="The warlock gains a ‹sidekick/familiar›, using her vigilante level as her effective wizard level. The ‹ability/familiar› also has a social identity as a seemingly normal animal, though warlocks with outlandish familiars might still need to hide them."} ::ab[Social Simulacrum (Sp)]{next prereq="8th-level vigilante" icon=magic ability="The warlock can create a short-lived simulacrum (as ‹spell/lesser simulacrum›) that duplicates her social identity, allowing her to appear to be in two places at once. Creating the duplicate takes 1 hour and requires no material component cost. It lasts for 4 hours before turning back into an inert pile of snow.~~~The duplicate replicates only the warlock's social identity, with the same alignment and social talents. It has no magical abilities, and can't assume a vigilante identity. As with the spell, the simulacrum isn't under the warlock's control." special="The warlock can create a social simulacrum no more than once per day and can have only one in existence at a time."} ::ab[Tattoo Chamber (Su)]{next icon=magic flavor="This talent functions as the ‹arc-vigilante/cabalist› ability of the same name. The text below is from that ability." order=a2 ability="The warlock can magically absorb items through a tattoo on his hand or wrist and easily retrieve them or activate their magical abilities without making them manifest. The items seemingly disappear into the tattoo, but actually enter an extradimensional space that the warlock can access via the tattoo. Stowing an item in this way requires a @HLfull-round_action, and the space can store a number of items equal to 1 + ‹misc/one-third› of his vigilante level. These items must be items the warlock can hold in one hand." ability2="Retrieving a stowed item requires mentally activating the tattoo as a @HLswift_action. The item appears in the warlock's hand, so worn items must still be donned to gain their benefits." special="The warlock can also activate any ‹misc/spell-trigger› abilities of a stored item as though he were wielding the item, producing the magic effect from his tattoo rather than from the item. If the warlock dies while items are within his tattoo chamber, those items fade into existence within 5 feet of the corpse."}

name: Wildsoul
sourceBook: Ultimate Intrigue, Blood of the Beast

features.name: Natural Course (Ex)
features.replaces: Vigilante talents gained at 2nd, 6th, 12th, and 18th levels

description: ## Wildsoul ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/61› Within some vigilantes are incredible innate abilities that, although normally the domain of natural beasts, inexplicably aid them in fighting their enemies. These vigilantes have ties to the creature whose abilities they emulate, whether from a distant lycanthrope ancestor, a divine touch, unnatural experimentation, or something else altogether. ::ab[Natural Course (Ex)]{icon=power l1="When a wildsoul chooses a vigilante specialization, he must also choose a natural course: *arachnid, falconine, feline,* or *ursine.* This represents the type of creature that influences his body, granting him his remarkable abilities. Once this choice is made, it can't be changed.~~~At 2nd, 6th, 12th, and 18th levels, a wildsoul gains a specific ability tied to his natural course. These abilities count as vigilante talents, as onlookers who see the wildsoul in his social identity use them overtly might suspect him of being something more than he appears; the more obvious animalistic abilities (like *bear form* and *shoot webs*) impart a -10 penalty on the wildsoul's Disguise check to appear as his social identity." alter="Vigilante specialization" replace="Vigilante talents gained at 2nd, 6th, 12th, and 18th levels"} ::h3[Arachnid]{jl} These wildsouls have the blood of spiders running through their veins. ::ab[Heightened Senses (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power flavor="An arachnid wildsoul can anticipate physical danger and react astonishingly quickly." ability="He gains the ‹vigtalent/stalker sense› vigilante talent, even if he is not a stalker."} ::ab[Shoot Webs (Ex)]{l=6 icon=zap ability="An arachnid wildsoul's wrists can produce thick, sticky webbing that he can shoot at his enemies. Shooting webbing is a ranged touch attack with a range increment of 10 feet. The webbing acts as a ‹eq-weapon/tanglefoot bag› when it hits a creature, except the DC of the Reflex save to avoid being glued to the floor or unable to fly is equal to 10 + 1/2 the arachnid wildsoul's vigilante level + his Constitution modifier. Like a tanglefoot bag, the webbing does not work underwater." useMod=Constitution3} ::ab[Web Specialist (Ex)]{l=12 icon=power order=am ability="An arachnid wildsoul can coat his hands and feet in super-sticky webbing, even over equipment such as gloves and boots. This gives him a climb speed of 30 feet." move="An arachnid wildsoul can use his webbing to create the equivalent of a 50-foot length of ‹eq-misc/silk rope «1d3 if he is Small›."} ::ab[Bear Jaws (Ex)]{l=6 icon=melee ability="An ursine wildsoul gains a bite attack while in his vigilante identity. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d4 points of damage if he is Medium or 1d3 if he is Small."} ::ab[Thick Hide (Ex)]{l=12 icon=def passive="An ursine wildsoul in his vigilante identity has skin that bristles with thick hair like that of a bear's. He gains a natural armor bonus of +1." increment="This natural armor bonus~12~4"} ::ab[Bear Form (Su)]{l=18 icon=magic flavor="An ursine wildsoul has learned how to take a bear's form." standard="He can change into bear form at will, and the transformation lasts until he changes back. While transformed, he becomes a ‹monster/grizzly bear› as ‹spell/beast shape II›. An ursine wildsoul loses his ability to speak while in bear form and is limited to the sounds that a normal bear can make, though he can communicate normally with other bears, as ‹spell/speak with animals›."} ::h3[Feline]{jl} ‹SOURCE Blood of the Beast/7› Feline wildsouls have the blood of great cats running through their veins. ::ab[Feline Attributes (Ex)]{l=2 icon=power-boost ability="A feline wildsoul gains the ‹umr/low-light vision› and ‹umr/scent› special abilities and reduces any penalty he takes on Perception checks due to distance by an amount equal to ‹misc/half› his vigilante level (minimum 0). If he also gains low-light vision or scent from a feat or racial trait, he instead gains a +2 bonus on Perception checks for each ability he already has." special="He can take ‹feat/Aspect of the Beast›, ignoring the feat's prerequisites."} ::ab[Feline Grace (Ex)]{icon=def l6="A feline wildsoul gains ‹ability/uncanny dodge›, using his vigilante level as his effective ‹class/rogue› level." l12="He also gains ‹ability/improved uncanny dodge›."} ::ab[Feline Pounce (Ex)]{l=12 icon=power flavor="A feline wildsoul can strike quickly and lethally at a moment's notice." ability="He gains the ‹vigtalent/mad rush› avenger vigilante talent, even if he is not an avenger."} ::ab[Nine Lives (Su)]{l=18 icon=def flavor="A feline wildsoul can survive attacks that would kill lesser vigilantes." ability="He gains the ‹talent/defensive roll› advanced rogue talent and can use this ability eight times per day."}

name: Zealot

features.name: Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells

description: ## Zealot ‹SOURCE Ultimate Intrigue/62;Inner Sea Intrigue/33› Dedicated to a single deity, the zealot hunts the enemies of his faith in secret, often because his religion is outlawed or persecuted in the region. ::cskill{gain=kr~spc lose=dd~ke~perf~soh} ::ab[Skill Ranks per Level]{icon=down info="A zealot gains a number of skill ranks equal to 4 + his Intelligence modifier at each level, instead of 6 + his Intelligence modifier skill ranks."} ::ab[Weapon Proficiencies]{icon=power ability="A zealot is also proficient in his deity's favored weapon, even if it is an exotic weapon, and if the deity's favored weapon is unarmed strike, he gains ‹feat/Improved Unarmed Strike› as a bonus feat." alter="Weapon proficiencies"} ::ab[Spellcasting]{icon=learn ability="A zealot casts divine spells and orisons as an ‹class/inquisitor› and uses the ‹main/spells_>inquisitor«'s spell list›." replace="4th-, 8th-, 10th-, 14th-, and 16th-level vigilante talents"} ::ab[Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells]{icon=down info="Zealots can't cast spells of an alignment opposed to his vigilante identity's alignment or that of his deity. Spells associated with particular alignments are indicated by the chaotic, evil, good, and lawful descriptors in their spell descriptions."} ::ab[Alignment]{icon=warning info="A zealot's alignment must be within one step of his deity's, along either the law/chaos axis or the good/evil axis, but only when in his vigilante identity. If his social identity's alignment isn't within one step of his deity's, he can't cast spells in his social identity."} ::ab[Aura (Ex)]{icon=aura info="A zealot of a chaotic, evil, good, or lawful deity has a particularly powerful aura corresponding to the deity's alignment (see ‹spell/detect evil› spell for details), but only when in his vigilante identity."} ::ab[Inquisition (Ex)]{icon=magic choice="A zealot picks a deity and picks a single ‹ability/inquisition<s› tied to that deity." special="He uses his vigilante level as his inquisitor level to determine level dependent inquisition abilities." replace="Vigilante specialization"} ::ab[Zealot Talents]{head icon=power info="A zealot can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general ‹ability/vigilante talents›." alter="Vigilante talents"} ::ab[Channel Energy (Su)]{next icon=aura ability="A zealot who takes this talent can ‹ability/channel energy› with an effective cleric level equal to his vigilante level - 4 (minimum 1) while in his vigilante identity. If good in his vigilante identity (or if he worships a good deity), the vigilante channels positive energy and can choose to deal damage to undead creatures or to heal living creatures. If evil in his vigilante identity (or if he worships an evil deity), the vigilante channels negative energy and can choose to deal damage to living creatures or to heal undead creatures. If the vigilante is neutral in his vigilante identity and worships a neutral deity, the vigilante must choose whether he channels positive or negative energy. Once this choice is made, it can't be reversed."} ::ab[Discern Lies (Sp)]{next icon=magic prereq="6th-level vigilante" immediate="The zealot can use ‹spell/discern lies› as a spell-like ability for a number of rounds per day equal to his vigilante level. The rounds need not be consecutive."} ::ab[Empower Symbol (Su)]{next prereq="6th-level vigilante" icon=magic standard="The zealot can empower his holy symbol. If the zealot is of good alignment while in his vigilante identity (or worships a good deity), this works as if the holy symbol was the center of a ‹spell/consecrate› effect. If the zealot is of evil alignment in his vigilante identity (or worships an evil deity), this works as if the holy symbol was the center of a ‹spell/desecrate› effect. If the zealot is neutral in his vigilante identity and worships a neutral deity, he can choose whether this ability acts as per consecrate or desecrate, but once the choice is made, it cannot be changed." imp10="The zealot treats his holy symbol as a permanent fixture for the purpose of determining the consecration or desecration effects."} ::ab[Harsh Judgment (Su)]{next icon=power ability="A vigilante with this talent can pronounce *judgment* upon his foes as per the ‹class/inquisitor› class feature. He can choose from among the following inquisitor judgments: *destruction, piercing, purity,* and *smiting.* For the purpose of determining the bonuses provided by this ability, the vigilante's level stacks with levels in any other classes that grant *judgment* or *harsh judgment.*" useInc=vigilante~3~1 useF="1~1~3"} ::ab[Stalwart (Ex)]{next prereq="12th-level vigilante" flavor="A zealot with this talent can use mental and physical resilience to avoid certain attacks." icon=def ability="If he succeeds at a Fortitude or Will saving throw against an attack that has a reduced effect on a successful save, he avoids the effect entirely. A ‹misc/helpless› zealot doesn't gain the benefit of this ability."} ::ab[Stern Gaze (Ex)]{next icon=boost flavor="A zealot with this talent is skilled at sensing deception and intimidating his foes." passive="The zealot gains a morale bonus on all Intimidate and Sense Motive checks equal to half his vigilante level (minimum +1)."} ::ab[Zealot Smite (Su)]{next icon=power-lower flavor="A zealot with this talent can use this power to smite a foe." useInc=vigilante~3~2 useF="2~1~3" order=nwu info="Zealots that are good in their vigilante identity (or worship a good deity) can *smite* evil creatures, those that are evil in their vigilante identity (or worship an evil deity) can *smite* good creatures, those that are chaotic in their vigilante identity (or worship a chaotic deity) can *smite* lawful creatures, and those that are lawful in their vigilante identity (or worship a lawful deity) can *smite* chaotic creatures. A zealot that is neutral when in his vigilante identity and that worships a neutral deity can pick to *smite* any one of the four alignments; other zealots must select from the alignments available based on their own alignment or their deity's. Once that choice is made, it can't be changed." swift="The zealot chooses one target within sight to *smite.* If this target is of the proper alignment, the zealot adds his Charisma bonus on his attack rolls (to a maximum of half his vigilante level) and his vigilante level on all damage rolls against the target of his *smite.* If the target of *smite* is an outsider with an alignment subtype of the *zealot's smite,* a similarly aligned dragon, or an undead creature (if the *zealot's smite* is against evil creatures), a good-aligned cleric or paladin (if the *zealot's smite* is against good creatures), a chaotic aberration (if the *zealot's smite* is against chaotic creatures), or a lawful-aligned cleric or paladin (if the *zealot's smite* is against lawful creatures), the bonus to damage on the first successful attack increases to 2 points of damage per vigilante level. Regardless of the target, the *zealot's smite* attacks bypass the creature's DR as if it were a weapon with a +5 enhancement bonus."}

name: Beast-Bonded
description: ## Beast-Bonded ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/83› While all witches are intimately tied to their familiars, a beast-bonded witch's craft focuses specifically on her familiar bond and developing the relationship with her patron through her familiar. ::ab[Transfer Feats (Ex)]{icon=info ability="Whenever the beast-bonded witch is capable of learning a new feat, she may choose to instead have her familiar learn the feat as a bonus feat. The familiar must meet the prerequisites for any feats that it learns this way." special="If her familiar is lost or dies, the witch can reclaim the feat slots and select new feats for herself, or apply the slots toward her new familiar."} ::ab[Enhanced Familiar (Su)]{l=4 icon=boost flavor="The beast-bonded witch's connection with her familiar strengthens." info="For the purposes of determining her familiar's powers and abilities, she treats her familiar as if she were one level higher than her actual witch level." replace="4th-level hex"} ::ab[Familiar Form (Sp)]{l=8 icon=magic ability="A beast-bonded witch may take the shape of her familiar (or a giant version of her familiar or a similar kind of animal) as if using ‹spell/beast shape II›. For example, a witch with a rat familiar can turn into a Tiny rat, Small dire rat, or a larger rodent; one with a cat familiar can turn into a Tiny cat or a Large feline such as a tiger or lion; one with a monkey familiar can turn into a Tiny monkey or a Large gorilla, and so on." useL=witch useUnit=minute replace="8th-level hex"} ::ab[Twin Soul (Su)]{l=10 icon=aid ability="If the witch or her familiar is gravely injured or about to die, the soul of the dying one immediately transfers to the other's body. The two souls share the surviving body peaceably, can communicate freely, and both retain their ability to think and reason. The host may allow the guest soul to take over the body temporarily or reclaim it as a @HLmove_action. They can persist in this state indefinitely, or the guest can return to its own body (if available) by touch, transfer into a suitable vessel (such as a ‹spell/clone›), or take over another body as if using ‹spell/magic jar› (with no receptacle)." replace="Major hex at 10th-level"} ::list[The following witch hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Beast of ill omen~charm~feral speech~ward"} ::list[The following major hex complements this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Beast eye"} ::list[The following grand hex complements this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Forced reincarnation"}

name: Flood Walker
description: ## Flood Walker ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/89› Witches who dwell in floodplains or along the banks of predictably dangerous rivers can tap into the underlying potential of surging waters in order to enhance their eerie powers. ::ab[Alignment]{icon=warning info="Flood walkers exult in the final gasp for air of a drowning victim and must be evil in alignment. A flood walker who becomes nonevil loses access to all abilities granted by this archetype but does not regain any abilities this archetype replaced."} ::cskill{gain=sur~swim lose=fly~heal} ::ab[Patron Spells]{icon=learn info="Regardless of which patron a flood walker selects, he replaces some of his patron spells with the following at the listed witch level." s4="Aboleth's lung" s10=Suffocation s16=Seamantle s18="Mass suffocation" alter="Patron spells"} ::ab[Gasping Breath Aura (Su)]{icon=aura-lower passive="A creature attempting to ‹misc/hold its breath› within 30 feet of a flood walker is treated as having taken a standard or full-round action when determining how long it can hold its breath, regardless of the number and type of actions it takes in a round." imp5="Increase the DC of Swim checks attempted within 30 feet of the flood walker by 5, and creatures actively engaged in combat or a similarly strenuous activity use air twice as quickly within the aura. The flood walker can exempt creatures within this aura from these increased penalties." replace="1st-level hex"} ::ab[River Stride (Su)]{l=6 icon=power ability="A flood walker and his familiar can walk on the surface of water and other liquids as if under the effects of a ‹spell/water walk› spell. The flood walker chooses at the beginning of his turn each round whether this ability is active or suppressed (for himself and his familiar separately), allowing him to walk on water or swim." replace="6th-level hex"} ::ab[Breath Siphon (Su)]{l=10 icon=boost flavor="A flood walker gains strength from his patron when creatures suffocate or drown." ability="Whenever a creature with an Intelligence of 3 or higher asphyxiates or drowns within 30 feet of him, the flood walker gains the benefit of a ‹spell/death knell› spell for 1 hour. If a flood walker drowns such a victim himself (such as by holding a grappled or helpless creature under water until it dies or by killing it with a *suffocation* spell), the duration is doubled, and the flood walker gains 4d8 ‹rule/temporary hit points› and a +6 enhancement bonus to Strength instead of the usual temporary hit points and enhancement bonus to Strength from *death knell.* Like *death knell* itself, this is an evil act." replace="10th-level hex"} ::list[The following witch hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Blight~prehensile hair~swamp hag~water lung"} ::list[The following major hex complements this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Weather control"} ::list[The following grand hex complements this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Natural disaster"}

name: Gravewalker
description: ## Gravewalker ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/84› Having much in common with necromancers, the gravewalker is obsessed with the occult manipulations of the dead, particularly mindless undead such as zombies. Unlike the creations of standard necromancers, a gravewalker's creations remain forever tied to her will, and she can produce vile apparitions of tremendous power. ::ab[Spells]{icon=learn info="A gravewalker replaces some of her patron spells at the following witch levels." s4="Command undead" s6="Animate dead" s12="Create undead" s14="Control undead" s16="Create greater undead" alter="Patron spells"} ::ab[Spell Poppet]{head icon=power ability="Each gravewalker carries around a gristly, inanimate poppet stitched from human skin and stuffed with shards of bone, fingernails, and grave dirt. A gravewalker's spells come from the will of evil spirits residing in the poppet, and its ability to hold spells functions in a manner identical to the way a witch's spells are granted by her familiar. The gravewalker must commune with her poppet each day to prepare her spells and cannot prepare spells that are not stored in the poppet." replace=Familiar special="The following familiar ability works differently for a gravewalker."} ::ab[Deliver Touch Spells (Su)]{next l=3 icon=zap ability="A gravewalker can use her poppet to deliver touch spells. After casting a touch spell, as a @HLfull-round_action, the witch can designate a target and stab a pin into her poppet, delivering the spell as a ranged touch attack. The target must be within range of her *aura of desecration* ability (see below)."} ::ab[Aura of Desecration (Su)]{icon=aura-boost l1="A gravewalker can create a 20-foot-radius aura of evil power. This aura increases the DC of channeled negative energy by +1 and the turn resistance of undead by +1." incrementPlain="The radius of the aura~1~2~25~5" incrementEnd=" feet." replace="1st-level hex" imp20="The radius of the aura increases to 70 feet."} ::ab[Bonethrall (Su)]{l=1 icon=magic ability="A gravewalker can take control of an undead creature within her *aura of desecration* by forcing her will upon it (Will negates, using her hex DC). If it fails the save, the creature falls under her control as if she had used *command undead* (once control is established, the undead remain controlled even if outside the witch's *aura*). Intelligent undead receive a new saving throw each day to resist her command." special="The witch can control up to 1 HD of undead creatures per caster level. If an undead creature is under the control of another creature, the witch must make an opposed Charisma check whenever her orders conflict with that creature's." replace="4th-level hex"} ::ab[Possess Undead (Sp)]{icon=magic l8="A gravewalker may take direct control of one of her undead minions within her *aura of desecration,* as if using ‹spell/magic jar›; the witch's poppet acts as the soul receptacle for this ability. The minion gets no saving throw against this ability." replace="8th-level hex"} ::list[The following witch hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Beast of ill-omen~evil eye~misfortune"} ::list[The following major hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Ice tomb~infected wounds~waxen image"} ::list[The following grand hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Death curse~summon spirit"}

name: Hedge Witch
description: ## Hedge Witch ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/84› Among witches, there are those who devote themselves to the care of others and restrict their practices to the healing arts. They often take the place of clerics in rural communities and may wander the countryside servicing the needs of several small communities. ::ab[Patron]{icon=info info="A hedge witch's ‹ability/patron<s› is normally one with a ‹patron/healing› theme."} ::ab[Spontaneous Healing (Su)]{icon=magic flavor="A hedge witch can channel stored spell energy into healing spells that she did not prepare ahead of time." ability="The witch can &quot&lose&quot& any prepared spell that is not an orison in order to cast any ‹main/cure spell<s› of the same spell level or lower, even if she doesn't know that cure spell." replace="4th-level hex"} ::ab[Empathic Healing (Su)]{icon=aid ability="A hedge witch can minister to a diseased or poisoned target, redirecting the affliction into herself. For a poisoned target, the witch must tend to him as a @HLstandard_action; he makes his next saving throw against the poison as normal, but the witch suffers the effects of the failed save instead of the poisoned creature.~~~For a diseased target, the witch must tend to the sick person for an hour; he makes his next saving throw against the disease as normal, but the witch suffers the effects of the failed save instead of the diseased creature." special="The witch does not actually become poisoned or diseased (and is not contagious and does not need to be cured), but suffers the effects of the affliction as if she had been. The witch normally uses this ability to extend the life of someone near death, giving him time to recover. This ability has no effect if the witch is immune to disease or poison." replace="8th-level hex"} ::list[The following witch hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Cauldron~feral speech~healing~tongues"} ::list[The following major hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Major healing~weather control~witch's brew"} ::list[The following grand hex complements this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Life giver"}

name: Herb Witch
sourceBook: Ultimate Wilderness, Heroes of the Wild
description: ## Herb Witch ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/89;Heroes of the Wild/11› Some witches dedicate their lives to the mastery of herb lore. Herb witches brew foul-tasting medicines, sweet poisons, and other concoctions from the untamed plants of the wild. ::ab[Patron]{icon=info info="An herb witch must choose a patron with a theme compatible with the needs of the natural world, selected from the following list: ‹patron/ancestors›, ‹patron/animals›, ‹patron/death›, ‹patron/elements›, ‹patron/healing›, ‹patron/plague›, ‹patron/strength›, ‹patron/time›, ‹patron/water›, ‹patron/winter›, ‹patron/wisdom›, or ‹patron/woodlands›." alter=Patron} :::ab{title="Herb Lore (Ex)" action=Remedy order=aC icon=power-boost ability="Herb witches are masters of herbalism, and they can use what they gather from garden or grove to duplicate many of the effects of alchemy. An herb witch can attempt Profession (herbalist) checks in place of Craft (alchemy) checks, and she gains a bonus on Profession (herbalist) checks equal to half her class level." replace="1st- and 10th-level hexes" imp10="While attempting to remedy a disease or poison, if she exceeds the DC of the check by 10 or more, the affliction immediately ends. While attempting to remedy a condition, if the herb witch succeeds by 10 or more, she can remove a permanent condition." special="If the disease or poison doesn't allow saving throws, the remedy is ineffective. Only a single condition, disease, or poison can be removed with each application of a remedy, and a creature can only benefit from one herbal remedy each day, whether or not the herb witch succeeds at her skill check."} Herb witches are adept at brewing thick herbal cure-alls called remedies. An herb witch prepares these remedies while communing with her familiar, during which she can prepare a number of remedies equal to 3 + her Intelligence modifier (minimum 1 remedy). A remedy becomes inert if it leaves the herb witch's possession, reactivating as soon as it returns to her keeping. A witch can never have more remedies than 3 + her Intelligence modifier. As a @HL[standard action], the herb witch can administer a remedy to herself or a creature within reach which consumes the remedy. The herb witch attempts a Profession (herbalist) check against the save DC of any one disease or poison currently afflicting the consumer. If she is successful, the affliction is suppressed for 1 minute. An herb witch can also use a remedy to attempt to remove the blinded, deafened, fatigued, nauseated, sickened, and staggered conditions. This requires a Profession (herbalist) check with a DC equal to the spell or effect that caused the condition, or a DC 25 check if the condition was caused by an effect that doesn't allow a saving throw. If the herb witch succeeds, the condition is removed unless the condition is permanent. ::: ::ab[Hexes]{icon=info info="An herb witch must select ‹hex/cauldron› as her hex at 2nd level."} ::list[The following witch hexes complement complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Fortune~healing~poison steep~swamp hag"} ::list[The following major hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Major healing~weather control~witch's brew"} ::list[The following grand hex complements this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Life giver"}

name: Sea Witch
description: ## Sea Witch ‹SOURCE Ultimate Magic/85› A sea witch's affinities are tied to the vast oceans and the rolling waves. Her magic concerns the moon, tides, water, and winds, and she is most at peace when she is upon or near the sea. ::ab[Patron]{icon=down info="A sea witch cannot choose a patron whose interests or theme opposes that of water (for example, earth or fire)."} ::ab[Spells]{icon=learn info="A sea witch replaces some of her patron spells at the listed witch levels." s2="Touch of the sea" s4="Gust of wind" s6="Water breathing" s8="Control water" s10=Cloudkill s12="Control winds" s14="Control weather" s16=Vortex s18=Tsunami} ::ab[Know Direction (Sp)]{icon=magic ability="So long as she near a sizable body of water (at least a lake with a diameter of 1 mile or more), a sea witch may cast ‹spell/know direction› at will as a spell-like ability."} ::ab[Sea Creature Empathy (Ex)]{icon=power ability="A sea witch can influence the attitude of water-dwelling animals and animals that live along coasts and shores, including birds, as if using ‹ability/wild empathy›. The sea witch uses her witch level as her ‹class/druid› level for this ability. If the sea witch has *wild empathy* from another class, her witch levels stack with the other class's levels to determine her wild empathy bonus for these kinds of creatures." replace="1st-level hex"} ::list[The following witch hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Charm~flight~water lung"} ::list[The following major hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Hag's eye~hidden home~weather control"} ::list[The following grand hex complements this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Natural disaster"}

name: Season Witch
description: ## Season Witch ‹SOURCE Ultimate Wilderness/90› Season witches gain their power from the cyclical and mystical exchange of energy passed from one season of nature to another. Often, season witches carry bitter grudges against their fellow witches, with many believing that the season prior to their chosen focus is inferior and the season that replaces their favored time is an usurper of time, but at other times season witches work together, understanding that all are a part of the cycle of the natural world. ::ab[Season of the Witch (Su)]{icon=info head info="A season witch observes the cycles of life through symbolic festivals and the very real passage of time. Their covens celebrate the seasons and their impact on magic. These seasonal cycles alter their magic and mind-set, focusing their spells and hexes on a predominant energy type and philosophy.~~~A season witch makes a commitment to embody the sacred symbolism of a season year round, and learns her spells through communion with nature, divining secrets from shapes in the clouds or the play of leaves on the wind. At 1st level, a season witch chooses the season that defines her abilities as her patron; this choice also provides her certain benefits." alter="Patron~1st-level hex"} ::ab[Spring]{next icon=boost-power order=np info="A spring witch has dominion over the renewing spirit of life and youth." passive="The save DCs of her spells that deal electricity damage increase by 1." imp1="She gains either the ‹hex/charm› hex or ‹hex/disguise› hex as a bonus hex."} ::ab[Summer]{next icon=boost-power order=np info="A summer witch has dominion over growth, the harvest, and toil." passive="The save DCs of her spells that deal fire damage increase by 1." imp1="She gains either the ‹hex/fortune› hex or ‹hex/misfortune› hex as a bonus hex."} ::ab[Autumn]{next icon=boost-power order=np info="An autumn witch has dominion over the provision of the land and the passing of life." passive="The save DCs of her spells that deal acid damage increase by 1." imp1="She gains either the ‹hex/blight› hex or ‹hex/slumber› hex as a bonus hex."} ::ab[Winter]{next icon=boost-power order=np info="A winter witch has dominion over hearth and home." passive="The save DCs of her spells that deal cold damage increase by 1." imp1="She gains either the ‹hex/healing› hex or ‹hex/ward› hex as a bonus hex."} ::list[The following hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Flight|spring~summer's heat|summer~poison steep|autumn~no place like home|winter"} ::list[The following major hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Speak in dreams|spring~agony|summer~hoarfrost|autumn~major healing|winter"} ::list[The following grand hexes complement this archetype]{link=hex hl all="Forced reincarnation|spring~natural disaster|summer~death curse|autumn~life giver|winter"}

name: Arcane Bomber
description: ## Arcane Bomber ‹SOURCE Ultimate Combat/75› To many wizards, the experimentation of the alchemist seems quaint, if not dangerous or frightening. A few wizards take up the secrets of the bomb, however, fusing alchemy with their already considerable magical power. ::ab[Bomb (Su)]{l=1 icon=ranged head ability="The arcane bomber gains an ability nearly identical to the ‹class/alchemist«'s› *bomb* ability. Unlike the alchemist, at 1st level, the arcane bomber chooses one type of energy from the following list: acid, cold, fire, and electricity. He can throw bombs of that type, but cannot modify them with discoveries. This ability stacks with the alchemist *bomb* ability to determine the level of bomb damage, but an arcane bomber that becomes an alchemist does not gain that class's *bomb* ability, nor does an alchemist that becomes an arcane bomber gain this *bomb* ability." replace="Arcane bond"} :::ab{next title="Bomb (Su)" flavor="Relevant text from the alchemist class ability." order=usC action=Info l=1 icon=zap provokes standard="You can make and throw bombs. Drawing the components of, creating, and throwing a bomb is a single action. Thrown bombs have a range of 20 feet and use the ‹rule/Throw Splash Weapon« special attack›. On a direct hit, your bomb inflicts 1d6 points of fire damage + additional damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (this bonus damage is not multiplied on a critical hit or by using feats such as ‹feat/Vital Strike›)." usage="You can use a number of bombs each day equal to your class level + your Intelligence modifier." special="Splash damage from your bomb is always equal to the bomb's minimum damage (so if the bomb would deal 1d6+4 points of fire damage on a direct hit, its splash damage would be 5 points of fire damage). Those caught in the splash damage can attempt a Reflex save for half damage, with a DC equal to 10 + ‹misc/half› your alchemist level + your Intelligence modifier." imp3="The base bomb damage becomes 2d6." imp5="The base bomb damage becomes 3d6." imp7="The base bomb damage becomes 4d6." imp9="The base bomb damage becomes 5d6." imp11="The base bomb damage becomes 6d6." imp13="The base bomb damage becomes 7d6." imp15="The base bomb damage becomes 8d6." imp17="The base bomb damage becomes 9d6." imp19="The base bomb damage becomes 10d6."} In addition to magical extracts, alchemists are adept at swiftly mixing various volatile chemicals and infusing them with their magical reserves to create powerful bombs that they can hurl at their enemies. Bombs are unstable, and if not used in the round they are created, they degrade and become inert - their method of creation prevents large volumes of explosive material from being created and stored.
